city.act.savings.prompt: E — go to the savings bank window
city.act.tickets.prompt: E — ask at the box office
city.ask.bakery.cat: Whose cat is in the basket?
city.ask.bakery.cat.1: "Nobody's and everybody's. Sleeps on the warm buns and we pretend it's on purpose. Customers stroke him and buy more."
city.ask.bakery.cat.2: "The lighthouse keeper has a cat too, a ginger one. Ours visits him along the pier. Comes back smelling of fish and pleased."
city.ask.bakery.morning.1: "The first batch at seven, the second at eleven, pies by evening. Whoever knows the hours eats it hot."
city.ask.bakery.morning.2: "Here's the first batch now. Take a loaf while it crackles. You'll eat half on the way, everyone does."
city.ask.bakery.rye.1: "Rye with caraway. The fishermen take it to sea and the librarian has it with tea on Tuesdays. Two extremes, one loaf."
city.ask.bakery.rye.2: "It's Maslenitsa: what bread? Pancakes! In a stack, with butter, the first one lumpy and free."
city.ask.beer.darts.1: "Freja Bondarenko. Throws calmly, like feeding pigeons, and everything goes in the middle. At the Cog she beats everyone at billiards too."
city.ask.beer.darts.2: "Thrown a few already? Then you've learned: the main thing is not to aim. Joking. Aim."
city.ask.beer.fishermen: What are they arguing about at the bar?
city.ask.beer.fishermen.1: "About the fish nobody caught. It's bigger every time. By closing time it'll be the size of a boat."
city.ask.beer.fishermen.2: "It's Fisherman's Day, everyone here's a hero. Listen and nod and they'll buy you a kvass."
city.ask.beer.kvass.1: "Kvass for you. From the barrel, cold, with a smell of bread. Beer when you grow a moustache, and not right away even then."
city.ask.books.library.1: "It's better there: they lend for free and stamp your diary. I'm not hurt, I go myself on Tuesdays."
city.ask.books.library.2: "They've an amnesty now: old books taken back without a fine. Maybe you've something at home from sixty-eight."
city.ask.books.rare.1: "Birds of the Baltic signed by a gull: a footprint on the cover. Not for sale, for showing."
city.ask.books.sale.1: "Poetry. There's always more of it than readers. Take a volume from the sale table: there are notes in the margins from the previous owners, a bonus."
city.ask.books.sale.2: "When it rains the books go under plastic, and so do the customers. Perfect time to stand and read for free."
city.ask.buffet.clock.1: "Found: they were on stage among the props for Time, Forward! The director swears he thought they were a dummy."
city.ask.buffet.clock.2: "Saturday is the Return of the Clock tournament. White plays at its own risk: the dial still runs fast."
city.ask.buffet.clock.3: "That's today! Run to the Cog, they're setting up the boards already."
city.ask.buffet.pies.1: "Cabbage, egg and onion, and one cherry, for the projectionist. That one isn't for sale."
city.ask.buffet.pies.2: "By evening only the cabbage ones are left. That's not a fault, that's patience."
city.ask.buffet.pies.3: "It's a holiday today, I bake double. It still won't be enough, I know this town."
city.ask.cable.kesha: Is it true a parrot announces the stops?
city.ask.cable.kesha.1: "Kesha, from the Saucer. He sat at the station announcing the wrong stops. Says 'Lighthouse' when you're going to Zenith. Don't get off."
city.ask.cable.kesha.2: "He's home now, on the coffee machine. But once he said 'Horizon', and that station doesn't exist yet. We wrote it down."
city.ask.cable.mitten.1: "A knitted mitten. Left behind since Monday, and it's been riding back and forth. It likes it; I can't speak for the owner."
city.ask.cable.mitten.2: "If it's yours, tell the driver at Zenith. If it isn't, wave at it when it goes by."
city.ask.cable.mitten.3: "In this cold it's better off in the cabin than on the wind's hand."
city.ask.cable.where.1: "Amber Shore to Zenith, that's the main line. From there to the Lighthouse. Horizon and Polar Star are only dotted lines on the map so far."
city.ask.cable.where.2: "You pay in the cabin. The advice is free: sit by a window on the sea side. There are windows everywhere, but that side's better."
city.ask.cable.where.3: "The last cabin is at 23:40. Whoever rides it isn't in a hurry to get home. That's normal."
city.ask.cafe.chess: Who plays chess by the window?
city.ask.cafe.chess.1: "The Professor and the Captain. The Professor says nothing and wins; the Captain plays only black, the 'lighthouse defence'. After school the schoolchildren join in."
city.ask.cafe.chess.2: "At weekends they play for coffee: the loser orders. The Captain pays most often, and he likes it."
city.ask.cafe.chess.3: "Word reached me that you beat somebody. The Professor says he's noted it. He only notes those he means to beat."
city.ask.cafe.chess.4: "The Cog has a ladder and even a notebook of games, but there the losers stand tea and here it's coffee. Choose what to risk."
city.ask.cafe.ck.after: Where should I go after lunch?
city.ask.cafe.ck.after.1: "After lunch to the Rassvet for the matinee at three: while the film runs, the soup has time to be forgotten. Or to the library: it's quiet and they stamp things."
city.ask.cafe.ck.after.2: "Been to the Rassvet already? Then the Cog: on Saturday evening it's the billiards league final. The more people, the quieter they play."
city.ask.cafe.ck.kefir.1: "Put it on the sill, I'm not turning round. Warm kefir makes fluffy pancakes, cold makes stubborn ones. This one's just right. Here's a pie: hot, so honest."
city.ask.cafe.ck.kesha.1: "Kesha eats only sunflower seeds. But he pinches from the table when I'm not looking. I look while he pinches: that's how we keep up relations."
city.ask.cafe.ck.kesha.2: "After you he spent half the day saying 'Thank you for the ride'. While I cooked I turned round three times, thinking it was about the soup."
city.ask.cafe.ck.pilaf: What's the crust in the pilaf?
city.ask.cafe.ck.pilaf.1: "That's the bottom. The crust isn't made, it happens if you don't stir and don't look. I don't look: I stand with my back to it."
city.ask.cafe.ck.pilaf.2: "Today it's pilaf for all. Come before two and you get the bottom. You don't argue with cooks: they carry the law in the ladle."
city.ask.cafe.ck.sour: Why is everything served with sour cream?
city.ask.cafe.ck.sour.1: "Sour cream is like conscience: everyone knows it exists and asks for it once the dish has gone cold. I put a pot on the edge of the hatch. Help yourself."
city.ask.cafe.ck.sour.2: "Only today there's none, and without it syrniki aren't syrniki. If you pass the department store, get me a kefir: I can make what's needed from it. Kefir is my plan B."
city.ask.cafe.ck.sour.3: "Friday, syrniki. I've put the sour cream on the edge. Whoever takes it stays to finish."
city.ask.cafe.espresso: How do you make your espresso?
city.ask.cafe.espresso.1: "Twenty-five seconds, not one more: after that it isn't espresso, it's a conversation. Watch the machine, it tells you itself."
city.ask.cafe.espresso.2: "The first of the morning is for Kesha. Not to drink, just to set beside him: while he listens to the machine cough, he's kind."
city.ask.cafe.espresso.3: "Towards evening people ask for it weaker. Weaker means holding the cup longer."
city.ask.cafe.guestbook: What do people write in the guest book?
city.ask.cafe.guestbook.1: "Everything. About ice cream, the lighthouse, the parrot. I read it every morning: that's how I know who came yesterday. The pages are running out, but the pen is right there, and if you've no thoughts, draw a saucer."
city.ask.cafe.guestbook.2: "The lighthouse keeper on duty looked in yesterday and confirmed: his beam can be seen from our window. It looks better from here than from his side."
city.ask.cafe.guestbook.3: "Is that your entry? I left it as it was: I do that with everyone. Now you're one of us."
city.ask.cafe.ice.flavours: What ice cream do you have?
city.ask.cafe.ice.flavours.1: "Plombir, crème brûlée and one scoop 'at discretion'. Whoever holds the scoop decides, and today that's me."
city.ask.cafe.ice.flavours.2: "In the heat the scoops melt faster than people choose. I've learnt: I take two in advance."
city.ask.cafe.ice.flavours.3: "On Saturday the Saucer cake sits in the case: ice cream is no rival, but it knows how to stand beside it."
city.ask.cafe.ice.gallery: Shall I take my ice cream up to the gallery?
city.ask.cafe.ice.gallery.1: "To the telescope: drop a coin and you get five minutes of sky. Keep the ice cream away from the lens: gulls have sharper eyes."
city.ask.cafe.ice.gallery.2: "In the evening from the gallery you can see the lights come on up the terraces: the lowest first, then upwards, like stitches."
city.ask.cafe.ice.gallery.3: "Seen Venus? The lighthouse keeper swears she winks only at her own. Check: if she winked, you're one of us."
city.ask.clinic.aquarium: What are the fish in the corridor?
city.ask.clinic.aquarium.1: "Guppies and one catfish. Watching fish is good for the blood pressure. The doctor prescribes it as a treatment."
city.ask.clinic.aquarium.2: "The catfish is called the Professor, after the chess player at the Saucer. Both think for a long time and watch with one eye."
city.ask.clinic.order.1: "First the scales, then the chart by the window, then the doctor. In that order, or the doctor takes offence."
city.ask.clinic.order.2: "Mornings the queue is pensioners: they're not ill, they're socialising. They let anyone under seventy go first."
city.ask.clinic.water.1: "Mineral water from the pump room at the Druzhba sanatorium. A glass in the morning, a glass in the evening, and no arguing with the doctor."
city.ask.clinic.water.2: "Had some already? Salty, yes. That's the sea saying hello from inside."
city.ask.clinic.water.3: "And in the cold, a scarf. A scarf cures better than any pill, only nobody prescribes it."
city.ask.cloak.hat.1: "It's hung there since the spring before last. Someone came to the dance in it and went home happy without it."
city.ask.cloak.hat.2: "The department store has the same thing with a yellow duck umbrella: the owner loses it on purpose so they'll say her name on the radio."
city.ask.cloak.tag.1: "Thirteen. Don't frown: thirteen is our quickest, I always hand it back first."
city.ask.cloak.tag.2: "Lose the tag and I'll give the coat back by description. Can you describe your coat? See, most people can't."
city.ask.cloak.weather: What are people checking in today?
city.ask.cloak.weather.1: "In summer umbrellas and one hat, in autumn raincoats, in winter everything woollen in town."
city.ask.cloak.weather.2: "Rain: hang the wet raincoat here by the radiator. By the end it'll be dry and warm as a pie."
city.ask.cloak.weather.3: "Shake the snow off your hat onto the mat, not onto me. Thank you. Mittens on a string? Very grown-up."
city.ask.cog.bf.cup: What's the cup with the bent cog?
city.ask.cog.bf.cup.1: "A bent cog on a stand: the billiards league cup. It was bent on purpose, so nobody takes it for a part. I dust it myself; the winner will forget it anyway."
city.ask.cog.bf.pingpong: Who can I play table tennis with?
city.ask.cog.bf.pingpong.1: "Here it's Kenji Kask: looks left, hits right. And at the sports centre Ursula Okonkwo is waiting for him. They can't agree to play: each expects the other to come."
city.ask.cog.bf.pingpong.2: "You've played? Against whom? If it was Kenji, you already know: he looks left."
city.ask.cog.bf.tea: What does "tea with sugar, no reproach" mean?
city.ask.cog.bf.tea.1: "The ladder's rule: the loser stands the tea. With sugar, no reproach. I put in two lumps, and asking is not allowed."
city.ask.cog.bf.tea.2: "This evening it's the billiards league final: tea is expected double. The winner comes back for the cup afterwards, having forgotten it."
city.ask.cog.cl.glider: Is it true the glider flew through the foyer?
city.ask.cog.cl.glider.1: "It flew over my counter and landed on a coat. I gave it 'four plus': it clipped a hat twice."
city.ask.cog.cl.glider.2: "Tests in the workshop are announced in advance, but the glider doesn't know and flies when it likes."
city.ask.cog.cl.where.1: "The library, the reading corner, the workshop with workbenches, the photo lab behind the red door, the stage. If the red lamp is lit behind the red door, don't go in until it goes out."
city.ask.cog.cl.where.2: "In the evening there are rehearsals in the hall and on stage: you may walk between the rows, but not through the actors."
city.ask.cog.ld.cat: Is the caretaker's cat really a club member?
city.ask.cog.ld.cat.1: "Without a vote: so it says in the minutes. But he's the only one who attends every meeting and has never fallen asleep."
city.ask.cog.ld.cat.2: "By day he's on the windowsill, in the evening by the buffet, keeping track of where the pies are. That counts as taking part in club life too."
city.ask.cog.ld.ladder: How do I join the chess ladder?
city.ask.cog.ld.ladder.1: "Sign up with Tamara Ilyinichna. You may play someone no more than two rungs above you. If you lose, you stand tea: with sugar, without reproach."
city.ask.cog.ld.ladder.2: "It's Thursday, blitz. The clocks are the club's, take care. Whoever finds the real ones gets first move for a week."
city.ask.cog.ld.ladder.3: "You've been entered in the game book, briefly: 'Won. No excuses.' That's a compliment: here there are usually more excuses than moves."
city.ask.cog.lh.clock.1: "About the clock you'd better ask the photo circle: Seryozha took it 'for a while, back on Thursday'. Our Thursday never ends."
city.ask.cog.lh.clock.2: "The clock is back in its place. Club member number twenty-four, that's you, just in case: I wrote it in pencil, I don't use the eraser."
city.ask.cog.lh.deposit: Why are books lent against a deposit?
city.ask.cog.lh.deposit.1: "The deposit is five roubles; I give it back on return and write a receipt. My receipts keep better than the books."
city.ask.cog.lh.deposit.2: "On Monday the returns trolley is full: after the weekend everybody returns everything at once. I sort and don't lose count."
city.ask.cog.lh.deposit.3: "By the weekend the trolley is almost empty: the readers take books away and return them later, on Monday. A law of nature."
city.ask.cog.lh.radio: What can I read about radio?
city.ask.cog.lh.radio.1: "The magazine Radio: lots of circuits, few words. A real receiver stands at the Rassvet, in the radio corner."
city.ask.cog.lh.radio.2: "It's Thursday: the radio corner at the Rassvet is open, and tonight it's Silence on the Air. The radio amateurs go as a circle."
city.ask.cog.lh.swap.1: "'Bring one, take one; take one, bring one.' It works without me. I only make sure nobody walks off with empty covers."
city.ask.cog.lh.swap.2: "On Mondays fresh stock comes from the workshops: Knowledge Is Power with blueprints on the inserts. Take the top one: the top one is always best."
city.ask.cog.lh.swap.3: "You took a magazine from the shelf, I saw. Bring something in return, even a postcard: the shelf isn't fussy."
city.ask.cog.minutes: What were the meeting minutes about?
city.ask.cog.minutes.1: "About the missing chess clock. Twenty-three members and the doorman's cat, without a vote. The minutes are on the shelf, have a read."
city.ask.cog.minutes.2: "Read it to the end? Then you know more than half the members. They fall asleep at item two."
city.ask.cog.models.1: "The model-makers' ship. It has clockwork and sails by itself when wound up. They launch it in the pool on Sundays."
city.ask.cog.regulars.1: "At chess, Giuseppe González, the chairman. At billiards, Joost Zhaksybekov: he aims so long the ball falls asleep."
city.ask.cog.regulars.2: "And at table tennis, Kenji Kask. Crafty: looks left, hits right."
city.ask.cog.regulars.3: "Three of them beaten by you already? We'll have to add to the meeting minutes."
city.ask.dumplings.cook.1: "The cook, from five in the morning, to the radio. With a waltz they come out rounder; with the news, angrier."
city.ask.dumplings.portion: How many dumplings in a portion?
city.ask.dumplings.portion.1: "Twenty. Twenty-one means the cook's in love. Nineteen means a quarrel. Count them and tell me."
city.ask.dumplings.portion.2: "Sour cream on the side. Vinegar for the brave. Pepper for those who've come in from the frost."
city.ask.dumplings.portion.3: "Pepper for everyone today. And a double portion if you walked down from the hill."
city.ask.dumplings.soup.1: "Only dumplings here. For fish soup go to the commune house canteen, on Thursdays. They say life improves after it."
city.ask.dumplings.soup.2: "You've read the cookbook about soup. So make it yourself and bring me a taste."
city.ask.fair.days.1: "Friday to Sunday, and on holidays till late, with lanterns. On weekdays we just warm ourselves in the sun."
city.ask.fair.days.2: "Today is the big fair: carts in from the farms, an accordion, honey straight from the comb."
city.ask.fair.games.1: "Ring toss at the ice cream kiosk, the lottery at the papers, the shooting gallery and the fortune globe at the toys, the strongman by the crates. Half an hour and half a pocket for the lot."
city.ask.fair.games.2: "Had a go on the strongman? Our bell is stiff. Only two have rung it: the blacksmith and one granny."
city.ask.fair.lanterns.1: "For Lantern Night, in November. Everyone carries one to the beach and makes a wish. The farther yours flies out over the sea, the sooner it comes true."
city.ask.fair.lanterns.2: "It's tonight! Take a lantern, there's a candle inside. Go down to the beach when it gets dark."
city.ask.fish.catch: Where could I catch one myself?
city.ask.fish.catch.1: "Off the pier, by the lighthouse. Get bait at the market, in the anglers' row: they'll throw in advice, advice is free."
city.ask.fish.catch.2: "Catch something, bring it in, I'll buy it. Except gobies. I've plenty of gobies of my own."
city.ask.fish.golden: What's the fish with the golden side?
city.ask.fish.golden.1: "Not for sale. It's for luck. Every morning I put it on top; in the evening it goes back on ice."
city.ask.fish.golden.2: "The fishermen look at it before going out. If it shines, they go. If it's dull, they drink tea at the Seagull."
city.ask.fish.today.1: "The flounder's from this morning, the Baltic herring yesterday's, the gobies: don't ask. This morning's is gone by lunch."
city.ask.fish.today.2: "The boats have just come in. Hear the gulls arguing at the jetty? Means a good catch."
city.ask.fish.today.3: "The boats didn't go out in this weather. Today it's only what's in the ice box, and stories."
city.ask.flowers.sunflowers: Why do the sunflowers face you?
city.ask.flowers.sunflowers.1: "They think I'm the sun. I don't argue: it pleases them and costs me nothing."
city.ask.flowers.sunflowers.2: "By evening they're tired and look at the street lamp. The lamp's pleased too."
city.ask.flowers.vases: Where can I get a vase?
city.ask.flowers.vases.1: "At the sports centre, in the brick shed, there's a pottery studio. The potter makes crooked vases, and flowers last longer in them."
city.ask.flowers.vases.2: "Only it's Wednesday, firing day: the kiln hums and no one goes near."
city.ask.flowers.vases.3: "It's Saturday: they open the kiln today! Go and look before it's all taken."
city.ask.flowers.vases.4: "Their week goes: raw on Monday, firing Wednesday, glaze Friday, ready Saturday. Like pies."
city.ask.flowers.when.1: "Thursday. Or Friday. Flowers aren't a bus. Meanwhile there are mine: daisies from the roadside and my wild rose."
city.ask.flowers.when.2: "Today's delivery day, as it happens. You can hear the van from the hill: it sings on the bends."
city.ask.hall.choir.1: "The Vaults choir. Rehearsals in the evenings. There are two basses, both fishermen, so in the fishing season the choir sings higher."
city.ask.hall.choir.2: "They're warming up right now. Stand by the door: they like it when people listen without a ticket."
city.ask.hall.dance.1: "Saturdays in the mirrored room. They teach the waltz to everyone who saw the Friday film at the Rassvet and caught fire."
city.ask.hall.dance.2: "It's Saturday! Do your shoes squeak? Leave squeaky ones at the cloakroom, they'll give you slippers."
city.ask.hall.pies.1: "Last time they ran out at 19:10, and someone wrote in the guest book: 'Bake more pies or start later.' We bake more."
city.ask.hall.pies.2: "You're just in time: the last apple one. Take it before the choir comes out for the break."
city.ask.icecream.beach: Is it all right to swim today?
city.ask.icecream.beach.1: "The lifeguard tower will tell you: flags and a board with the water temperature. I only judge by the queue."
city.ask.icecream.beach.2: "Long queue means warm water. Today it's long."
city.ask.icecream.beach.3: "Today the queue is just you. So the sports centre pool is the better idea."
city.ask.icecream.eskimo.1: "It's been there since last summer. No one dares sell it, no one dares buy it. The freezer's mascot."
city.ask.icecream.eskimo.2: "In the evening it almost glows. Don't stare too long or you'll want it."
city.ask.icecream.eskimo.3: "If one day it's gone, summer's really over."
city.ask.icecream.which.1: "The plombir in a wafer cup. The rest is for people who don't know what they want. The spoon's wooden, you can chew it."
city.ask.icecream.which.2: "In the cold only true northerners and children eat ice cream. Which are you?"
city.ask.icecream.which.3: "In this heat take two: one to eat, one to melt. It's more honest that way."
city.ask.keeper.cat.1: "Mine and the lighthouse's. He catches mice and watches the ships. The bakery cat visits him: they swap news."
city.ask.keeper.light: Why a lighthouse when there's radio?
city.ask.keeper.light.1: "Radio goes quiet when it breaks. Light doesn't break: if the lamp goes out, I stand next to it with a lantern. It happened once."
city.ask.keeper.light.2: "Watch: the beam's coming round. One, and the whole town is bright for a moment. I call it 'the roll call'."
city.ask.keeper.weather.1: "I write it in the log every day: wind, sea, clouds. The paper copies from me later and gets it wrong."
city.ask.keeper.weather.2: "Fog. The horn will sound all night. If you can't sleep, count the blasts; by the fortieth everyone's asleep."
city.ask.keeper.weather.3: "A clear night. You can see Venus from the gallery, and the Saucer has a telescope for a coin."
city.ask.lib.chessbook.1: "The chess pod on the first level: Chess Openings, Told to a Neighbour. It reads like a letter, not a textbook. When you finish, drop in at the Cog: Tamara Ilyinichna keeps the game notebook and is looking for someone to show it to."
city.ask.lib.chessbook.2: "Finished it? At the Rassvet there's a ladder of names in chalk on the board, and the bottom line is empty."
city.ask.lib.chessbook.3: "I hear you beat somebody. Bring the book back with a bookmark at the page where you slipped: that's its favourite bookmark."
city.ask.lib.g_n: Who is G. N. in the ledger?
city.ask.lib.g_n.1: "The reader with card 3-217. He took the Guide to Sundials in May sixty-eight and still hasn't brought it back. I keep rewriting the due date: my hand is used to it."
city.ask.lib.g_n.2: "We wrote to each other in pencil in the margins of the loan card. I haven't erased anything since: the eraser lies in the drawer so I won't be tempted."
city.ask.lib.map: Where is the old map of the town?
city.ask.lib.map.1: "By the book wall, next to Six Terraces. Find your house. If you can't, it's newer than the map. That's worth a stamp too."
city.ask.lib.map.2: "Finished Six Terraces? Then you know the hill wasn't cut down, it was asked to move over. Rare politeness for architects."
city.ask.lib.map.3: "It's Friday, the theme of the day is our town: find your own house on the map. Do it before closing and the stamp is yours."
city.ask.lib.office_work: What do you do when nobody is in?
city.ask.lib.office_work.1: "I glue the spines back, check loan cards against the shelves, write cards for books with no author. Those have the most beautiful cards."
city.ask.lib.office_work.2: "In the morning I sort the returns box. Sometimes it's warm inside, like a mitten."
city.ask.lib.office_work.3: "Towards evening there's tea and quiet. Until we close it's best not to knock on the staff door: our kettle has a temper."
city.ask.lib.piano.1: "The piano is in a pod on the first level. The lid is stiff, the pedal quiet: the player hears it, and the wall a little."
city.ask.lib.piano.2: "Evenings are better: the reading room empties and the neighbour through the wall doesn't mind. He never minds. It's a cupboard."
city.ask.lib.piano.3: "Was that you, playing the tune with no beginning? Keep going. It must have an ending: I checked, and it isn't written down anywhere."
city.ask.lib.postcard.1: "Four roubles. People write little on them and keep them for decades. Our books hold more bookmarks than margin notes."
city.ask.lib.postcard.2: "If you feel like writing and don't know to whom, leave it by the Returned shelf at the window. I won't ask whose it is. I'll pass it on."
city.ask.lib.postcard.3: "You slipped a card into the Guide, I saw. Don't be surprised on Tuesday at tea: the second cup is already warm."
city.ask.lib.quiet_hours.1: "Ten to eleven: the readers are still finishing their tea at home and the cleaner has already gone. The best hour for the Sea shelf."
city.ask.lib.quiet_hours.2: "Towards six the schoolchildren come and solve one problem three at a time. Their whispering is good, but noticeable."
city.ask.lib.quiet_hours.3: "On a rainy day it's crowded and quiet at once: everybody came for the same thing, to wait it out."
city.ask.lib.quiet_hours.4: "Quietest on weekday evenings, and quietest of all on Tuesdays. You choose: the quiet or the tea."
city.ask.lib.seventeen: How many stamps are there in all?
city.ask.lib.seventeen.1: "Fifteen for the shelves, one at the desk, that's me, and one for the Returned. Seventeen. Count without hurrying."
city.ask.lib.seventeen.2: "Twelve? What's left doesn't lie in plain sight. One of them is by the shelf where all the spines face the window."
city.ask.lib.seventeen.3: "All seventeen! Come on a Tuesday for tea and I'll show you what we do with readers like that."
city.ask.lib.stamp_why: Why is the stamp "for quiet hours"?
city.ask.lib.stamp_why.1: "The stamp isn't for pages, it's for an hour spent unhurried. The lamp with the green shade is for weekdays. The open book with wings is for weekends."
city.ask.lib.stamp_why.2: "Today it's the winged book: for reading with no use at all. The most expensive stamp in my pad."
city.ask.lib.stamp_why.3: "Eight already? Then carry the diary in your left pocket, closer to the heart. It's got heavier."
city.ask.lib.tuesday.1: "On Tuesdays the kettle is on for two and we don't ask questions. I only put it on; the rest is up to chance."
city.ask.lib.tuesday.2: "It's Tuesday: the kettle is on for two. If you come in, the second cup is yours."
city.ask.lib.tuesday.3: "You've had tea with us. So you're a witness. Witnesses finish their tea."
city.ask.library.birds.1: "The bird shelf by the window, and the field guide behind the desk: ornithologists buy it, and everyone who mixes up one gull with another."
city.ask.library.birds.2: "Finished The Starlings? Then the bird stall at the market will understand you at half a word."
city.ask.library.birds.3: "Seed and feeders are at the hardware shop under the wave tower. The birds don't mind where from, but it pleases the seller."
city.ask.library.diary: How do I get a stamp in my diary?
city.ask.library.diary.1: "Read at a shelf, sit in a pod, then come to the desk. The stamp is for quiet hours, not pages."
city.ask.library.diary.2: "Each shelf has its own stamp: birds, the sea, the sun, chess. Seventeen in all. The last one is a secret."
city.ask.library.diary.3: "Four already? Your diary's swelling. A good swelling, a reader's one."
city.ask.library.diary.4: "Today's Monday, the books' day off. The stamps are resting too."
city.ask.library.returned.1: "Books that came back on their own. The first was A Guide to Sundials, issued in May sixty-eight."
city.ask.library.returned.2: "The bookmark was a cable car ticket to the Lighthouse. 'Read slowly,' he wrote. We're not cross."
city.ask.library.returned.3: "On Tuesdays I put the kettle on for two. In case he comes. You can be the second while he isn't here."
city.ask.lifeguard.lost: What gets lost most on the beach?
city.ask.lifeguard.lost.1: "Sun hats, single sandals and patience. The hats are in the box on the tower; the sandals come one at a time, never a pair."
city.ask.lifeguard.rules: What matters most in the water?
city.ask.lifeguard.rules.1: "Don't swim out alone and don't argue with a wave. The wave is always right, even when it's wrong."
city.ask.lifeguard.rules.2: "Tired? Lie on your back and look at the sky. The sky holds you up better than you'd think."
city.ask.lifeguard.water.1: "I read the thermometer every morning and write it in the log. The Baltic is never warm; it's 'all right'."
city.ask.lifeguard.water.2: "Today it's 'all right'. White flag. Only as far as the buoys; they're not for decoration."
city.ask.lifeguard.water.3: "Red today. The only ones swimming are the winter bathers and my thermometer."
city.ask.market.days.1: "Saturday: people come in from the farms and the market spills onto the square. Come by seven; by nine you can't get through."
city.ask.market.days.2: "It's on today! Hear the scales ringing? That's the weights laughing."
city.ask.market.days.3: "Right now is the best time: the fish is still wet, the bread still hot."
city.ask.market.jam.1: "Zoya's sea buckthorn from the vegetable row. Second was gooseberry with mint, third pine cones. Pine cones take courage."
city.ask.market.jam.2: "And the jar with no label still stands by the scales. We weigh it every morning. It doesn't get any lighter."
city.ask.market.scales.1: "The check scales are by the office, for honesty. A hundred grams must be a hundred grams, even by the sea."
city.ask.market.scales.2: "Weighing yourself is for the clinic. The nurse will put down your height too, for free."
city.ask.news.crossword.1: "The Friday crossword is a hard one, the whole town suffers. Fourteen down is 'tide'. Don't tell anyone."
city.ask.news.crossword.2: "Ask the library for the rest: they have a dictionary as thick as a brick and a librarian who knows everything and says nothing."
city.ask.news.crossword.3: "Read page two? About Kesha the parrot. It's no joke, he really does announce the stops."
city.ask.news.postcards.1: "One a day is free, courtesy of the town council. More isn't fair: it's a small town, there has to be enough for everyone."
city.ask.news.postcards.2: "There are six kiosks at the stops and each has its own card. Collect all six and you'll know the town like a postman."
city.ask.news.postcards.3: "Been round all six? You're a local now. I keep the evening paper back for locals."
city.ask.news.weather.1: "The lighthouse knows the weather here; the paper only guesses. The keeper writes it in his log on the pier every day."
city.ask.news.weather.2: "Rain till evening. Paper under your jacket, and you into the Saucer: rain over the sea is pretty from up there."
city.ask.news.weather.3: "Fog. Hear the foghorn? That's the lighthouse saying hello. On days like this the cable car runs slow."
city.ask.news.weather.4: "Clear. They'll run up the white flag at the lifeguard tower: that means the water's good."
city.ask.news.weather.5: "Snow! The winter fair's not far off then. Put a calendar on the wall, we'll count the days."
city.ask.pasty.beach: Where's the best place to eat it?
city.ask.pasty.beach.1: "On the parapet, facing the sea. The gulls will watch; don't meet their eyes, they take it as an invitation."
city.ask.pasty.beach.2: "Better here at the counter today. The gulls are under cover too, but they don't pay."
city.ask.pasty.hot.1: "Straight out of the oil. Bite from the edge and hold it over the paper: our juice runs faster than our customers."
city.ask.pasty.hot.2: "Lunchtime: the queue is lifeguards and builders. Lifeguards take two, builders three."
city.ask.pasty.recipe.1: "The dough's made with mineral water from the sanatorium pump. The bubbles make the blisters. Don't tell, the sanatorium would be hurt."
city.ask.photo.booth.1: "The photo booth is in the Cog's foyer. Four frames in ten minutes. Everyone comes out funny, that's its gift."
city.ask.photo.booth.2: "Been in already? Show me. Well, there you are, and you said you were photogenic."
city.ask.photo.darkroom.1: "The Cog has a darkroom: red light and silence. The circle meets on Wednesdays; bring your own film."
city.ask.photo.portrait: When will the portrait be ready?
city.ask.photo.portrait.1: "Thursday. Always Thursday, even if we took it on Wednesday. Our developer is ceremonious, it doesn't like to hurry."
city.ask.photo.portrait.2: "It's Thursday today, see: the faces of the whole town drying on the line."
city.ask.ps.b.complaints.1: "Forty pages, thirty-five of them thanks. The manager says that's not normal and asks people to write complaints. They don't."
city.ask.ps.b.complaints.2: "There's an entry from six-year-old Boris: the toy train never takes him to the station. They answered: 'On Monday it will.' So far it just goes round."
city.ask.ps.b.library: What should I buy after reading at the library?
city.ask.ps.b.library.1: "The science magazine for those who didn't finish Physics with One Spoon. The travel one for those who've walked it all and want to again."
city.ask.ps.b.library.2: "You're supposed to return the spoon from Physics with One Spoon to the kitchen afterwards. Many forget."
city.ask.ps.b.library.3: "Eight stamps in your diary? Then you're not a customer but a colleague. No discount, but I'll smile."
city.ask.ps.c.menu.1: "The pies are hot until noon, then warm, then 'like everybody's'."
city.ask.ps.c.menu.2: "On Saturday we have ice cream: it's last on the menu and first to go."
city.ask.ps.c.menu.3: "By closing, tea is what's left. Tea is always left."
city.ask.ps.c.saucer: How are you better than the Saucer?
city.ask.ps.c.saucer.1: "In no way. We're closer, they're higher. People go there to look and here to snack between departments. We're no rival to Kesha."
city.ask.ps.c.saucer.2: "They say Kesha says goodbye with 'Thank you for the ride'. Our buffet could do with that."
city.ask.ps.c.saucer.3: "On rainy days we're crowded: umbrellas stand at every table and count as guests."
city.ask.ps.cl.hooks.1: "Empty in the morning, full by lunch, and in the evening one coat that nobody collects. Always one."
city.ask.ps.cl.hooks.2: "In the morning it's quiet at my place: you can hear the coats sigh on the rack as they settle."
city.ask.ps.cl.umbrellas: Whose umbrellas are in the stand?
city.ask.ps.cl.umbrellas.1: "Three black ones, one checked, a walking stick with a rubber tip. Each has a tag and each waits for its owner like a dog."
city.ask.ps.cl.umbrellas.2: "The yellow umbrella isn't here, it's at lost and found. Don't bring it to me: it's busy, waiting for Lidiya Sergeyevna."
city.ask.ps.cl.umbrellas.3: "Rain: all the umbrellas stand wet and happy. By evening you may want to borrow one: I lend by tag, and they come back every other time."
city.ask.ps.d.bottles.1: "At the back door. The porter counts out loud, but clinks louder than he counts."
city.ask.ps.d.bottles.2: "On delivery days the empties go back in the same crates: the bottles leave the way they came, ringing."
city.ask.ps.d.which: Which is better: Baikal or Tarkhun?
city.ask.ps.d.which.1: "Baikal is for talking, Tarkhun for those who keep quiet. Buratino is for kids who've already decided, Duchesse for anyone who wants to remember summer."
city.ask.ps.d.which.2: "In hot weather people take Tarkhun: green, it stays on the tongue till evening."
city.ask.ps.d.which.3: "In the rain nobody buys lemonade, they buy water. Wisely: lemonade likes the sun."
city.ask.ps.g.delivery.1: "Dairy on Tuesday by ten, fish and cheese on Friday. The queue starts at the red carpet, no more than two per customer."
city.ask.ps.g.delivery.2: "It's Tuesday! The kefir came at ten and there's enough for everyone in line. Don't fret: it doesn't like the fretful."
city.ask.ps.g.delivery.3: "Friday: fish and cheese. Cheese first, fish as you feel. Three people have already given me that advice."
city.ask.ps.g.delivery.4: "Wednesday and Thursday are our quiet days: choose without hurry."
city.ask.ps.g.seeds: Where do your sunflower seeds come from?
city.ask.ps.g.seeds.1: "Roasted, in a paper cone made from newspaper. People buy them for pigeons, for parrots and for themselves, in that order."
city.ask.ps.g.seeds.2: "The parrot at the Saucer takes them only after the word 'Terminus'. The barista told me herself, laughing, and bought seeds."
city.ask.ps.g.seeds.3: "So you're the one who treated Kesha? The barista came by and said: 'Tell him Kesha has a new favourite word.' She won't say which."
city.ask.ps.ga.box: Where should I hang a feeder on a terrace?
city.ask.ps.ga.box.1: "Not in the wind: behind the box of geraniums, away from the wall. Birds like to see where trouble will come from."
city.ask.ps.ga.box.2: "Read A Garden on Concrete? Then you already have fish crates: they're salted through and afraid of nothing."
city.ask.ps.ga.feed: What should I feed the birds?
city.ask.ps.ga.feed.1: "Grain for sparrows, peanuts for tits, suet for anyone not proud, niger for goldfinches: the seeds are dark as night and the goldfinch loves it."
city.ask.ps.ga.feed.2: "After the Field Guide people hang the feeder differently: lower, so you can see it from the kitchen and the cat doesn't dream."
city.ask.ps.ga.feed.3: "In frost, only unsalted suet. It's bad for birds too."
city.ask.ps.h.badge.1: "There's one badge, but everyone sees their own thing in it: some the lighthouse, some the cable car. Twelve roubles, the pin is a gift."
city.ask.ps.h.badge.2: "Before a holiday the lapels go bare: everybody buys one. If you want one, come before lunch."
city.ask.ps.h.mitten: Has the left mitten turned up?
city.ask.ps.h.mitten.1: "I haven't got any left ones. The right one, red with stripes, is upstairs at lost and found. Ask there: maybe the left one is an orphan too."
city.ask.ps.h.mitten.2: "Did you hear it on the radio? That was my mitten. Well, not mine, the one that was announced. I knew it by the stripes."
city.ask.ps.l.accept.1: "Everything. Umbrellas, keys, mittens. Once we took in an accordion: it turned out to be a wedding one. I take things in on a record and hand them back on a record."
city.ask.ps.l.accept.2: "The record is written in triplicate: one for me, one for the owner, one for the item. The item signs in silence."
city.ask.ps.l.accept.3: "The first thing I ever took in was a child's shoe. The owner grew up and came for it at sixty with a pie for me. The shoe is still here: it stands too well."
city.ask.ps.l.gloves: Has the left mitten turned up?
city.ask.ps.l.gloves.1: "The right one, red with stripes, lies under the glass. I'm waiting for the left. Mittens find each other: they're not things, they're people."
city.ask.ps.l.gloves.2: "In frost they bring one pair a day: one, then the other. The owners then turn up, as a rule, in just one."
city.ask.ps.l.month.1: "We keep things for a month. Then they go to the fair square as lottery prizes: better to make somebody happy. One hat has won twice."
city.ask.ps.l.month.2: "It's festival time and the fair square is buzzing. If you're missing something, it may be winning a prize there."
city.ask.ps.l.umbrella: Is the yellow umbrella here today?
city.ask.ps.l.umbrella.1: "The yellow one with the duck's head? He's always a bit here and a bit in other departments. I count him as three."
city.ask.ps.l.umbrella.2: "Lidiya Sergeyevna confessed she loses it on purpose. I tell her: just not on inventory day. She nods."
city.ask.ps.l.umbrella.3: "They say it was you at the microphone. The hall froze, then applauded. Forty years in lost and found, and the first time anyone clapped at a handover."
city.ask.ps.s.candy: Are sweets by weight or one at a time?
city.ask.ps.s.candy.1: "One at a time, eight roubles each. The boys swap the wrappers for pins and badges: they run their own exchange by the stairs."
city.ask.ps.s.candy.2: "Mornings bring the most honest customers: they buy one sweet and carry it off to show their mother."
city.ask.ps.s.candy.3: "On Saturdays an old man spends half an hour choosing until closing and always takes the same one. We don't rush him."
city.ask.ps.s.chocolate.1: "One kind and one wrapper. Twenty-five roubles, so people buy a bar for a holiday and a square for the pocket."
city.ask.ps.s.chocolate.2: "It's a holiday, people buy double. A square for everyone: an old tradition, we haven't started a new one."
city.ask.ps.s.chocolate.3: "In the cold the bar snaps in half by itself. People buy two halves: one to eat, one to share."
city.ask.ps.sh.galoshes: Why does nobody buy the galoshes?
city.ask.ps.sh.galoshes.1: "The lining is red. Everyone thinks it means rain, there's no rain, and they wait. You can wait for years."
city.ask.ps.sh.galoshes.2: "It's raining, see? Two have taken a pair and one brought them back: he says the lining is red, awkward for puddles. I said: puddles don't look."
city.ask.ps.sh.galoshes.3: "Lidiya Sergeyevna bought a pair, they stand at home. She wore them once and said: 'What a pity, the rain stopped.'"
city.ask.ps.sh.size: How do I find my size?
city.ask.ps.sh.size.1: "Stand on a sheet of paper, I'll trace round with a pencil and add a finger for growing room. Everybody argues about the finger, then thanks me."
city.ask.ps.sh.size.2: "In frost, go a size up: a woollen sock and the air between it and the sole warm better than a second pair."
city.ask.ps.sh.size.3: "The first boots I ever sold went in sixty-eight to a boy on his way to the cable car for his birthday. A year later he brought them in to show how worn they were. The boots were proud."
city.ask.ps.sh.sport: What shoes do I need for the gym?
city.ask.ps.sh.sport.1: "Rubber soles, but not black ones: the coach scolds black soles, they mark the floor. He walks round the hall checking soles like a customs officer."
city.ask.ps.sh.sport.2: "Have you been to the coach? Did he talk about soles? He tells everyone, so I tell you too: to save him saying it twice."
city.ask.ps.so.amber.1: "Real. Easy test: rub it on a woollen sleeve and hold it near a scrap of paper; the paper jumps. Try it, I won't take offence."
city.ask.ps.so.amber.2: "Before a holiday people buy gifts: amber for grandmothers, badges for friends, postcards for those with no time."
city.ask.ps.so.amber.3: "Before closing the amber glows in the light like tea. The best time to choose."
city.ask.ps.so.cards.1: "The lighthouse, the cable car, the promenade. Four roubles, no stamps needed: our postcards are mostly for oneself."
city.ask.ps.so.cards.2: "One of our postcards now rides in the Guide to Sundials, I hear. Good work."
city.ask.ps.sp.bite.1: "Perch take the spoon, pike the wobbler, gulls the bread. We don't fish for gulls, but someone always tries."
city.ask.ps.sp.bite.2: "In fog the spoon glimmers and the fish think it's dawn. They come without asking questions."
city.ask.ps.sp.bite.3: "Read about the fish first: Fishes of Our Shore is sold here and at the library desk, forty either way."
city.ask.ps.sp.wobbler: What's the difference between a wobbler and a spoon?
city.ask.ps.sp.wobbler.1: "A spoon flashes and spins, a wobbler swims as if alive. The spoon is for the hurried, the wobbler for the believers."
city.ask.ps.sp.wobbler.2: "The wobbler costs more because there's more patience in it. That's how I count; the accountants count otherwise."
city.ask.ps.t.coins: Have you got change in coins?
city.ask.ps.t.coins.1: "No coins since morning. I'll give you a boiled sweet: it rattles in the pocket like a coin."
city.ask.ps.t.coins.2: "By evening the till holds only roubles and a great deal of patience. The patience, sadly, can't be broken into change."
city.ask.ps.t.coins.3: "On Thursdays at noon it's payday: I pay out in small notes so the sales staff enjoy counting."
city.ask.ps.t.sunday: Why is it so quiet on Sundays?
city.ask.ps.t.sunday.1: "Sunday: no sales staff, the till is open. Looking is allowed, bread is tomorrow. That's what the board says, and the board doesn't lie."
city.ask.ps.t.sunday.2: "Today I'm everybody. If you need me, that's me. If you need a department, wait till Monday. I water the windowsill flowers between customers."
city.ask.rassvet.bf.break: What does the poster mean by "the break is in the buffet"?
city.ask.rassvet.bf.break.1: "On Saturdays the shows run without a break, so the break is mine. I close the hatch for twenty minutes and sit like a spectator myself. Don't knock."
city.ask.rassvet.bf.friday: Is it true the buffet stays open later on Fridays?
city.ask.rassvet.bf.friday.1: "Half an hour after the evening show. Friday, Waltz on the Pier: afterwards everybody is hungry and somebody's eyes are wet."
city.ask.rassvet.bf.friday.2: "Today! I've boiled the tea half an hour ahead, and the pies are all cabbage. They're well matured."
city.ask.rassvet.bf.projectionist: What does the projectionist eat at the interval?
city.ask.rassvet.bf.projectionist.1: "A cherry pie, one. I send it up to the booth on a string; he thought of it himself, so he needn't leave the reel."
city.ask.rassvet.bf.projectionist.2: "On Saturdays he's in the hall, not the booth. I carry the pie straight to his seat. 'You're disturbing the audience.' 'I'm feeding an audience member.'"
city.ask.rassvet.cl.dance: May I dance in outdoor shoes?
city.ask.rassvet.cl.dance.1: "Changing shoes, clean and smooth: so say the rules by the mirror. The floor is polished on Fridays and is grateful for it."
city.ask.rassvet.cl.dance.2: "It's waltz day: the teacher is already clapping, you can hear her from here. One-two-three, young man."
city.ask.rassvet.cl.dance.3: "Wednesday, foxtrot. The faces are serious as at an exam, and the coats come in pairs."
city.ask.rassvet.cl.umbrella: Whose is the black umbrella with the note?
city.ask.rassvet.cl.umbrella.1: "'I'll drop by as soon as it rains.' It hasn't rained, so he hasn't come. Now I wait for the rain more than he does."
city.ask.rassvet.cl.umbrella.2: "Rain! I look at the door. No, not him. He must have a second one."
city.ask.rassvet.film: What's on at the Rassvet today?
city.ask.rassvet.film.1: "The Rassvet has two showings: the matinee at three, the evening one at seven. Posters by the ticket window, tickets in the hall."
city.ask.rassvet.film.2: "Today the matinee is the comedy about the hat that blew away, and tonight the fisherman who waited for the lighthouse. Bring a handkerchief."
city.ask.rassvet.film.3: "Tuesday: the newsreel of the town being built in the afternoon. Look for your granny with a tape measure. In the evening, the night shift on the cable car."
city.ask.rassvet.film.4: "Wednesday is science day: the one about the sun, eight minutes for the rays, the whole hall counts along. In the evening, the girl with the letter in a bottle."
city.ask.rassvet.film.5: "Thursday: three friends carry a watermelon across town in the afternoon, a radio ham chases a call sign in the evening. Our radio club goes as a whole."
city.ask.rassvet.film.6: "Friday: the boy practising table tennis against a wall, and in the evening dancing on the jetty. Afterwards everyone tries a waltz on the promenade."
city.ask.rassvet.film.7: "Saturday: a children's detective about a missing gull in the afternoon, and in the evening the film about a projectionist. That night ours sits in the hall, not the booth."
city.ask.rassvet.film.8: "Sunday: the cartoon about the hedgehog on the cable car, and a silent film with a live pianist in the evening. He comes in a hat."
city.ask.rassvet.film.9: "You've been already, haven't you? Then you know the third seat in row five squeaks. Sit one to the left."
city.ask.rassvet.tk.after: Where should I go after the show?
city.ask.rassvet.tk.after.1: "After the evening show it's nice to walk to the Saucer: while you were watching, Kesha may have announced the last stop. And if the radio picks up interference, blame the Cog: the radio amateurs are there."
city.ask.rassvet.tk.after.2: "It's Friday: at the Cog there's the billiards semi-final, and here the buffet stays open another half hour after Waltz on the Pier."
city.ask.rassvet.tk.after.3: "It's Saturday: the Cog has the final this evening, spectators sign up with Tamara Ilyinichna. Our shows run back to back, so choose one of the two."
city.ask.rassvet.tk.costume: What are the costumes for the play?
city.ask.rassvet.tk.costume.1: "A fairy tale about the Sun and the Wind. The Wind's cloak is ready, the Sun's isn't yet: the seamstress says the rays must be sewn on so that they warm."
city.ask.rassvet.tk.costume.2: "It's Thursday, fittings day. The seamstress rang: let the Sun wait. I explained it to the Sun. The Sun doesn't mind: it has eternity."
city.ask.rassvet.tk.costume.3: "Did you visit the seamstress? If she still has that yellow, 'like seven in the evening', tell her: the Sun will wait, but not forever."
city.ask.rassvet.tk.reel.1: "The tin turned up in the storeroom, behind the radiator. The lid bears the same word as the front of the building. The projectionist says the house was named after it, though everyone thought the film was made up."
city.ask.rassvet.tk.reel.2: "I don't give the card 'In memory of what was never finished' to everyone. Only to those who stayed to the white light."
city.ask.rassvet.tk.stubs.1: "Red stubs are matinee, yellow evening. I count at night and it doesn't always add up. I'm not cross: it means the hall was alive."
city.ask.rassvet.tk.stubs.2: "At weekends there are twice as many stubs. I weigh the pile down with a cup, and my cup is always empty: I never notice drinking it."
city.ask.rassvet.tk.times.1: "The matinee at three for those who like a quiet hall. The evening one at seven for those who like the buffet afterwards. Any seat you like."
city.ask.rassvet.tk.times.2: "Wednesday: please arrive before the bell, not together with it. I'm not being fussy, it's on the poster."
city.ask.rassvet.tk.times.3: "On Fridays and Saturdays come twenty minutes early for the evening show: the hall fills before the bell, though any seat is allowed."
city.ask.rental.bikes.1: "All being repaired. At the same time. The workshop says it's a mystery. I think they conspired."
city.ask.rental.boats.1: "Until sunset. The deposit is your word of honour. Oar seven is missing: it went to sea last July, we're expecting it back."
city.ask.rental.boats.2: "Not today: look at the tower, there's a red flag up. No one argues with the flag."
city.ask.rental.flags: What do the flags on the tower mean?
city.ask.rental.flags.1: "White: swim. Yellow: stay near the shore. Red: sit on the sand and watch the waves. Black is the lifeguard's washing drying."
city.ask.rental.flags.2: "The lifeguard writes it all in the water temperature log. Ask him: he's pleased when someone takes an interest."
city.ask.repair.clock: What about the clock with the crack?
city.ask.repair.clock.1: "The chess clock from the Cog. The left dial's cracked and it runs two minutes fast. They brought it to me and I refused to fix it."
city.ask.repair.clock.2: "Why? White plays at its own risk with it. That's part of the game now. You can't repair a tradition."
city.ask.repair.clock.3: "Played with them? Then you know: two minutes is a lot when you're thinking."
city.ask.repair.radio.1: "Valves, yes, transistors, yes, the longing on the air, no. For longing, see the radio hams at the club's station."
city.ask.repair.radio.2: "Thursday night the Rassvet shows a film about a radio ham. The whole club will go and the station will be silent."
city.ask.repair.watch: Whose is the watch 'L. from L.'?
city.ask.repair.watch.1: "Don't know. Brought in last winter, fixed, never collected. They tick loudly, as if calling."
city.ask.repair.watch.2: "Whoever remembers who they're from can have them. Few letters, lots of people in town."
city.ask.repair.watch.3: "At night they tick more quietly. Maybe they hope less."
city.ask.sana.evening: What do the guests do in the evening?
city.ask.sana.evening.1: "Dancing in the winter garden to the piano. A waltz, then a tango, then everyone goes to bed at ten sharp."
city.ask.sana.evening.2: "Hear that? They've started. Come in, we're short of young people; the grannies will be glad of a partner."
city.ask.sana.kesha: Is it true a parrot shouted on the roof?
city.ask.sana.kesha.1: "Kesha from the Saucer. He sat on the roof shouting 'Sun! Sun!'. The guests applauded and the treatments ran half an hour late."
city.ask.sana.kesha.2: "It's clear today: he might do it again. The head doctor says it was the best heliotherapy of the season."
city.ask.sana.pump: When is the pump room open?
city.ask.sana.pump.1: "Morning to evening, the water's free, bring your own mug. Drink slowly, in small sips, looking out of the window."
city.ask.sana.pump.2: "It's morning-glass time: the guests in dressing gowns queue like penguins."
city.ask.sand.cure.1: "Show me your card. Every treatment stamps it: water, cocktail, quartz, check-up, exercises and quiet hour. Six squares, six treatments, nothing extra."
city.ask.sand.cure.2: "A start has been made. One square on the card is no longer 'I have arrived' but 'I am being treated'. That is a big difference."
city.ask.sand.cure.3: "Halfway! Pink cheeks, a steady walk. At this rate I shall discharge you at the end of the week, with regret."
city.ask.sand.cure.4: "All six! The course is done by the book. I write 'practically healthy' and stamp it. I use that stamp once a season, so look after the card."
city.ask.sand.games: Are chess and draughts part of the course?
city.ask.sand.games.1: "Chess, draughts and dominoes are listed here as 'mental gymnastics': after lunch, in pairs, no prompting. I don't put a win on the card, but it does improve the mood."
city.ask.sand.letter: Has anyone left a letter here?
city.ask.sand.letter.1: "Letters? Only postcards. Actually no: on the lounge table in the lobby there is an envelope without a stamp. Nobody asks for it and nobody has the heart to throw it away."
city.ask.sand.letter.2: "You've read it? Then you know more than I do. I haven't, but I could tell from the handwriting it was personal. Let it lie until the next intake."
city.ask.sand.night: Where is the duty nurse at night?
city.ask.sand.night.1: "Here, at the desk, from ten at night to seven in the morning: a thermometer, valerian, a spare blanket. If you can't sleep you may sit in the lobby, but under one lamp only."
city.ask.sand.night.2: "You've come just in time: boiling water in the flask, the tea is brewed. Quietly, though, it's lights-out."
city.ask.sand.piano.1: "You may, if it's gentle and not after ten. Don't take the notebook off the lid: it belongs to everyone."
city.ask.sand.piano.2: "(whispering) Not now, though: it's quiet hour. At five, please do."
city.ask.sand.piano.3: "On Saturday evening, absolutely! The dancers need music and our pianist is being discharged."
city.ask.sand.quartz: Why the goggles at the quartz lamp?
city.ask.sand.quartz.1: "So that you don't look where you shouldn't. The lamp is kind, but it does not like the curious."
city.ask.sand.quartz.2: "You have already sat under the lamp? Did you notice everything turns blue? We call it the 'blue hour'. Good for the mood."
city.ask.sand.sleep.1: "Window ajar, a light supper, the radio low. And don't count sheep: count the sips of water at the pump room."
city.ask.sand.sleep.2: "(whispering) By day no more than an hour, or at night you will be counting the ceiling tiles."
city.ask.seagull.evening: Where should I go in the evening?
city.ask.seagull.evening.1: "If you're flush, the Yantar restaurant: tablecloths and quiet music. If not, the promenade: louder music, and free."
city.ask.seagull.evening.2: "Tonight is Lantern Night: everyone goes to the beach. Get a lantern at the fair and let it go into the sky. If you've made a wish, watch it till it's gone."
city.ask.seagull.fishermen: Who sits here in the mornings?
city.ask.seagull.fishermen.1: "The fishermen, when the golden fish in the shop is dull. They drink tea and argue over who wiped it wrong last time."
city.ask.seagull.fishermen.2: "It's their time now. Don't take the table with a newspaper under the sugar bowl: that one's taken for good."
city.ask.seagull.window.1: "By the window, the left one. You see the sea and the cable car cabins. The others are by the window too, but the left one has character."
city.ask.seagull.window.2: "In the rain it's better here than by the sea: you see the sea, and only the sea gets wet."
city.ask.souvenir.amber.1: "Real, from our own shore. After a storm it washes up at Amber Shore, that's why the station has that name."
city.ask.souvenir.amber.2: "After weather like this, walk the waterline early in the morning. Look for what glows like a boiled sweet."
city.ask.souvenir.badge: Where can I get a cable car badge?
city.ask.souvenir.badge.1: "At the kiosk by the first stop. And the information kiosk at the fifth will tell you where to ride with it on."
city.ask.souvenir.best: What should I take home as a keepsake?
city.ask.souvenir.best.1: "A shell from the pier, a free postcard from a kiosk and a photo from the studio. The rest is dust."
city.ask.souvenir.best.2: "You seem to know the whole town. Then take addresses home, not things."
city.ask.sport.pingpong: Who can I play table tennis with?
city.ask.sport.pingpong.1: "With Ursula Okonkwo. She serves sharply, as if she's cross, then laughs. No shame in losing to her, everyone does."
city.ask.sport.pingpong.2: "Friday the Rassvet shows the film about the boy who practised against a wall. Afterwards you can't move in here."
city.ask.sport.pool.1: "With a doctor's note. The clinic gives you one after the scales and the eye chart. A cap is a must; we've a box of lost ones."
city.ask.sport.potter.1: "The pottery studio and easels. The kiln has its own week: Monday raw, Wednesday firing, Friday glaze, Saturday ready."
city.ask.sport.potter.2: "Firing today: no more than three peeks into the kiln. The potter counts."
city.ask.sport.potter.3: "They're opening the kiln today! They say bowl number seven came out green as the sea on a grey day."
city.ask.sport.potter.4: "You sat at the wheel yourself. Your bowl is in the queue for firing too, I saw the tag."
city.ask.stall.bait.1: "Off the pier, at dawn, by the third lamp post. Bait with worms or dough; our fish aren't fussy."
city.ask.stall.bait.2: "They bite better in fog: the fish can't see who's holding the rod."
city.ask.stall.bait.3: "It's Fisherman's Day! Whoever catches the smallest fish gets a prize, honestly."
city.ask.stall.birdseed: What should I feed the birds?
city.ask.stall.birdseed.1: "Tits get suet and seeds, sparrows millet, pigeons whatever you can spare. Not bread, it makes them sad."
city.ask.stall.birdseed.2: "There's a 'Feed the birds' poster on the board by the library. Children drew it; the birds are fatter than real ones."
city.ask.stall.tea: Where did the samovar come from?
city.ask.stall.tea.1: "My grandfather's. I fire it with pine cones. Pier water won't do; I carry it from the pump by the sanatorium. It's a little salty and makes the tea softer."
city.ask.stall.tea.2: "In weather like this the queue for tea is longer than for fish. I'm not complaining."
city.ask.store.floors.1: "Downstairs: food, sweets and the tills. Upstairs: fabrics, toys, records and the lost and found. The café's by the stairs, you'll smell it."
city.ask.store.floors.2: "First to the department for a slip, then to the till, then back. Whoever remembers that is one of us."
city.ask.store.tree.1: "In December, in the stairwell, up to the ceiling. Ornaments from the third-floor stockroom, forty years old."
city.ask.store.tree.2: "See? There it is! The porter put the star on from a ladder; the whole department held its breath."
city.ask.store.tree.3: "It's snowing, so it won't be long. The stockroom is already jingling with ornaments."
city.ask.store.umbrella: What's the announcement on the radio?
city.ask.store.umbrella.1: "The lost and found. The yellow duck umbrella has turned up again: records one day, fabrics the next. The owner is delighted."
city.ask.store.umbrella.2: "At noon they also announce that nothing has been lost. Just in case someone was waiting."
city.ask.t3.cf.cups: Whose are the cups over the counter?
city.ask.t3.cf.cups.1: "The Surf sports society's. The smallest is engraved: 'For the will to win. Nearly won.' Everybody wants that one. So do I."
city.ask.t3.cf.cups.2: "The courtyard league table by the entrance: Surf Juniors in third place. In pencil: 'there will be more.' The coach wrote it, but I suspect the cleaner."
city.ask.t3.cf.kefir: What should I drink after training?
city.ask.t3.cf.kefir.1: "Kefir, not chocolate: that's what the coach says. Chocolate comes after the kefir, because the coach isn't looking."
city.ask.t3.cf.kefir.2: "The basketball players come out at seven red as crayfish and sweep up the kefir. By half past seven only apples are left."
city.ask.t3.cf.kefir.3: "In the cold they ask for tea. I drink with them: we take turns warming up."
city.ask.t3.co.drill: What if I can't do anything at all?
city.ask.t3.co.drill.1: "Come at five, stand by the back wall, pick up. Collecting balls is half the game, and the most honest half."
city.ask.t3.co.drill.2: "Today it's girls' gymnastics: quiet. Lidiya Pavlovna is counting jumps. Throw her off and they start again, and I have to listen."
city.ask.t3.co.drill.3: "I hear you picked up honestly. Now throw from the far mark. Wear the face of someone who scored. The rest follows."
city.ask.t3.co.elsewhere.1: "Table tennis at the Cog: there Kenji Kask looks left and hits right. It trains the eyes better than any wall. And patience at the Saucer, with the Professor."
city.ask.t3.co.elsewhere.2: "Played Kenji? How are the eyes? Look left, hit right: no need to hand on our tactics, he knows them himself."
city.ask.t3.co.elsewhere.3: "In the morning the hall is empty, just right for the shy. Come before eight, I don't use the whistle."
city.ask.t3.co.league.1: "The Seagulls are first, the Lighthouse second, we're third. In pencil on the table: 'there will be more.' I wrote it. Don't tell Taya."
city.ask.t3.co.league.2: "Forty-one, forty-two: the score is still up on the board. Taya says: to wipe it is to agree. I agree with her."
city.ask.t3.co.windows: Why are the windows dearer than the balls?
city.ask.t3.co.windows.1: "A ball costs a few roubles and comes back. A window costs more and doesn't. In a year eight balls were lost and no windows. I look after them."
city.ask.t3.co.windows.2: "After the game you didn't break a single window, I noticed. Whoever doesn't gets to pick the ball. Don't take the ginger one: he's a man of principle."
city.ask.t3.co.yellow: Why are you painting the balls yellow?
city.ask.t3.co.yellow.1: "So the stands can tell the ball from us. Though we're plenty visible: the ball still jumps better."
city.ask.t3.co.yellow.2: "On Saturday the weights section runs in the morning and no balls are needed. I can paint undisturbed; the paint dries just in time for the games."
city.ask.t3.co.yellow.3: "In the rain the paint dries slower but doesn't give up. Like me."
city.ask.t3.rc.after: What do I do after training?
city.ask.t3.rc.after.1: "After the gym walk to the Rassvet for the seven o'clock show: you sit, your legs hum, and nobody demands push-ups. Or to the library: they even stamp you 'for quiet hours'."
city.ask.t3.rc.after.2: "Today it's The Yard Champion in the afternoon: about the boy who practised against a wall. After it there's no room at the table."
city.ask.t3.rc.locker.1: "Number seven, the lucky one. Don't mix it up with eight: that's the coach's. Seven has scratched on it: 'Don't open until victory.' If it opens, victory has come."
city.ask.t3.rc.locker.2: "The number-five jersey is in my drawer and locker five is free. The coach said: a jersey has a number, not a towel."
city.ask.t3.rc.pool: How do I get into the pool?
city.ask.t3.rc.pool.1: "A doctor's note from the clinic: they weigh you, test your eyes, stamp it. With a stamp we let you in, with a smudge too, if the stamp is recognisable."
city.ask.t3.rc.pool.2: "Got the note already? Then you're nearly a swimmer. Take a cap from the box: lost ones wait for owners too."
city.ask.t3.rc.sections.1: "The timetable is by the door: gymnastics, basketball, weights, painting, the pottery studio. Sign up with the coach, entry is free, the socks are yours."
city.ask.t3.rc.sections.2: "Today it's basketball, Surf Juniors, three to seven. No outdoor shoes on the court: the coach asks impolitely."
city.ask.t3.rc.sections.3: "Today it's girls' gymnastics, Lidiya Pavlovna. Don't disturb the jump count: if they lose it they start over."
city.ask.tarelka.jukebox: What should I play on the jukebox?
city.ask.tarelka.jukebox.1: "Button seven. A waltz with a crackle. When it plays, the cups ring along in time by themselves."
city.ask.tarelka.jukebox.2: "You know the records better than I do already. The Cog and the Vaults have machines too, with records of their own."
city.ask.tarelka.kesha.1: "Sits on the coffee machine and announces: 'Terminus, please vacate the cars.' Then everyone finishes up and goes. Handy."
city.ask.tarelka.kesha.2: "He only takes roasted seeds, from the kiosk at the third stop. Bring some and he'll tell you a station."
city.ask.tarelka.kesha.3: "Mornings he's grumpy: silent until the first espresso. Not his, someone else's."
city.ask.tarelka.telescope: What can you see through the gallery telescope?
city.ask.tarelka.telescope.1: "By day, ships and cable car cabins. Drop a coin and you get five minutes of sky. I clean the lens myself, so no fingers."
city.ask.tarelka.telescope.2: "It's clear tonight: Venus will be out. Our lighthouse keeper says she only winks at her own."
city.ask.tarelka.telescope.3: "Looked already? Then you saw the cactus in the dispatcher's window at Zenith. That's its holiday."
city.ask.tobacco.chess.1: "The chess lot from the Cog. They buy one paper between three and go over the game on the back page."
city.ask.tobacco.chess.2: "Giuseppe González is their chief. Plays carefully, argues boldly. If you sit down with him, don't hurry."
city.ask.tobacco.chess.3: "They say you beat one of them. Now they buy the paper between four: they're waiting for you."
city.ask.tobacco.fog: What's that booming over the sea?
city.ask.tobacco.fog.1: "The foghorn on the lighthouse. It sounds in fog, every half minute. The keeper says it's not a signal, it's a temper."
city.ask.tobacco.fog.2: "Hear it? It's going today. Walk out on the pier: the keeper likes company on days like this."
city.ask.tobacco.seeds.1: "Pensioners, pigeons and Kesha. The parrot at the Saucer takes them roasted and only from the hand."
city.ask.tobacco.seeds.2: "Buy a bag and say 'Terminus' to him. Then he'll announce something nice."
city.ask.tobacco.seeds.3: "Heard all about Kesha at the information kiosk? Then you know more than the dispatcher."
city.bed.nap.1: I shut my eyes for a minute. When I opened them the window's shadow had crept onto the other wall.
city.bed.nap.2: I dozed to the ticking of the clock in the corridor. The dream was short and warm, like a sandwich.
city.bed.nap.3: A nurse looked in, tucked the blanket round me and left without a word.
city.bed.night.1: The sheets crackled with starch. The sea was murmuring outside, and then I heard nothing at all.
city.bed.night.2: I dreamt I was climbing an endless staircase to the sun and not getting tired at all.
city.bed.night.3: I woke to spoons ringing in glasses in the corridor: someone was bringing tea.
city.bed.private.1: This is someone's bed. The cover's been smoothed by a hand, there's a dent in the pillow. No.
city.bed.private.2: A stranger's bed smells of a stranger's soap. I just stood next to it.
city.bed.private.3: Someone else sleeps here. I have to find a place of my own.
city.bh.bed.1: The bed is made so tight you could ring it: a pillow with a tiny patch on the case, a dressing gown folded on the blanket. One doesn't sit on someone else's blanket.
city.bh.bed.2: At the head: pills for the days of the week, an alarm clock for seven, a wireless. Everything stands where it can be found in the dark.
city.bh.bed.3: Neat slippers under the bed, toes to the door: the owner is used to getting up facing the day's business.
city.bh.bike.1: A bicycle leans against the wall by the letter boxes. A tag on the frame says: "Don't touch. The wheel has a secret." It looks like a wheel.
city.bh.bike.2: A string bag of empty glass jars is tied to the carrier. The owner meant to go shopping, then changed his mind.
city.bh.bike.3: A dried maple leaf sits on the bell. The bicycle hasn't gone out for a long time, but someone wipes it with a cloth every week.
city.bh.books.1: "The Road Foreman's Handbook", "Slopes and Gradients", "Small-Span Bridges". Pencil marks on the spines: "read", "read twice", "don't trust table 7".
city.bh.books.2: Between the road manuals a slim book of poems is squeezed in: "Wind over the Plain". The bookmark is an old cable-car ticket.
city.bh.books.3: One book stands with its spine turned in. You turn it round: a blank notebook, on the flyleaf "For those who come after".
city.bh.chair.1: The armchair is turned to the window as if its owner isn't reading but keeping watch. A dent from an elbow on the arm. From here you see the terrace's south edge and not one needless building.
city.bh.chair.n: At night from the chair you see the capsules' lights and your reflection beside the lamp. The owner probably talks to it when no one is here.
city.bh.clerk.book.1: "The book lies on a lectern on the gallery. Everyone writes in it, residents and visitors alike. I don't read it, but I hear them laugh."
city.bh.clerk.book.2: "Write specifics: what you saw, at what time, from which bench. Those entries get read better afterwards than poems."
city.bh.clerk.book.3: "This week some bird left a red ribbon on the ledge, and the book has three entries about a gull. I'd have entered the ribbon too."
city.bh.clerk.hi.1: The duty clerk looks up from the ledger: "Good day. The post you sort yourself; the lift is our responsibility."
city.bh.clerk.hi.2: "Going up to the gallery? Quite right. You can always get there later, but the sunset won't wait."
city.bh.clerk.hi.3: Under the glass on the desk a clipping from an old paper: "Bridge House accepted by the commission". The clerk nudges it a little closer, as if that is how it should be.
city.bh.clerk.lift.1: "The lift runs round the clock. The gallery is always open, but after nine every second lamp goes out. The switch is by the lift if you want light."
city.bh.clerk.lift.2: "Two cars, but one runs more often: the second is for prams or furniture. There's a stop on the fourth floor too, where Hargreaves lives."
city.bh.clerk.lift.3: "If the car sticks, don't shout. Press the red button and count. They call me at the second count."
city.bh.clerk.who.1: "The house is big but everybody knows everybody. Hargreaves on the fourth is our old-timer, and Hanna Nasser on the second is our chess player. She plays quietly and without mercy."
city.bh.clerk.who.2: "The Abenovs are on the sixth. Their girl Thao brings me a drawn plan of the house once a week. In the plan the lift has eyes."
city.bh.clerk.who.3: "Sanne Sokolova on the third waters the gallery plants and pretends it isn't her. I thank her, but I won't tell her you know."
city.bh.door.1: The door is flung open and held by a chair. The room smells of tea, paper and a little paraffin. You tap the frame, not loudly, as asked.
city.bh.door.2: On the frame in neat ink: "Guests welcome from nine to nine. The lift is on the right. Wipe your feet, I've just mopped."
city.bh.forest.1: At the northern end, the slope: pines and spruce in a wall, a ridge above. Between the trunks someone's path shows white.
city.bh.forest.2: The binoculars pick out a hawk over the forest: it stands in the air without a wingbeat, as if hung there.
city.bh.forest.3: Above the forest the tiny upper station of the cable car: a matchbox on a branch.
city.bh.forest.fog: The forest is gone: grey wool in the binoculars, and your own breath.
city.bh.forest.n: The forest is solid black. A red light blinks on a pylon above it, and nothing else.
city.bh.garden.1: The winter garden is a long box of soil by the window: a palm, a monstera, a cactus in a jar. The lemon, they say, was planted by Hargreaves. It has never fruited.
city.bh.garden.2: Drops on the palm leaves: freshly watered. A slip in the pot: "Watering: Sokolova, 3-06. Please don't pick the leaves."
city.bh.garden.night: At night the garden is dark. Only a monstera leaf catches the embankment's lights like a small mirror.
city.bh.garden.rain: Rain taps on the glass and the garden is dry. The earth smells of rust and leaves.
city.bh.garden.warm: The sun has heated the glass, the palm's leaves hang heavier. It smells like a hothouse and a little like a bathhouse.
city.bh.garden.winter: Snow behind the glass and here it smells of earth and warm concrete: the radiator under the box works for the garden, not for people.
city.bh.gauge.1: The needle trembles by the 4: a steady wind off the sea. Beside it in pencil, in small handwriting: "normal".
city.bh.gauge.2: The gauge reads 6 and dances a little. You repeat the number to yourself so as not to forget it: Hargreaves asked.
city.bh.gauge.3: The needle all but lies on zero. A calm: on the gallery you can hear the samovar cooling.
city.bh.gauge.fog: In fog the needle hardly moves, as if the wind too had got stuck in the wool.
city.bh.gauge.rain: In the rain the needle jumps between 5 and 9: the gusts hit the glass like handfuls of peas.
city.bh.gauge.snow: Snowstorm: the needle is by ten and the glass hums. Hargreaves writes such numbers in red pencil.
city.bh.gchess.1: Chess on the gallery: games go slowly because the players keep glancing out of the window. A rook sits forgotten on a square's edge while a barge crosses the water.
city.bh.gchess.2: On the board a game stopped halfway: Black waits, White has gone. A note under the board: "We finish on Saturday. Don't touch! — H. N."
city.bh.globe.1: The globe spins with a creak and stops a finger's breadth east of the Black Sea. A pin and a red thread to a small circle: Tbilisi.
city.bh.globe.2: There is no pin in the Baltic on the globe: the owner would say he knows where he is without one.
city.bh.guard.chess.1: "Hanna Nasser plays until midnight if there's someone to play. She wins more often than she loses. Don't take offence: that's how she lives."
city.bh.guard.chess.2: "There's a board in the lobby too. By day they argue there, by night they finish the games. I sometimes put the pieces back; they wander off."
city.bh.guard.chess.3: "If you beat Hanna, she'll give you something. What, I won't say, but she serves a special tea."
city.bh.guard.hargreaves.1: "He spent thirty years calculating gradients for the Ministry of Highways. He says this house is the most honest gradient he ever saw: not a single slope."
city.bh.guard.hargreaves.2: "His knee has hurt since autumn. But every day he records the wind: morning, noon, evening. If you go up, write it down for him."
city.bh.guard.hargreaves.3: "He doesn't ask; he pretends not to be asking. Look in on him; his kettle is always hot."
city.bh.guard.hi.1: The night guard sits under the lamp with a cup: "Quiet tonight. The wind has gone to sleep; the lift hasn't lain down yet."
city.bh.guard.hi.2: "Go on up and look. The gallery is better at night than by day: fewer people and more stars."
city.bh.guard.hi.3: The guard checks his watch against the wall clock. "It's {time} now. No need to rush: the lift will come on its own."
city.bh.guard.night.1: "After nine it's quiet up there. Don't take the binoculars, they're screwed down. And don't knock on the glass: it doesn't bring the stars closer."
city.bh.guard.night.2: "On clear nights you can see the lighthouse beam fall on the glass. Count the seconds between flashes: it runs evenly, like a clock."
city.bh.guard.night.3: "In winter the gallery lamps burn lower: we economise. But from the lighthouse there is always light."
city.bh.hats.1: On the stand: somebody's raincoat, somebody's child's bobble hat and a wool scarf with a flat number sewn in: 4-03.
city.bh.hats.2: A theatre programme sticks out of a coat pocket with a chess move marked in red pencil. Somebody has been going over a game on the way.
city.bh.house.1: Bridge House. To residents. The lift runs round the clock; after nine please don't slam the doors. And don't leave prams by the lift: they ride up with the buttons. — The Board
city.bh.house.2: We water the winter garden on the gallery in turns. This week it's Sanne Sokolova (3-06). Thank you, Sanne: the palm looks better than the rest of us.
city.bh.house.3: R. Hargreaves (4-03) asks: whoever goes up to the gallery, please look at the wind gauge by the north window and remember the number. He hasn't come down for three days himself: his knee.
city.bh.house.4: The door of 4-03 stays unlocked by day. If you look in on Hargreaves, there's tea and letters from Tbilisi: he likes to hear them read aloud. Don't knock loudly.
city.bh.house.5: The gallery's visitors' book is nearly half full. Whoever wrote about the gull with a red ribbon on its leg, please answer: Thao Abenova (6-01) wants to know whose bird it is.
city.bh.house.6: Chess evening on the gallery on Saturday. Hanna Nasser (2-02) promises to play until her first lost game. Please don't let her win.
city.bh.house.7: Hargreaves is back upstairs: he came out himself, with a stick, sat on the south bench and wrote "W 5". The wind log now lies on the little table by the lift: write in the numbers you saw. Thank you all.
city.bh.house.8: Found on the outer ledge of a gallery window: a red ribbon. The bird's owner is unknown. The ribbon is with the porter; ask.
city.bh.lchess.1: The chess table in the lobby: a board, two chairs, and always somebody standing by to advise. Today no one is advising.
city.bh.lchess.2: The pieces stand as at the start. Somebody has moved a knight a square forward: an invitation to play.
city.bh.mail.1: The boxes carry names in pen and in typescript: Abenov, Sokolov, Yilmaz, Sato, Zaitsev. A folded paper sticks out of Hargreaves's slot; he only collects it after lunch.
city.bh.mail.2: On the sill by the boxes lies a letter with a Georgian stamp: "R. Hargreaves, 4-03". Somebody put it up high so it wouldn't be trodden on.
city.bh.mail.3: Hanna Nasser's box bulges with a bakery flyer. A note is stuck on it: "Please don't. I buy my own bread."
city.bh.mail.4: Electricity bills lie in a pile on top of the boxes. Femke Kavanagh's box is labelled by hand: "Writer. Letters politely, bills even more politely."
city.bh.mail.5: Yael Öztürk labelled her box in big felt pen: her eyes are poor. Chalked on the tile under it, in someone else's hand: "Careful, wet."
city.bh.mail.6: A key on a string is taped under Sato's box: a spare, for anyone who loses theirs. Sato claims it is safer than under the doormat.
city.bh.p.chair: E — sit down by the window
city.bh.p.diary: E — open the notebook on the desk
city.bh.p.door: E — knock on the open door
city.bh.p.garden: E — look over the winter garden
city.bh.p.hats: E — look over the coat stand
city.bh.p.letters: E — take the letters from the envelope
city.bh.p.mail: E — look over the letter boxes
city.bh.p.map: E — read what one sees from the windows
city.bh.p.roads: E — study the map on the wall
city.bh.p.tea: E — pour tea from the samovar
