city.bh.p.window: E — look out of the big window
city.bh.photos.1: A black-and-white photograph: people in hard hats on a slope, a tape measure at their feet and a theodolite on a tripod. Third from the left is young Hargreaves, thin, cap on one side.
city.bh.photos.2: A snapshot of a bridge over a mountain stream: an arch with nothing on it but sky. On the back: "The road opened a year later. The bridge still stands."
city.bh.photos.3: A group photograph on this very gallery on opening day: everyone in a coat, everyone looking not at the lens but out of the window. One of them is crying.
city.bh.plants.1: The earth by the ficus is dry. You pour some water from the mug that stands here for the purpose. A leaf bends toward you as if nodding.
city.bh.plants.2: The palm in the tub by the door catches a draught every time the door opens and holds up well. You wipe the dust off a frond.
city.bh.plants.3: There's water in the saucer from someone's watering. A card: "Hanna watered. Don't flood." You decide not to interfere.
city.bh.plants.mon: On Mondays the porter waters, by the rota. The leaves are taut and shiny, as if polished.
city.bh.plants.rain: Rain outside, and by the entrance it's as damp as a hothouse. The plants seem content: it's all one to them what waters them.
city.bh.pram.1: The Abenovs' pram with its rain cover pulled tight. In the pocket: a small tin spoon and a note, "Gone to the pier, back by four."
city.bh.pram.2: The pram is empty, but a blanket lies folded in it. The handle is warm: somebody has only just left it.
city.bh.pram.3: Two pairs of rubber boots stand under the pram, a big pair and a small one, toes to the wall. Like people who expect rain.
city.bh.radio.1: The wireless murmurs the coastal forecast: wind westerly, moderate, gusty by evening. The announcer reads as if he can hear it himself.
city.bh.radio.2: A violin is playing, and you can tell nobody has touched the dial for a long time. You turn the volume down as if someone were asleep in the room.
city.bh.radio.n: At night the wireless catches only the marine station: pressure figures and a deep voice naming capes and banks like a prayer.
city.bh.radio.rain: The bulletin warns: rain, wind up to nine. On a sheet beside it in pencil the same thing, shorter: "9".
city.bh.roads.1: On the town map a line in red pencil: a hairpin road that climbs between the terraces without a single stair. A red cross through it and the words: "not allowed".
city.bh.roads.2: Slopes are pencilled along the map's edge: 6, 7, 5.5, 8. A correction beside it: "if one drops the extra tier, exactly 6". The owner is still haggling with the map.
city.bh.roads.3: A point on the map by the upper terrace is ringed twice. A caption: "Here I would put a bench. Just so a person stops."
city.bh.sea.1: Sea to the very edge. Dashes of fishing boats on the pale water; a white thread at the horizon is a freighter, going along the coast in no hurry.
city.bh.sea.2: In the eyepiece: the lighthouse at the pier head, a lattice tower with a narrow golden lantern. Tiny people with rods at its foot.
city.bh.sea.3: Coloured patches on the beach under the terraces: towels. The lifeguards on their towers stand like two matches and turn together.
city.bh.sea.fog: The fog has eaten everything but the lighthouse's light: just a golden smudge. The horn reaches here a second after the flash.
city.bh.sea.n1: At night the lighthouse beam crosses the water and the gallery glass every few seconds. You count: one, two, three... and again.
city.bh.sea.n2: The embankment lights are laid out in a ruler's line. Beyond them black water, and at its edge a few stars.
city.bh.sea.rain: Rain comes in from the sea in a wall. The embankment is grey, umbrellas crawl along the pier like beetles.
city.bh.sea.snow: Snow. The sea is leaden, the pier dusted white, the lighthouse stands like a pen in an inkwell.
city.bh.sit.n1: The north windows look along the terrace: the round roof of the sanatorium and the ribbed vaults of the hall, a shell beside a saucer.
city.bh.sit.n2: It is slightly cooler here: the north wind finds a gap in the frame. But the bench is always empty, and the view a hand's breadth wider.
city.bh.sit.nn: In the north at night there isn't a light: only the sanatorium's round roof glows along its rim, like a saucer over a candle.
city.bh.sit.s1: The south windows show the terrace's edge: the capsule towers on the slope, their windows lit at different hours like grains being poured from hand to hand.
city.bh.sit.s2: The bench is warm: the glass has heated it since morning. You read other people's entries in the book on the sill and the hour goes.
city.bh.sit.sn: The south windows are black at night: only your reflection and the far yellow dots of the capsules.
city.bh.tea.1: The samovar is warm: a resident heats it each morning. Beside it a saucer of sugar lumps and a note, "Cups on the sill, please return them."
city.bh.tea.2: You pour tea into somebody's cup with a chipped handle. The tea is strong, the way it is with people who expect guests and know no other way.
city.bh.tea.3: A tiny puddle under the samovar. It is wiped up every morning and comes back every day. Bridge House knows and puts up with it.
city.bh.tea.k1: You put the kettle on. Beside it a tin with a note: "For guests, help yourself. Only one kind, but the real thing." You take a bag.
city.bh.tea.k2: The kettle on the stove is still warm. The owner must be near: a cup on the sill, a little steam over it, set on the side where the window is open.
city.bh.tea.n: The samovar has cooled: at this hour people take tea at home. Only the smell of the morning is left, and an empty cup.
city.bh.town.1: The terraces step down to the water, each with its own roof and shade of concrete. There the long snake of a block on the second, there the wavy tower on the third.
city.bh.town.2: The cable car: a cabin slides along the rope, the saucer of Zenith station glints. Two ropes part like whiskers.
city.bh.town.3: In the courtyards of the lower town washing and children; on the square, at the fountain, a point of light: water playing with the sun.
city.bh.town.n1: The cable-car pylons glow red at their tops. A cabin with a yellow window crawls up toward us and is lost behind the edge.
city.bh.town.n2: The terrace windows burn differently: here a blue television, there a yellow lamp. You guess the houses by the colour of the light.
city.bh.town.rain: In the rain the cabins run with their lights on, like lanterns on a string.
city.bh.tx.diary.1: A notebook in an oilcloth cover. In pencil on the front: "The road that was never built". Inside, level lines as if drawn with a ruler.
city.bh.tx.diary.2: "For thirty-one years I calculated gradients. I know how a road lies on a slope and how the slope answers the road. This house stands on a slope and asks for nothing. That is why I love it."
city.bh.tx.diary.3: "From the window I see the pier and the beam. I used to think a lighthouse was about ships. Now I think it is about those who watch. I write the wind down not for science but to know that the day happened."
city.bh.tx.diary.4: "The knee failed me. I did not go up to the gallery. I asked the neighbour's girl, Thao, to look at the gauge. She repeats the numbers aloud like a counting rhyme. The numbers are right."
city.bh.tx.diary.5: "If somebody reads this, here is a request. Don't pity me. Come in, drink tea, tell me what is visible from the windows. And enter the needle in the log: it is on the desk. I shall check the handwriting."
city.bh.tx.diary.6: "I went out myself today. The lift, the bench by the south window, a gull without a ribbon. Everything in its place. Wrote W 5. I write here so as not to forget: I must thank Thao."
city.bh.tx.diary.title: Rohan Hargreaves's diary
city.bh.tx.guest.1:
The Bridge House gallery's visitors' book. Opened on the day the lift started. The handwriting varies: some lovely, some jumping.
"Strong wind, but you can see everything. — a group from Sukhumi"
"The lighthouse by day and by night are two different wonders. — L."
city.bh.tx.guest.2:
"My husband and I come every Saturday. He counts ships, I count gulls. Yesterday: 14 and 31. — Hanna Nasser, 2-02"
"The best chess in town here. Lost three games in a row, but the view behind the glass makes up for it. — A."
city.bh.tx.guest.3:
"Thank you to whoever brought the rugs for the benches. And to whoever returned the samovar. — The Board"
"The binoculars at the north end show a hawk. A real one. — a pupil from 5B"
city.bh.tx.guest.4:
"A gull with a red ribbon on its leg sat on the outer ledge for three days. Whose is it? — Thao A., 6-01, aged 11"
"Hargreaves asks that nobody tap the wind gauge's glass: the instrument has kept its records unbroken for years. — R. H."
city.bh.tx.guest.5:
"The gull flew north. Thao fished the ribbon out with a rod and the whole house applauded. — N. A."
"Rohan Hargreaves hasn't come up again. Thao keeps the wind records: numbers in a child's hand, but correct. — a neighbour"
city.bh.tx.guest.6:
"For newcomers: come on a clear evening, at sunset. Sit on the south bench and wait until a red path lies on the pier. — Sh. S."
"Reading the entries I see the book thickening like a tree. It will soon be a hundred pages. — R. Hargreaves"
city.bh.tx.guest.title: The gallery's visitors' book
city.bh.tx.letters.1: An envelope with a Georgian stamp, three letters inside. The first: "Dear Rohan! We have a bridge house too: the Ministry of Highways sits in it like a hand in a sleeve. But we have no gallery and the lift stops one floor below the dream. You are a lucky man. Levan."
city.bh.tx.letters.2: "You ask how my back is. I answer: concrete endures and so do I. Bring me some sea pebbles from your beach. I'll put them on the sill and watch them dry. There is something in it."
city.bh.tx.letters.3: "Do you remember the road they would not let us build, the hairpin on the slope? I found the drawing in the archive. They did not throw it out: it lies in a folder marked 'For inspiration'. I've been laughing for two days. Come in autumn and we'll look at it together."
city.bh.tx.letters.title: Letters from Tbilisi
city.bh.tx.view.1: The south end, the big window: the sea, the pier with its lighthouse, the embankment, the square with the fountain. That is the town's axis, a straight line from this window to the water. In summer the sunset stands exactly on it.
city.bh.tx.view.2: The long windows look along the terrace. From the south side you see the capsule towers on the slope, from the north the sanatorium's round roof and the hall's ribbed vaults. The benches face them, not each other.
city.bh.tx.view.3: The north end: the slope, the pine forest, the upper cable-car station. Binoculars on a stand; on a clear day a hawk is visible over the ridge. Telescopes at the south wall: the sea, and the town with its cable car.
city.bh.tx.view.title: What one sees from the gallery
city.bh.tx.wind.1: Wind log, Bridge House gallery. Kept by R. Hargreaves: morning, noon, evening. W is off the sea, E off the land, the figure is the gauge's reading.
city.bh.tx.wind.2: Entries: W 4 · W 5 · SW 7 · SW 9 (gusts) · N 3 · W 4. Small even handwriting, blue ink. In the margin: "Will drop by evening. Did not."
city.bh.tx.wind.3: Further on the hand grows larger and wobbles: "W 6. The knee. This evening Thao looks in my place." One spot of the page got wet and dried in a wave.
city.bh.tx.wind.4: A new hand, a child's, round: "Reading 7, the needle trembles by the figure. Written by Thao A." A line below: "Reading 5, the needle calm. Thao."
city.bh.tx.wind.5: Two hands alternate: an even one and a child's. At the foot of the page a note in Hargreaves's hand: "Thanks for the needle. The house has two observers now. R. H."
city.bh.tx.wind.6: The last entry is still not dry: "W 5. Entered by a visitor from the gallery." Below it an empty line and a pencil tied on a thread, in case somebody else comes.
city.bh.tx.wind.title: The wind log
city.bh.win.d: Noon: the sea is scaly with glare, the pier a thread, the embankment flat as a postcard.
city.bh.win.e: Toward evening the light runs along the water and each terrace casts its shadow on the next.
city.bh.win.m: Morning: the sun is behind you and the whole sea ahead is flooded with light. The boats head for shore as if pulled on a thread.
city.bh.win.n: At night the glass gives you back to yourself. Behind the reflection a line of lights and the beam, arriving in turn.
city.bh.win.sun: The sunset stands exactly on the town's axis: from the lighthouse along the embankment, the square, the stairs, to this window. Everyone on the gallery is silent.
city.book.keys: E, D, → next · A, ← back · Esc, W, S close
city.book.keys_last: E, Esc, W, S close · A, ← back
city.cafe.book.0: The first page, the ink faded: "Open at last. The coffee smells, the stair spirals, and we seem to be sitting inside a saucer. Thanks to the architect. — The first guests."
city.cafe.book.1: "Came with my daughter. She demanded ice cream three times, and three times we didn't mind." Next to it, a cone with three scoops.
city.cafe.book.2: In green ink, in a hurry: "The parrot told me 'Mind the doors, please' and I stepped back. There are no doors here. Thank you, Kesha!"
city.cafe.book.3: "Played chess with the Professor. Lost in seven moves. He said: 'Never mind, you resigned in good time.' A good school."
city.cafe.book.4: In a different pen: "Lighthouse keeper on duty. Dropped in off my watch. I confirm: my beam can be seen from your window. It looks better from here than from my side."
city.cafe.book.5: Two hands side by side, two pens: "We both came. Sat by the window until closing. One told about the static, the other about how long it had been since he'd heard a voice without noise. Paid half and half. No static. — I. and G."
city.cafe.book.6: In a corner of the page someone has drawn a saucer with eyes and written: "This is us." Below, in the barista's hand: "Leaving it as it is."
city.cafe.book.7: A fresh entry by the manager: "The pages are running out, we'll start a new book soon. The pen is next to the book, and if you've no thoughts, draw a saucer. We love saucers."
city.cafe.cake.fri: Friday: the "Anthill", a brown mound with nuts. A small boy at the case has already chosen and is waiting for his mother to.
city.cafe.cake.mon: Monday: the case holds a chocolate "Potato" and two eclairs. The eclairs, judging by the price tag, hope to last until Tuesday.
city.cafe.cake.sat: Saturday: the "Saucer" cake, round, glazed, with a small spiral wafer on top like the stair. People take it whole, for tea.
city.cafe.cake.sun: Sunday: pastries for everyone on a tray with a red rim. A card: "One each, please. In exceptional cases, two."
city.cafe.cake.thu: Thursday: apple puffs. A hand-written line on the price tag: "The last one, don't be shy."
city.cafe.cake.tue: Tuesday: Napoleon cake. The layers are so thin it looks as if someone counted them with tweezers.
city.cafe.cake.wed: Wednesday: little cream baskets with a berry. Each berry sits exactly in the middle, like a seal.
city.cafe.chess.1: I took the Captain's place at the board: he said he had "business at the lighthouse", though he was probably just tired of losing. The Professor moves his pawns as if apologising. Twenty moves later I was the one apologising.
city.cafe.chess.2: After school the board belongs to two schoolboys. They play fast and loud, whispering at every move. They let me into the third game as a newcomer from outside.
city.cafe.chess.3: At weekends the chess moves to the nearest table: here they play for coffee. The loser orders. I lost, but the Captain ordered himself: "A newcomer's first coffee is on us."
city.cafe.chess.4: The Professor mates me on the ninth move, silently, without taking off his hat. Then, just as silently, he sets the pieces back and shows where I could have won. It turns out, on the sixth.
city.cafe.chess.5: The Captain plays only black and only one opening. He calls it the "Lighthouse Defence". He doesn't explain what it means, and wins in such a way that you can't take offence.
city.cafe.chess.6: The game was interrupted by the parrot announcing "Terminus". We finished in a draw: everyone looked at Kesha and forgot whose move it was.
city.cafe.chess.prompt: E — sit down with the chess players
city.cafe.cook.fri: "Friday: syrniki. Sour cream comes with them, but only whoever remembers to ask gets it."
city.cafe.cook.mon: The cook, without turning round: "Monday, noodle soup. My grandmother's recipe; don't ask my grandmother."
city.cafe.cook.prompt: E — ask the cook about the dish of the day
city.cafe.cook.sat: "Saturday: pilaf for everyone. Whoever comes first gets the bottom of the pot, the best part."
city.cafe.cook.sun: "On Sundays I don't cook. I only warm up what I left from Saturday and call it home cooking."
city.cafe.cook.thu: "Thursday: stuffed cabbage. Probably the best in the district today. Tomorrow merely good."
city.cafe.cook.tue: "Tuesday: cutlets and mash. I make the mash myself and don't spare the butter; dieticians are asked not to look."
city.cafe.cook.wed: "Wednesday: fish and potatoes. The fish came from the pier this morning, still arguing."
city.cafe.crate.1: A crate of sleeves: the records stand on edge like books in a library. On the spines, in pencil, the button numbers. The numbers stopped matching the buttons long ago.
city.cafe.crate.2: A sleeve marked "Left behind in April". Inside, a postcard of the sea and a record of the same sea, only audible.
city.cafe.crate.3: One record is labelled "D-3 (by request, do not take away)". Someone has underlined "do not take away" twice. So it has been taken away.
city.cafe.crate.4: Deep in the crate, a shabby sleeve: "To the Saucer's best listener. Thank you for never interrupting. — The Sanatorium Orchestra."
city.cafe.crate.5: A note is stuck on the side: "The machine takes coins. Not buttons: Kesha tested it." Next to it, a beak print.
city.cafe.crate.6: In the evening the crate is half empty: the records have gone round the tables, and the sleeves stand without them like coats without owners.
city.cafe.crate.7: At weekends the dance records go on top: couples mid-turn on the sleeves and, in big letters, "An Evening Out".
city.cafe.crate.8: When it rains somebody always puts the record of the surf on top. So the sea won't feel left out, they say.
city.cafe.esp.d1: At lunchtime the machine never stops: steam, click, steam, click. The cups leave on a tray and come back empty, with spoons in the saucers.
city.cafe.esp.d2: A dark thread creeps slowly from the spout. Watch it for over a minute and you want a glass of water and a second cup.
city.cafe.esp.e1: By evening the coffee is made less often and the steam lasts longer. While the stream runs, the barista looks out of the window: that is where the best part is now.
city.cafe.esp.e2: A note is taped to the machine's panel: "Don't tap the gauge. It's nervous." The needle trembles as if it has heard everything.
city.cafe.esp.m1: By eight everything is ready: the bar wiped, the machine warm, the chairs down on their legs. Now the barista silently watches the pressure gauge like a barometer before a long journey.
city.cafe.esp.m2: The first cup of the morning is not for the guests. It is set on the edge of the bar on its saucer and left to cool until the first visitor comes in. They say the café treats itself first.
city.cafe.esp.m3: The grounds are tamped with one short, level press. A click of the lever, a hiss, and the hall smells so good the chairs seem to shuffle closer.
city.cafe.esp.n: The machine cools, ticking softly. In the morning it will be woken again.
city.cafe.espresso.prompt: E — watch the coffee being made
city.cafe.feed.1: I poured the seeds into the saucer and said "Terminus". Kesha waited until I had finished, cracked one, thought, and announced: "Please vacate the cars." The barista laughed and took a pastry from the case: "Finder gets one on the house. You've found him again, more or less."
city.cafe.feed.2: Kesha pecked a seed and said: "Thank you for the ride." He never used to say that. The barista set a pastry on a saucer in front of me.
city.cafe.feed.3: Kesha ate one seed and hid the rest under his perch "until the next stop". The pastry on the house is already waiting on the bar.
city.cafe.feed.4: Morning, and Kesha is still sleepy. He took one seed, held it in his beak and whispered, "Mind the doors." The barista put a pastry in front of me.
city.cafe.feed.5: Rain outside, and Kesha has fluffed himself up. He ate the seeds in silence and only at the end muttered, "Don't forget your umbrellas." My pastry came with a napkin.
city.cafe.feed.6: It's a holiday, and Kesha has a paper flag on his perch. He cracked the seeds and shouted, "Happy holiday, dear passengers!" The whole room answered.
city.cafe.feed.7: The first time, Kesha studied me with one eye, then the other. He must have decided I was all right, and took a seed straight from my palm.
city.cafe.feed.prompt: E — treat Kesha to sunflower seeds
city.cafe.guestbook.prompt: E — leaf through the guest book
city.cafe.juke.a1: Button A-1: a waltz on a record worn to silver. The machine sighs, creaks, then gives out the waltz as if it had never done anything else.
city.cafe.juke.a4: A-4, a march. Without looking up, the barista turns it down a notch: someone by the window is reading the paper and the drum is in his way.
city.cafe.juke.b1: B-1: a song about the sea in a foreign language. An elderly couple at a table falls silent on the second line and listens to the end, holding on to their cups.
city.cafe.juke.b5: B-5: a twist. The chairs at the nearest table suddenly start tapping along by themselves, and there are shoes underneath them too.
city.cafe.juke.c2: C-2: instead of music, an announcer's voice reading the coastal weather. Someone must have mixed up the sleeve. I listened to the end: no rain tomorrow.
city.cafe.juke.c6: C-6. Next to it, by hand: "DO NOT PRESS". I pressed. A flute began, very quietly, as if from far away. Now I see why nobody presses it.
city.cafe.juke.d3: The third button from the left, D-3: the tune I was looking for plays whole, with no static, to the last note. The barista nods: "It's the most requested. They say someone taped it off the air."
city.cafe.juke.g1: In the morning the jukebox is quiet: G-1, a soft little waltz under the hiss of the coffee machine. The barista nods along without noticing.
city.cafe.juke.g3: In the evening the jukebox is louder: G-3, a foxtrot, and someone by the stairs is already tapping a foot, pretending to tie a shoelace.
city.cafe.kesha.0: Kesha sits on his perch at the end of the bar and looks with one eye as if checking a ticket. Then he announces: "Next stop, the Saucer." We're already on it, but I didn't argue.
city.cafe.kesha.1: Today Kesha is silent and only bobs his head to the jukebox. The barista whispers: "He's on leave after the tour."
city.cafe.kesha.2: "Mind the doors, please!" Kesha announces when someone heads for the stairs. There are no doors in the hall, but everyone ducks a little.
city.cafe.kesha.3: Kesha has learned a new word and says it only when nobody asks. The word is "Horizon". I think he just likes the sound of it.
city.cafe.kesha.4: Kesha studies me for a long time, then says very clearly: "Ticket." I show him my empty palms. Kesha turns away, disappointed.
city.cafe.kesha.5: Beside the perch is a saucer, marked in felt pen: "For Kesha. Sunflower seeds. But first say 'Terminus'." Kesha waits without blinking.
city.cafe.kesha.6: Kesha has got used to me: he no longer turns away but tilts his head a little. The barista says he does that for people who bring seeds.
city.cafe.ledge.d1: By day the glass is warm as a stove, and the spoons on their saucers throw sunbeams on the ceiling. It is hot and very cheerful to sit here.
city.cafe.ledge.d2: On a paper napkin, in pencil: "The window is best at seven in the evening. Do come." No signature.
city.cafe.ledge.m1: The ledge by the glass is still cool, the light grey and soft. Below, the promenade wakes: first the street-washing truck, then the first bicycle.
city.cafe.ledge.m2: Somebody has left a glass of water with a twig in it on the ledge. The twig has already put out a white root.
city.cafe.ledge.n1: At night the ledge is the quietest place in the Saucer. The lamps reflect in the glass, and it seems another hall hangs outside, empty and upside down.
city.cafe.ledge.n2: Below, the promenade lights; above, the stars; between them a black strip of sea. One far-off boat crawls along it, and I feel like waving my glass at it.
city.cafe.ledge.s1: There it is. By seven the glass turns copper, then pink, and every cup throws a long shadow all the way to the stairs. At the nearby tables everyone falls quiet at once.
city.cafe.ledge.s2: A disc of sun lies in my palm, still warm. In a minute it will slide to the floor and go toward the stairs, and I'll sit beside it a little longer.
city.cafe.ledge.s3: The ledge lamp is on but not needed yet: there is light enough. The barista has quietened the machine so as not to disturb it. Nobody says it aloud, but this is called "the minute of sunset".
city.cafe.mags.1: In the morning the magazines still lie in a neat pile. On top, the new issue with a mountain lake on the cover; the pages stick together.
city.cafe.mags.2: By lunchtime the magazines are dog-eared, and there's a cup ring on the spread about steamers. Like a harbour stamp.
city.cafe.mags.3: On a cold day everybody takes the same magazine, the one about the south: palms, white liners. It goes from table to table.
city.cafe.mags.4: New issues come on Mondays. The barista ties up the old ones with string and takes them away, but one always stays: somebody hasn't finished it.
city.cafe.painting.1: Over the sofa, the sea in oils: grey water, a white line of surf and a small red buoy. The painter seems to have added the buoy at the last moment, for courage.
city.cafe.painting.2: The morning sun falls right on the frame, and the painted water turns brighter than the real water outside.
city.cafe.painting.3: Towards evening the painting darkens before the window does. Only the line of surf is left, and the buoy, as if someone had lit it.
city.cafe.painting.4: In fog you can't see the sea from the window, so everyone looks at this one. The barista says on days like these the painting does the work of two.
city.cafe.painting.5: On the bottom of the frame, a slip of paper: "A gift from the holidaymakers, summer." Somebody has rubbed out the year with a finger, probably by accident.
city.cafe.pen.1: I wrote: "Was here. It's good for thinking, with a staircase underfoot." Thought a moment and added the date.
city.cafe.pen.2: I didn't know what to write, so I drew a saucer. It came out more like a hat. I captioned it: "Saucer (view from below)."
city.cafe.pen.3: I added in a corner: "Hi, Kesha!" with an exclamation mark. Thought and added a second.
city.cafe.pen.4: Under someone else's entry I wrote: "Agreed." What with, I only worked out as I closed the book, but I didn't rub it out.
city.cafe.pen.5: In the morning the book lies open at a clean page. I wrote first: "Good morning, Tarelka." The handwriting came out sleepy, but honest.
city.cafe.pen.6: The pen leaves blots: everyone's sleeves are wet. I wrote, "Rain. Coffee. Life goes on," and blotted it with a napkin.
city.cafe.pen.7: The page is covered with snowflakes cut from napkins and glued between the wishes. I wrote mine in the very corner so as not to touch any of them.
city.cafe.pen.8: I leaf back and find my first entry. Under it somebody has added: "Me too." I don't know who, but it feels warmer.
city.cafe.tel.d1: By day the town in the lens is a scale model: the cable car crawls from station to station, and a tiny cyclist on the promenade never reaches the corner while I watch.
city.cafe.tel.d2: I found the sanatorium roof in the lens. Something is drying on it: washing or flags, I can't tell from here. Maybe both.
city.cafe.tel.m1: In the morning the telescope shows the fishing boats coming home, each with a white thread of gulls behind it. One gull sits on a bow and is in no hurry at all.
city.cafe.tel.m2: Down on the promenade someone is hosing the paving. Through the telescope it shines like a freshly washed plate.
city.cafe.tel.n1: At night the lighthouse beam crosses the lens slowly, like a clock hand. I count: four seconds until the next sweep.
city.cafe.tel.n2: The windows on the hillside burn in different ways: warm ones, blue ones from a TV, and one that blinks. Is somebody signalling? Most likely a bad bulb.
city.cafe.tel.n3: No moon, but for a second the dark eyepiece reflects the whole Saucer from inside: the lamps, the tables, and me with my eye to the tube.
city.cafe.tel.s1: Toward evening the sun settles on the water like a yolk on a saucer, and the water around it turns pink. The coin ran out before the sunset did.
city.cafe.tel.s2: The lighthouse lamp is lit while the sky is still bright. In the lens the beam looks like a thread just pulled through a needle.
city.cap.back.d: On the other side of the bridge: the slope and the steps of the next terrace, little gardens, aerials on the roofs.
city.cap.back.n: Behind: the dark of the slope and a few windows. Someone is awake. That glow is probably somebody's radio.
city.cap.back.rain: The slope behind the bridge drowns in a wet haze. The rooftop aerials gleam like thin needles.
city.cap.bell.d: Ding. Nobody comes: the front desk must have gone for tea. The sound dissolves in the passage.
city.cap.bell.n: Ding: too loud for the night. The echo runs to the lift and comes back softer.
city.cap.bike.1: A city bike, its bell wrapped in blue tape. A tag on the frame reads: Not mine, but hands off.
city.cap.bike.2: The tyres were pumped up recently: a fresh cap on the valve. Somebody rides in the mornings.
city.cap.bike.rain: The frame drips: it was ridden in the rain and then left to dry against the wall.
city.cap.bike.snow: The bike stands as if wintering: a bag over the saddle, a knitted mitten on the handlebar.
city.cap.ext.1: A fire extinguisher with several tags: Checked. The signature is sweeping, like a flourish on a postcard.
city.cap.ext.2: On the wall beside it an arrow and a line: Stairs are on the left. Do not call the lift in a fire.
city.cap.hats.1: On the stand: a hat, a beret and a scarf tied in a knot. The scarf has hung there so long it counts as a local.
city.cap.hats.cold: Winter hats with ear flaps hang in rows. It smells of warm wool.
city.cap.hats.rain: Wet raincoats hang on the stand, puddles under them. Someone hung one inside out.
city.cap.hats.warm: In warm weather the stand is nearly bare. Only a straw hat with a ribbon is left.
city.cap.hooks.1: On the hooks: a raincoat and headphones with the cord tied in a bow. Ilmar hangs them where he can reach from the bed.
city.cap.hooks.2: In the raincoat pocket: a folded QSL card and a pencil stub.
city.cap.hooks.rain: The raincoat is still wet: the caretaker has just come back from his rounds.
city.cap.keys.1: A board for spare keys. The tags carry numbers; one has the word BRIDGE instead.
city.cap.keys.d: By day half the hooks are empty: some were lent, some never came back.
city.cap.keys.e: In the evening every hook is taken. Only BRIDGE is empty: someone is lingering up there.
city.cap.keys.m: In the morning the hooks are nearly bare: those who forgot their keys have been given them.
city.cap.lift.1: The call button glows red. Somewhere above a winch hums: the lift is coming.
city.cap.lift.2: The plate lists three stops: the lobby, the seventh-floor bridge, the top bridge. The house promises no fourth.
city.cap.lift.night: At night the lift rides quietly, as if on tiptoe: the front desk oils it on Saturdays.
city.cap.log.1: The front desk's duty book: the time on the left, what happened on the right. It lies open as if just put down.
city.cap.logp.1: 06:10: the lift hums louder than usual, oiled it. 07:30: the milkwoman left a crate by the door and signed the book in red. 09:00: the ninth floor asks for a new bulb on the bridge.
city.cap.logp.2: 13:20: the boy from the third floor lost a mitten; it turned up on the lift roller. Wrote a notice. 16:00: the office came to count the capsules and counted one too many. Counted again: it was the moon in a round window.
city.cap.logp.3: 22:40: someone left a little box of tape on the bench of the seventh-floor bridge. Didn't touch it; the owner will come himself. 23:05: quiet. I listen to the lift, it listens to the house.
city.cap.logp.4: 07:00: nobody has collected the box on the bridge; hung a notice by the letter boxes. 12:00: the boy from the third floor brought a second mitten: "So the first one won't be lonely."
city.cap.logp.5: If you are reading this, you didn't come for the post. The lift runs, the lamps are lit, the bridge is warm. Come in whenever you like.
city.cap.logp.title: The front desk's duty book
city.cap.mail.1: Letter boxes with paper names. On one, a lamp is drawn instead of a name.
city.cap.mail.d: The postman has been: corners of envelopes and rolled newspapers stick out of the boxes.
city.cap.mail.e: By evening the post is gone: every box is empty but one. In it, a letter with a foreign stamp.
city.cap.mail.m: Morning, and the boxes are still empty: the postman comes at ten.
city.cap.mail.n: At night the boxes are quiet. Only one lid clicks in the draught.
city.cap.mail.sun: Sunday: no post, the boxes shut and tidy as teeth.
city.cap.news.1: To residents: from 11 pm to 1 am please do not bang doors or pipes. In the capsule by the entrance contact is being made with far stations. Thank you. Caretaker I. Singh.
city.cap.news.2: Found on the bench of the seventh-floor bridge: a box with a reel of magnetic tape. The owner is asked to collect it from me, in the capsule by the entrance. No owner? We'll listen to it together.
city.cap.news.3: Whoever brings the box from the seventh-floor bridge to the caretaker gets tea. Real tea, on Thursdays and whenever. I. S.
city.cap.news.4: Thank you all. The tape turned out to be a recording of the air: a voice out of the night that nobody had looked for in forty years. I listen in the evenings; do come in. I. Singh.
city.cap.news.base: House notices: The lift is mended on Saturdays only; the bridge is no place to dry laundry; quiet hours 11 pm to 1 am. The rest is on other slips.
city.cap.news.thu: On Thursdays the caretaker brews tea at the fold-down table. Bring your own cup.
city.cap.p.hats: E — look at the coat stand
city.cap.p.keys: E — look at the key board
city.cap.p.log: E — leaf through the duty book
city.cap.p.mail: E — look at the letter boxes
city.cap.p.street: E — look out at the street
city.cap.p.table: E — pour tea at the fold-down table
city.cap.phone.1: A black telephone with a cord as long as a fishing line. A slip beside it: If Gunnar calls, say I'm on my rounds.
city.cap.phone.m: In the morning the telephone is silent: everyone sleeps, and the caretaker sorts the post.
city.cap.phone.n: At night the bell is switched off: only the air is left. The receiver is cold as if nobody has touched it for ages.
city.cap.plant.1: The leaves shine: someone wipes them with a cloth on Thursdays.
city.cap.plant.2: A stick in the pot carries a sign: Water on Tuesdays. No cigarette ends.
city.cap.plant.3: Someone wrote Misha on a leaf in pencil. The leaf has grown and the name has stretched.
city.cap.plant.rain: With the rain it is a little close in the lobby, and the plants look content.
city.cap.plant.snow: The plants watch the snow behind the glass as if they'd like to go out themselves.
city.cap.plant.warm: In the heat the leaves droop a little. A watering can stands beside it for anyone who notices.
city.cap.pram.1: The pram is empty and dry, the blanket folded into a triangle. Its owner lives on the ninth floor, it seems.
city.cap.pram.2: A rattle and a little knitted lion lie in the pram. Someone has carefully parked it under the lamp.
city.cap.pram.n: At night the pram stands by itself like a watchman. The baby has long been asleep upstairs.
city.cap.reel.1: A cardboard box tied with string. On the reel, red tape and a pencilled line: Night air. Do not erase. I'll take it to the one who is waiting.
city.cap.reel.2: The bench is warm: someone sat here not long ago. The tape lies beside it as if its owner forgot to stand up and take it.
city.cap.s7.d: From the seventh-floor bridge the street lies on the palm of your hand, people the size of matchsticks. The lobby roof below is downy with pigeon feathers.
city.cap.s7.n: At night the street below is a chain of lamps. From up here you can see someone walking home.
city.cap.s7.rain: Rain sounds different here: on the rails, on the concrete, on the next capsules like drums.
city.cap.sill.1: Three radio valves stand in a row on the sill like gnomes. Ilmar calls the smallest one "the baby".
city.cap.sill.n: At night the valves glow faintly with a reflected streetlamp, as if the set were on without power.
city.cap.sill.rain: Rain taps the glass and, if you listen, it comes out almost as Morse.
city.cap.street.d1: Through the lobby glass the street runs both ways; people walk past the tower as if they hadn't noticed it.
city.cap.street.d2: The capsules hang over the street. Look up and the house seems about to sway.
city.cap.street.fest: There is a festival outside: people pass with little flags. Someone waves up at the capsules.
city.cap.street.fog: Fog has eaten the street. Only the lamp by the entrance and the edge of the canopy are left.
city.cap.street.n: At night the glass turns into a mirror: a lamp, an armchair and a bit of you.
city.cap.street.rain: Rain drums on the canopy; the lobby is dry and smells of wet umbrellas.
city.cap.street.snow: Snow settles on the canopy and slides off in sheets. From the lobby it looks like a slow film.
city.cap.table.1: The fold-down table is lowered: a flask, two cups and a sugar bowl with a chipped rim. The cups don't match: guests are expected here.
city.cap.table.2: The tea is strong as the night air. "Drink," Ilmar would say if he were home.
city.cap.table.thu: Thursday: the cups are already laid out, and on the saucer a note: For whoever brings the tape.
city.cap.tapes.1: A reel-to-reel recorder with two reels, four tape boxes beside it. The spines carry frequencies.
city.cap.tapesp.1: Tape 1. First contacts. A young hoarse voice: "Hello, hello, who hears me? Capsule, twenty metres up, signal good." Out of the static: "I hear you, capsule..." Then laughter, and a cut.
city.cap.tapesp.2: Tape 7. The night of the thunderstorm. Crackle, hiss, and suddenly an even, distant voice reads a forecast for sailors in three languages. Ilmar mutters over it: "Now that is range."
city.cap.tapesp.3: Tape 12. Gunnar's voice: "Lyudmilovsk-11 calling the capsule. Ilmar, are you there?" A pause of seven seconds. Then, quietly: "I'm here. I always was." After that only hiss.
city.cap.tapesp.4: An unnumbered tape. One recording: the silence of the room. You can hear the lift hum behind the wall, a bed creak, someone sigh. On the box: The house as it is. To remember later.
city.cap.tapesp.title: Ilmar's tapes
city.cap.top.d: From the top bridge half the town shows: roofs, chimneys, a grey strip at the edge, probably the sea. The wind roams between the tower's cores.
city.cap.top.fog: Fog lies below the bridge: the tower sticks out of it like a mast out of milk.
city.cap.top.n: At night the town below is a scatter of windows. The dark far off is the sea: it doesn't glow.
city.cap.top.rain: Up here the rain comes sideways. The rails are cold and wet, and my cap grows heavy at once.
city.cap.top.snow: Snow flies past sideways. On the rail it stays; on my palm it melts at once.
city.cap.umb.1: Three umbrellas in the stand: a black one, a checked one and a tiny one with a duckling.
city.cap.umb.2: Someone's umbrella has stood here so long that a note is pinned to it: Take it if it rains.
city.cap.umb.rain: The umbrellas are wet and drip into a tin tray. One stands open, drying with its handle up.
city.cap.umb.snow: Melted snow runs off the umbrellas. Good that there is a tray under them.
city.clock.2: The clock shows {time}. The second hand twitches as if it had somewhere to be.
city.clock.3: {time}. The clock ticks louder than you'd expect from something so small.
city.clock.4: The dial says {time}. A dried fly under the glass: it must have wanted the time too.
city.closed.cafe.bar: The bar is empty, the coffee machine under a towel. A note on the till: "Open at eight."
city.closed.cafe.chairs: The chairs are up on the tables, legs in the air. The floor is still damp from the mop.
city.closed.cafe.machine: The plug is pulled and hung neatly on a hook. The music is asleep.
city.closed.club.counter: The window is latched shut. A card on the glass: "Closed till tomorrow."
city.closed.club.screen: The screen is behind its velvet curtain. The next show is tomorrow.
city.closed.club.seats: The hall is empty, the seats folded up. It smells of curtain dust and, faintly, of tangerines.
city.closed.cog.games: Everything is under covers, the balls and pieces locked away in the cupboard.
city.closed.cog.seats: The chairs are pushed under the tables in neat rows. Someone left a scarf on one.
city.closed.library.desk: The lamp on the lending desk is out, the date stamp put away in the drawer. Waiting for morning.
city.closed.library.shelf: A cord with a card is strung across the shelf: "The library is closed. The books are asleep too."
city.closed.market.stall: The stall is under a tarpaulin weighed down with a brick. The scales went home.
city.closed.store.counter: The department is closed. The display case is under grey cloth with a card: "Stocktaking."
city.cm.boardA.1: Notice: on Wednesday at 19:00 the house committee meets in the hall. Agenda: 1) the leak from 3-05 into 1-05, 2) the kettle in the hall, 3) any other business. There will be tea.
city.cm.boardA.2: Added by hand: "In 1-05 it drips from the ceiling onto the piano. The piano is in tune, the ceiling is not. Please take measures. The neighbours below."
city.cm.boardA.3: Reply: "Nobody in 3-05 poured anything. It is condensation. The residents of 3-05." Below, in another hand: "Condensation does not come with soap suds."
city.cm.boardA.4: Minutes of the meeting: the commission went up to 3-05 with a basin. Established: the bath tap was shut, but not all the way, and the sink drain was shut all the way, but not where it should be. The parties made peace over tea.
city.cm.boardA.5: The committee reports: the tap in 3-05 has been replaced and the stain on the ceiling in 1-05 whitewashed. The person on duty drew a small cloud on the whitewash with her palm: "Let it stay as a keepsake." Thanks to all.
city.cm.boardA.6: Notice: on Saturday at 19:00, a joint evening at the television. A film about sailors will be shown. Bring your own chairs: we have very few.
city.cm.boardA.7: The committee's note: "On Saturday please do not talk, do not rattle the chairs and do not comment on the sailors. Latecomers stand by the wall. The little cloud on the ceiling may be viewed after the film."
city.cm.boardB.1: A cat is missing. Grey, with a white shirt-front, answers to "Markiz" and to the sound of a tin being opened. Last seen in the hall near the kitchen. If you find him, don't feed him, call flat 3-07: he is on a diet.
city.cm.boardB.2: Markiz has been seen: 1) in the cellar, Lidiya is sure; 2) on the roof, the boy from 3-07 is not sure; 3) in the canteen by the fish-soup pot, the cook is upset. Three versions, one cat.
city.cm.boardB.3: Added: "If Markiz is not back by Thursday, he has gone to the fishermen. Don't be cross with the cat: he has taste."
city.cm.boardB.4: A girl from 1-03 brought a drawing: a cat in a fur hat and a sign "I'm not lost, I'm out for a walk." The committee accepted the drawing and hung it up. The search goes on.
city.cm.boardB.5: The committee is glad to announce: Markiz the cat has been found! He was asleep in the laundry basket by the folding table, on somebody's sailor vest. The vest is in the lost-property box; let its owner collect it.
city.cm.boardB.6: Notice: on Saturday at 19:00, a joint evening at the television, a film about sailors. Markiz the cat is invited; his place is on the committee's bench. Bring your own chairs.
city.cm.boardB.7: The committee's note: "Please don't talk, rattle the chairs or wake Markiz during the finale. He watches the sailors more closely than anyone."
city.cm.book.1: The complaints and suggestions book, first page: "Please bring the raisins back into the compote. Flat 3-02." The cook's reply in pen: "The raisins boiled down. They are in there, only in a scattered form."
city.cm.book.2: "The cutlets are good. But the cook sings too loudly at the serving line, and his voice, forgive me, is better than the cutlets. Flat 1-06." Reply: "Thank you. I'll sing quieter. I make no promise for the cutlets, they are quiet enough."
city.cm.book.3: "I suggest pancakes on Saturdays. Lyova, flat 3-07, aged 11." Beside it in blue ink: "We support it! The whole third staircase." The cook: "Pancakes will come when somebody gives me a bigger pan."
city.cm.book.4: "Thanks to the cook for Thursday's fish soup: after it, life gets better. Pyotr Semyonovich and the chess section." The cook added: "Passed your regards to the fishermen."
city.cm.bread.1: The bread is still warm, cut in thick slices. In chalk above the tray: "Help yourself. We count only the crumbs." I took a loaf and left, feeling rich.
city.cm.bread.2: By evening the tray holds half a loaf and a note: "Bread is free, but you won't carry all of it off. One loaf each." I carried off one, as asked.
city.cm.bread.3: The tray is covered with a towel: the bread sleeps until breakfast.
city.cm.bread.prompt: E — take bread from the tray
city.cm.charter.1: CHARTER OF THE COMMUNE HOUSE. Adopted by the general meeting, copied out by hand on a second sheet. §1. The house is shared, the slippers are personal.
city.cm.charter.2: §2. The hall is open to residents and guests. Guests must say hello; residents must not ask "who are you visiting?" twice.
city.cm.charter.3: §3. Laundry by sign-up. Nobody scolds the queue; the queue is shared. Machine No. 3 hums, and that is no reason to pity it.
city.cm.charter.4: §4. The kettle is common. Whoever drinks the last of the hot water fills a new one. Whoever does not know how asks the samovar, and the samovar answers in steam.
city.cm.charter.5: §5. In the hall people play, sing, read and argue, but not all at once. Exception: Saturday, 19:00, the television.
city.cm.charter.6: Amendment to §5, brought on Wednesday: "A chess draw 'on account of age' counts only for games older than forty minutes." Passed by seventeen votes with one abstention (Pyotr Semyonovich, on account of age).
city.cm.charter.7: Amendment to §1: "Slippers are permitted in the hall, but not on the tables." Signed: Lyova, flat 3-07, for the children's section. Beside it: "Adopted without a vote, because it's funny."
city.cm.charter.8: At the bottom an empty space and a pencil on a string: "Residents wishing to propose an amendment sit on this bench and think aloud. A signature is required. Tea afterwards."
city.cm.chess.1: In the morning the board is taken: Pyotr Semyonovich plays white against Uncle Gena from the third floor, both in slippers. I sat opposite the winner. The game was long and ended in a draw "on account of age".
city.cm.chess.2: In the afternoon Pyotr Semyonovich sits alone at the board, playing himself. "When there is no opponent, one must be honest on both sides," he said, and slid the black pieces to me. I lost with dignity.
city.cm.chess.3: Towards evening spectators gather at the board: all of them know how one ought to move, none of them knows how to play. I was advised from three sides and made a fourth move, my own. I lost beautifully.
city.cm.chess.4: At night the main light is put out and only the lamp over the chess table stays on. We don't finish the game: we set the clock to "till morning". The pieces won't go anywhere.
city.cm.chess.prompt: E — sit down with the chess players
city.cm.closed.bread: The bread tray is empty and covered with a towel. There will be bread by breakfast.
city.cm.closed.counter: The serving line is shut: the pans are covered with towels, and on the door in chalk: "Breakfast from 8:00, supper until 19:00. On Sundays the cook rests."
city.cm.closed.machine: The samovar's tap is tied with a rag: after ten the hot water sleeps, like the whole house.
city.cm.coll.title: Corners of the house
city.cm.diary.1: The readers' notebook of the nook. On the cover: "Took a book, write it down. Returned it, cross it out. Didn't return it, Lidiya Arkadyevna will find you, and that is not a threat but a schedule." The first entry: "Taken: Treasure Island. Lyova, flat 3-07. Will return on Friday."
city.cm.diary.2: Treasure Island, Lyova: crossed out. Beside it in pencil: "Returned on time, with a bookmark at page 112. The bookmark is a sleeve pattern." A new entry right there: "Taken: Treasure Island. Uncle Gena, flat 3-02. I want to check how they do for fish."
city.cm.diary.3: Uncle Gena returned the book and wrote in the notebook's margin: "There is no fish there. But there is a parrot, and he gives orders louder than our house committee." Below: "Taken: Treasure Island. Lidiya Arkadyevna, flat 1-03. I will check whether it is really that frightening."
city.cm.diary.4: Lidiya Arkadyevna returned the book on the second day: "Read it without stopping. Put the door on the chain at night. Recommended to everyone who is afraid only of queues." Under her signature in a child's hand: "I'm not afraid. L."
city.cm.diary.5: A new entry in a tidy hand, like a top pupil's: "Taken: Treasure Island. Pyotr Semyonovich, flat 1-06. Reading it for the fourth time, but every time as if for the first. Chess can wait until the last chapter."
city.cm.diary.6: A note on a loose sheet: "The book is worn out. Sent for repair to the mending corner, by the sewing machine. Lyova is gluing the cover and asks not to be disturbed." I confirm: it smells of glue and sea by the machine.
city.cm.diary.7: The book is back in a new cover of blue cloth. On the spine Lyova wrote: "TREASURE ISLAND, repaired once, read by 5 people." The notebook records: in a week the house has gained five more dreamers.
city.cm.diary.8: The last entry has no handwriting yet. Only a line: "Taken: Treasure Island. ______________. Will return on Friday." The pencil on its string is waiting.
city.cm.dom.1: In the morning the dominoes table is empty, the tiles only lined up in two rows: the game was put off until evening. I shuffled them the proper way and sat down to wait for an opponent.
city.cm.dom.2: In the afternoon they play for a stake: the loser pours tea for everyone. The tiles click as if somebody were cracking nuts.
city.cm.dom.3: In the evening the chairs stand in two rows round the table: the spectators. "Double six!" somebody shouts by the wall, and everyone pretends not to have jumped.
city.cm.dom.rain: In the rain they play with extra zeal: water roars outside, tiles click in the hall, and the house seems to be sailing, and we are playing in the crew's quarters.
city.cm.duty.extra: A note in red pencil: "We are preparing a general clean for the clean-up day. Wash the hall windows only from the inside. Outside, they are washed by those not afraid of heights: Lidiya Arkadyevna and the wind."
city.cm.duty.fri: Friday, flat 1-08: get the hall ready for the weekend, wipe the board by the door, take forgotten mittens to the lost-property box.
city.cm.duty.mon: The hall duty rota. Monday, flat 1-03: sweep, wipe the tables, check the water heater. Signed: "Lidiya Arkadyevna. Already swept, already checked."
city.cm.duty.sat: Saturday. The general clean-up at 10:00: buckets and rags by the kitchen. Whoever is on duty is in command; the rest obey at least until lunch.
city.cm.duty.sun: Sunday, the hall rests, nobody is on duty. The rule from the wall: "Whoever made the mess cleans it up. Whoever didn't, take a rag anyway if one is near."
city.cm.duty.thu: Thursday, flat 3-02: fish day, air the hall before lunch and after. A note: "Twice. I am not joking."
city.cm.duty.tue: Tuesday, flat 3-06: the hall, the windows, the flowers. Water the flowers from a kettle, but not the one people drink from. The signature is a child's, with a tail on the letter D.
city.cm.duty.wed: Wednesday, flat 1-07: take out the paper, fold the chairs after the committee meeting. Count the chairs by heads and by legs.
city.cm.fold.1: I fold somebody's sheets: two corners in one hand, two in the other, as Lidiya Arkadyevna showed me. It comes out as neat as in a shop.
city.cm.fold.2: A striped sleeve sticks out of the basket. I pulled it out: a sailor's vest, a big one, smelling of the sea and laundry soap. I put it back and laid a pillowcase over it like a blanket.
city.cm.fold.3: The folding table creaks on one leg. I put a folded newspaper under it. Now it creaks on two, but in a different key.
city.cm.gymtt.1: The "Health" section. Monday and Wednesday, 19:00: exercises for all who make it. Led by Zinaida Pavlovna; she has one whistle for everybody.
city.cm.gymtt.2: Tuesday and Thursday, 18:00: parallel bars and pull-ups for schoolchildren. Pencilled underneath: "Whoever can't pull up will explain why afterwards."
city.cm.gymtt.3: Friday and Sunday: the gym is free. One mat, one wall of bars, a shared conscience.
city.cm.gymtt.4: Saturday, 9:00: the pensioners. Gently, no jerking, tea afterwards. Everyone else, do not disturb until ten.
city.cm.honour.1: A frame on a nail with a sheet of exercise-book paper: "A good resident is one who knows his house: chess, television, sewing machine, tea, laundry, dominoes, notebook, bread. Come, sit a while and we will note it down." No ticks yet.
city.cm.honour.2: Three ticks on the sheet, put by another hand, the hand of Lidiya Arkadyevna, who sees everything. "Knows the house on a C grade," is added. "But no longer a guest."
city.cm.honour.3: Six ticks out of eight. Lidiya Arkadyevna added: "Not much left. If you get stuck, look for where the samovar is, where the notebook is, where the bread is." That is not a hint, only an address.
city.cm.honour.4: All eight! At the bottom in red ink: "Resident for one evening. Signed: the general meeting, unanimously, Pyotr Semyonovich abstained." Your own mug now hangs by the samovar too.
city.cm.kids.1: Children's drawings: a house on legs, big, with a red roof. From every window somebody looks out with a cup. The caption: "Us." Lyova, aged 11.
city.cm.kids.2: The second drawing: the hall and a samovar as huge as a lighthouse. Little people in hats stand around it. The caption: "We drink tea. The tea never runs out."
city.cm.kids.3: A very small sheet: a cat in a fur hat. The caption "Markis", with one letter turned the wrong way.
city.cm.kids.4: A charcoal drawing: a cable car over the sea, three gulls and one person in the cabin. The person is waving. The gulls look dignified.
city.cm.lostA.1: The lost-property box. On top: one red-striped mitten, a scarf with no owner, a child's galosh for the right foot and a tag "Lyova, 3-07". Let him collect it. We'll wait for the second mitten.
city.cm.lostA.2: A blue basin has appeared in the box with a tag "from 3-05". Added: "The basin walked about the floors until it found the way down. Its owner asks forgiveness and wants it back."
city.cm.lostA.3: The basin has been returned. In its place a jar of cherry jam, on the lid: "For the ceiling." A jar is not lost property, but it was put in the box for the kindest of reasons. Let it stand.
city.cm.lostB.1: The lost-property box: one mitten, an umbrella without spokes and a collar with a tag "Markiz, flat 3-07". The collar is empty. That is worrying.
city.cm.lostB.2: A note lies by the collar: "Found in the laundry basket by the table, asleep on a sailor's vest." The vest itself is next to it: big, striped, smelling of the sea and a little of cat.
city.cm.lostB.3: The vest was collected by its owner from 1-04, a retired sailor. In its place sits Markiz the cat, looking at everyone like a commission. A note on the box: "A cat is not lost property. But let him sit."
city.cm.menu.fri: Friday. Pea soup, sausages with cabbage, compote. "On Fridays the cook promises pies. If he doesn't forget."
city.cm.menu.mon: Monday. Cabbage soup with sour cream, meatballs with buckwheat, stewed-fruit compote. In chalk underneath: "Bread is free, seconds by conscience."
city.cm.menu.sat: Saturday, short menu: the soup of the day, a pie, tea. We close at 19:00, as always, and not a minute later.
city.cm.menu.sun: Sunday. The canteen is closed. Hot water is in the hall, at the samovar, free. Come on Monday, hungry.
city.cm.menu.thu: Thursday is fish day. Fish soup, hake with potatoes, fruit jelly. Added by hand: "Open the windows early! This is not a joke."
city.cm.menu.tue: Tuesday. Borscht, navy-style pasta, fruit jelly. Added by hand: "Borscht on Tuesdays is a law, not a wish."
city.cm.menu.wed: Wednesday. Pickle soup, a chicken leg with rice, tea with lemon. "One slice of lemon per person. We are counting."
city.cm.menu2.1: Breakfast 8 to 11: porridge (semolina or millet, as luck has it), a cheese sandwich, tea. Bread is on the tray; no need to count it.
city.cm.menu2.2: Lunch 11 to 15: the set meal. Soup, a main, compote. Take a tray on the left, walk along the line; the cook will say what's gone.
city.cm.menu2.3: Supper 15 to 19: a bake, a pie, kefir. Whoever comes five minutes before closing gets what is left, and a smile.
city.cm.menu2.4: Closed. Breakfast from 8:00. In pencil at the bottom: "The cook is a person too. The kettle is in the hall, don't knock."
city.cm.menu2.5: Today is Sunday and the canteen rests. The cook left a note on Saturday: "Pots washed, spoons counted, see you Monday."
city.cm.news.1: The wall newspaper "Our House". "The month in numbers: 16 flats, 41 residents, 1 chess section and 0 quiet evenings. The editors consider this a success."
city.cm.news.2: The column "Our Talents": Lyova from 3-07 drew a house on legs, just like ours, only with paws. The drawing hangs in the hall by the window.
city.cm.news.3: The sports column: pull-ups in the hall. Lidiya Arkadyevna, 14 times, on a bet with her grandson. The grandson counted aloud but lost count out of respect.
city.cm.news.4: Poems by residents. "Our house is long as a station hall, / with soup in it, and chess, and all, / and a row of washers in a line, / and water for tea, boiling fine." Flat 1-04, an amateur poet.
city.cm.news.5: The editors ask residents to hand in notes about the television evening: how we sat, what we argued about, who fell asleep first. The winner gets a seat in the front row.
city.cm.pull.1: On the board in chalk: "Pull-ups. House record: L. A. — 14." Beside it a drawn bar and a little man with a very pleased face.
city.cm.pull.2: A new line: "Lyova (3-07): 3." Below: "L. A. advises starting with one. L. A. started with one herself. In her youth."
city.cm.pull.3: "Lyova: 5." Somebody rubbed out the five and wrote "6", then rubbed out the six and wrote "5 and a half". Honesty in this house is at a great height.
city.cm.pull.4: "Pyotr Semyonovich: 1, but solemnly." A note: "All chess players present. They applauded sitting down."
city.cm.pull.5: At the bottom a new line: "Your record?" Chalk and a rag beside it. The bar by the wall is waiting.
city.cm.queue.1: The laundry list. Mon, Wed, Fri: floors one and two. 1) flat 1-02, "everything"; 2) flat 1-05, pillowcases; 3) flat 1-07, said he'd come, but he need not be believed.
city.cm.queue.2: Tue, Thu: floors three and four. 1) flat 3-04, towels; 2) flat 3-06, children's things, urgent; 3) flat 3-01, curtains. At the bottom: "Machine No. 3 hums. That is normal."
city.cm.queue.3: Sat, Sun: whoever gets there first. The sheet hangs, the pen is on a string, the string is chewed through. Sign up by word of mouth, and we'll remember together.
city.cm.sam.1: The samovar has been warm since the morning. I poured hot water from the tap into a mug and blew on it. The mug is on a chain, burnt into it: "COMMON".
city.cm.sam.2: The hot water in the hall stays hot all day; the person on duty sees to it. The tea leaves are in a tin "for everyone". Thank you, tin.
city.cm.sam.3: The samovar has cooled. On the tap, a note: "It is not necessary to wake the person on duty, but you may."
city.cm.sam.mug: On a chain beside the mug marked "COMMON" hangs a second, smaller one with the word "GUEST" burned into it. I poured into that one. The same taste, but nicer.
city.cm.sew.1: A treadle machine, black, with a golden beast on its side. I hemmed trousers: straight at first, then crooked, then I unpicked it and did it again. The trousers agree to be shorter.
city.cm.sew.2: I stitch a torn edge of a curtain. A note on the basket: "From 3-01, urgent." Now the curtain will have a seam and a story.
city.cm.sew.3: Beside it a biscuit tin: buttons of every size, one golden with an anchor. On the lid: "Take what fits. Lidiya Arkadyevna."
city.cm.text.charter.title: Charter of the commune house
city.cm.text.diary.title: The readers' notebook
city.cm.today.cold: In chalk at the bottom, in a shivering hand: "Frost. Tea at the samovar is free until it runs out. One can warm up with chess too."
city.cm.today.fri: "TODAY IN THE HALL." Friday: 16:00 exercises for those who still remember how it is done. 19:00 games evening: dominoes, draughts, chess, tea. Winners wash the cups.
city.cm.today.mon: "TODAY IN THE HALL." Monday: 18:00 the chess section (Pyotr Semyonovich plays white, the rest as it comes), 19:30 tea for the losers.
city.cm.today.prompt: E — read the chalk on the board
city.cm.today.rain: In chalk at the bottom, because of the rain: "Umbrellas in the corner by the door, not on the tables. Whoever brought the puddles wipes them up."
city.cm.today.sat: "TODAY IN THE HALL." Saturday: 10:00 the clean-up, buckets by the kitchen. 19:00 the whole house at the television. Bring your own chairs.
city.cm.today.sun: "TODAY IN THE HALL." Sunday: the canteen rests, but the samovar, the dominoes and the readers' notebook are at work. Come with nothing to do: that is also something to do.
city.cm.today.thu: "TODAY IN THE HALL." Fish day, the windows have been open since morning. 18:00 a lecture, "What hake is and why it doesn't take offence", by the cook. Admission free, the smell too.
city.cm.today.tue: "TODAY IN THE HALL." Tuesday: 17:00 the children's drawing circle, low chairs, shared paints, aprons by the door. 19:00 quiet hour for adults, that is, chess without comments.
city.cm.today.warm: In chalk at the bottom: "Hot. Open the windows, the kefir is in the fridge, the samovar is only for the brave today."
city.cm.today.wed: "TODAY IN THE HALL." Wednesday: 19:00 house committee, the agenda is on the door. After the meeting count the chairs by heads and by legs.
city.cm.tv.1: Morning exercises. The presenter in a blue leotard counts: "And one, and two..." and the whole hall, without standing up, raises its right arm. Someone by the wall has already breathed in on "three".
city.cm.tv.2: A school broadcast: geography, the Baltic. A map, a pointer, a sea the colour of overcast. The announcer says: "This is where we live." And so we do.
city.cm.tv.3: "The Film Travellers' Club": the host in a scarf walks across a desert and complains of the heat. The hall sympathises, though outside there is a wind from the sea.
city.cm.tv.4: An interval. On the screen a striped test card and a soft tune. Nobody switches over: there are only two channels, and both are on a break.
city.cm.tv.5: A cartoon: a hare and a bear swap hats. The children go quiet. The grown-ups pretend to look out of the window, but they are watching too.
city.cm.tv.6: The news. The announcer reads sternly about the harvest and the Baltic fishermen. Then the weather: "North-westerly wind, sea state three." The hall nods as if it were about their own walk.
city.cm.tv.7: The evening film: black and white, about sailors and letters. The plot is clear from the third minute, and still everyone waits for the end.
city.cm.tv.8: Saturday, the television evening. The hall is full: chairs carried down from the flats, latecomers standing along the wall. Lidiya Arkadyevna comments under her breath, Pyotr Semyonovich "is not asleep, he is thinking". When the heroes embrace, somebody sighs loudly. This is what the television in the hall is for.
city.cm.tv.9: The screen is grey and hissing, a test card in the middle. The announcer said good night at eleven. The television does not sleep, but the hall must, and somebody switched it off with a click.
city.cm.wash.1: I loaded the washing and pulled the lever. The machine sighed, took in water and began to rattle like a small tractor. On the stool beside it, somebody's dry shirt waits for its turn.
city.cm.wash.2: While it washes I watch the little window: a striped shirt, my vest, a stripe again. A strange machine: it gives back exactly what it took, and a bit of soapy air.
city.cm.wash.3: Evening wash. The hall smells of washing powder and soup at the same time. Someone at the next machine is quietly counting socks, and seems to be losing.
city.cm.wash.4: At night the drum thunders through the whole house, so I left the washing to soak in a basin. I'll fetch it in the morning. Above the machines, a sheet: "The committee is asleep."
city.cog.bench.boat.1: Today we cut. Lev Arkadyevich laid a sheet of plywood on the bench and pencilled the frames on it. I cut three with the fretsaw. The fourth came out with character. Tomorrow we glue.
city.cog.bench.boat.2: Today we glue. The frames stand on the keel like a fish's ribs. I spread glue on the joints and clamped them with clothes-pegs. The glue smells of apples, which is odd. Now it dries until tomorrow.
city.cog.bench.boat.3: Today we paint. The hull is skinned in veneer and smooth as a pebble. Red below, white deck, blue wheelhouse. Paint up to my elbows. Lev Arkadyevich said that is the first sign of a good model-maker.
city.cog.bench.boat.prompt: E — work on the model launch
city.cog.bench.glider.1: Glider: today the ribs. Thin as kindling. I broke one and cut a new one. Lev Arkadyevich believes a glider loves the patient.
city.cog.bench.glider.2: Glider: today we cover the wing in tissue paper. Glue on every rib, paper without a single wrinkle. A wrinkle, they say, is an air pocket.
city.cog.bench.glider.3: Glider: today we spray the paper with water so it tightens. I watch it dry and breathe, and I know nothing duller or more fascinating.
city.cog.bench.glider.4: Glider: test day. We launched it from the stair landing into the foyer. It made a circle and landed on a bench. The cloakroom attendant, without getting up, gave it a "good".
city.cog.bench.glider.prompt: E — work on the glider's wing
city.cog.bil.1: On Tuesday and Thursday evenings the table belongs to the juniors' section: five of them walk round it counting angles. I was let in last. I learned that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection even when the ball doesn't want it to.
city.cog.bil.2: Friday evenings the league plays: men from the shipyard with their sleeves rolled up. The loser buys tea from the buffet. They poured me one for nothing: witnesses, they say, always get tea.
city.cog.bil.3: On Saturday they play in pairs, two against two, and all four argue over whose ball it was. I stood aside with a cue feeling like a referee. Nobody asked me once.
city.cog.bil.4: Sunday afternoon at the table: fathers with their children. The children stretch on tiptoe, the fathers pretend to miss. I potted two and was a little proud.
city.cog.bil.5: The league final is near. The cushions have been wiped to a shine and the table looks solemn, as before an oath.
city.cog.board.1: Thursday: a blitz grid on the board, eight names and empty squares. In the corner I wrote "guest", small, so it can be rubbed out.
city.cog.board.2: On Monday the board is clean, just a cloud-shaped smear from the rag in the corner. I drew rain under the cloud and stepped away before anyone noticed.
city.cog.board.3: In the evening there's a glider wing drawn on the board with its dimensions. One of the club members has corrected a figure and written: "Tested in a draught."
city.cog.board.4: For the holiday someone has written on the board in coloured chalk: "Happy holiday, everyone! Tea in the buffet from six." The words "tea" and "six" are traced over twice.
city.cog.cart.1: The returns trolley: the books lie with their spines every which way, and you can tell who read what. On top, "Chess for Beginners" with a bookmark at page forty-one. He clearly got no further.
city.cog.cart.2: On Monday the trolley is full: after the weekend everyone returned everything at once. Tamara Ilyinichna sorts without lifting her head or losing count.
city.cog.cart.3: By the weekend the trolley is nearly empty: readers take books away and bring them back later, on Monday. A law of nature.
city.cog.cart.4: In the pile, someone's note: "I didn't take the clock, I only took 'Photography for Amateurs'." On that book's spine, the photo circle's stamp.
city.cog.catalogue.1: The catalogue drawers are labelled by hand: "Club History", "The Town", "Sea and Harbour". In the morning they smell of varnish: they were polished yesterday.
city.cog.catalogue.2: At weekends pensioners queue at the catalogue: each is looking for a photograph of himself young. They find it, and argue about who's standing next to them.
city.cog.catalogue.3: One card is filled in a child's hand: "The club. Built. Very big." The librarian didn't throw it away and put it right at the front.
city.cog.chess.1: We played on the hourglass from the first-aid room. The sand runs as it pleases. They said it's an ancient method: whoever is faster, the sand is theirs.
city.cog.chess.2: Thursday evening is blitz at the tables. At each, two play and one watches with an opinion. The opinion is louder than the chess.
city.cog.chess.3: Today they play more quietly than usual. Someone is listening for a chess clock to tick somewhere. None does.
city.cog.chess.4: A game with the clock: the left dial cracked, the right whole, both ticking a bit faster than you'd like. I won on time but not on position. They say that counts too.
city.cog.chess.5: A five-minute blitz: the pieces fly, the hand can't keep up with the thought nor the thought with the hand. I lost on the last second and smiled. Tamara Ilyinichna wrote in the log: "Clock in place."
city.cog.clock.1: A chess clock with two dials. The left one has a crack like a lightning bolt. It is ticking. It turns out they use it as a stopwatch: press, the exposure runs, press again, stop.
city.cog.clock.2: Under the clock a note: "Borrowed for a while, will return Thursday. S. G." "Thursday" is crossed out and another Thursday written. Then another.
city.cog.clock.3: The clock ticks as before, but a little sheepishly. Seryozha said he would have taken it back himself but was ashamed, and asked: "Maybe you could carry it? They won't scold you." I thought I would.
city.cog.clock.prompt: E — look at the clock on the bench
city.cog.cues.1: The cues stand by height and by temper. The first was too light. The second was too proud. The third, worn at the tip like an old friend, turned out to be mine.
city.cog.cues.2: On the rail there is a tin of chalk. I chalked the cue and blew on the tip the way the older ones do. At once I felt part of the league.
city.cog.cues.3: At weekends the duty member hands out the cues: "One cue, one person. No waving." I didn't wave.
city.cog.dance.1: Saturday dance night. The accordion player is on the same tango for the third time, because the couples won't leave the floor.
city.cog.dance.2: In the daytime the stage is empty, the floor freshly waxed. I waltzed across it counting aloud, and the echo counted with me.
city.cog.dance.3: New Year's evening: streamers under the ceiling, a fir tree by the stage, and everyone dancing in paper hats. Someone put a hat on me too without asking.
city.cog.dance.4: A woman from the choir took my hand: "Don't worry, I'll lead." And she did. For the first time I didn't tread on anybody's foot.
city.cog.dark.1: Today, negatives. We wind the film in total darkness, by touch, counting in whispers. Seryozha says the dark is where he manages best to stay calm.
city.cog.dark.2: Today, contact sheets: all the frames on one sheet, small as stamps. We choose one. I chose the lighthouse frame; it was the only one not blurred.
city.cog.dark.3: Today, printing. The sheet under the enlarger, red light. We count the exposure on the clock on the second bench: click the left button, click the right; at twelve we lift the frame.
city.cog.dark.4: Today, drying. The prints hang on the line and drip, and it smells of vinegar. Someone is already arguing whether gloss or matt is better.
city.cog.dark.prompt: E — work in the photo lab
city.cog.draft.1: On the drafting board is a drawing: a cable-car lift at 1:20. The angle of the cable is written twice, the second time in red with a question mark.
city.cog.draft.2: A note in the margin: "Seryozha from the photo circle's idea: a mirror in the cabin so passengers see the sea from both sides." Lev Arkadyevich disagreed and agreed.
city.cog.draft.3: A new sheet: "Cabin, model 1:20." The window is cut round, like a porthole. They argued whether it needs a wheel. Those for the wheel won.
city.cog.dry.1: Two finished little boats dry side by side. One has its red side to the very edge, on the other the paint has run a little onto the deck. A card: "Paint takes a day to dry. A day, not five minutes." Underlined twice.
city.cog.dry.2: The little boats on the shelf are dry now and stand upright. A note: "Collect by Sunday or they go to the club fund." Whether anyone will is unknown.
city.cog.dry.3: The shelf is taken up by paint tins: red, white, blue, all open and covered with gauze. It smells like a small harbour.
city.cog.league.1: The Cog Club billiards league: a table in chalk. The top three places belong to the shipyard, fourth to "Unknown", and fifth is a bottle of kefir someone put there for tidiness.
city.cog.league.2: Under the table: "Semi-final on Friday evening. Spectators, please don't stand by the pockets: the pockets get nervous."
city.cog.league.3: The semi-final has been played: a fitter from the shipyard won 3-2 on the last ball. The loser bought tea for everyone, and twice for the witnesses.
city.cog.league.4: "Final on Saturday evening. Spectators sign up with Tamara Ilyinichna. The more people, the quieter they play."
city.cog.league.5: The final has been played. The cup, a bent cog on a stand, sits by the buffet. The winner forgot about it and came back an hour later.
city.cog.lounge.1: "Please do not screw either players or attachments to the table football. Players especially."
city.cog.lounge.2: The machine takes only five-rouble coins and angrily gives back everything else. If anyone knows why, please share.
city.cog.lounge.3: In the photo lab in the evenings something ticks, as if a chess game were being played with nobody there. Anyone in the know, tell Tamara Ilyinichna.
city.cog.meet.1: Circles' meeting on the first Saturday of the month. Agenda: tea. Additionally: the kettle.
city.cog.meet.2: Minutes of the meeting: the clock is to be fixed to the chess table with a chain, and the photographers are to buy a stopwatch. Signed by all, including the stopwatch, which does not exist.
city.cog.models.1: On the stand is yesterday's launch: painted, shining, drying. Next to it a pencilled card: "Don't touch, sticky."
city.cog.models.2: The shelf is almost empty: the launch has gone to the bench, leaving its drawing and an empty stand.
city.cog.models.3: On the stand the launch is unpainted, pale, smelling of pine and glue. Today it gets painted, and tomorrow it will be red.
city.cog.models.4: Next to the launch stands a glider covered in russet paper. On its wing: "Flew. Came back by itself."
city.cog.piano.1: In the morning the piano in the hall is cold, the keys like ice. The first chords come out cautiously, as if the instrument hasn't woken yet.
city.cog.piano.2: Wednesday, choir practice. I managed one scale before the choir leader asked me to free the instrument. Politely, but in a way that has you up at once.
city.cog.piano.3: Playing is easier with rain drumming on the roof: the mistakes drown. I played the whole waltz and only slipped once.
city.cog.piano.4: Under the piano lid lies a forgotten music book. On the cover, in a child's hand: "Studies. Not for everyone."
city.cog.place.1: On the cloth by the board there is a pale rectangle where the clock stood and a slip: "The clock stood here." For now it's empty.
city.cog.place.2: I pictured the cracked clock coming back to the pale rectangle. For now its only home is the photographers' bench, where it counts the seconds of other people's pictures.
city.cog.place.3: I set the clock on the pale rectangle and the cloth under it seemed to sigh. Tamara Ilyinichna, without getting up, wrote in the log: "Clock in place." There will be a blitz on Thursday.
city.cog.place.prompt: E — look at the clock's place
city.cog.prints.1: A strip of film hangs on the line with wet frames, like a tiny movie. The frames are dark, the faces light: it's always like that with negatives.
city.cog.prints.2: On the line hangs a contact sheet: thirty-six frames in rows. The best are ringed in red. One is ringed three times.
city.cog.prints.3: A large print on the line, still wet: a lighthouse, a dune, a girl with a string bag. The edges curl like pages in a damp book.
city.cog.prints.4: The print has dried and flattened. A pencilled caption: "Dune, six in the evening. S. Gusev." Next to it an empty space for the next one.
city.cog.prints.prompt: E — look at the line of prints
city.cog.rd.1: Tamara Ilyinichna: there is no chess clock in the reading room, we looked under the cupboards. We found a button. The button is waiting for its owner at the cloakroom.
city.cog.rd.2: "The clock is loud: it ticks like a grasshopper. If you've heard a grasshopper in the club, please report to the cloakroom before 7 p.m."
city.cog.rd.3: The Thursday blitz is back on! Sign up with Tamara Ilyinichna. We play on any clock that ticks. Not the hourglass, though.
city.cog.reh.1: The rehearsal schedule on squared paper: Tuesday, Thursday, drama circle, 5 p.m. Wednesday, dance, 4 p.m. Saturday, amateur evening, 5 p.m. Sunday: "the stage rests."
city.cog.reh.2: Today the drama circle rehearses at 5 p.m. Added: "Latecomers play the trees."
city.cog.reh.3: Today dance at 4 p.m. Added: "Indoor shoes required. Socks are not shoes."
city.cog.reh.4: Tonight, the amateur evening. A hand-lettered poster: "Choir, accordion, verse. Entrance free, exit too."
city.cog.reh.5: Today the stage is free. Added: "If you want to rehearse, sign up with the cloakroom attendant."
city.cog.reh.6: A notice: "On Thursday after the blitz, the prize-giving on stage. The drama circle has promised to present the cup with expression."
city.cog.sh.art.1: An album, "Painting of the Baltic." Under the dunes someone has written: "Went there yesterday. Just the same, only no mosquitoes." You can tell the painting was checked against the shore.
city.cog.sh.art.2: An exhibition catalogue. On the print of the lighthouse there is a tea stain shaped like a small cloud. Tamara Ilyinichna said the stain now counts as part of the display.
city.cog.sh.birds.1: "Birds of the Baltic", the borrower's slip on the last page: "Returned. The gull turned out not to be a gull." The pages about gulls are the most thumbed.
