city.ps.train.4: A date is stamped under the little locomotive: before I was born. The spring still remembers how to run.
city.ps.tv.1: In the radio department every television is on the same channel. The announcer speaks out of six sets at once, and in each one he's a slightly different colour.
city.ps.tv.2: In the daytime it's the schools programme, a physics lesson for the eighth grade. Two pensioners stand in front of the screens arguing with the teacher.
city.ps.tv.3: At weekends there's a crowd at the televisions: football's on. The salesman gave up trying to sell anything long ago and watches too, leaning on the till.
city.ps.tv.4: Before New Year the same old film is on every screen, and people watch it standing, in their coats, with string bags of tangerines in their hands.
city.ps.type.1: I put in a sheet and typed: "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog." Every letter is there. I left the sheet in the carriage for the next customer.
city.ps.type.2: The carriage rang at the end of the line and I jumped: I'm used to keys being silent. The test sheet is full of names: "Vasya", "Masha", "We were here".
city.ps.type.3: One letter, the Russian "zh", sticks. The assistant says it isn't a fault but a character. A typewriter with character costs five roubles more.
city.ps.type.4: By evening there's no room left on the test sheet. The salesman put in a new one, and I was first to type on it: "Hello."
city.ps.type.5: On Mondays the typewriter gets oiled: it taps more softly, and the Zh no longer sticks. The salesman seems upset: "It's lost its character."
city.ps.type.6: On the test sheet, among the names, someone has typed: "If you're reading this, you're here too." Below it I typed: "Here."
city.ps.umbstand.base.1: In the stand by the cloakroom: three black umbrellas, one checked, and a walking stick with a rubber tip. Each has a token tied to the handle. All very orderly.
city.ps.umbstand.base.2: The cloakroom attendant says you can tell the weather from the umbrellas: if they stand dry, by evening you'll be borrowing one.
city.ps.umbstand.y1: Among the umbrellas there's a yellow one with a duck-head handle. A tag on the handle reads: "Found. Awaiting owner." The duck looks at me with dignity.
city.ps.umbstand.y2: The yellow umbrella isn't in the stand. On the hook beside it hangs an empty tag, and on it in pencil: "Gone on business."
city.ps.umbstand.y3: A note is pinned to the stand: "The yellow umbrella is at the lost and found, not here. It is busy: waiting for Lidiya Sergeyevna." Signed: the cloakroom attendant.
city.ps.umbstand.y4: The umbrella is back in the stand, wiped clean. Beside it a note: "For Lidiya Sergeyevna. Returned at noon over the radio. Please don't lose it until next Tuesday."
city.ps.window.am.1: Behind the glass a woman stands on a stepladder with pins in her mouth. She is dressing a dummy in a coat and keeps turning it until the folds fall right.
city.ps.window.am.2: A second dummy stands next to her, headless for now, waiting its turn. The window is half empty. The winter things have arrived, the autumn ones haven't been taken away yet.
city.ps.window.am.3: On the window floor, chalk footprints mark where each dummy's foot belongs. The woman checks them the way a dancer checks steps.
city.ps.window.day.1: The window is finished. The dummies, all in the same pose, look out over the passers-by at the square. A small card says modestly: "Display piece. Not for sale."
city.ps.window.day.2: On the inside of the glass chalk marks are left, showing where each foot goes. The dummies' shoes cover them now.
city.ps.window.day.3: One coat is pinned at the back: perfect from the front, a gamble from behind. The window is honest from one side only.
city.ps.window.night.1: The window glows alone. The dummies gaze at the empty square as if they too had something to think over at night.
city.ps.window.night.2: The lamp in the window flickers a little. In that light the dummy's coat looks blue, then grey. In the morning it will be dressed all over again.
city.ps.window.umb: The dummy in the blue coat holds a yellow umbrella with what looks like a duck-head handle. Up close I read the tag: "Duplicate. In case the original goes off to the toy department again."
city.pu.ask.barber.cut.1: "I'll cut it so that your mother says 'you look different' and can't tell why. That is the best haircut."
city.pu.ask.barber.cut.2: "Before a holiday I cut more carefully than usual: holidays get photographed, and photographs last forty years."
city.pu.ask.barber.radio.1: "Our radio catches one station. But it catches it honestly: not one song has slipped past without permission."
city.pu.ask.barber.radio.2: "In the evening they have a request concert. The customers write the requests, and for some reason they play something else entirely."
city.pu.ask.barber.towel.1: "A hot towel is not a luxury, it is five minutes of quiet. Hot, smells of soap, and nobody talks."
city.pu.ask.barber.towel.2: "In a frost you need it twice as much. Come in to warm up, you needn't have a haircut, no one will mind."
city.pu.closed.bakery.1: The bakery is closed: the shelves are empty, yet the air is still warm. On the door: "The bread has all gone. Tomorrow from six."
city.pu.closed.bakery.2: Through the glass: sacks of flour, and a cat asleep on one. She isn't on the staff, but she stays the night.
city.pu.closed.barber.1: The barber's is closed: the mirrors are draped with towels so they can rest. The chairs face the wall.
city.pu.closed.barber.2: A sign: "Haircuts by appointment. Appointments in the morning. In the morning, by appointment."
city.pu.closed.beer.1: The beer bar is closed: mugs upside down, stools lifted, the dartboard waiting. On the door: "Throwing resumes tomorrow."
city.pu.closed.beer.2: A sign: "No kvass, no beer, but news: we open in the daytime."
city.pu.closed.books.1: The bookstall is closed: the crates are pushed together under a tarpaulin. A note on the handle: "Read while we sleep."
city.pu.closed.books.2: Through the glass, the lamp above the armchair: the owner leaves it on in case somebody needs a page at night.
city.pu.closed.cafe.1: The café is closed: chairs on the tables. Through the glass I see the cat on the windowsill. She is on duty.
city.pu.closed.cafe.2: A sign on the door: "Gone for milk. Back with milk."
city.pu.closed.dumplings.1: The dumpling shop is closed: the pots are washed and stand upside down. On the door: "The broth is resting."
city.pu.closed.dumplings.2: A sign in the window: "No more pinching today. Tomorrow from dawn."
city.pu.closed.fish.1: The fish shop is closed. The ice is gone from the window, and the sign on the door reads "The fish are asleep".
city.pu.closed.fish.2: Through the glass: an empty counter and clean scales. In the morning it will smell of the sea again.
city.pu.closed.pasty.1: The pasty shop is closed: the stove is cooling and the oil settling. On the door: "Chebureki sold out, as always, just in time."
city.pu.closed.pasty.2: An empty tray with a napkin in the window. In the morning it will sizzle here again.
city.pu.closed.photo.1: The photo studio is closed. A sample portrait in the window: the man smiles as though somebody promised him they would open soon.
city.pu.closed.photo.2: On the door: "Lights off: developing dreams."
city.pu.closed.rental.1: The rental is shut: the bicycles lean in a row like tired horses. A wheel-shaped fob hangs on the lock.
city.pu.closed.rental.2: A sign: "The boats sleep until eight. The bicycles until nine. The owner by timetable."
city.pu.closed.souvenirs.1: The souvenir shop is closed: the amber is covered with a little scarf like a sleeping bird. The lamp over the window is lit.
city.pu.closed.souvenirs.2: A sign: "All the souvenirs have gone to the sea on holiday. Back at dawn."
city.pu.closed.workshop.1: The workshop is closed. A green lamp burns over the bench: the master never puts it out, so the tools don't get bored.
city.pu.closed.workshop.2: A note on the door: "Gone to mend the world. Opening hours: until it's mended."
city.pu.coll.stamps.title: Seawall stamps
city.pu.pu_bakery_cat.1: A ginger cat sleeps on a flour sack and has gone floury herself. The baker: "She catches no mice. But she makes sure nobody steals."
city.pu.pu_bakery_cat.2: The cat has woken and is looking at the roll in my hand. I hide the roll behind my back. She is not fooled.
city.pu.pu_bakery_cat.3: At night the cat watches the cooling oven: while it is warm, the flour sack will not leave its post.
city.pu.pu_bakery_chat.1: "Still warm. You have to take bread while it breathes: in an hour it's just bread."
city.pu.pu_bakery_chat.2: "The rye is Lyuba's doing, not mine. The starter is seventeen years old, older than the two of us and cleverer."
city.pu.pu_bakery_chat.3: "By evening it's buns that are left. Take some: in the morning they're better than they looked in the evening, and in the evening they're better than you'd think."
city.pu.pu_bakery_chat.4: "On Sundays the baker's off, so it's yesterday's bread. But yesterday's bread is still bread. And the toast is better."
city.pu.pu_bakery_chat.5: "A jam bun is the most honest food in the world: what you see is what you get, plus a bit sticky."
city.pu.pu_bakery_dough.1: The dough is springy and a little alive. You press and it answers. Flour sticks to hands, sleeves, and the nose I scratched for no reason.
city.pu.pu_bakery_dough.2: The baker looked in, shrugged and showed me how to fold. I folded, and the dough visibly became kinder.
city.pu.pu_bakery_dough.3: I made one crooked loaf. They didn't give it to me ("for order's sake") but set it in the common row. I don't know why that pleases me so.
city.pu.pu_bakery_orders.1: The order book lies on the counter. The handwriting is even, like loaves in a row. The pages smell of vanilla.
city.pu.pu_bakery_oven.1: The brick oven breathes heat from a distance. From its door comes a smell that makes the stomach cheerful.
city.pu.pu_bakery_oven.2: The oven is cooling, but the bricks remember the morning. Hold a palm near it and you feel a warm breeze.
city.pu.pu_bakery_stamp.1: The bakery's stamp: an ear of wheat and a round loaf. The print is warm, as if from the oven.
city.pu.pu_bakery_stamp.2: In the morning the bread queue is longer than the stamp queue, but the stamp is quicker.
city.pu.pu_bakery_starter.1: A crock of starter under a cloth and string. It smells of bread that is not yet bread. I add a spoon of flour, and the baker nods as though I had passed an exam.
city.pu.pu_bakery_starter.2: Early in the morning the starter rises and breathes: the bubbles pop with a soft sigh.
city.pu.pu_bakery_starter.3: On Mondays it is fed extra generously: a whole week of bread lies ahead.
city.pu.pu_bakery_today.1: On the sandwich board by the door: "The starter woke at 4:10. First tray at 5:00, rye at 7:00. Poppy buns by nine, if the poppy seeds don't fly off."
city.pu.pu_bakery_today.2: In chalk: "Yesterday the starter was fussy. The baker talked to it for half an hour. It helped. The bread is cheerful today."
city.pu.pu_bakery_today.3: In chalk: "Order: a name-day pie, Thursday. Volunteers needed to roll the dough. Paid in buns."
city.pu.pu_bakery_today.4: In chalk: "The pie is baked! Thanks to those who rolled. The leftover dough goes to the children. Volunteers: come in, the table's free."
city.pu.pu_barber_book.1: The appointment book lies on the counter: time, name, request. Most of the requests say "The usual."
city.pu.pu_barber_bottles.1: On the shelf under the mirror stand flasks: Shipr, Troinoi, Neptune. I opened the Shipr and at once remembered a grandfather's razor, though I have none.
city.pu.pu_barber_bottles.2: Beside it a glass of combs, each in its own pocket. The most worn is labelled: "For the management."
city.pu.pu_barber_chat.1: "Sit down, there is one at the mirror. Read the papers: good news and bad in equal parts, like any queue."
city.pu.pu_barber_chat.2: "It's quiet in the afternoon: everybody thinks a haircut belongs to the morning. You're lucky, sit down, no queue."
city.pu.pu_barber_chat.3: "Come tomorrow. The mirrors are tired today, and the scissors need a rest: they have a past."
city.pu.pu_barber_cologne.1: Psst. Chypre: the smell of being grown up and of somebody's grandfather. The barber: "Cheap, but real."
city.pu.pu_barber_cologne.2: At the weekend people take Chypre away in little bottles: "so as not to repeat ourselves."
city.pu.pu_barber_cologne.3: On a holiday everybody takes cologne, even those with nothing to shave.
city.pu.pu_barber_newspapers.1: Newspapers on the table, with rings of cups on them. The local news page: "The cable car stopped for five minutes; everybody looked at the sea." The barber adds: "Best five minutes of the year."
city.pu.pu_barber_newspapers.2: News: "The bakery has a new sign. The bread is painted a little too rosy. The baker is pleased." The barber: "The bread is said to be offended."
city.pu.pu_barber_newspapers.3: News: "The photo studio has put up a new portrait of the newcomer boy." The barber, without turning: "And his haircut could go straight to an exhibition, if you take my meaning."
city.pu.pu_barber_radio.1: The radio on the shelf softly airs the morning exercise show. The barber hums along with the brisk announcer without lowering his scissors.
city.pu.pu_barber_radio.2: A request concert is on. The announcer reads: "For the girl on the promenade, who knows this is for her." The barber nods as if he knows her.
city.pu.pu_barber_radio.3: A football commentary riding on a wave of hiss. The barber argues with the announcer in a whisper so as not to spoil a customer's haircut.
city.pu.pu_barber_sink.1: The tap hisses and gives a thin warm stream as if reluctantly. The basin is white-flecked with soap, and a forgotten comb lies on the edge.
city.pu.pu_barber_stamp.1: The barber's stamp: a comb and scissors crossed. The print smells of cologne.
city.pu.pu_barber_stamp.2: The barber, without stopping the shave: "Go ahead, go ahead. Just not on a cheek."
city.pu.pu_barber_strop.1: A leather razor strop, worn shiny in the middle. It smells of leather and a little of soap.
city.pu.pu_barber_strop.2: The barber shows how to strop: away from you, smoothly, blade trailing. "Don't hurry. A razor likes not to be rushed." I ran a bare finger along it, felt nothing, but it felt good.
city.pu.pu_barber_towels.1: I lift the lid: a cloud of steam and a smell of soap. The barber: "Don't touch, it burns honestly."
city.pu.pu_barber_towels.2: In frost the steam from the steamer is thick as fog over the mole. The towels have no time to cool.
city.pu.pu_barber_towels.3: In the morning the towels are hot, by evening warm, by night a memory.
city.pu.pu_beer_chat.1: "We open at two, and at two sharp somebody's already waiting. The ones who just need to sit."
city.pu.pu_beer_chat.2: "Evening is league hour. Darts on Tuesdays, dominoes on Thursdays, everybody lies about fish on Fridays. I take notes."
city.pu.pu_beer_chat.3: "After ten it's quieter. I set mugs down softly, the radio lower. Boys after nine get only soda; not my rule, but reasonable."
city.pu.pu_beer_chat.4: "Friday: everybody who held out all day is here now. Look for a free barrel; they're not always where they stood."
city.pu.pu_beer_chat.5: "I've got a rule here: a mug must have time to sweat before it's finished. So take your time, lad."
city.pu.pu_beer_domino_chair.1: A stool at the little table: dominoes here are played as seriously as chess, only with louder knocking.
city.pu.pu_beer_domino_chair.2: I sit at the table: the tiles lie in a stack, waiting for an opponent. The fishermen by the barrels keep a respectful silence.
city.pu.pu_beer_kvass.1: A yellow barrel on wheels. The kvass is rye, dark, a little sour. The bartender: "Cold in a heatwave it's medicine, in a frost it's science."
city.pu.pu_beer_kvass.2: In hot weather kvass is drunk standing and in silence, out of respect for the barrel.
city.pu.pu_beer_kvass.3: In the cold the kvass stands untouched. It does not mind, it is waiting for summer.
city.pu.pu_beer_league.1: In chalk on the blackboard: "Darts league. Tuesday: Beer Bar v. Fish Shop. Score 3:2 to us. The fishermen demand a recheck: the bartender threw."
city.pu.pu_beer_league.2: In chalk: "Wednesday: the recheck. Everybody threw except the bartender. Score 3:3. The bartender pretends that's what he wanted."
city.pu.pu_beer_league.3: In chalk: "Thursday, the final. Saturday: the return match at the fish shop; the target there is cardboard, but honest."
city.pu.pu_beer_league.4: In big chalk letters: "The final is played. Friendship won, and one fisherman's bullseye. Lads may fetch the ball: there's table football in the corner, go on!"
city.pu.pu_beer_radio.1: The radio airs the five o'clock news: "Weather at the sea unchanged. Wind south-westerly." The bartender nods as if it were his doing.
city.pu.pu_beer_radio.2: A football commentary! Everyone has turned to the radio like flowers to the sun. "Goal!" and five mugs clink at once.
city.pu.pu_beer_radio.3: Quiet music with a gentle hiss: someone hums along without knowing the words.
city.pu.pu_beer_stamp.1: The beer bar's stamp: a mug with a head of foam. The bartender: "Not on your palm, like last time."
city.pu.pu_beer_stamp.2: In the evening the stamp goes quicker: everyone is hurrying to the league board.
city.pu.pu_beer_taps.1: Chalk labels over the taps: Zhigulevskoye, Rizhskoye, Martovskoye, Kvass. Kvass is underlined twice: "For those at the helm of a boat."
city.pu.pu_beer_taps.2: On the Friday label an addition: "Fresh barrel! Poured with exactly two fingers of foam." The foam is measured by the bartender's finger, not the customer's.
city.pu.pu_beer_taps.3: Label "Weekend range": beer, beer and a little beer. Kvass, just in case somebody wants variety.
city.pu.pu_books_board.1: A notice: "Looking for The Mysterious Island. Blue, no cover, with a pencilled 'it will all work out' on the endpaper. Tea and thanks for whoever returns it."
city.pu.pu_books_board.2: Under it, a new one: "Saw a blue book at the baker's: it props open the pantry door. I report as a citizen."
city.pu.pu_books_board.3: A third notice: "The book has been returned. The baker apologised and left a bookmark: a cable-car ticket. Thanks, all. Tea is on the table."
city.pu.pu_books_board.4: New: "The second-hand dealer arrives Saturday. If you need a book about the sea, birds or stars, write down the title. We'll look in the box."
city.pu.pu_books_chair.1: The armchair is cosy as a boat without oars. The lamp's green light lies on the page and the words become calmer.
city.pu.pu_books_chair.2: Towards evening someone has left a plaid on the chair. I didn't ask whose. I wrapped myself up and listened to others turning pages.
city.pu.pu_books_chat.1: "It's quiet here in the morning. Readers wake later than books. Read what you see; we'll sort out what you've bought afterwards."
city.pu.pu_books_chat.2: "After lunch people come for detectives and leave with poetry. Or the other way round; I don't know which is worse."
city.pu.pu_books_chat.3: "By evening the light is green from the lamp and someone's already asleep over a page in the chair. Don't wake him; it's the best review."
city.pu.pu_books_chat.4: "Saturdays a second-hand dealer comes from the city with a box. I look first, you look second. But you can come earlier."
city.pu.pu_books_chat.5: "If you find something good, leave a bookmark: a ribbon, a ticket, a letter. The next reader will know the book was loved."
city.pu.pu_books_globe.1: A globe on a tall stand. Pencilled on it: "N. lived here" and a cross by the sea. N. isn't named. I don't ask.
city.pu.pu_books_globe.2: I turned the globe: where the map is blank, a small fish is drawn. Someone decided there's no such thing as empty.
city.pu.pu_books_ladder.1: I climb three steps: from up here the spines look different, like a town seen by a bird. The bookseller: "Not above the fourth, there is nowhere to read up there, only dust."
city.pu.pu_books_ladder.2: From up here you can see which books were taken recently: there is no dust on their spines. Dust is an honest reader.
city.pu.pu_books_lectern.1: A heavy dictionary on a stand, the bookmark always at the same page. The pages smell of sea salt and dust.
city.pu.pu_books_mags.1: Magazines on the shelf: Science and Life, Around the World, Young Naturalist. One is open at an article "How a Gull Is Built"; the page is thumbed to softness.
city.pu.pu_books_mags.2: A stamp with a distant island is tucked in Around the World as a bookmark. I study the island longer than the article.
city.pu.pu_books_stamp.1: The bookstall's stamp: an open book with a bird flying out of the pages. The bookseller: "On the card, please, not in a book."
city.pu.pu_books_stamp.2: The ink pad stands by the till, though there is no till as such: the money sits in a tea box. The print smells of tea leaves.
city.pu.pu_cafe_cat.1: A grey cat is curled up on the windowsill. The barista calls her the Inspector: she checks whether the glass has warmed up enough.
city.pu.pu_cafe_cat.2: The cat sits side-on to the street and pretends she has no interest in the gulls. Her tail gives her away.
city.pu.pu_cafe_cat.3: The cat watches the rain the way one watches a dull film: to the end, and with dignity.
city.pu.pu_cafe_cat.4: The cat sleeps as a loaf. The coffee machine does not wake her, but a spoon on a saucer does.
city.pu.pu_cafe_chat.1: "Good morning. I'm making coffee in a pot for now, the old way: the Leningrad machine is at the repair shop. The foam is the real thing, though."
city.pu.pu_cafe_chat.2: "Lunch? Pies and tea. Tea, by the way, never breaks down."
city.pu.pu_cafe_chat.3: "By evening the sea turns pink; you can watch it from right here. We don't charge for the window."
city.pu.pu_cafe_chat.4: "Weekends are packed, and there are still only four chairs by the window. Sit down before they're gone."
city.pu.pu_cafe_chat.5: "Monday. The gulls are resting, and so am I. Nearly."
city.pu.pu_cafe_chat.6: "Foam is just patience. Don't rush the coffee and it will tell you everything."
city.pu.pu_cafe_mugs.1: The shelf of the regulars' mugs: names in chalk on the bottoms. I was shown which ones not to touch.
city.pu.pu_cafe_papers.1: A binder of the Lyudmilovsk Evening News: in the "Fish Tuesday" column the flounder won again.
city.pu.pu_cafe_papers.2: The Sunday paper: a crossword. Eight down, "Sea bird, four letters." Pencilled in: "gull." Correct.
city.pu.pu_cafe_papers.3: A binder of local papers. Weather on the back, ads in the middle, the horoscope at the bottom: "Today you will be offered a cup of something hot."
city.pu.pu_cafe_papers.4: Someone underlined an ad: "I take in knitting, I give back warmth." Beside it, scribbled: "Call!"
city.pu.pu_cafe_specials.1: In chalk on the board: "Today, coffee from the pot. The Leningrad machine is ill; the repair shop has promised to look into it."
city.pu.pu_cafe_specials.2: In chalk: "Pot coffee again today. Please don't rush us or knock on the counter; we're sad enough."
city.pu.pu_cafe_specials.3: In chalk: "They are hunting the whole coast for a valve for the Leningrad. If you've seen a valve, tell the barista."
city.pu.pu_cafe_specials.4: In chalk: "The valve is found! At the fish shop, from an old paraffin stove. The machine comes back tomorrow."
city.pu.pu_cafe_specials.5: In big chalk letters: "LAUNCH! The first cup from the Leningrad goes to whoever comes and asks."
city.pu.pu_cafe_stamp.1: The Seagull's stamp: a gull with a coffee cup in its beak. The print is even, only the cup has run a little.
city.pu.pu_cafe_stamp.2: Early in the day the pad is fresh and the print dark and thick, like the first cup.
city.pu.pu_cafe_stool.1: From the stool you can see the barista whip the foam and quietly taste it. I won't tell.
city.pu.pu_cafe_stool.2: Towards evening the ones who don't feel like going home yet gather at the bar. The talk is quiet, and so are the cups.
city.pu.pu_cafe_stool.3: The clock ticks quietly. It smells of coffee and the damp wood of the sill.
city.pu.pu_cafe_window.1: Waves roll right up to the wall. One gull bobs on them and acts as if it were all planned.
city.pu.pu_cafe_window.2: By day you can see bathers and boats from the window. Someone waves, probably not at me.
city.pu.pu_cafe_window.3: The sunset has tinted the glass pink. The cups on the sill have gone pink too.
city.pu.pu_cafe_window.4: Beyond the window, the dark sea and the lighthouse's spark. The darker outside, the cosier in here.
city.pu.pu_deckchair.1: The canvas deckchair gives and takes my shape. Beyond the wall you can hear the waves sorting pebbles.
city.pu.pu_deckchair.2: The sun has moved and the deckchair's shadow has slid right. I shift the chair after it. All clever people do.
city.pu.pu_deckchair.3: The chair creaks in the same spot. If you lie quite still, the creak becomes part of the song.
city.pu.pu_deckchair_2.1: This striped deckchair stands closer to the window. From here you see sandalled feet walking by, and not one face.
city.pu.pu_deckchair_2.2: A boy outside presses his nose to the glass, looks at me and sticks out his tongue. I do the same. We're even.
city.pu.pu_dumpling_chat.1: "We shape them in the morning. While you sleep we're up to our elbows in flour. Come after eleven; everything will be hot."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_chat.2: "Lunch hour: plates in hand and don't be shy. Everyone here is one of us, even first-timers."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_chat.3: "Evenings are quieter: people from work finish off the dumplings. I like this hour; steam from the pots clouds the window."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_chat.4: "On Sundays I put in a thirteenth. Don't tell the pasty bar; they'd take it the wrong way."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_chat.5: "Twelve to a portion. I count every one. Not because I'm stingy, but because there must be order."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_pot.1: Dumplings float in the big pot. They rise one by one like small pillows. When the last one has risen, it's time.
city.pu.pu_dumpling_pot.2: Warm steam over the pot, smelling of bay leaf and pepper. I stand there like a fool, smiling. That seems to be the point.
city.pu.pu_dumpling_rolling.1: I roll a disc, add a spoonful of filling, and pinch the edge. A dumpling with character. The cook grunts approvingly.
city.pu.pu_dumpling_rolling.2: In the morning the board holds only flour and silence: the cook rolls dough the way others write letters, slowly and without a blot.
city.pu.pu_dumpling_rolling.3: At the weekend the whole kitchen pinches dumplings: twice the dumplings, three times the talk.
city.pu.pu_dumpling_rules.1: Self-service rules on cardboard: "1. Take your own tray. 2. Bread is free, but not the whole loaf. 3. Return the trays. 4. Don't take the plates home; there's one set for everyone."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_rules.2: Beneath, in a different hand: "5. Thank you is also a payment. 6. Smiling isn't compulsory, but advisable."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_stamp.1: The dumpling shop's stamp: a dumpling with a pigtail. The print smells of broth, or so it seems.
city.pu.pu_dumpling_stamp.2: At lunch the stamp is pressed on the move: the queue behind sighs, but is patient.
city.pu.pu_dumpling_today.1: In chalk on the board: "Dumplings, 12 pieces. With sour cream, 12 pieces and sour cream. The argument with the pasty bar over "three chebureks" continues."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_today.2: In chalk: "Yesterday the pasty bar said our portion is smaller. We counted. Not smaller. Counted again. Still not smaller."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_today.3: In chalk: "Peace proposal: two dumplings for one pasty, exchange through the window. Negotiations under way."
city.pu.pu_dumpling_today.4: In chalk: "The exchange has taken place. The pasty turned out tasty. The dumpling, they say, too. Both sides satisfied. Tea on the house."
city.pu.pu_fish_chat.1: "Morning fish is the most honest: it hasn't had time to lie yet. Take it while it still smells of the sea."
city.pu.pu_fish_chat.2: "A bit dry? Happens. By noon what's left is what the fishermen couldn't hide from their wives."
city.pu.pu_fish_chat.3: "Saturday is fish-soup day. Want soup? Take some ruffe and don't ask whose they are."
city.pu.pu_fish_chat.4: "Bait? Worm for flounder, shrimp for everything else. Cheap, and worth a hundred times the price."
city.pu.pu_fish_chat.5: "Off to the pier with a rod? Remember: fish bite on silence, not bait. The bait is just for manners."
city.pu.pu_fish_knots.1: Scraps of rope are pinned to the board, each with a knot and a label: fisherman's, bowline, clove hitch, sheet bend. I touched them. The knots are real.
city.pu.pu_fish_knots.2: Under the longest piece, a note: "A knot that holds needn't be pretty. A knot that's pretty must hold."
city.pu.pu_fish_knots.3: One knot hangs with no label, pulled impossibly tight. Somebody must have argued with a fish and lost.
city.pu.pu_fish_log.1: On the wall hangs the catch log in an oilcloth cover. The entries read like the log of a very small ship.
city.pu.pu_fish_net.1: A net under the ceiling: not for fishing, for tidiness. Glass floats hold it up the way they once held it on the water. One float is cracked, and nobody replaces it: they say it remembers a storm.
city.pu.pu_fish_net.2: In the dark the floats gleam green, like fish eyes. The net is drying: everything in the shop has to be dry by morning.
city.pu.pu_fish_rods.1: Rods in the rack: bamboo, fibreglass, and one sea rod as thick as my wrist. The tag on the sea rod: "Not for beginners. Nor for the modest."
city.pu.pu_fish_rods.2: The reel is wound with line the colour of water. While you look it seems not to be there at all; that must be the idea.
city.pu.pu_fish_scale.1: The hanging steelyard swings and settles. The needle says "a little less than you'd have liked"; that's what it says to all customers.
city.pu.pu_fish_scale.2: I put my palm on the pan. The needle didn't stir: a hand apparently weighs nothing.
city.pu.pu_fish_stamp.1: The fish shop's stamp: a herring curled in a ring. It smells a little of the sea and a little of the ink pad.
city.pu.pu_fish_stamp.2: The pad is a little cold in the morning: it sat next to the ice. The fishmonger says a print holds better that way.
city.pu.pu_fish_tides.1: A framed tide table. Below it, in chalk: "No herring. Waiting." Three earlier "waiting"s are crossed out and written again.
city.pu.pu_fish_tides.2: In chalk under the table: "A shoal seen off the Far Buoy. Eino says it's fry. Eino is rarely wrong."
city.pu.pu_fish_tides.3: In chalk: "Gulls flying low over the water. Herring at Grey Rock, at the pier by evening. Get your buckets ready."
city.pu.pu_fish_tides.4: In chalk, in a shaky hand: "HERRING! Three crates. Fresh until lunch!"
city.pu.pu_fish_tides.5: In chalk: "Eino has left a little bait at the bottom of a crate for those who know how to wait. Ask at the counter."
city.pu.pu_pasty_chat.1: "From ten. The first chebureks are the crispiest because they don't yet know they're being eaten. Take them before they find out."
city.pu.pu_pasty_chat.2: "Lunch hour: our queue is special, everybody pretends not to be hungry and then takes two."
city.pu.pu_pasty_chat.3: "By evening the oil is in character. Evening chebureks aren't worse, just calmer."
city.pu.pu_pasty_chat.4: "On Sundays I serve with vinegar and red pepper. Those who are afraid, take tea with it. Those who aren't, take tea as well."
city.pu.pu_pasty_chat.5: "A cheburek is a little pie that once decided to grow big. Don't stop it: let it crunch."
city.pu.pu_pasty_fryer.1: Oil boils in the cauldron. A cheburek creeps slowly to the edge, flips and turns golden with bubbles. It's beautiful, like a little eruption.
city.pu.pu_pasty_fryer.2: The cook lifts out a cheburek with a skimmer, shakes it and lays it on a napkin. The napkin turns see-through at once. "Don't touch, you'll burn," he says. I touched only with my eyes.
city.pu.pu_pasty_mincer.1: I turn the handle of the mincer and something inside purrs with satisfaction. The cook: "Don't overdo it: we have one handle and a lot of guests."
city.pu.pu_pasty_mincer.2: In the morning the mincer turns in time with the radio. The cook is sure the filling is tenderer for the music.
city.pu.pu_pasty_stamp.1: The pasty shop's stamp: a chebureki with a pattern round the edge. The print came out crisp, or so it seemed.
city.pu.pu_pasty_stamp.2: At lunch they stamp and leave at once with a hot paper bag: the ink pad smells of fried dough.
city.pu.pu_pasty_table.1: On the tall table stand a salt cellar, a bottle of vinegar and a stack of paper napkins. One napkin corner is pencilled: "I was here, it was delicious."
city.pu.pu_pasty_table.2: The vinegar on the table is the real kind, dark, in a lemonade bottle. Somebody has carefully labelled it: "Careful: vinegar."
city.pu.pu_pasty_today.1: The board by the door: "Crimean-style chebureks, 16 kopecks. Pepper on request. We make no comment on the dumpling bar's "twelve"."
city.pu.pu_pasty_today.2: In chalk: "We were told: 'three chebureks is a portion.' We agree: a portion of chebureks is three. Of dumplings, however they count."
city.pu.pu_pasty_today.3: In chalk: "Exchange proposal received. Considering. Dumplings for tasting, cheburek for tasting. Talks over tea."
city.pu.pu_pasty_today.4: In chalk: "The exchange has taken place. The dumplings turned out good. Quietly admitted. Chebureks go out the window while hot. Thanks, neighbours."
city.pu.pu_pasty_treaty.1: In a frame on the wall hangs a sheet of squared paper in two hands. The heading: "Treaty of the Dumpling and the Pasty."
city.pu.pu_photo_album.1: An album on the stand: the promenade over a year. Captions in ink, so neat they might have been written by flashlight.
city.pu.pu_photo_bench.1: The bench for those waiting for a portrait. Samples on the wall: everybody is smiling, and nobody wants to go first.
city.pu.pu_photo_bench.2: I sit on the bench. A lamp hums softly over the studio. Somebody rehearses a smile in the glass of a pocket watch.
city.pu.pu_photo_camera.1: Under the black cloth, on the ground glass, the whole studio upside down. The lamp stands on the floor and the ceiling is underfoot. You get used to it.
city.pu.pu_photo_camera.2: Aim it at the door and the glass shows the sea and people walking upside down and still hurrying somewhere.
city.pu.pu_photo_camera.prompt: E — look into the ground glass
city.pu.pu_photo_cutout.1: The "Captain of the Seven Seas" board: a round hole for the face, a cap on a nail. The photographer: "The cap is your choice, a moustache costs extra." The moustache is painted.
city.pu.pu_photo_cutout.2: In the evening the round hole catches the lamp's glow. The captain is faceless today, but in good spirits.
city.pu.pu_photo_cutout.3: At the weekend a queue of little ones forms at the board: each wants to be captain for at least one flash.
city.pu.pu_photo_lightbox.1: A negative against the light: black clouds, white sea. Once you get used to it, you begin to see how it ought to be.
city.pu.pu_photo_lightbox.2: A negative with a cat: she is white on it, like a ghost. The photographer: "Cats don't like posing, but they like light."
city.pu.pu_photo_lightbox.3: A negative of an empty pier: even better than it was. In the light you can see every board.
city.pu.pu_photo_lightbox.4: A negative of someone's face under the loupe: the wrinkles glow like rivers on a map.
city.pu.pu_photo_lightbox.prompt: E — hold a negative to the light
city.pu.pu_photo_negatives.1: A drawer of negatives. The envelopes are labelled: "Fishermen", "Roofs", "Children at the fountain", "Unidentified". "Unidentified" is the thickest.
city.pu.pu_photo_negatives.2: I held a negative to the light: white is black, black is white, and the person in it laughs just the same. Laughter doesn't invert.
city.pu.pu_photo_negatives.3: In the "Unidentified" envelope the last frame: an empty promenade at dawn. Caption: "Taken to remember that nobody was here and it was good."
city.pu.pu_photo_props.1: On the stand, costumes for shoots: a captain's cap, a veiled hat, a sailor's striped vest. A tag on the cap: "Take care; it has already been to sea once."
city.pu.pu_photo_props.2: In the raincoat pocket a note: "Don't want to, don't put it on. Do want to, still don't put it on, but hold it." I held it. The coat is heavy and honest.
city.pu.pu_photo_samples.1: The wall of samples. A new picture in the corner: "Fishermen on the pier, 1957." Everyone looks at the camera and nobody smiles except the dog.
city.pu.pu_photo_samples.2: A new picture: "The first cable car, a test run." Two people stand rigid in the cabin as if for a portrait; they're afraid.
city.pu.pu_photo_samples.3: A new picture: "A wedding on the promenade. The wind took the veil; in the second take the groom holds it." The photographer has captioned: "Take two, the most honest."
city.pu.pu_photo_samples.4: A new picture pinned over the others, still damp at the edges: a boy in a jacket looks at the camera closely, as if he wants to ask something. Caption: "Newcomer. Stayed."
city.pu.pu_photo_stamp.1: The photo studio's stamp: a lens and a flash star. The print is sharp. The photographer should focus like that.
city.pu.pu_photo_stamp.2: The stamp sits next to the telephone. The photographer: "Quietly, please, my negatives are drying."
city.pu.pu_rental_bikes.1: The bicycles stand in a row: red frames, blue, green, and a yellow one. A paper on the yellow one's carrier says: "For those who hurry slowly."
city.pu.pu_rental_bikes.2: A tag with a number and a price is tied to each handlebar. On the red one, added: "The bell is louder than it looks."
city.pu.pu_rental_bikes.3: There's sand on the tyres: someone has already ridden along the beach. The owner doesn't scold; he says it's the best advertising.
city.pu.pu_rental_boats.1: A school blackboard with the boat schedule: No. 1 Seagull, running. No. 2 Neptune, running. No. 3 drying on the shore. No. 4 Swallow, at the repair shop being painted.
city.pu.pu_rental_boats.2: A note in chalk: "Swallow is being painted blue with a white stripe. Don't touch with a finger: it's drying. There have been cases."
city.pu.pu_rental_boats.3: Swallow is back on the water! A trial circuit done; she leaks through only one crack, but romantically.
city.pu.pu_rental_boats.4: Notice: "Saturday at 4 p.m., the Race to the Buoy (rowing, in pairs). Prize: the warmest tea on the whole coast. Sign up at the counter."
city.pu.pu_rental_boats.5: The sign-up list: the baker and the souvenir seller, two fishermen, one stranger in a raincoat. The last line is empty. "There's room for you," someone has added.
city.pu.pu_rental_chat.1: "Morning is for bicycles. Brakes checked, bell rings, the chain only grumbles a little. A rouble an hour, and thirty kopecks extra for the wind in your face."
city.pu.pu_rental_chat.2: "Afternoons are for boats. Oars go out by number and come back in order. Number seven is missing; don't ask."
city.pu.pu_rental_chat.3: "Deckchairs till six. After six I fold them, and you watch the sunset standing, like people from the past."
city.pu.pu_rental_chat.4: "Saturday is the Race to the Buoy. I sign people up in pairs. No singles: they row in circles."
city.pu.pu_rental_chat.5: "Today is the Race to the Buoy. Those with a partner, onto the water. Those without, onto a deckchair to cheer."
city.pu.pu_rental_chat.6: "The deposit's a passport. No passport? Then your word of honour. No word either? Then at least a smile."
city.pu.pu_rental_keys.1: A plywood board of hooks and numbers. Lock keys hang on the hooks, and on one, a little plush fish too. That's the key to Swallow; she likes to be treated gently.
city.pu.pu_rental_keys.2: A receipt is pinned nearby: "Left in storage: one umbrella, one left shoe, one notebook. Come and collect."
city.pu.pu_rental_log.1: The hire register hangs on a string on the wall. The entries are in different hands and one pencil.
city.pu.pu_rental_pump.1: I pump, and the tyre sighs and firms up. The owner, without turning round: "Don't wait for the needle, the pump is older than the gauge."
city.pu.pu_rental_pump.2: In the morning there is a queue for air: waiting in line for air is both unfair and funny.
city.pu.pu_rental_pump.3: In the rain the pump stands gathering dust: the boats sleep, the bicycles think.
city.pu.pu_rental_route.1: A map of the coast with a red thread marking the route "to the buoy and back". It shows where to fill a bottle and where not to stop for the wind.
city.pu.pu_rental_route.2: The thread on the map glints under the lamp, but nobody rides to the buoy in such darkness. The route can wait until morning.
city.pu.pu_rental_stamp.1: The rental's stamp: a bicycle wheel in a circle. The spokes came out better than the handlebars.
city.pu.pu_rental_stamp.2: The owner pushes the tray closer: "Just not on the register, it has enough stains already."
city.pu.pu_rental_tariff.1: On the board: "Bicycle, 1 rouble an hour. Boat, 2 roubles an hour, for two. Deckchair, 30 kopecks an hour; umbrella free if the wind doesn't take it."
city.pu.pu_rental_tariff.2: Below, in chalk: "Children under 10 with parents. Parents under 40 with children. Everybody else as it turns out."
city.pu.pu_souvenir_amber.1: In the case are pieces of amber. One holds a gnat with splayed legs, another a tiny air bubble. The tag: "Summer, about forty million years ago."
city.pu.pu_souvenir_amber.2: Held to the light, amber turns to honey. I didn't pick it up: it turns out it looks fine without me.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_boxes.1: Boxes on the shelf: caskets with shells on the lids, painted spoons, wooden fish on strings, gull-shaped whistles. The whistle sounds like a kettle regardless.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_boxes.2: A paper stuck to one casket lid says: "If you open it, you buy it." I didn't open it.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_chat.1: "Amber is frozen time. The resin flowed for millions of years so we could hang it on a string. Take the one you like; each has its own age."
city.pu.pu_souvenir_chat.2: "Towards evening come the ones who forgot about presents. I know them by their eyes. Postcards are for them."
city.pu.pu_souvenir_chat.3: "Weekends bring the passengers from the suburban train. They ask: 'What's the most local thing?' I say: 'The wind.' But I sell what I have."
city.pu.pu_souvenir_chat.4: "Take your time. Everything lies in its place here, and if it doesn't, someone bought it and put it back."
city.pu.pu_souvenir_globe.1: A globe on a tall stand. Lyudmilovsk isn't marked with a pin, but looking from the right it's somewhere around here. The sea is labelled small: "Baltic".
city.pu.pu_souvenir_globe.2: I gave the globe a spin. It rolled for a long time and stopped on the Pacific. Far away. I nodded: I'm fine here.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_guestbook.1: A guestbook open at page five. An entry: "Yerevan, July. The sea turned out bigger than on the postcard. Thank you." A little boat is drawn beside it.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_guestbook.2: A new entry: "Riga, but Mum was born here. Found the house where Grandma lived. The house is there. The windows are different." Signed with just a first name.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_guestbook.3: An entry in a child's hand: "Tashkent. Saw a gull up close. It looked at my bun. Didn't give it up. Proud."
city.pu.pu_souvenir_guestbook.4: An entry written in several languages at once: "It was good here." Beneath it three signatures and one blot.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_guestbook.5: The next page is blank. A pencil on a string lies on top. It seems to be waiting for my entry, even if only in my head.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_snowglobe.1: I shake the globe: the flakes swirl and settle quietly on a tiny lighthouse. The owner: "It won't break, tested by children."
city.pu.pu_souvenir_snowglobe.2: Snow falls in the globe, and outside too. The lighthouse inside stands as if nothing were happening.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_snowglobe.3: A blizzard in the globe, rain outside. There is no arguing with the globe: it has its own weather.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_snowglobe.4: It is clear outside and a blizzard inside. As if the lighthouse made a wish for its own weather and is waiting for it to come true.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_spinner.1: A spinner rack of postcards. It turns with a squeak, as if each card carried a wind of its own.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_stamp.1: The souvenir shop's stamp: an amber drop with a gull inside. The print comes out like a wrapped gift.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_stamp.2: The owner lifts a little scarf off the ink pad: "We treat it like jewellery: hidden from the dust."
city.pu.pu_souvenir_suncatcher.1: Morning light passes through the amber drops and lies on the floor in warm patches, like in a tea room.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_suncatcher.2: At midday the amber is clear to the bottom: you can see bubbles and one gnat that was unlucky sixty million years ago.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_suncatcher.3: Towards evening the amber darkens and turns almost red. The drops chime softly in the draught.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_suncatcher.4: At night the drops are just dark beads on strings. In the morning they will be sun again.
city.pu.pu_souvenir_suncatcher.5: Rain behind the glass, yet the amber still glows: they say it saves up sunshine in advance, for a rainy day.
city.pu.pu_workshop_bins.1: Little drawers with labels: "M3 screws", "M4 screws", "assorted washers", "nothing special", "will sort later". The last is the heaviest.
city.pu.pu_workshop_bins.2: One drawer holds only buttons. Beside it a tag: "For those who came to mend trousers and stayed to mend life."
city.pu.pu_workshop_chat.1: "In the morning I solder. Don't distract me; at that hour even silence costs extra."
city.pu.pu_workshop_chat.2: "Afternoons I take things in. They bring everything: radios, irons, clocks; once they brought a nightingale. A mechanical one, but offended."
city.pu.pu_workshop_chat.3: "Saturday's a short day. What I haven't fixed by three gets fixed on Monday, and comes out better."
city.pu.pu_workshop_chat.4: "The Leningrad from the café? The valve is the problem. They say the fishermen have one. If so, it'll be singing by midweek."
city.pu.pu_workshop_chat.5: "Bring it and I'll fix it. If I can't, I'll say so, and then at least you'll know your sorrow wasn't for nothing."
city.pu.pu_workshop_ledger.1: On the counter lies the repair ledger: date, item, what was said, what was done. It reads better than any novel.
city.pu.pu_workshop_radios.1: The radios on the shelf wait their turn, each with a tag. One purrs the Blue Light show, another is silent, and a third broadcasts the weather for a town next door.
city.pu.pu_workshop_radios.2: One set is open: inside are valves like small glass cities. The master calls them by name.
city.pu.pu_workshop_stamp.1: The workshop's stamp: a cog with a screwdriver. The print is almost perfect: the master carved the stamp himself.
city.pu.pu_workshop_stamp.2: The master, without looking up: "Go on. I changed the pad this week, don't spare it."
city.pu.pu_workshop_tags.1: Tags on nails. No. 41: a Riga-6 radio, won't sing. No. 42: an iron that heats unevenly. No. 43: the Leningrad coffee machine (Seagull café), needs a valve.
city.pu.pu_workshop_tags.2: No. 43: "No valve in Lyudmilovsk or in Riga. Searching old things." The master has been searching old things for two days.
city.pu.pu_workshop_tags.3: No. 43: "Found it! At the fish shop, from a written-off paraffin stove. Fits with a hair's gap. Filed it to size."
city.pu.pu_workshop_tags.4: No. 43: DONE. To go back to the café the same day; I'll carry it myself. No. 44: "alarm clock, rings at the wrong time"; bring it in and we'll cure it.
city.pu.pu_workshop_tags.5: A new tag, no number yet: "The boy's torch. A bulb, a battery and a promise." It seems they already know me here.
city.pu.pu_workshop_tester.1: A valve tester: you put a valve in and the needle twitches. "A good one," says the master. The needle does not argue.
city.pu.pu_workshop_tester.2: In damp weather the needle trembles: the master says the valves get nervous when the air is wet.
city.pu.pu_workshop_tv.1: The screen shows the test card: circles, stripes, squares. A perfectly steady picture is rare; the shop is proud of it.
city.pu.pu_workshop_tv.2: A television with a screwdriver left inside. The most peaceful sight on the coast: the blue bar doesn't move.
city.pu.pu_workshop_vise.1: I clamp a nail in the vise. The master: "No harder, it won't run away."
city.pu.pu_workshop_vise.2: A little key to something is clamped in the vise. The master leaves problems unsolved on purpose: "Let it think."
city.pu.stamp.fest: On a holiday the ink pad never gets a rest: the people ahead of me already have a whole row of stamps.
city.pu.stamp.rain: Rain drums on the glass, yet the stamp comes out dry and sharp. The card in my pocket stays dry.
city.pu.txt.pu_bakery_orders.p1: "Cabbage pie for eight, for Saturday. A wedding loaf, with salt and no jokes. Twelve rolls for the school choir, warm but not hot."
city.pu.txt.pu_bakery_orders.p2a: On weekdays the orders carry a note: "Collect before eight. After that the rolls go out on the street and do not come back."
city.pu.txt.pu_bakery_orders.p2b: At the weekend the note says: "We don't hand them over hot: let them walk home first. Bread likes the road."
city.pu.txt.pu_bakery_orders.p3: The last entry at the foot of the page: "A roll for the cat. No raisins. The baker knows." A little paw is drawn over it.
city.pu.txt.pu_bakery_orders.title: Orders for tomorrow
city.pu.txt.pu_barber_book.p1: "The usual" is written five times in a row. The barbers somehow understand that everyone's usual is different.
city.pu.txt.pu_barber_book.p2a: Weekdays: "Nine: the driver. Ten: a fisherman with a beard, just a trim. Eleven: a boy with his mother, she will write down how to cut."
city.pu.txt.pu_barber_book.p2b: Weekends: "Two lads before the dance. One wants it like an actor's but won't say which. We will guess."
city.pu.txt.pu_barber_book.p3: At the foot, in fine ink: "Free to anyone who brings good news." So far two have had free haircuts: one for news, one for politeness.
city.pu.txt.pu_barber_book.title: The appointment book
city.pu.txt.pu_books_dictionary.p1: MOLE. A stone arm held out into the sea, so the wave calms down before it reaches the boats.
city.pu.txt.pu_books_dictionary.p2: HIGH TIDE. The sea takes a deep breath; the ebb is the breath out. Fishermen know when it breathes evenly.
city.pu.txt.pu_books_dictionary.p3: BUOY. A red barrel that will not sink on principle. A landmark for those who mean to come back.
city.pu.txt.pu_books_dictionary.p4a: FOG. The sea has put on a cap. Ships move in it by touch, and gulls by memory.
city.pu.txt.pu_books_dictionary.p4b: RAIN. The sea from above: another sea, yet the same. The drops fall into it as if repaying a debt.
city.pu.txt.pu_books_dictionary.p4c: WIND. A word without a definition: it is on every page, and nobody has dared to explain it.
city.pu.txt.pu_books_dictionary.title: A sea dictionary for landlubbers
city.pu.txt.pu_cafe_mugs.p1: Four mugs on the shelf. On the bottoms in chalk: "Eino", "Master", "Baker", "Rental". The master's is black with a chipped handle: he thinks a mug with a whole handle is boring to drink from.
city.pu.txt.pu_cafe_mugs.p2a: Weekdays: the mugs are taken by nine, and by noon they all stand in a row by the sink like tired little soldiers.
city.pu.txt.pu_cafe_mugs.p2b: Weekends: the mugs hang on their hooks longer, their owners are asleep. The barista writes little notes: "Don't run away, we are waiting."
city.pu.txt.pu_cafe_mugs.p3a: At the end of the shelf a fifth mug, without a name, painted with a gull. The label says: "For whoever comes in first after the rain."
city.pu.txt.pu_cafe_mugs.p3b: At the end of the shelf a fifth mug, with no name. The label says: "For a newcomer. When he comes, we will know." Nobody has drunk from it yet.
city.pu.txt.pu_cafe_mugs.title: The regulars' mugs
city.pu.txt.pu_fish_log.p1: Columns: "date, place, what, how much, caught with". Today's first line is still blank, but a pencil tick is already in it: "waiting".
city.pu.txt.pu_fish_log.p2a: Yesterday's entry: "Mole. Sprat, forty kilos, on a bottom line. Eino also caught two perch, but they did not ask to go in the log."
city.pu.txt.pu_fish_log.p2b: A weekend entry: "Quiet. The fishermen are on the mole, and so is the trade: they caught, they sold, and they told how much each one did not catch."
city.pu.txt.pu_fish_log.p3a: A note in red: "Fog. No fishing. Eino went into the fog after the gulls and came back at noon with one word: 'Quiet.'"
city.pu.txt.pu_fish_log.p3b: A note: "Rain and snow. The fish are deeper, the fishermen closer to the stove. We wait for herring until the first clear morning."
city.pu.txt.pu_fish_log.p3c: On the last page a note: "Leave Grey Rock alone: the gulls have their own catch there." Underlined twice.
city.pu.txt.pu_fish_log.title: The catch log
city.pu.txt.pu_pasty_treaty.p1: The heading: "Treaty of the Dumpling and the Pasty." At the top two hands: one has letters round as dumplings, the other sharp as the edge of a pasty.
city.pu.txt.pu_pasty_treaty.p2: Clause one: dumplings are boiled, pasties are fried, and neither takes offence or is compared.
city.pu.txt.pu_pasty_treaty.p3: Clause two: if the neighbours run out of flour, we help with flour, mutually. Clause three: on a holiday the queue is shared.
city.pu.txt.pu_pasty_treaty.p4: Two signatures. Beside them in a third hand: "Witness: the bakery cat." And a paw print in ink.
city.pu.txt.pu_pasty_treaty.title: Peace on the promenade
city.pu.txt.pu_photo_album.p1: "Spring. The ice has gone, the gulls have come." In the picture a young fisherman mends a net and looks not at it but at a gull on the quay.
city.pu.txt.pu_photo_album.p2: "Summer. The mole at seven in the morning." Empty, as if it had not been invented yet. Only the shadows of lamp posts lie across it.
city.pu.txt.pu_photo_album.p3: "Autumn. Fishermen with flasks." One looks into the lens: "I don't get photographed." The picture came out well.
city.pu.txt.pu_photo_album.p4: "Winter. Footprints on the sand lead to the water and back: someone changed his mind." Nobody else is in the frame, and it is the best thing in the album.
city.pu.txt.pu_photo_album.title: Album: the promenade over a year
city.pu.txt.pu_rental_log.p1: "Red bicycle: the family from the Roofs, two hours. Boat no. 3: to the buoy and back. Blue deck chair: until lunch." A tick against every line: returned.
city.pu.txt.pu_rental_log.p2a: Weekdays: "Yellow bicycle: fisherman Eino, to the mole. Said he'd bring it back by evening. Did. Both of us were surprised."
city.pu.txt.pu_rental_log.p2b: Saturday: "All the boats are at sea, all the bicycles are on the promenade, the owner alone in the shop and very pleased."
city.pu.txt.pu_rental_log.p3: The last line in pencil: "Nobody returned the bicycle bell, because nobody took it. But thank you for thinking of it."
city.pu.txt.pu_rental_log.title: The hire register
city.pu.txt.pu_souvenir_cards.p1: The postcards on the rack are not for sale: the owner coaxed them out of guests. The first: "Greetings from Yalta! The sea here is like yours, only warm. No offence."
city.pu.txt.pu_souvenir_cards.p2: The second: "Greetings from Baikal! The water is so clear the fish are shy. I will tell you when I'm back."
city.pu.txt.pu_souvenir_cards.p3a: The third, a Friday one: "Greetings from Tbilisi! Everyone sings here, even those who came to be quiet."
city.pu.txt.pu_souvenir_cards.p3b: The third: "Greetings from the Riga seashore! Pines, sand, wind, and you probably have the same. So we are neighbours."
city.pu.txt.pu_souvenir_cards.title: Postcards from far away
city.pu.txt.pu_workshop_ledger.p1: "Iron: heats as it likes. Done: now heats as it should. The owner asked what was wrong. Answered: its mood."
city.pu.txt.pu_workshop_ledger.p2a: Weekdays: "Radio 'Riga-6': doesn't sing. Done: sings. Station chosen at the customer's request; his favourite song is about the sea."
city.pu.txt.pu_workshop_ledger.p2b: Saturday: "Cuckoo clock: the cuckoo is hoarse. Done: replaced the spring. The cuckoo now calls with purpose, once."
city.pu.txt.pu_workshop_ledger.p3: The last line is undated: "Clock without hands. Brought in as an ornament. Not for repair: they decorate."
city.pu.txt.pu_workshop_ledger.title: The repair ledger
city.px.ask.gull: Who is that gull on the rail?
city.px.ask.gull.1: "Nikolai. Don't laugh, he answers to it. Comes every evening for a crust, carries it to the very edge and eats it there. The other gulls envy him and tease."
city.px.ask.gull.2: "In rain he sits under the eaves and pretends he isn't wet. Familiar behaviour, if you ask me."
city.px.ask.maria.0: "Maria is Captain Laptev's seiner. Whatever happens to her I put in the watch book by the stair, and I write it honestly."
city.px.ask.maria.1: "She went out for herring, promised to be back by evening. We are waiting for now. Come again: you will be the first to know."
city.px.ask.maria.2: "A storm, and no Maria. I ring the bell every two minutes, my hands shake but I ring. The radio is silent. Don't tell Aram I'm afraid."
city.px.ask.maria.3: "She's back! The engine died, they drifted for a day, and then they saw our light. Laptev left a bottle with a note, it stands on the shelf by the little ship. Don't open it."
city.px.ask.night: What do you do at night?
city.px.ask.night.1: "Every two hours I wind the clockwork. The crank is stiff as a coffee grinder's. Between windings I drink tea, read, watch the water. The sea is very talkative at night."
city.px.ask.night.2: "Best around four. Everyone sleeps, the water is like glass, and suddenly you hear someone singing far, far away. A seiner, I suppose. Or a gull in its sleep."
city.px.ask.steps.1: "One hundred and eighteen. I climb it three times a night and every time I count to one hundred and twenty. Two extra from tiredness."
city.px.ask.steps.2: "Did you look through the telescope on the gallery? On a clear day you can see the far shore at the edge of the water. The old keeper showed it to me, and it is our secret. Well, yours too now."
city.px.ask.visitors.1: "Schoolchildren in spring, photographers in summer, couples in any weather. In winter an old man comes with a barometer: he checks his against ours and leaves pleased, ours lies less."
city.px.ask.visitors.2: "Did you read about the nut in the book? I meant to be cross and laughed instead. Read it, everything there is honest, even my lectures."
city.px.ask.visitors.3: "Read the book to the end? Then you know more about the tower than I do: I never reread my own entries."
city.px.bell.1: I pulled the rope. The bell struck thickly, bong, and the sound went out over the water, far, far away. The gulls on the rail flinched but came back within a minute.
city.px.bell.2: I rang slowly, as you do in fog: once a minute. Nobody answered from the sea. But a lantern lit on the next pier: someone heard and is awake.
city.px.bell.3: On a day off the order is to ring politely: people are resting on the promenade. I rang as softly as one can ring a bell the size of a person.
city.px.bottle.1: A model brigantine on a stand, sails of cigarette paper. Arkady took three winters to make it. Beside it a green bottle with a cork: "Open only together."
city.px.bottle.2: The bottle is sealed with tar, a rolled note inside. Chalked on the glass: "Do not open until Maria returns." The chalk is fresh: they renew it every day.
city.px.bottle.3: The bottle has been opened and closed again. The note inside: "We saw your light eleven miles off. Thank you. Captain Laptev." The cork is freshly tarred, this time for keeps.
city.px.bottle.prompt: E — look at the little ship
city.px.bottlepost.prompt: E — send a bottle with a note
city.px.bp.1: A tarred chest with a slot and three bottles. On the tag: "Write a note, drop it in, throw it from the gallery over the rail. Delivery not guaranteed." I wrote two words, corked it and threw: the bottle flew a long way and went under without a splash.
city.px.bp.2: Writing a note at night is hard: the pencil cannot see the paper. I wrote by feel and it came out "helo" with one l too few. The bottle flashed in the beam and was gone.
city.px.bp.late: The keepers say one bottle came back last spring. A boy found it on the beach and brought it back. Inside was his own note from three years before.
city.px.bp.rain: In rain the bottle goes willingly: a wave takes it and tows it to the channel. If anyone finds it, let them think I wrote it in a storm.
city.px.cat.1: The keepers' cat sleeps curled in the basket, one ear still on duty. I scratched his cheek: he kept sleeping, only noticeably louder.
city.px.cat.2: The cat opened one eye, appraised me and closed it again. I think I've been taken on probation. Until the first herring, probably.
city.px.cat.3: The cat isn't asleep: he sits upright in the basket, watching the light turn above. I looked at the ceiling too. A pale patch walks across the walls and he follows it with his eyes.
city.px.cat.4: At weekends the cat sleeps even harder. The keepers swear he's the only one in town who reads the timetable, and his day off is on it.
city.px.clockwork.1: The lens's turning gear: a weight in the shaft, wheels in brass cheeks. By day no beam is needed and the lens is under a linen cover, but they wind it ahead so there's no waiting at dusk. I gave it ten turns.
city.px.clockwork.2: Sunset: the covers are off and the clockwork wound. The handle goes stiffly. The weight crawls up the shaft, then the wheels take it and start counting time.
city.px.clockwork.3: At night you can hear the gear all through the house: tick, tick, tick, and every twenty seconds the beam comes round upstairs. I wound it: the weight must never be left at the bottom.
city.px.coll.sights.title: Views from the gallery
city.px.cup.1: I set a hot cup beside the log. The steam climbs and the lamp behind it goes hazy. Whoever comes will find it, smile first and drink after.
city.px.cup.2: I left the cup by the night log so that whoever comes on watch finds it warm. Slid it right up to his pen. Now this place belongs to someone.
city.px.desk.1: "Good evening. Sign the book by the door and climb carefully: the steps are iron and slippery when it's damp. Ask whatever you like, there is little talk at night."
city.px.desk.2: "Quieter, please: at night sound travels up the stair like through a pipe. But you may climb. The lamp does not sleep and neither do I."
city.px.desk.3: "We are not here by day: we sleep after the night. The book is by the door, climb if you don't fear heights."
city.px.desk.closed: A note on the table: "The keeper sleeps after the night watch. Come back after six. The stair is open and the visitors' book may be read." A mug beside it, still warm.
city.px.desk.prompt: E — go up to the keeper's table
city.px.flags.1: The yellow flag of the signal code means: "My vessel is healthy, I request permission to enter." The keepers keep it at the top of the pigeonholes: visitors are always welcome here.
city.px.flags.2: Red and yellow on the diagonal: "Man overboard." The flag is worn at the folds. It has never once had to be raised, but it is checked every spring. First they check it, then they say nothing.
city.px.flags.3: The white and blue flag: "Divers below, keep clear." It goes up when the piles at the pier are cleaned. In the next pigeonhole lies a small whistle for the divers.
city.px.flags.4: In one pigeonhole there's a checked kerchief instead of a flag, with a slip: "For Maria. If they ask what it means: 'We're waiting for you.'" The kerchief is freshly washed.
city.px.floats.1: Glass floats, green as bottle glass, and one blue. They lie in a rope sling like a necklace. One is cracked, but it is kept: they say it is lucky.
city.px.floats.2: I held a float to my ear: a steady hum inside. They say it is the sea left in it from the last catch. The keepers swear to it, and whether they are fibbing they won't say.
city.px.floats.3: For the sea festival the floats were carried out to the pier rails. They catch the light like huge drops. By evening each holds a small sunset.
city.px.floats.4: At night the floats glow dimly with the lamp's light. Green as a cat's eyes.
city.px.game.morse.title: The keeper's key
city.px.gauge.1: The sea-level staff: red marks every decimetre, blue and white bands every ten centimetres. Today the water stands at "+7": quiet and level.
city.px.gauge.2: The water has dropped to zero: the wind blows off the land and pushes water out of the bay. On such days fishermen set their nets farther out.
city.px.gauge.3: "+22". An onshore wind has pushed the water up to the very edge of the pier. The lowest step is gone and gulls stroll over it as on a pavement.
city.px.gauge.4: "-5". An offshore wind, the water has gone, boulders show at the foot of the pier and cormorants sit on them drying their wings.
city.px.gauge.5: "+3". Quite still. The water is smooth as a tray, rings spreading from a fish. In the log the keepers wrote: "calm, boredom, thank goodness."
city.px.gauge.fog: In the fog the staff sticks out of the white like a thermometer from milk. The numbers hardly show but the red marks glow.
city.px.gauge.rain: Rain drums on the staff and the numbers look brighter. By the level you can tell the water will rise a hand's width by evening. The keepers have put out buckets, just in case.
city.px.gb.1: The lighthouse visitors' book. On the first page in a neat hand: "Please write your name, the date and what you saw. The stair: one hundred and eighteen steps. Count them yourself, we do not cheat. The keepers, Arkadiy and Aram."
city.px.gb.2: "Came with Mum. Mum counted to sixty and sat down. I counted to one hundred and eighteen and did not sit. Tima, aged 9." Under it, in another hand: "We all sat. Mum."
city.px.gb.3: "Saw dolphins! The keepers said: a seal. Dolphin all the same. Zhenya."
city.px.gb.4: "Newspaper photographer. Took forty frames, not one catches the wind." Beside it an inky cat's paw print and a signature: "Approved."
city.px.gb.5: "Lyova and I argued how many metres to the water. He said twenty, I said thirty. We dropped a nut and counted aloud. The nut won: it landed before we finished counting. Rita." Below in chalk: "NOTHING IS TO BE THROWN DOWN! Arkadiy." And lower still: "But the argument was settled fairly. Aram."
city.px.gb.6: "Captain Laptev, seiner Maria. Thank you for the light. We saw it from eleven miles away, and these last nights we told the hours by it." Below in chalk: "And for the tea! Aram."
city.px.gb.7: The page is almost clean. In the corner in pencil: "For those who come after Maria. Don't be shy, there is plenty of room." The pencil hangs beside it on a string with a knot at the end so nobody carries it off.
city.px.gb.8: On the last page a new line: "Thank you to everyone who rang the bell. Fog is promised for tomorrow, mind your ears. The keepers." And a drawn mug with steam.
city.px.guestbook.l1: The visitors' book lies on its stand, the pencil on its string beside it. The pages rustle in the draught from the door.
city.px.gweather.1: The instrument screen: white louvres, two thermometers inside. The vane points west: that's where weather comes from, the keepers say. The anemometer spins evenly, like three small suns.
city.px.gweather.2: At night the anemometer rings thin and fine. The screen is dark, chalked on its door: "Readings at 02:00. Arkady." Added smaller in chalk: "Don't sleep."
city.px.hist.1: THE LIGHTHOUSE TOWER ON THE PIER. Built by engineers from straight steel bars, like spokes. Each section is a hyperboloid: the bars are straight, yet the tower comes out curved. A curve grows out of straight lines, that is the whole trick.
city.px.hist.2: At the top there is a water tank with the lantern above it. First it was a water tower, then a lamp was set on it. Now it works on two fronts: it gives drink and it gives light.
city.px.hist.3: RULES FOR VISITORS. Climb without shoving. Throw nothing down (except bottle post: the chest by the rail). Do not feed the gulls, they feed themselves. In fog the bell is for everyone, but in turn.
city.px.hist.4: One hundred and eighteen steps to the gallery, twenty metres above the ground. Higher, to the lamp itself, another sixteen, but only the keepers go there. From the gallery you can see all worth seeing.
city.px.keeper_bottle.prompt: E — look at the little ship
city.px.keeper_clockwork.prompt: E — wind up the lighthouse clockwork
city.px.keeper_cup.prompt: E — set a cup of tea on the desk
city.px.keeper_watch.prompt: E — open the clockwork's watch book
city.px.morse.1: The key is stiff and shiny. On the paper tape in pencil: "···  ———  ···: distress signal, but a practice one." I tapped, and the lamp beside it blinked in time.
city.px.morse.2: At night the key knocks especially loud and the sound goes out over the water. Far away someone's light blinked, a coincidence probably.
city.px.morse.draw.1: Half the words came out, half turned into "rat-a-tat". The lamp thinks it is almost a joke.
city.px.morse.lose.1: I lost the beat on the third sign. The lamp blinked out of time as if laughing. Never mind, it is kind.
city.px.morse.win.1: The lamp echoed every tap you made. From the tower below came an approving "Steady!"
city.px.morse.win.night: At night the key carries far: the lamp answered you and over the water a black speck seemed to blink back. Imagination, probably.
city.px.oilskins.1: Two yellow oilskins and one small, a child's. The linings are stitched "A. O." and "A. K.", the small one "For guests". It goes to whoever is taken up top in the rain.
city.px.oilskins.2: The oilskins are still damp: someone has just been out on the gallery to check the bell. A thin drip crawls from a hood into an old boiled-sweet tin set on the floor.
city.px.oilskins.3: The sou'wester hangs on its hook with its brim toward the door. A habit, so you don't forget it going out. Aram says no storm ever starts without it.
city.px.plaque.l1: A wooden stand by the rail: rules, the tower's history, a slightly faded diagram. The edges of the notice are pinned with a rusty clip.
city.px.scope.clear: It is clear, and at the very edge of the water a thin strip has appeared: the far shore. One dark smudge, then another, forests probably. I wrote it down: "far shore".
city.px.scope.d1: The telescope points straight out to sea. The horizon is ruler-straight. Just left of the range marks there is a dark speck: a fisherman at his net. The way he nods his head, he is singing.
city.px.scope.d2: I turned the focus: the waves broke into separate crests, each with its own white tail. I watched them run to the pier for a minute and lost count.
city.px.scope.d3: At the weekend the sea is full of sails: white triangles tacking back and forth, nobody in a hurry. One almost ran into a buoy and swung away neatly.
city.px.scope.dawn: The sun climbs straight out of the water, red as a yolk. The telescope filled with gold and I had to look away. Against it the gulls are black, as if cut from paper.
city.px.scope.ferry: A ferry! White, with two funnels, following the channel. Tiny figures on deck wave at something behind me, the lighthouse probably. I waved back, though it could not see me.
city.px.scope.fog: The telescope shows milk. But from far off comes a horn, muffled as if from a jar. A ferry, maybe, or just the fog joking.
city.px.scope.n1: At night the telescope shows only lights. Green, red, white: somebody's seiner is heading home and its lights line up into an arrow.
city.px.scope.n2: There is a moon path on the water with a black speck crawling along it. If I rock the telescope a little, the path trembles like a string.
city.px.scope.rain: The rain walks across the sea like a wall. You can see it crawl toward the pier: a grey curtain far off, then a line on the water, then the first drops on my lens.
city.px.scope.stars: I tilted the telescope up. The stars in it are not dots but tiny sharp needles. One right at the horizon flickers red, green and white: the keepers say low stars always do.
city.px.ships.1: The table of ships' lights: white masthead, red to port, green to starboard. By day a seiner on the sea: a dark silhouette and a flock of gulls over it.
city.px.ships.2: Far off a passenger steamer crawls: white as sugar and as small. By the table, at night it will show three white lights and a red and a green.
city.px.ships.3: A barge along the shore, a thread of smoke, riding low. The table: "Tug with tow: two masthead lights in line." Checked: true, down to the last detail.
city.px.ships.4: An empty sea, only glints. The keepers joke that on days like this you look for ships and find thoughts. I found one, but it was a small one.
city.px.ships.5: At night two lights side by side on the water, red and green: a ship heading straight at me. By the table it's bound for the pier, but not yet, another forty minutes.
city.px.ships.6: A white light low over the horizon, another a little higher: a seiner, fishing. The lantern beams rock on the water with her side.
city.px.ships.7: A single green light at the very edge. By the table: starboard side, the vessel is going left. I wished it were Maria, and was surprised how easily the wish came.
city.px.ships.8: Darkness, only the beam touching the water once every twenty seconds. Between beams the dark is so thick it seems alive and very attentive.
city.px.signal.1: By day the lamp is hardly seen. I clacked the shutter three times anyway: "I'm here." Someone in the port waved a red rag: the tug's mechanic, probably.
city.px.signal.2: At night the lamp strikes like a fist: three flashes toward the sea. A blink came back from the horizon. My heart went thump with it and kept the rhythm a long while.
city.px.storm.1: A painting: a stormy sea and a lone seiner on a crest. Pencilled on the frame: "Not ours, but very like Maria." The painter clearly saw a storm up close.
city.px.storm.2: By lamplight the waves in the painting seem alive. Look long enough and the seiner is about to vanish behind a crest. I looked away first.
city.px.stove.1: I lit the little stove with birch logs. The kettle starts to hum before I've found a mug. I poured myself some and slipped a second helping into my pocket.
city.px.stove.2: The kettle puffs and the shadow of its lid jumps on the wall. It smells of smoke and dried mint from a tin. Good strong tea, with sea salt in the air.
city.px.stove.3: The night watch begins with the kettle. The fire crackles softly in the stove while above the ceiling the light slowly turns. The tea came out nearly as good as the keepers'.
city.px.text.gb.title: Visitors' book
city.px.text.hist.title: About the tower
city.px.tides.1: Monday. High water at the pier 06:40 and 19:05, low water 00:30 and 12:50. In chalk: "Order chalk."
city.px.tides.2: Tuesday. High water 07:25 and 19:50, low 01:15 and 13:35. By evening the mussels on the piles will show: enough for supper.
city.px.tides.3: Wednesday. High water 08:10 and 20:35, low 02:00 and 14:20. A note below: "Boatmen: toward eight there's a pull under the pier."
city.px.tides.4: Thursday. High water 08:55 and 21:20, low 02:45 and 15:05. The figures are written clearly, as for an exam.
city.px.tides.5: Friday. High water 09:40 and 22:05, low 03:30 and 15:50. In the corner a little fish is drawn, winking at the reader.
city.px.tides.6: Saturday. High water 10:25 and 22:50, low 04:15 and 16:35. Saturday's tide is the longest: Aram says even the sea is in no hurry.
city.px.tides.7: Sunday. High water 11:10 and 23:35, low 05:00 and 17:20. Underlined in red: "Many people on the promenade by evening. Ring the bell softly."
city.px.v1.d: Open sea here, all the way to the horizon. A dark band of channel runs over the water, the buoys beside it standing like dots, as if someone started drawing a line and gave up.
city.px.v1.n: Dark water and lights: red on the shoal, green on the buoy, yellow on a far ship. The wind carries salt and wet iron.
city.px.v1.w: Rain drums on the rail and runs down the iron. The channel shows only by its lights. The gulls sit on the buoys one each, like stamps on a document.
city.px.v2.d: On this side the shore runs off into dunes. The pines on the ridge lean all one way, as if the wind combed them once and left them. The beach is empty and golden.
city.px.v2.n: The dunes are black on dark blue. A campfire flickers on the beach and the wind brings smoke and baked potatoes. Someone sings to a guitar, the words lost.
city.px.v2.w: The fog has eaten the dunes and left only the pine tops. They float in the milk like islands.
city.px.v3.d: From here the town's roofs show: red, grey, one green. Columns of smoke over the chimneys, the wind sending it toward the woods today. Something glints between the houses: windows catching the sun.
city.px.v3.n: The town at night: the windows go out one by one, a few still lit. I picked one and began to imagine who is awake there. I decided: someone with a book.
city.px.v3.w: Snow settles on the roofs evenly, like flour. Every house has grown one cap taller and the smoke goes straight up.
city.px.v4.d: The promenade lies like a palm: benches, kiosks, people the size of grains. Over it the cable car cabins crawl, one down, one up, and for a moment they pass each other in the air.
city.px.v4.n: The promenade glows with a garland of lamps. The cable car cabins crawl in a string of lights, and from afar it looks like fireflies drawn along a thread.
city.px.v4.w: In the rain the promenade empties, but umbrellas bloom like flowers: yellow, red, one checked. The cabins go through the rain with their lights on.
city.px.watch.1: The clockwork's watch book. "06:10. Wind south-west, force four, visibility good. Seiner Maria sailed for herring, promised to be back tomorrow by evening. Arkady."
city.px.watch.2: "21:00. We wait for Maria till midnight. The light was lit twenty minutes early: let them see it from far off. Aram."
city.px.watch.3: "23:50. No Maria. The radio is silent. The barometer is falling. I wound the clockwork every four hours, not only by the book. Arkady."
city.px.watch.4: "04:00. Storm. We ring the bell every two minutes, a second night running. Hands shaking, but it rings. Told the port by radio: Maria not seen. Aram."
city.px.watch.5: "A night without sleep, the beam runs true, the gale never knocked it off once. The kettle is empty, the bread gone. If anyone comes in, please make us tea. Arkady."
city.px.watch.6: "05:20. It's eased. A faint voice on the radio: 'Lighthouse, this is Maria. Engine failed, we drifted a day. We saw your light. Coming to you.' Aram wept, Arkady pretended not to notice."
city.px.watch.7: "18:40. Maria is at the pier. Captain Laptev left a bottle by the door, a note inside. Put it on the shelf by the little ship. The bell rang this time for nothing: for joy."
city.px.watch.8: "Quiet. A day off by order of both of us. Wrote verses: Aram offered the rhyme 'came back, grinned back', Arkady rejected it, but wrote it down just in case."
city.px.weather.1: Barometer: 1018, the needle planted. Thermometer: nine. Humidity middling. Everything promises a fine day and a dull watch. Pencilled beside it: "Maria sailed."
city.px.weather.2: Barometer: 1014. The needle has crept a hair to the left, or I imagined it. I tapped the glass: it holds. On the card: "Check again this evening."
city.px.weather.3: Barometer: 1006, and the needle is crawling as I watch. Aram's note: "Hand the watch over with sandwiches. It will be noisy tonight." Under it, Arkady's: "Noisy and long."
city.px.weather.4: Barometer: 998. The needle presses against the word "Storm" and trembles. The glass is hairlined from old tapping. Someone has stuck a slip beside it: "Don't tap. It knows."
