city.san.duty.night: The night nurse looks up from her book: “Can't sleep? There is hot milk in the flask. But quietly: everyone here is asleep, even those who say they are not.”
city.san.duty.quiet: The nurse whispers and writes on a slip: “Quiet hour. Keys on the hook, tea at the buffet.” You read it and keep quiet too.
city.san.evening.day: The lobby by day. The parquet by the door is polished to a shine, and on a little table by the wall a gramophone sits under its lid. A sign: "Dances and lectures in the evening. Programme at the reception."
city.san.evening.early: Evening is near. Guests drift into the lobby: some with a book, some with chess, some just to look at people.
city.san.evening.fest: On a holiday the parquet is polished to a shine. The nurse puts on a record and everyone dances the first waltz, even those who came for a thermometer.
city.san.evening.fri: Friday, tea with music. The gramophone plays old ballads, then a jazz band. Guests drink tea and discuss the weather, which is wonderful today, and of course that is their doing.
city.san.evening.late: The lobby at night: the parquet is dark, the gramophone sleeps under its lid. The night attendant leafs through a ledger and nods: "Quietly, please, people are resting."
city.san.evening.prompt: E — look in on the lobby evening
city.san.evening.rain: In the rain the evening in the lobby is thicker than usual: armchairs have been brought from the winter garden and the parquet cleared for dancers and spectators alike.
city.san.evening.sat1: Saturday dancing! The receptionist winds the gramophone and guests in indoor shoes circle on the parquet. A waltz, then a foxtrot, then another waltz, because they ask for it.
city.san.evening.sat2: I dance too: awkwardly at first, then however it goes. An elderly watchmaker leads his partner like an engineer building a bridge. She smiles: the bridge will hold.
city.san.evening.wed: Wednesday, the doctor's lecture "How to Sleep So That You Wake Rested". The listeners sit along the walls. The doctor says the main secret is not to think about sleep. Half the hall has already thought about sleep and fallen asleep.
city.san.ex.1: In the mornings people do their exercises on the parquet by the door, to the radio: arms out, breathe in, breathe out. Now it is empty, only squares of light.
city.san.ex.closed: The parquet by the door is empty. On the wall: 'Exercises from 7 to 9. The nurse on duty switches the radio on.'
city.san.ex.draw.1: Half the exercises on the beat, half by inspiration. The doctor calls it an 'individual rhythm'.
city.san.ex.fest: On a holiday the exercises have music: the winter-garden piano plays instead of the radio and everybody pretends it is how it should be.
city.san.ex.lose.1: You lost the count at the second beat. The radio did not take offence: it simply went on counting.
city.san.ex.lose.2: Your arms went up before the music. The neighbour on the parquet smiled and showed how it is done.
city.san.ex.morning: The radio counts: 'And one, and two!' Guests in slippers swing their arms like windmills. Try to keep up.
city.san.ex.prompt: E — morning exercises on the parquet
city.san.ex.rain: When it rains the exercises move from the veranda to the parquet and there is little room: you have to wave your arms in turns.
city.san.ex.title: Morning exercises
city.san.ex.win.1: You hit the beat three times in a row. The announcer on the radio would approve. The guests applaud with their slippers.
city.san.ex.win.2: Crisp as a ruler: shoulders level, breathing calm. The stamp went onto the treatment card at once.
city.san.garden_read.1: I settle into the armchair among the palms. The morning sun lays the window squares on the pages. I notice I am reading the same line for the third time: it is that pleasant.
city.san.garden_read.2: In the afternoon the garden is quiet and warm and smells of earth and tea. Somewhere in the pipes water murmurs. I read a chapter and dozed a little over the next one.
city.san.garden_read.3: In the evening one small lamp burns in the garden and the leaves on the panes look like ink blots. Reading is hard, but listening to the quiet is easy.
city.san.garden_read.quiet: Quiet hour: the pages are turned with two fingers. In exchange you can hear the water gurgling in the pipes.
city.san.garden_read.rain: When it rains the winter garden is full: a book by every armchair, a listener by every palm. You count the drops on the glass along with everyone.
city.san.gwin.clear: From the winter garden the courtyard shows through the palms: deck chairs set round the fountain, and it seems they are sunbathing too.
city.san.gwin.day: From the winter-garden window you see the courtyard: the fountain, the lawn and the windows opposite. The palms stand by the glass like spectators.
city.san.gwin.night: At night the winter-garden glass turns into a mirror: the palms, you, and somewhere deeper the lights of the windows opposite.
city.san.gwin.rain: Rain taps on the glass and the courtyard is empty. But the winter garden is full: someone with a book, someone with a chess rook, someone just watching the water run down.
city.san.gwin.snow: The courtyard is white and round. The fountain wears a cap of snow, the deck chairs are in the shed and lights burn in the windows opposite.
city.san.labels.1: A plate by the palm: "Fan palm. Called Galina Petrovna. Brought by train in 1974, travelled in the compartment with the conductor and complained of draughts. Please do not stroke the leaves."
city.san.labels.2: A plate: "Monstera. Name: Boris. Grown from a cutting a guest gave on leaving. The card said: 'Let it grow, since I cannot.'"
city.san.labels.3: A plate by the arch: "Ficus Semyon. The garden's oldest resident. His leaves are wiped with a damp cloth on Fridays, and he has never once complained."
city.san.labels.4: A plate: "Cacti Petya and Pasha. They flower once in three years, usually at night. Last time both bloomed at once, and the night attendant stood watch beside them till morning."
city.san.labels.5: A plate: "Fern. No name. Naming it has been proposed many times, but every guest proposes their own. On the list: Klava, Motya, Elvira and 'The one on the left'."
city.san.labels.6: A plate by the door: "It is always +22 in the winter garden. The plants are used to it, and so are the guests. If you feel cold, it is not the garden."
city.san.let.1: 'Huseyn Rashidovich! I am writing on the back of the daily regime, there is no other paper. If you are reading this, I have once again left a letter where it will be found sooner than it should be. — V. L.'
city.san.let.2: 'About the rook. Do not look for it in the administrator's drawer: I have it. I took it by accident while you were thinking aloud. I return it with the game in which you did checkmate me after all. Show nobody.'
city.san.let.3: 'The notebook on the piano can be played. You copied the third bar with a mistake: it is F sharp there, not G. I did not correct it. Now when I reach that place I can hear you thinking aloud.'
city.san.let.4: 'At Mayak a goods train passes at 4:10 every day. When it has gone, the clock stays in the pump room and the piano in the garden. Come on the next intake. I will take 3-14 and you 2-09. If the rooms are taken I shall go to the treatment room: there is a couch and a screen. — V. L.'
city.san.letter.1: An envelope without a stamp lies on the table. There is no address, only 'G. R.' and a small chess rook in place of a full stop.
city.san.menu.fri: Menu, Friday. Pickle soup, meatballs in tomato, pasta, kefir for supper. The guests' opinion: the meatballs were better last week. The cook's opinion: it is the same every week.
city.san.menu.mon: Menu, Monday. Vegetable soup, steamed cutlet with mash, dried-fruit compote, a cabbage pie.
city.san.menu.sat: Menu, Saturday: festive lunch. Cold kefir soup, chicken Kiev, a 'potato' chocolate cake. There is dancing after lunch, so be careful with the cake.
city.san.menu.sun: Menu, Sunday. Pancakes with sour cream and jam in the morning, chicken broth, a casserole, tea with lemon. Second helpings come without questions.
city.san.menu.thu: Menu, Thursday. Cabbage soup, chicken pilaf, beetroot salad, compote. The pilaf is made by a cook who sailed as a ship's cook on a freighter before the sanatorium.
city.san.menu.tue: Menu, Tuesday. Borscht (sour cream only on a doctor's prescription), fish in marinade, buckwheat, tea.
city.san.menu.wed: Menu, Wednesday: fish day. Fish soup, pike-perch with potatoes, cranberry kissel. Whoever dislikes fish gets an apple and sympathy.
city.san.oxygen.1: The white cylinder hissed and the glass filled with pink foam to the brim. It tastes like a cloud with raspberry. My head went light and a little giddy.
city.san.oxygen.2: The cocktail came in a tall glass: foam on top, raspberry syrup underneath. A sign: "No more than two a day: after the third you start talking to the flowers."
city.san.oxygen.closed: The oxygen bar is closed: the flask is covered with a napkin and a note on it says: 'The cloud works from 10 to 19.'
city.san.oxygen.quiet: In quiet hour the barman serves the cocktail in silence, hands over a straw and puts a finger to his lips.
city.san.oxygen.rain: Rain, and the queue for oxygen is made of pyjamas and umbrellas. The barman only nods and whips up the foam.
city.san.pclock.time: The pump-room clock is running and the nurse points a finger at it: it is {time}. The 'Do not touch' sign is still there but now it is about the time, not the clock.
city.san.quartz.1: The doctor gave me dark goggles and told me not to look at the lamp. I want to look anyway: it is blue and hums softly like a hive. After five minutes I was warm, as after the sea.
city.san.quartz.2: The lamp came on with a click. "No more than ten minutes," said the doctor, "and don't fall asleep." I didn't. Almost.
city.san.quartz.3: Under the lamp my skin glows and my head goes quiet. The doctor explains it is good for the joints, the mood and 'generally'. 'Generally' is the key word of medicine.
city.san.quartz.4: The goggles sit funnily, like an aviator's. In the wall mirror I see a patient in blue light who looks far healthier than I do.
city.san.quartz.closed: The lamp is under a cloth cover. A note: 'Quartz on weekdays from 9 to 17. Do not take the goggles away.'
city.san.quartz.prompt: E — sit under the quartz lamp
city.san.quartz.quiet: The doctor switches the lamp on without a click and whispers the minutes. In quiet hour the blue light seems especially quiet.
city.san.quiet.1: An armchair by the palms. Until quiet hour it is just an armchair and you are just sitting in it. Pleasant, but no stamp.
city.san.quiet.2: Quiet hour. Nobody in the garden speaks, not even the palms. You hear the fountain dripping far off and the notebook lying quietly on the piano. A stamp for the card.
city.san.quiet.3: Quiet hour ended long ago but the armchair is still quiet. You can sit and think that tomorrow will be a day by the regime.
city.san.quiet.4: The nurse passes on tiptoe, puts a glass of water on the table and vanishes. You had no time to thank her, but it seems you do not have to. A stamp for the card.
city.san.quiet.prompt: E — sit for the quiet hour
city.san.quiet.rain: When it rains the garden is full: a quiet person in every armchair and nobody rustling a newspaper.
city.san.radio.1: The radio at the head of the couch plays dance music quietly. The announcer reads the forecast: south-west wind, sea state two, mood excellent.
city.san.radio.2: At night the radio plays under its breath: first a waltz, then a lullaby, then the time signals. A good accompaniment for counting sheep and waiting for morning.
city.san.reg.1: A new notice: "Please do not close the lid of the winter-garden piano. The instrument has to breathe, and in the evenings it is opened for playing."
city.san.reg.10: 'An envelope without a stamp has been found; it lies on the lounge table in the lobby. The owner may collect it. Everybody else is asked not to read it... at least until lunch.'
city.san.reg.2: "The pump-room clock has stopped. The repairman has been called three times: he comes, looks and leaves with a sad face. The healing water runs on schedule regardless."
city.san.reg.3: "Dancing in the lobby on Saturdays at 19:00. Bring indoor shoes, records and a good mood. Trodden feet are a matter for your partner, not the receptionist."
city.san.reg.4: "Wednesdays at 18:00, the doctor's lecture 'How to Sleep So That You Wake Rested'. Free entry. Please do not leave until the lecturer wakes up." The last sentence is crossed out but still readable.
city.san.reg.5: "Found: a chess rook, either ivory or very good plastic. It waits for its owner in the receptionist's drawer. The owner is asked first to say what colour it is."
city.san.reg.6: "The pump-room clock is running! Please do not touch the hands, and do not be late: it shows now." Next to it another: "Thanks to G. R. Aliyev from the staff and from the water."
city.san.reg.7: "V. S. Lunz and G. R. Aliyev have checked out. A notebook of music is left on the winter-garden piano. Request: do not take it away, play it. The management."
city.san.reg.8: 'The guest's treatment card is issued by the doctor. Six treatments, six stamps. Whoever fills every square gets the doctor's word and tea at the sanatorium's expense.'
city.san.reg.9: 'Draughts on the round table in the pump room, dominoes on the lounge table in the lobby. Please play in pairs and do not help the spectators.'
city.san.regime.1: "Daily regime. Morning: 7:30 exercises, 8:00 thermometer and weighing, 8:30 breakfast." Underneath, by hand: "Whoever slept through exercises slept through them with pleasure."
city.san.regime.2: "Daily regime. Before lunch: 9:00 pump room, first glass (small sips), 10:00 treatments as prescribed, 11:00 oxygen cocktail, 12:00 a walk along the promenade. Heal without hurry."
city.san.regime.3: "Daily regime. 13:00 lunch. 14:00 quiet hour." The word "quiet" is underlined twice, and beside it someone has drawn a kettle and written: "Shhh."
city.san.regime.4: "Daily regime. 15:30 second glass at the pump room, 16:00 afternoon snack, 17:00 chess, books, letters home, 18:00 free time: the sea, a bench or the clouds, your choice."
city.san.regime.5: "Daily regime. 19:00 supper. 20:00 evening in the lobby: a doctor's lecture on Wednesdays, tea with music on Fridays, dancing on Saturdays. The other evenings are quiet, as they should be."
city.san.regime.6: "Daily regime. 22:00 lights out. Silence in the corridors, silence in the pump room, silence on the piano." In small letters below: "The night attendant stays awake and will tell nobody who went for water."
city.san.regime.fest: A slip is pinned to the daily regime: 'On holidays the regime is the same, but the music is louder. The doctor has allowed one extra pie.'
city.san.text.brochure.title: The sanatorium leaflet
city.san.text.card.title: The treatment card
city.san.text.ledger.title: The guest book
city.san.text.letter.title: The unstamped letter
city.san.trolley.1: On the trolley are books left by guests: a coverless Martin Eden, three crosswords filled in with pencil to the last square, a cookbook with a jam stain on the pancake page.
city.san.trolley.2: Someone's bookmark in Martin Eden: a cable-car ticket. Yesterday's date. So the reader is still here, with about fifteen pages left.
city.san.trolley.3: A book about sea salt: "Salt is the only stone that people eat." In the margin in pencil: "Checked. True."
city.san.trolley.4: A 1979 issue of the magazine Health, the article "How Not to Fear the Doctor". Someone circled the title and wrote: "Didn't help, but it was fun."
city.san.trolley.5: A thin booklet, "Reading Music in One Evening". The pages are worn through, with fingers and numbers drawn in the margins. On the cover, a signature: "V. L."
city.san.trolley.6: A book of chess problems. A slip is tucked into page 41: "Mate in three. Guseyn Rashidovich, it can be solved. Don't be cross." Below, a crossed-out answer: "No peeking."
city.sch.apples.1: The crate of apples stands by the line like a small red warehouse. "Take one, we will eat the rest ourselves," is written on the lid.
city.sch.apples.2: I picked an apple with a small dark side: those, they say in the canteen, have the sweetest character. I wiped it on my sleeve and bit into it on the move.
city.sch.bag.1: Behind the mats in the corner hides a blue bag. The strap is worn, "L.K." in ink on the side, a sneaker's sole sticking out of the pocket. Found it, it seems.
city.sch.bag.2: The bag smells of rubber and a banana that has probably lived here since Friday. The sneakers inside: one laced, one not. The owner was in a hurry.
city.sch.bag.3: I put the bag on the bench by the gym door where it can be seen. Someone will collect it.
city.sch.balls.1: The ball cart: two red balls, a yellow one, a white volleyball and a blue one, apparently from another planet. I took a red one: it knows how to lie in the palm.
city.sch.balls.2: The ball hit the floor with a boom and the echo answered from every corner of the hall. One ball was left in the cart, and it rolled lazily aside as if everything was already clear.
city.sch.balls.3: At the bottom of the cart I found a smooth pebble and a note: "This is not a ball. But someone brought it here, so it must stay." I left it.
city.sch.bbio.1: On the board, a heart with four chambers in chalk. Two are labelled; the other two say "we'll sort it out."
city.sch.bbio.2: On the board, the structure of a leaf: stalk, veins, green arrows everywhere. At the bottom: "Whoever picked a leaf off the ficus knows."
city.sch.bbio.3: No biology today. On the board, yesterday's skeleton in a funny pose, and someone has drawn it a hat.
city.sch.bbio.4: In the empty room the board says only: "Water the plants! Duty pupils." The plants, by the way, are alive.
city.sch.bell.1: I rang it so loudly that three heads looked out from behind a classroom door at once. First lesson: don't be late.
city.sch.bell.2: I rang in the middle of a lesson. A teacher looked out of the nearest door, regarded me, and quietly shut it. She said nothing, but she will remember.
city.sch.bell.3: The bell ran as an echo through the emptying corridors. Somebody laughed far away: "You again!"
city.sch.bell.4: In an empty school the bell sounds different, longer than by day. I put it back and went on tiptoe.
city.sch.bl.1: Tuesday, biology. The teacher takes a live leaf of waterweed from a jar, puts it under the microscope and asks us to find a single cell that is in no hurry. Nobody found one.
city.sch.bl.2: Friday, biology. We draw a leaf: stalk, veins, edges. My vein came out longer than the leaf itself, and the teacher said that is called an artist's vision.
city.sch.bl.3: Thursday, chemistry. Red cabbage in a glass turns pink with vinegar and green with soda. The whole class gasped in chorus and the teacher calmly said: "Write it down." We wrote with our mouths open.
city.sch.bl.4: There is no lesson in the biology room today. The stools are pushed in, the benches hold clean sheets and the aquarium blows bubbles so solemnly it might be giving its own lecture.
city.sch.choir.1: Tuesday, rehearsal. The choir leader raises a hand and the class breathes in all at once: "Song about the Sea." I stand in the second row and catch myself singing a little louder than I meant to.
city.sch.choir.2: Thursday: the second voice finally comes in on time and the first stays quiet, as agreed. The choir leader shuts her eyes in happiness and says "once more" twice.
city.sch.choir.3: The tuning fork rings and everyone goes quiet for a second, listening to it let the note go. Then someone in the back row asks softly: "Do we really have to go that high?"
city.sch.cloak.1: "I have more tags than children, and still someone comes without a tag but with a description. 'Blue, with a hood, smells of bun.' I find it. The jacket smelled of bun."
city.sch.cloak.2: "The owner collects the red coat with the hare on the sleeve every day at exactly 13:41. You could set a clock by her. If the coat is not there, it is either Saturday or a catastrophe."
city.sch.cloak.3: "The striped scarf has hung here since October. I straighten it sometimes so it does not look completely alone. Perhaps its owner will remember."
city.sch.cloak.hello: The cloakroom attendant peeps out from behind the racks as if from the wings. "Come in, dear. Jacket on the hook, hat in the sleeve, or it will get lost again."
city.sch.cloak.rain: "Wet things I hang apart, by the radiator. Otherwise the whole cloakroom smells like a flock of sheep after a storm. And that is not the smell you want to take into a lesson."
city.sch.cloak.snow: "Shake the snow off your boots onto the mat, not the floor. The mat is hurt enough that nobody ever thanks it."
city.sch.clock.1: The clock over the back door of the hall says {time}. A plaque under it lists the bells: 1st lesson 8:30, 2nd 9:25, tea break 10:10, 3rd 10:30, 4th 11:25, 5th 12:55, last bell 13:40.
city.sch.clock.2: The clock says {time}. Lessons ended long ago and the hands tiptoe across the empty hall. The plaque of bells is just decoration now: the next one rings tomorrow at 8:30.
city.sch.clock.3: A day off. The clock says {time}, but nobody in the school is in a hurry. The bells on the plaque sleep until Monday, 8:30.
city.sch.clock.4: Evening, the clock says {time}. Only one lamp is lit in the hall, by the watchman. Someone has pencilled under the bell plaque: "At 18:00 the watchman has his tea. Do not disturb."
city.sch.closed.any: The watchman shakes his head from behind his desk: "The school is closed already, and at weekends, as you understand, even more so. Come in school hours, 8 to 16, Monday to Friday."
city.sch.closed.board.1: The notice is behind glass, and on the glass a slip from the watchman: "Reading is allowed in school hours, 8 to 16, on weekdays. In the evenings and at weekends the school is quiet, and even notices try not to rustle."
city.sch.closed.board.2: On the glass of the case someone's curiosity has left a palm print. The watchman has added: "Wipe in the morning." It is too dark to read; the lamp is off until morning.
city.sch.closed.counter.1: The hatch is shut and the light at the counter is off. The watchman nods from the hall: "Everyone has gone. Tomorrow morning. The canteen opens at ten. By that hour the pasties have already decided whom they will go to."
city.sch.closed.craft.1: The school desks stand as after a lesson: stools pushed in, benches clean. The watchman has drawn a smiling sun on the board in chalk: "Until Monday." Or until morning.
city.sch.closed.machine.1: The watchman looks in from the hall: "You touch this in school time, 8 to 16. In the evening everything in the school sleeps: the globe, the bell, the hamster." He speaks quietly so as not to wake anybody.
city.sch.closed.machine.2: Everything is switched off under your hand: the light is out and things are covered. A neat slip on the handle: "Do not touch till morning." The watchman's hand, he makes the letters square.
city.sch.closed.play.1: The checkers and chessmen are in the box. A note on the board: "The games are unfinished but are not going anywhere. Come in school hours." The watchman, it seems, counts the pieces in the evenings.
city.sch.closed.play.2: No rackets, no balls, no opponent. Only a table with the net neatly set and a slip: "At weekends the hall is open for sport in the mornings. The table waits."
city.sch.closed.seat.1: The chairs stand in rows, as if obediently waiting for tomorrow's lesson. Sitting is not allowed today: the school is closed, and the watchman himself regards them with respect.
city.sch.closed.shelf.1: The shelf is shut, with the watchman's slip on the door: "The museum and the books during school hours. At night they read to themselves." The door creaked, of course, but said nothing.
city.sch.closed.sport.1: The hall is locked against light and sound. The balls are in the cart, under lock. On the door in pencil: "8 to 19, Monday to Saturday." The watchman is, in general, always right.
city.sch.closed.sport.2: In the dark hall you hear only the radiators cooling and a ball sighing in the cart. Everything that could be done here has been done until morning.
city.sch.closed.take.1: The crate of apples is covered with a clean cloth: "Until tomorrow." The watchman, they say, counts the apples in the evenings, but the apples, they say, do not mind.
city.sch.clubs.1: The notice stand. Monday: young naturalists' club, biology room, 16:00-18:00. Bring empty pickle jars and patience.
city.sch.clubs.2: Tuesday: choir, music room, 16:00-18:00. We are learning "Song about the Sea". Those afraid to sing may stand in the back row and move their lips without a sound.
city.sch.clubs.3: Wednesday: chess club, the first classroom by the entrance, 16:00-18:00. Added below: "Put the pieces back. Especially the rook. Yes, that one."
city.sch.clubs.4: Thursday: choir, music room, 16:00-18:00. "The second voice arrives on time, the first voice does not comment on the second." Signed: the choir leader.
city.sch.clubs.5: Friday: young naturalists, 16:00-18:00. Topic: "What grows on the dunes and why we do not pick it". For the most curious, a walk to the sea after the club.
city.sch.clubs.6: Saturday and Sunday: no clubs. But the sports hall is open on Saturday mornings to anyone who can walk quietly. That is written down too.
city.sch.coats.1: The racks are stuffed: checked jackets, a red coat with an embroidered hare, three hats on one hook. Under the bench, a brood of indoor shoes.
city.sch.coats.2: The hooks are nearly empty. On one hangs a forgotten scarf, long and striped, smelling of autumn. It waits for its owner.
city.sch.coats.3: The empty cloakroom smells of wet wool and cooling radiators. Only the scarf on its hook has not lost hope.
city.sch.coats.4: A sleeve sticks out of the red coat with the hare, and something is breathing in the sleeve: small, even and very content. The cloakroom lady pretends to straighten the tags and tries very hard not to look.
city.sch.concert.1: Poster: "On Saturday at 15:00 in the gym, the school concert. Everyone who failed to hide will sing. Performing: a girl from 8A (piano), the spoon orchestra of 5B."
city.sch.concert.2: A handwritten addition: "The Song about the Sea needs a second pianist. Rehearsals every day after sixth period. Metronome provided."
city.sch.drawers.1: Top drawer: a ruler, a red pen without a cap, a box of paper clips, a dried-up orange. The orange has apparently been here a long time and is content.
city.sch.drawers.2: Middle drawer: a stack of tests held with a rubber band, and a note to herself: "Mark by Friday. Not that Friday, the next one."
city.sch.drawers.3: Bottom drawer: confiscated things. A slingshot, a bag of sunflower seeds, bubble gum with a toy plane, and a note: "Don't copy from Misha, he doesn't know either." The note looks oddly familiar.
city.sch.drawers.4: The chalk drawer: white, coloured, and one very tiny piece the teacher saves for the hardest words.
city.sch.drawers.5: At the very bottom, under clean registers, an envelope without a stamp: "If you found this, you are curious. A good sign. Shut the drawer and do not tell anyone."
city.sch.dt.1: "The bell is in my hand. I write down the late ones, but always kindly. The record of the week came four minutes after the bell with a bun and an iron argument: the bun was warm."
city.sch.dt.2: "Look into the lost-property box more often: things get sad there when nobody comes. And if you are looking for something important, ask the cloakroom lady. She remembers everything, even what never happened."
city.sch.dt.3: "The concert poster hangs on the wall, and the concert, as usual, comes sooner than anyone is ready. If you want to help, go to the music room. We always have fewer pianists than pianos."
city.sch.dt.hello: The duty teacher looks up from the register. "Hello. Come in, but do not run: this is neither a stadium nor a station, though it looks like both."
city.sch.dt.rain: "It is raining, so remember your indoor shoes and wipe your feet, all right? The cleaner has enough to do as it is."
city.sch.dt.studious: The duty teacher turns a page and smiles. "I hear you have been going to all sorts of lessons. In our school that is called curiosity, and it earns an unmarked top grade."
city.sch.duty.1: The school duty log. Entries in a column: "8:10 opened the doors. 8:25 Petrov late, but with flowers. 9:40 the pointer broke in 5A; the pointer was mended."
city.sch.duty.2: "Remarks: a blue bag with gym shoes has gone missing from the cloakroom. Please check the lost-and-found box." Beside it: "Checked already. No."
city.sch.duty.3: "Duty rules: greet at the door, keep shoes off the wet floor, answer the bell on time, answer questions politely." Someone has added: "and patiently."
city.sch.duty.4: On the last page, in a child's hand: "If you're on duty, don't panic. The bell doesn't bite." Next to it, a drawing of a bell with teeth.
city.sch.gdraw.basket.1: Half the throws went in. The coach, who is not here, would have nodded anyway: "Not bad for someone who came without a warm-up."
city.sch.gdraw.checkers.1: A draw at checkers: both kings are still on the board and each side decided it had won morally. The game was put off until the next break.
city.sch.gdraw.chess.1: A draw. King against king, pawn against pawn and nobody ready to give way. It was decided the game was too good to finish.
city.sch.gdraw.tt.1: A draw: the score was, as on the scoreboard, nil-nil in the last game. My partner said the real rally stayed in our palms anyway.
city.sch.glass.1: A rack of six test tubes: three with water, one with water tinted red, two empty. Next to it a flask with a rubber stopper and a card: "Experiment No. 4. Do not drink."
city.sch.glass.2: The test tubes ring against each other when a tram passes, that is, when somebody passes too fast. If anything in a chemistry room can be loved, it is that ring.
city.sch.glass.3: A sheet attached to the rack: "Red cabbage + vinegar = pink, + soda = green. Show Mum only after the experiment." Sounds like a rule for life.
city.sch.glass.4: Thursday, chemistry. The tubes are filled with cabbage juice: one pink, one blue, one green, and the fourth is still neutral and waits to be persuaded.
city.sch.globe.1: The globe creaks on its axis. My finger stopped on the Pacific, where, as usual, there is not a single town.
city.sch.globe.2: I looked for our bay on the globe. Or rather for the place where it ought to be: no Lyudmilovsk, not even a dot. The scale let us down.
city.sch.globe.3: I spun it too hard: Africa merged with Antarctica and Australia turned into a rainbow for a second. I braked with my palm.
city.sch.globe.4: Under the stand a slip of paper: "Do not spin during tests." The paper has yellowed, so the rule is old and our parents broke it too.
city.sch.glock.1: I struck the bars with the beater. Out comes do-re-mi, then the bars ask for a breather. My palm remembers the metal's tremble for a long time.
city.sch.glock.2: I played the first bars of "Song about the Sea": slowly, with one finger and three mistakes. Somebody from the next room picked it up, and there were fewer mistakes.
city.sch.glock.3: I hit the longest bar: the note hums and hums until it dissolves into the radiator. With my eyes closed it sounds like a small bell in a small harbour.
city.sch.glose.basket.1: A miss. The ball hit the backboard, bounced as if thinking it over and rolled to the bench. The bench took it without comment.
city.sch.glose.checkers.1: I lost at break: the checkers were put in the box and carried off until next time. The bell rang at the perfect moment, as if on purpose.
city.sch.glose.chess.1: I lost, but beautifully: the queen went first and the king tried to keep his dignity for another minute. My opponent held out a hand: "A good game. Shall we play again?"
city.sch.glose.tt.1: I lost: the ball made an elegant arc and went past the table, into the hall, under the mats. We searched together and found it in a shoe. The shoe was not mine.
city.sch.gwin.basket.1: I sank the ball: it went through the ring so quietly that the net only sighed. Someone in a corner of the hall said a soft "wow", and that "wow" was worth more points.
city.sch.gwin.checkers.1: I won a game of checkers in the hall: my opponent stared at the board a long time, then shook my hand and said it was not a clean win, but a very beautiful one.
city.sch.gwin.chess.1: I won the game: the player opposite said nothing for a long time, then said "hm", which in school chess counts as the highest praise. The pieces went back to their places, even the rook.
city.sch.gwin.tt.1: I won at table tennis: the last ball clipped the edge of the table, hung for a moment and still fell on my side. The echo in the hall applauded first.
city.sch.gz.child: An issue for Children's Day: "Today the children are in charge and the teachers are helpers. Tomorrow everything is as usual, but today the duty pupils may ring the bell once without blushing."
city.sch.gz.cold: The "Weather" column: "Frost. Hats are compulsory. The hamster advises wearing two. The hamster, as is well known, knows warmth." Under it are drawn two hats on one head.
city.sch.gz.fest: A festive issue of the wall newspaper! The whole front page is in coloured squares and in the middle in big letters: "Today is a holiday. Lessons go on, but the mood goes separately."
city.sch.gz.newyear: The New Year issue: "The tree in the assembly hall is up, the tinsel hangs, the tree duty has been assigned. The presents are still where they should be: in secret." Stars are drawn round the tree.
city.sch.gz.rain: The "Weather" column: "Rain. Umbrellas to be folded by the door, not in the classroom. 6A went swimming yesterday." Below it a drawing: a little man under an umbrella with a smaller umbrella over him.
city.sch.gz.snow: The "Weather" column: "Snow. The editors ask you not to build snowmen in the hall: they melt before your eyes and cause the cleaner unjustified emotion." A snowman is drawn alongside for clarity.
city.sch.hamster.1: Doughnut the hamster sleeps in his house, only a comma-shaped tail sticking out. A sign on the cage: "Do not wake. He is thinking."
city.sch.hamster.2: Doughnut has stuffed his cheeks with grain until he looks like a little cushion with eyes. He watches me, chews and seems to be deciding whether I deserve a front-row seat.
city.sch.hamster.3: The cage door is ajar and it is empty inside: only the wheel creaks quietly from inertia. A note on the cage: "Doughnut is on holiday. Do not worry. Worry anyway."
city.sch.hamster.4: Doughnut is back. A new lock on the door, a clothes peg, and a paper badge "Escapee" above the house. The hamster sleeps like someone who has fulfilled all his plans for the year.
city.sch.herb.1: Herbarium of 7A: daisy, clover, plantain, a maple leaf with veins drawn on. Calligraphic labels; the plantain's has two spelling mistakes.
city.sch.herb.2: A frame with eelgrass thrown up on the beach by a storm. The card: "Zostera. Collected by Katya L. after the storm of 14 October. Still smells."
city.sch.herb.3: A pine twig with a cone and a tiny dried mushroom. Beneath: "For the lesson on the forest. Do not eat the mushroom."
city.sch.herb.4: An empty frame with a card: "What you find will go here. Do not pick anything protected."
city.sch.honours.1: The honours board: "Best jump: 6B. Best voice: Anna P., 8A. Best lateness: the watchman, who arrived a minute early." An arrow points to a heart.
city.sch.honours.2: Today the board has a photo of the school basketball team. Everyone stands very seriously except a boy at the edge, who is evidently eating an apple and is not ashamed in the least.
city.sch.honours.3: The list "Table tennis, school league". First place: "Lyosha K. (if he finds his bag)". Second: "Someone from 7A, we will clarify". Third: "The ball".
city.sch.honours.4: At the bottom of the sheet someone has pencilled: "The newcomer who goes to every lesson." An eraser lies nearby, but nobody has used it yet. Perhaps nobody will.
city.sch.honours.5: The pencilled line has been traced over in pen: "The newcomer who has been to all the lessons and to the museum." A little star is drawn beneath it. Struck out three times and drawn again.
city.sch.honours.6: A new slip in the corner: "Break winners (checkers, table tennis, basketball): a free pasty on showing your bruises." Signed: "The canteen".
city.sch.lesson.1: Monday, geography. The teacher ran her pointer along our own coast and asked for three towns starting with L. I named two and nearly named the one we were sitting in.
city.sch.lesson.2: Tuesday, literature. We read aloud from Turgenev's night in the meadow. The girl in front read so quietly that even the radiators fell silent.
city.sch.lesson.3: Wednesday, physics. The teacher hung a weight on a thread and said: "Watch how everything comes back." It swung, and we counted the swings and kept losing count.
city.sch.lesson.4: Thursday, history. We heard about the old port. Where our seafront is now, nets used to dry, and every house had its own little jetty.
city.sch.lesson.5: Friday, drawing. We had to draw what we could see from the window. I drew a seagull. My deskmate said it came out as a potato, but a contented one.
city.sch.lesson.6: The first lesson. The room smells of chalk and wet jackets; everyone is still a little asleep with their eyes open.
city.sch.lesson.7: The last lesson. The clock hands crawl a centimetre at a time while the sun is already out strolling. The teacher pretends not to notice our glances.
city.sch.lesson.8: A lesson like any lesson: a squared notebook, a faded blotter and somebody's note: "don't copy from Misha, he doesn't know either."
city.sch.lost.1: The lost-and-found: a mitten (left), a mitten (right, another colour), a seventh-grade geography book bookmarked at the Pacific. The things wait for owners with the patience of old toys.
city.sch.lost.2: Also an unpaired slipper, a spectacle case, a bobble hat and a note: "If the hat is yours, tell us the shape of the bobble."
city.sch.lost.3: No blue gym bag here. But a note is pinned to the box: "Lyosha K., 6B, look in the gym, not here: that's where you last jumped."
city.sch.lost.4: At the bottom: a pencil, a comb and a photograph of an unknown cat. Photographs are what is left in the box most often. Nobody comes for them.
city.sch.mboard.1: A staff in chalk: a clef, four bars and the title "Song about the Sea." Over the third bar a fat question mark.
city.sch.mboard.2: At the bottom: "We take breath from the belly, not from the ears." Next to it, a smiling belly.
city.sch.mboard.3: A notice: "Choir: Tuesday and Thursday after sixth period. Spoon orchestra: as the mood takes it."
city.sch.menu.1: Monday's menu: pea soup, a cutlet with mash, dried-fruit compote. In the corner in chalk: "Bread: unlimited."
city.sch.menu.2: Tuesday: borscht, navy-style pasta, kissel. Today's kissel is so thick the spoon stands up by itself.
city.sch.menu.3: Wednesday is fish day: pickle soup, fish and potatoes, tea. The seagulls have already gathered in the yard with serious faces.
city.sch.menu.4: Thursday: cabbage soup, goulash with buckwheat, compote. Someone added: "Lyudmilovsk-style goulash." Nobody knows what that means.
city.sch.menu.5: Friday: vermicelli soup, cheese pancakes with sour cream, cocoa. Two pancakes per person. Buffet: pies, buns, kefir, apples.
city.sch.menu.6: No menu is written for the weekend: the canteen is closed and the board is wiped squeaky clean. Only a little drawn plate is left in the corner.
city.sch.metro.1: Tick. Tick. Tick. The weight swings to and fro like the pendulum of a very calm clock. It makes you want to breathe in time.
city.sch.metro.2: I slid the weight up: the metronome bustled as if it were late. I slid it down: it sighed and waddled along.
city.sch.metro.3: On the lid are scratched "adagio" and "don't touch if you can't." I can only listen. I listened.
city.sch.ml.1: Monday, music. The teacher plays a single note and asks us to guess how it feels. The class decided the note was tired. The teacher said that was right.
city.sch.ml.2: Thursday, music. We learn a rhythm with palms on knees: one, two, three-e, pause. Nobody can hold the pause. It turns out the hardest thing in music is playing nothing.
city.sch.ml.3: There is no lesson in the music room today, but the chairs stand in a half circle as if waiting for listeners. The piano is covered, but the glockenspiel on the table seems to have winked.
city.sch.museum.1: An abacus with darkened beads. The label: "Used until the school got its first calculating machine, which broke on the third day. The abacus still works."
city.sch.museum.2: A small brass bell with a wooden handle. The caption: "Rang the lessons in until the electric bell came. Rumour has it the duty pupils still secretly love it."
city.sch.museum.3: A non-spill inkwell with a steel nib beside it. The card: "The first letters of our school were written with these. The blots are kept in the notebook next to them. The blots are better than the letters."
city.sch.museum.4: A yellowed photograph: the first graduating class in front of the school, everyone looking in different directions, one boy in the front row chewing a pasty. Caption: "The beginning was the same as it is now."
city.sch.museum.5: A fresh card on the shelf: "Exhibit No. ?? A shell brought from the future. Please do not hold it to your ear: it is quiet in there for now." Someone has put a smaller one next to it.
city.sch.nat.1: Monday, the young naturalists. On the table three pickle jars of soil labelled "peas", "radish", "don't know what". In the third something seems to be climbing already.
city.sch.nat.2: Friday: we discuss the dunes. The club leader draws a wavy line on the board with chalk and says: "This grass holds the whole shore together, which is why we walk on the dunes only along the path."
city.sch.nat.3: Someone brought a jar of seawater and a shell to the club. Something tiny and displeased stirs quietly in it. It is decided to be a crab until proven otherwise.

city.sch.p.balls: E — take a ball from the cart

city.sch.p.glass: E — look over the test tubes
city.sch.p.hamster: E — peek in at the hamster
city.sch.p.lost: E — rummage in the lost-and-found box
city.sch.p.museum: E — look at the school museum shelf
city.sch.p.tea: E — take a glass of tea
city.sch.pend.1: I nudged the brass ball. It went right, came back, went left and was never once late. If you watch long enough you start to think it is you swinging and the ball standing still.
city.sch.pend.2: A paper on the stand: "The period of swing depends on the length of the thread, not on the mass of the ball. Tested with an eraser, a weight and despair." Despair apparently swings too.
city.sch.pend.3: I counted the swings: forty-two, then lost track at forty-three. The teacher says that is normal: that is exactly why clocks were invented.
city.sch.pend.4: Wednesday, physics: the ball is already swinging, a formula stands on the board, and in someone's notebook all the results of the experiment have miraculously agreed. The miracle is marked in red pen.
city.sch.periodic.1: The table of elements in a frame. Hydrogen has been given a pencilled grin in the first cell, and next to gold someone has added "Well, obviously."
city.sch.periodic.2: I found oxygen: eighth, second period. In the margin someone worked out that a person can last about three minutes without it and added: "This is not a record, do not try."
city.sch.periodic.3: A crumb of real salt in a clear bag is glued to sodium. The caption: "Chlorine is not kept in the classroom. Salt is in the canteen. Salt is better anyway."
city.sch.periodic.4: Thursday: a sheet of homework hangs on a nail beside the table: "Name three elements you saw at breakfast today." "Bread" is not accepted as an answer.
city.sch.recital.1: I stepped to the edge of the stage. The hall is empty but the chairs are set out, which is somehow scarier than a full house. I said "hello." The echo said: "...llo."
city.sch.recital.2: I read two quatrains about the sea aloud. At the second, somebody clapped softly from behind the curtain. I turned: no one, only the curtain swaying.
city.sch.recital.3: I took an imaginary microphone and announced: "The Song about the Sea. Performed by the entire coast." I bowed. So did the echo.
city.sch.reg.1: Wall newspaper "Young Lyudmilovsker." Urgent: on Friday after PE a blue bag with gym shoes went missing. Owner: Lyosha K., 6B. A finder gets thanks in the paper and a glass of tea.
city.sch.reg.10: A new notice: a red ball has gone missing from the gym. We assert nothing, but we advise looking under the mats.
city.sch.reg.11: The editors' conclusion of the week: everything in a school turns up, you just have to stop hurrying.
city.sch.reg.12: News from the nature corner. Urgent: Doughnut the hamster opened his cage door at night and left. The door was apparently "not shut by someone." The editors suspect that someone was Doughnut himself.
city.sch.reg.13: The investigation about Doughnut: sawdust trails lead down the corridor towards the cloakroom. The cloakroom lady swears she has not seen him but smiles in a way that makes the editors think.
city.sch.reg.14: Found! Doughnut was asleep in the sleeve of the red coat with the hare, in the warmest corner of the cloakroom. The coat has been checked for crumbs and its owner agrees to share the sleeve.
city.sch.reg.15: The rules of the nature corner are now these: the duty pupils water the flowers, the hamster is fed by the timetable, the door is shut with two hands. The editors thank everyone who searched, and the one who was not lost, just away.
city.sch.reg.2: Column "You asked, we answer": "Why is there no ice cream in the buffet?" Answer: "Because winter starts before summer ends." The editors ask you not to cry.
city.sch.reg.3: The editors have investigated. Questioned: the cloakroom attendant, the duty pupil, the geranium on the sill. It turns out the bag is not in the cloakroom. The search goes on.
city.sch.reg.4: The PE teacher declared that the bag "was definitely there the last time I saw it." The pupils' council formed a search party of two people and one draught.
city.sch.reg.5: Music page. We are preparing the "Song about the Sea" for Saturday's concert. A pianist is needed: the spoon orchestra cannot manage the accompaniment. Ask in the music room.
city.sch.reg.6: The bag hunt: checked the lost-and-found (mitten, mitten, textbook), the cloakroom, the corridor. The gym is not fully searched: the mats are heavy and Lyosha is afraid to look.
city.sch.reg.7: Lyosha K. goes to PE in his socks. The teacher allowed it but asks him not to step on the draughts. The editors wish Lyosha warm weather and somebody's dry sneakers.
city.sch.reg.8: Good news: the bag has been found! It was behind the mats in the gym. Somebody who gave no name brought it to the duty pupil. Lyosha promises never to leave his shoes lying about. We ask the unknown helper to come for a glass of tea.
city.sch.reg.9: The concert took place: the "Song about the Sea" was played twice, the second time at the cloakroom attendant's request. The pianist came out without sheet music and made no mistakes. Almost.
city.sch.run.1: A PE lesson: two lines, a whistle, and the class jogs round the hall. I tagged on at the back and nobody noticed an extra.
city.sch.run.2: After lessons the hall belongs to the club: balls thud, sneakers squeak. I jogged along the edge without getting in the way and got a nod from the coach.
city.sch.run.3: A day off: the hall is draughty and smells of floor polish. The floor is waxed so well you only want to run in socks.
city.sch.run.4: The evening hall is huge and dark. You run and hear only your own steps, with the echo failing to keep up.
city.sch.scope.1: Under the glass, a slice of geranium leaf: green cells stand in even bricks, like our school's wall.
city.sch.scope.2: A fly's leg from the collection: so many hairs that the magnification felt almost impolite.
city.sch.scope.3: The little mirror catches the lamp's light. Somebody left a drop from the aquarium on the slide: unhurried beads drift through it.
city.sch.score.1: The board is frozen at "7 : 5." The girls of 7B are beating the boys, and the PE teacher pretends to referee fairly.
city.sch.score.2: After lessons the board says "0 : 0": basketball club has not started, but someone is already bouncing a ball.
city.sch.score.3: A day off. The board shows "0 : 0," as if the match was put off until Monday.
city.sch.score.4: In the evening the board is dark; the digits only glimmer in the windows. The score is whatever it was.
city.sch.tea.1: The big break. Thick tea with lemon peel comes out of the urn; the duty teacher pours it into a faceted glass and nods: "Just don't run."
city.sch.tea.2: The queue has melted away. The tea in the urn is the colour of old copper, but still hot, and the glass is warm as a mitten.
city.sch.tea.3: The urn is cooling and clicking quietly. Nobody is pouring tea right now.
city.sch.tray.1: Put the tray on the trolley. Spoons in the glass, plates in a stack: the paper on the wall says so, and so does common decency.
city.sch.tray.2: On the top shelf: somebody's unfinished crust and a pencilled note: "Duty pupils, it wasn't me." I didn't investigate.
city.sch.tray.3: The trolley rolled a little: one wheel has a mind of its own. Someone nodded from the serving hatch: a good lad.
city.sch.tt.1: Timetable, Monday: 1. Russian, 2. geography, 3. maths, 4. music, 5. PE. At the bottom in red: "Don't forget your gym shoes!"
city.sch.tt.2: Tuesday: 1. literature, 2. algebra, 3. biology, 4. English, 5. drawing.
city.sch.tt.3: Wednesday: 1. physics, 2. algebra, 3. history, 4. PE, 5. form period. Physics, they say, always sways a little.
city.sch.tt.4: Thursday: 1. history, 2. Russian, 3. chemistry, 4. music, 5. crafts. In crafts the boys go to the workshop and the girls to the kitchen, then the other way round.
city.sch.tt.5: Friday: 1. maths, 2. literature, 3. biology, 4. drawing, 5. double PE. The last bell is at 13:40.
city.sch.tt.6: Saturday and Sunday are not in the timetable. Someone has pencilled under the table: "Thank goodness."
city.sch.tt2.1: "I teach geography and physics because a town by the sea does not have too many teachers either. In geography we trace the coast with a pointer. In physics we swing the pendulum and count how many times the class manages to sigh."
city.sch.tt2.2: "In the bottom drawer of my desk I keep the confiscated things. A slingshot, sunflower seeds, a note: 'I like you, but do not copy.' I will not name the rest. I give them back at the end of the year, and only to parents."
city.sch.tt2.3: "Our school museum stands in the corner. An abacus, an inkwell, a bronze bell. The children bring me all sorts of things for it. Recently someone brought a shell, and now it is 'The first exhibit from the future'."
city.sch.tt2.hello: The teacher looks up from the exercise books and takes off her glasses. "Ah, a visitor. Sit wherever there is room. Just not at the last desk on the left: someone's note lives there, it is three years old."
city.sch.tt2.rain: She looks out of the window. "Rain. Good weather for the pendulum: like us, it likes it when nothing outside distracts it."
city.sch.tt2.studious: The teacher narrows her eyes. "I am told you have already sat through several lessons. Then you know that Tuesday smells of literature and Wednesday of physics. That is the most important thing about our school."
city.sch.watch.1: The watchman looks up from his crossword. "Clubs run till six. If you are looking for a teacher, they are on the bus already. If you want a club, follow the sound down the corridor."
city.sch.watch.2: The watchman nods at the clock. "In the evening you can hear everything in a school: the radiators, steps, the sea thinking beyond the window. I am used to it. The kettle is used to it too, only louder."
city.sch.watch.3: On a day off the watchman is alone in the whole school. "I walk the floors every two hours checking the windows. I say good morning to the hamster. The hamster does not seem to mind."
city.sch.watch.4: "Our bell is electric, and the old brass one lies on the duty desk in case the lights go out. A school without a bell still goes on, only uncertainly."
city.sch.watch.5: "I carry the keys on a ring like a ship's captain. The biggest is for the sports hall. The smallest is for a box with someone's letters, but whose I will not say."
city.sch.watch.6: "The hall has a draught of its own, with character. Sometimes it slams the door as if it was not let in. I do not offend it, I hold the door."
city.sch.watch.fest: The watchman has hung a paper garland on his desk. "A holiday, and the school is still mine. Come in, but no balls in the hall."
city.sch.watch.rain: "The rain knocks on the canopy like a late pupil: softly, with no hope of being let in." He stands a wet umbrella in the corner and sighs quietly.
city.sch.water.1: I took the watering can and watered the ficus: first round the edge of the pot, then closer to the stem. The soil drank it all greedily. A leaf sighed, or I imagined it.
city.sch.water.2: The cactus needs hardly any water: I gave it a spoonful and it stayed content, in the manner of cacti, silent. The fern opposite looked reproachful and got three times as much.
city.sch.water.3: On the windowsill a labelled jar with a sprout: "Bean, 6B. Do not touch, it is growing." I gave it three drops from my palm. The bean pretended it had noticed nothing.
city.sch.water.4: The pupil on plant duty today, judging by the note on the table, is "L.K.". I had to water for him. I put the can back with the handle toward the door, the way it should be.
city.sch.water.bio: Since you have been to a biology lesson, you understand why roots like to drink slowly. I watered a teaspoon at a time. The ficus seems to have appreciated it.
city.sch.water.fest: On a holiday the flowers get a slightly bigger portion than usual, as written on a paper with a heart. I watered them as prescribed. The geranium seems to have nodded.
city.sch.water.rain: Rain outside, and the flowers on the sill seem to pretend they need no watering. But I know they do: the rain is out there, and they have a household one of their own.
