city.sp.baq.1: Four guppies, each with a name: Pilot, Navigator, Cook and Deckhand. Colette says she tells them apart by their gait.
city.sp.baq.2: The fish gather at the glass as you come: they have decided you bring food.
city.sp.baq.3: In the evening the aquarium glows like a window into another flat. Colette sits beside it and keeps quiet along with the fish.
city.sp.baq.4: The floor is half empty: where the broken glass was, a smooth ring of fine sand. The fish swim around it.
city.sp.baq.5: There are four pieces of glass on the floor now. The pale one from the sea lies in the middle and the fish circle round it.
city.sp.bdoor.1: A note on the door: "Don't knock before ten. I'm an owl. C. B."
city.sp.bdoor.2: The door is ajar: it smells of bergamot tea and something salty, of the sea.
city.sp.bdoor.3: A radio mutters quietly behind the door. A strip of yellow light shows under it.
city.sp.bdoor.4: Quiet. Blue trembles in the gap under the door: the aquarium, which never goes dark.
city.sp.bdoor.prompt: E — read the note on the door
city.sp.bikes.1: In the morning half the bicycles are gone: their owners are already at work and at school.
city.sp.bikes.2: The daytime bicycles are resting. The red one has a flat, a note on the handlebar: "Will mend at the weekend."
city.sp.bikes.3: By evening the bicycles are back. The blue one's frame has beach sand on it.
city.sp.bikes.4: At night the spokes glint. Someone left a torch switched on, clamped to a handlebar.
city.sp.bikes.5: The frames are dripping: somebody rode in the rain and parked wet.
city.sp.bnet.1: The needle goes round: a knot, another knot. The meshes come out even as honeycomb. Hands remember what the head forgot long ago.
city.sp.bnet.2: An unfinished net is stretched on the frame. Colette says she is making it for the fish: it catches nothing, it just hangs by the window.
city.sp.bnet.3: Knot after knot and an hour has gone. The light outside the window is different now.
city.sp.board1.a: The concierge takes letters and keys from nine to nine. At lunch, knock louder.
city.sp.board1.b: The stairs are washed by rota. Whoever forgets their turn finds the bucket at their door.
city.sp.board1.c: Colette Bauer, flat 17 (first floor, along the gallery to the left of the stairs). The coloured glass on my aquarium's floor broke and the fish are sulking. I need a piece of sea glass, any kind, smooth. Come after ten in the morning: I am an owl, don't knock earlier.
city.sp.board1.d: Colette Bauer, no. 17: two pieces turned up, a green and a blue. I need one more, preferably a pale one. My door on the gallery is open from ten till midnight.
city.sp.board1.e: Flat 17 thanks everyone. The aquarium floor sparkles and the fish are content. Tea on the gallery in the evenings, come without a reason.
city.sp.board2.a: The aquarium in the hall belongs to everyone. The food is in the little box under it: a pinch, no more. The fish aren't asking for more, they are pretending.
city.sp.board2.b: A key with a red tag has been found. Ask the concierge.
city.sp.board2.c: We have been given some fry. Names by vote: if you are for, put one tick, if against, put two.
city.sp.board2.d: The hall thanks Colette B. of no. 17 for her advice: our guppies no longer fall ill. The advice is simple: don't overfeed.
city.sp.board_0.a: Bicycles go against the right wall, not in front of the letter boxes. The block's warden.
city.sp.board_0.b: Saturday at four we paint the yard benches. Bring your own brush, the paint is shared.
city.sp.board_0.c: Bohdan Kalniņš, 2nd floor: Colette in no. 17 wants a piece of sea glass for her aquarium. I won't give mine, my wife keeps it for luck. Try the beach after a storm.
city.sp.board_0.d: Has anyone seen a grey cat with a white paw? She sleeps on the first-floor gallery. Please don't shoo her, she belongs to a neighbour. Colette B., flat 17.
city.sp.bphotos.1: A trawler at the quay. On deck a young sailor in a cap, beside him a girl holding a net. On the back: "Swallow", 1968.
city.sp.bphotos.2: The net loft: long tables, nets like cobwebs, women in headscarves. Third from the left is Colette, staring down the lens.
city.sp.bphotos.3: Colette's first aquarium: a jar on a windowsill and three guppies. Caption: "Deckhand, Navigator, Cook. No Pilot yet."
city.sp.bphotos.4: An empty quay at dawn. No caption, but the frame is newer than the others.
city.sp.bradio.1: The radio on the shelf mutters the fishermen's forecast: north wind, force three, fog near the shore.
city.sp.bradio.2: An old song about ships is playing. Colette softly corrects the singer in the third verse.
city.sp.bradio.3: The night broadcast: the announcer reads out the tide table. Colette pencils the numbers right onto the wallpaper.
city.sp.bradio.4: The radio is silent. A note beside it: "Not before ten."
city.sp.bshelf.1: A ship in a bottle: masts folded down, sail cut from a rag. A lemonade bottle, the neck neatly sealed with wax.
city.sp.bshelf.2: Two glass floats in a net: one green, one pale blue, both full of tiny bubbles. Nets were once kept afloat with these.
city.sp.bshelf.3: A bone netting needle, smooth as a pebble. Scratched on the handle: "C. B. 1968".
city.sp.bshelf.4: Books about the sea, about fish and one tattered cookery manual: the most read of them all.
city.sp.btea.1: Colette pours from the samovar into a faceted glass: "Drink while it's hot. With bergamot, like at the port."
city.sp.btea.2: Evening tea: strong, with gooseberry jam. Colette says fish get used to people faster than people get used to fish.
city.sp.btea.3: The samovar is cold. A note beside it: "Let the tea sleep until ten."
city.sp.btv.1: Morning exercises for pensioners: Colette copies exactly half the movements and argues aloud with the other half.
city.sp.btv.2: Requests concert: a fishermen's choir sings. Colette hums along with no words, lips only.
city.sp.btv.3: The evening town news. Colette turns the sound down for the weather and up for the tides.
city.sp.btv.4: A test card and a soft hiss. Colette says you can hear the sea better like this.
city.sp.bwindow.1: From the first-floor window you see passers-by under the sun-breaker: legs, bags, dogs' tails.
city.sp.bwindow.2: Through the grille of the facade you can't see the sea, but you can hear it: the wind brings it in pieces.
city.sp.bwindow.3: At night the glass reflects the room and the fish swim straight down the street.
city.sp.cat.1: The grey cat with a white paw is washing on the bench. She lets you scratch behind an ear: one.
city.sp.cat.2: The cat sleeps on the warm concrete, curled so that you can't tell where the tail is.
city.sp.cat.3: The cat sits watching the door of no. 17. Supper is coming.
city.sp.cat.4: In the dark only her eyes and white paw show. The cat has moved closer to Colette's door.
city.sp.cat.5: The cat has squeezed under the bench and pretends there is no rain.
city.sp.chess.1: Chess in the hall: the pieces stand as if the game has been going on for a week.
city.sp.chess.2: The white king is dented: it was dropped on the tiles once and has not forgotten.
city.sp.chess.3: The black rook is a lemonade bottle cap: the real one went missing before the oldest residents moved in.
city.sp.chess.prompt: E — sit at the chessboard by the window
city.sp.closed.flat: The flat is quiet: its owner is asleep. Better come after ten.
city.sp.desk.1: The concierge knits a sock without looking up: "Who are you here for? Colette? First floor, stairs in the left corner, then along the gallery."
city.sp.desk.2: A rota for washing the stairs is pinned behind the glass. Your name isn't on it, thank goodness.
city.sp.desk.3: The chair is empty. A note on the desk: "Gone to check the yard. Keys in the drawer, letters in the drawer, back soon."
city.sp.desk.4: One desk lamp burns like a lighthouse. Beside it, cold tea in a faceted glass.
city.sp.dish.1: Colette sorts the finds on the saucer: "This one for the floor, by the dark stone. And this one can just lie there and enjoy itself."
city.sp.dish.2: On the saucer: a button, a shell and two bits of glass. You add yours to the rest and Colette nods: "A good one."
city.sp.dish.3: She holds your glass up to the window: "A bottle's. Twenty years in the sea, I'd say. This is the real thing."
city.sp.dish.prompt: E — put your find on the saucer
city.sp.dom.1: The table by the door is taken every afternoon: the tiles clack so loud it carries to the second floor.
city.sp.dom.2: A pencil on a string is tied to the table: the score goes on a napkin, and napkins are kept since last spring.
city.sp.dom.3: The loser pays for the tea. The kettle stands at the concierge's and is always warm.
city.sp.fish.1: The hall's guppies belong to everybody: anyone who feels like it feeds them. Few fish, many names.
city.sp.fish.2: The fattest guppy is nicknamed the Concierge: she is always on duty by the food.
city.sp.fish.3: At night the fish sleep close to the bottom and the aquarium glows softly like a night light.
city.sp.fish.4: The aquarium light is never switched off: they say it keeps both the fish and the entrance calmer.
city.sp.flowers.1: Boxes of marigolds and geraniums: red, yellow and one white "for variety".
city.sp.flowers.2: The flowers are wet with morning dew and smell of earth and a little of the sea.
city.sp.flowers.3: A bee is working on the geraniums. You stand still and it doesn't mind.
city.sp.flowers.4: The rain waters the boxes better than any can. For once the owner is pleased.
city.sp.gview.1: Morning: the yard is still in shadow, a white strip of sea beyond the roofs.
city.sp.gview.2: Someone below is beating a carpet. The sound comes back from the next block, a little later and softer.
city.sp.gview.3: Midday: the gallery is warm, below children chalk hopscotch squares and argue about the rules.
city.sp.gview.4: From the gallery you see several entrances and as many small windows, each with its own steam.
city.sp.gview.5: Evening: the windows light up one by one, as if the house were counting its tenants.
city.sp.gview.6: It smells of fried fish, pepper and somebody's fresh washing. That is evening in the serpent house.
city.sp.gview.7: Night: the long ribbon of windows bends in the dark. Far away a lighthouse blinks.
city.sp.gview.8: Quiet. You hear a tap dripping below, a neighbour coughing through a wall, and the sea breathing behind the blocks.
city.sp.mail.prompt: E — peek at the letter boxes
city.sp.mail0.1: The boxes have darkened with age. Next to number 22 a sticker: "Do not lose letters to my son!"
city.sp.mail0.2: A flyer for fish pies lies on the floor. Nobody picks it up, but nobody throws it away either.
city.sp.mail0.3: On Mondays the postman comes before anyone: newspapers stick out of every slot.
city.sp.mail1.1: Box 17 is stuffed with newspapers: its owner gets up late.
city.sp.mail1.2: Box 17 is empty: Colette has already been.
city.sp.mail1.3: At night the boxes rattle softly: somewhere above a door has slammed.
city.sp.mail2.1: One box is taped shut crosswise: the owners are away, their post goes into a bag at the concierge's.
city.sp.mail2.2: Box 8 has chalk on it: "Don't write to us, we phone."
city.sp.mail2.3: The boxes are dripping: someone came in with a wet umbrella.
city.sp.net.prompt: E — pick up the netting needle
city.sp.pram.1: The pram is empty with a forgotten rattle in it. Mum must have gone for milk.
city.sp.pram.2: Someone very small sleeps in the pram, tucked up to the nose. Better walk past quietly.
city.sp.pram.3: The pram is empty, a string bag of apples hangs on the handle.
city.sp.pram.4: The pram is folded and stands by the wall: nobody needs it till morning.
city.sp.shelf.prompt: E — look over the shelf of little ships
city.sp.stairs.1: The stairs in the left corner lead up to the first-floor gallery. The handrail is warm from the light of the slit windows.
city.sp.stairs.2: One bulb burns on the stairs. You hear your steps before you climb.
city.sp.wash.1: The sheets flap in the wind like sails. Under them you can see the light moving.
city.sp.wash.2: The washing is still wet: slow drops fall on the floor.
city.sp.wash.3: The washing is dry and smells of wind and salt.
city.sp.wash.4: The washing has been taken in; only the pegs are left, creaking on the line.
city.sp.wash.5: The washing was taken in early. The housewives here can hear the weather coming.
city.sp.water.1: The watering can is full to the brim. The palm will last till evening.
city.sp.water.2: You water: the soil sighs and darkens, the palm straightens a little.
city.sp.water.3: The leaves smell of damp earth. Under the pot a note: "Don't drown it!"
city.story.kiosk1.prices.1: "Evening paper 5 rub. Cosmos and Us 40. Shores 40. Postcard 4. Fresh news after lunch, yesterday's at a discount."
city.story.kiosk1.prices.2: Under the glass, a list headed "Asked for but out of stock": "a magazine about cats", "today's weather for tomorrow", "a letter from my son".
city.story.kiosk1.prices.3: In chalk on the side: "The crossword in Friday's issue is hard. 14 down is 'tide'. Don't mention it."
city.story.kiosk2.freezer.1: The freezer glass has misted up from inside. Someone drew a sun on it with a finger, and it's slowly thawing.
city.story.kiosk2.freezer.2: The cups lie in rows like toy soldiers in a box. Winter breathes out of the chest, though outside it's July.
city.story.kiosk2.freezer.3: At the bottom of the chest, a lonely ice lolly from last summer, furred with frost like a coat. Nobody seems to have the heart to sell it.
city.story.kiosk2.freezer.prompt: E — look into the freezer chest
city.story.kiosk2.prices.1: "Plombir in a cup 28 rub. Buratino, Duchesse 18. Water 20. Ice cream doesn't melt if you eat it fast."
city.story.kiosk2.prices.2: At the bottom of the price list, in a child's hand: "Can I have two scoops?" Underneath, in a grown-up's: "Yes. If it's very hot."
city.story.kiosk2.prices.3: "On sale today: sun, free; shade under the awning, also free. Ice cream, for money."
city.story.kiosk3.prices.1: "Skvorets cigarettes 35 rub. Lighters 10. Seeds 10. Under-sixteens: seeds and good advice only."
city.story.kiosk3.prices.2: On the counter, a shell-shaped ashtray and a sign: "No smoking here. Thinking allowed."
city.story.kiosk3.prices.3: Over the hatch, a faded poster: a smoker whose lungs are two grey clouds. Under it someone has added: "Lovely weather, though."
city.story.kiosk4.buckets.1: Buckets of water, and in them carnations, daisies and one big sprig of dog rose, clearly picked on the way to work.
city.story.kiosk4.buckets.2: It smells of wet stems and a little of the sea. The sunflowers stand apart, facing south, like people at a bus stop.
city.story.kiosk4.buckets.3: In the last bucket, a single daisy with its petals plucked. Someone was asking it. From the look of it, the answer was "loves me".
city.story.kiosk4.prices.1: "Carnation 3 rub., daisies 5 a bunch, sunflower 7, dog rose not for sale, it's mine."
city.story.kiosk4.prices.2: Under the prices: "Bouquets for weddings, graduations and making up. Making up at a discount."
city.story.kiosk4.prices.3: In chalk: "Flowers arrive Thursday. Or Friday. Flowers aren't a bus."
city.story.kiosk4.talk.1: "The tulips are sad today, don't take them. Take the daisies, they're silly and cheerful. Though it's look-only: they haven't sent us anything to sell yet."
city.story.kiosk4.talk.2: The flower seller trims stems and tells me the sunflowers turn to the kiosk window every morning. "They think I'm the sun. I don't argue."
city.story.kiosk4.talk.3: "A bouquet for a girl? For your mum? For yourself? For yourself is the best kind. Come back when they're in and I'll make you one."
city.story.kiosk4.talk.4: A note on the counter: "Anahit! Don't put the buckets out till it's dark: the lilac is afraid of the sun." Signed: "Ales, evening shift."
city.story.kiosk5.prices.1: "Cable-car pin: next door at kiosk No. 1. Information 0 rub. More information, also 0. Advice on where to go: depends on my mood."
city.story.kiosk5.prices.2: Under the glass, a photo: a cabin over the sea at dawn, all pink. Caption: "6:04. Empty. Beautiful, though."
city.story.kiosk5.prices.3: "Children, pensioners and first-timers get a window seat. Everyone else too: it's all windows in there."
city.story.kiosk5.talk.1: "A cable-car ticket? You pay in the cabin; we only give information. Ask away: where, when and why. 'Why' is free."
city.story.kiosk5.talk.2: "Twelve minutes to Zenith if the wind doesn't argue. If it does, the cabin sways, a free ride on top."
city.story.kiosk5.talk.3: The information clerk leafs through a thick exercise book: "Passengers' Questions". The last one: "Why do the cabins never meet in the middle?" No answer.
city.story.kiosk5.talk.4: "The last cabin to the Lighthouse leaves at sunset. Not by the timetable, by the sun. The operator decided, and nobody objected."
city.story.kiosk5.timetable.1: "Cable car. Akademgorodok to Aton. Amber Shore to Zenith. Lighthouse. Interval: as long as the cabin is visible from the window."
city.story.kiosk5.timetable.2: The route map is drawn by hand in coloured pencils. Horizon and Polar Star are dotted in and labelled: "Only in dreams, for now."
city.story.kiosk5.timetable.3: "The cable car does not run in a thunderstorm. In a rainbow it runs, but slower, so everyone has time to look."
city.story.kiosk5.timetable.4: Added in pencil: "Whoever left a knitted mitten in cabin No. 7: it's been riding back and forth since Monday. It likes it."
city.story.kiosk6.prices.1: "Key 6 rub. Zip 10. Heel tips 8. Watches: depending on the watch's state of mind."
city.story.kiosk6.prices.2: "Urgent repairs: tomorrow. Very urgent: the day after; it needs thinking about."
city.story.kiosk6.prices.3: Clocks on the wall, each showing a different time. A sign underneath: "The right one is third from the left. Probably."
city.story.kiosk6.talk.1: The repairman doesn't look up from a watch movement. "Put it on the counter. What's broken? It'll mend itself? Then why are you here?" I've nothing to mend, and he seems pleased about that.
city.story.kiosk6.talk.2: "I cut keys, replace zips, treat watches. A heart? No, hearts go to the clinic. Though people do bring them to me sometimes."
city.story.kiosk6.talk.3: The hatch has a "Lunch" sign. The repairman sits right there eating and looking at me. "'Lunch' doesn't mean I'm not here. It means I'm eating."
city.story.kiosk6.talk.4: "A watch that runs fast is better than one that runs slow," says the repairman. "At least it wants to get somewhere."
city.story.kiosk6.tray.1: A tray of things mended but never collected: an alarm clock, an umbrella, one sandal. Each has a dated tag. The alarm clock has been waiting since spring.
city.story.kiosk6.tray.2: A bunch of keys with no tag. The repairman says they're keys "to everything that came before". He'll give them to whoever remembers what they open.
city.story.kiosk6.tray.3: A pocket watch engraved "To L. from L." It ticks loudly, as if in a hurry to be collected.
city.story.photo_desk.1: The photographer wipes a lens and squints at me. "You've got a face for a portrait. Not for a passport, for a portrait. Sit on the stool."
city.story.photo_desk.2: Envelopes of finished prints on the desk, a surname on each. One just says: "The boy who was looking at the sea." Not mine. Not yet.
city.story.photo_desk.3: "A portrait is sixty, ready on Thursday. Stick it in your diary and it'll show you were here," says the photographer, surprised at how that sounded.
city.story.photo_desk.4: Behind the desk, prints dry on pegs: weddings, school leavers, an old man with a dog. Everyone is squinting, as if he'd shot straight into the sun.
city.story.sanatorium_night.1: The receptionist took the money, handed me a towel with a little sun embroidered on it and made up the couch in the treatment room. "Breakfast at eight; we won't wake you."
city.story.sanatorium_night.2: All night mineral water murmured in the pipes behind the wall like a distant stream. I dreamt I was drinking it and turning transparent.
city.story.sanatorium_night.3: I woke at seven exactly, when the sun reached the pillow. Everyone here seems to wake that way.
city.story.sanatorium_night.4: In the night the duty nurse looked in with a torch, tucked my blanket in and tiptoed away. As if I were here for treatment. Maybe I am.
city.story.sanatorium_night.prompt: E — stay the night at the sanatorium
city.t1.arcade.d: Gennady's cabinet stands in the corner of the living room; he took the coin slot out so it plays for free. The record reads "GL 41,200", and below in pencil: "HC 41,190".
city.t1.arcade.n: At night the cabinet blinks quietly in its corner. The demo runs, but someone has left fingerprints in the dust on the buttons.
city.t1.deckboard.0: Notice: "The chess table is free every day except Tuesday, when it is always taken."
city.t1.deckboard.1: A handwritten notice: "The second cube (house 0-02) seeks a gardener for the weekend. Come in by the niche, there is one lift. Tea in the blue tin."
city.t1.deckboard.2: A note from a circle: "The club above the deck welcomes dominoes players. Easy to enter, hard to leave."
city.t1.deckboard.3: Notice: "A blue umbrella with one bent spoke has been found. Owner, collect it from Isla, if you can catch her in."
city.t1.deckboard.4: A note on sticky tape: "The pie was baked by Gennady. The pie was eaten by Hokon. This is just."
city.t1.diary.1: Day 1. Six seeds of the hot pepper "Baltic Flame" into warm soil. Planted upstairs: light from both sides at once, like a real greenhouse. Hokon said peppers do not grow from the floor. They do.
city.t1.diary.2: Day 3. Three out of six have sprouted. The rest is a matter of time. I named the strongest the General. Hokon: "And me?" "You are the soil."
city.t1.diary.3: Day 5. Left the lamp over the bed on overnight: the sprouts leaned toward it all night and in the morning stood as if on parade. The roof window must stay shut: wind.
city.t1.diary.4: Day 8. Repotted. The first true leaf. Showed it to Isla, she said "oh". The best review in the world.
city.t1.diary.5: Day 11. Flowers! White, five petals. Hokon looked at them through the glass with a face as if he had grown them himself. I will not argue.
city.t1.diary.6: Day 15. The first fruit has turned green. If you are reading this, you watered while we were away. Thank you. Take some seeds from the tin; I will grow more. G.
city.t1.diary.title: The greenhouse diary
city.t1.fridge.0: Notes on magnets on the fridge. Hokon: "Gen, your pot by the stove again. This is a kitchen, not a greenhouse." Gennady below: "The greenhouse is upstairs. This is a guest pot."
city.t1.fridge.1: Gennady: "The peppers have sprouted: three out of six! No stamping upstairs." Hokon: "I don't stamp, I walk. Congratulations."
city.t1.fridge.2: Hokon: "The milk is gone. I bought more, but it is still your fault." Gennady: "What for?" Hokon: "I will think of something."
city.t1.fridge.3: Gennady: "Saturday Isla and I go to the lakes. Water the greenhouse morning and evening, no more than a glass per pot!" Hokon: "I remember. The can is by the cactus."
city.t1.fridge.4: Hokon: "Gen, I forgot to water on Thursday. Everything seems alive." Gennady: "HOKON." Hokon: "I watered double on Friday." Gennady: "HOKON!!"
city.t1.fridge.5: A fresh sheet in Hokon's hand: "If you are the one who sits on the bench under our cubes looking up, come up. The can is by the cactus, the tea in the blue tin. H."
city.t1.fridge.6: Gennady: "The first pepper has turned red! Just one. Hokon does not get it until he apologises for Thursday."
city.t1.fridge.7: Hokon: "Sorry about Thursday. Gen, I brought you seeds. Not peppers. Almost." Gennady: "Accepted. Half the pepper is yours."
city.t1.fridge.f: A magnet octopus on the fridge holds a list: "milk, milk, pepper (hot), lightbulb."
city.t1.games.1: Boxes: Battleships, draughts, dominoes, chess with one rook missing. In its place a champagne cork with a tower drawn on it.
city.t1.games.2: The rules of the games lie apart in an envelope marked "so Hokon stops arguing". The envelope is visibly worn.
city.t1.hooks.day: The stand is nearly empty: Hokon's and Gennady's jackets went out with their owners. A scarf and an umbrella remain.
city.t1.hooks.eve: The jackets hang on their hooks; a seed packet and a pencil stub stick out of Gennady's pocket.
city.t1.hooks.night: The jackets sleep on their hooks, the scarf's sleeve hanging to the floor.
city.t1.p.deckboard: E — read the notices on the stand
city.t1.p.games: E — go through the game boxes
city.t1.p.hooks: E — look at the coat stand
city.t1.p.photos: E — look at the photos on the shelf
city.t1.p.postcards: E — leaf through the postcards on the shelf
city.t1.p.sky: E — look up through the glass over the bed
city.t1.p.slate: E — read the slate by the lift
city.t1.p.sleep: E — lie down under the sky
city.t1.p.tipshelf: E — look over the little shelf
city.t1.p.trays: E — look at the seed trays
city.t1.photos.1: Photos on the shelf: Hokon with his sister before a fjord; Gennady in a tent, red with frost; Isla with a backpack, sticking her tongue out at the photographer.
city.t1.photos.2: Another picture: both on the deck under the cubes on the day they moved in. Caption: "Here. Forever. Probably."
city.t1.post.1: A postcard of Bergen harbour. "Hokon, how is your cube? Mum asks whether it is scary to live on an edge. I said: he isn't scared, only of the lift. Love, Siri."
city.t1.post.2: A second one, of the fish market. "Sending you a herring (that is, a picture). I come in June; send me a photo of the sky from the window in the roof. Siri."
city.t1.post.3: "Hokon, you still haven't written what your flatmate is called. Mum is afraid he is an artist. I said: a gardener. Siri."
city.t1.post.4: "Thanks for the photo. Your sky is somehow huge. I come in June. And do not forget to water what they left you. Siri."
city.t1.post.title: Siri's postcards
city.t1.shoes.1: Gennady's trainers and Hokon's boots stand in pairs: Gennady's soles carry pine needles, Hokon's carry sand.
city.t1.shoes.snow: Snow melts on the soles. Hokon put his boots on the grate, Gennady his on a newspaper; the grate seems to be winning.
city.t1.shoes.wet: Both pairs have wet soles today, a small puddle under the rack. One boot stands on a newspaper, the other does not.
city.t1.sky.1: An atlas of constellations lies on the pillow, a bookmark at Orion: "to know who is who".
city.t1.slate.cube: On the slate a cube is drawn standing on its corner, captioned: "The house that does not fall."
city.t1.slate.eve: The slate: "We are home. Whoever needs us, call the lift once, it understands. The blue tin is tea."
city.t1.slate.night: The slate: "Quiet! H. sleeps downstairs, G. upstairs, under the sky. The lift creaks, do not be alarmed."
city.t1.slate.note: Below, in another hand: "Gen, you left the lamp over the peppers on again!" Under it: "It is there FOR the peppers!!"
city.t1.slate.week: The slate: "Weekend. H. at the club, G. at the lakes, key with Isla. Water the greenhouse!!"
city.t1.slate.work: The slate by the lift: "H. and G. at work until half past three. Post in the box, parcels to Isla."
city.t1.sleep.1: A note on the pillow: "If a neighbour is tired, lie down, don't be shy. G." The mattress under the roof smells of warm wood.
city.t1.sleep.2: Over your face is the sloping glass and the sky moves across it. You fall asleep counting how many clouds fit into the frame.
city.t1.sleep.3: The lift creaks below and goes quiet. Somewhere in the cube a clock ticks. You wake rested, and on the glass lies a patch of morning sun.
city.t1.tipshelf.1: The little shelf: a star atlas, a book about alpine flowers and a globe with a dent in Africa: "fell, but held up well".
city.t1.tipshelf.2: A seed packet sticks out between the books as a bookmark. On it: "sow when Hokon stops arguing".
city.t1.trays.0: A seed tray: six hollows, three with green loops of sprouts. The tallest has a stick label reading "General".
city.t1.trays.1: The seedlings have grown: true leaves in every hollow; the General is already taller than his label and looks down on the rest.
city.t1.trays.2: The trays are empty: the seedlings moved to pots by the window. The labels remain and one forgotten sprout in the corner, unnamed but alive.
city.t1.water.1: A glass per pot, as Gennady asked: peppers, seedlings, the cactus (half a glass for him). The soil smells of rain and drinks willingly.
city.t1h2.baro.1: The needle rests at "Change" as if that were its final decision.
city.t1h2.baro.clear: The needle has crept towards "Fair" and stopped. Under it the slip says "Like me": the word "like" is crossed out and "nearly" written above it.
city.t1h2.baro.cold: The needle goes down slowly, like a person into cold water.
city.t1h2.baro.fog: Damp on the glass, the needle at "Humid". It's good that the instrument sees our weather too.
city.t1h2.baro.rain: The needle has gone over to "Rain". I tapped the glass and it didn't change its mind. In this house they trust the barometer more than the radio.
city.t1h2.baro.snow: The needle has swung to "Storm": the mark a barometer gives to anything colder than October.
city.t1h2.bench.1: A bench under the pilotis: concrete above, grass below, the path beside. From here you see who comes into the house, and it is easy to pretend you aren't looking.
city.t1h2.bench.2: The columns hold the house above us and we sit and don't worry. That is probably what architecture means.
city.t1h2.bench.n: At night the only sound under the pilotis is the lamp. If you sit quietly you can hear somebody upstairs putting a kettle on.
city.t1h2.bench.rain: The rain falls on the far side of the columns and the bench is dry. The best shelter in the block.
city.t1h2.bike.1: A blue town bicycle by the end pillar. The tyres are flat, the chain is oiled: whoever it belongs to, someone looks after it.
city.t1h2.bike.2: A tag on the handlebar: "Not stolen: waiting." The handwriting is angular, a navigator's.
city.t1h2.bike.n: In the dark the bicycle stands like a horse resting on a march. I left the bell alone.
city.t1h2.bike.rain: It's dry under the pilotis; only the bell has misted over.
city.t1h2.cards.1: Rotterdam, 1974: "Vitya, e4. Rain in the port, dark beer, you wouldn't approve. — K."
city.t1h2.cards.2: Genoa, 1985: "e5. The lighthouse here is broader than ours and twice as lazy. Give Nina my regards, if she still puts up with me. — K."
city.t1h2.cards.3: Lisbon, 1998: "Knight f3. My daughter married; at the wedding I played chess with her father-in-law. Lost. He's a navigator. — K."
city.t1h2.cards.4: The last: "Queen f5. Your move, old pirate. Write. — K." The postmark is two months old. There is no reply in the stack.
city.t1h2.cards.5: On top lies one more, unsigned: a lighthouse, and on the back "Q takes e6, check" and three words: "Lost address. Found." I laid it face up so he'd see it at once.
city.t1h2.cards.title: Postcards from K.
city.t1h2.charts.1: On the table, a chart of the coastal waters covered in pencil lines: a course, another course, a correction for drift. The lines end at Lyudmilovsk; beyond is clean paper.
city.t1h2.charts.2: Brass dividers stand in the chart like a little flag, the legs opened exactly one nautical mile. There seems to be nothing left to measure.
city.t1h2.charts.3: In the margin, a column of figures: 6:12, 6:13, 6:15. Sunrises, one after another, each a minute later than the last.
city.t1h2.charts.n: At night the chart seems alive: the lamp's shadow moves over the paper and the coastline breathes.
city.t1h2.compass.1: A pocket compass with a lid. The needle trembles and settles, pointing at the cabinet of pilot books. "North is that way," I thought. Then I thought that cabinets can pull a needle too.
city.t1h2.compass.2: Engraved under the lid: "Course for home. 1958." The glass is missing, probably long since lost in a storm.
city.t1h2.games.1: Dominoes laid out, the game stopped halfway. On one side of the table a run of blanks; on the other, somebody has got tangled in it.
city.t1h2.games.2: Lars keeps the score in pencil on a corner of the table, rubs it out and writes it again. He says: "An honest score is one you can rub out."
city.t1h2.kettle.d: An enamel kettle, the spout chipped, still warm. A note on the mug: "Whoever needs it, pour. V. S." I poured myself some navigator's tea: strong, dark as old copper.
city.t1h2.kettle.n: At night the kettle is cold, but there's tea waiting under the lid: he brews it in the evening so as not to lose time in the morning. Cold tea can be good when you've been told you may.
city.t1h2.notice.1: "Residents! The lamps under the pilotis are switched at the wall by the path. If you leave last, please turn them off."
city.t1h2.notice.2: "The bicycle by the end pillar belongs to nobody in particular. If it is yours, take it. If it is not, leave it: it isn't lost, it's waiting. — The residents' board."
city.t1h2.notice.3: "Please don't stuff box 0-01 with flyers. The owner checks it himself, morning and evening. — The concierge."
city.t1h2.notice.4: "Saturday: dominoes under the pilotis. Lars plays, and anyone who comes. The table is by the path, the tiles are already on it."
city.t1h2.notice.5: "We are not shutting off the tap for winter until the caretaker says so. The bucket under it is everyone's."
city.t1h2.notice.6: "Anyone with spare fern cuttings: bring them to the end planter. It shares, but only with those who sign the tag."
city.t1h2.notice.7: "Postcards with a lighthouse keep turning up under the post boxes: no address, no signature. If it is yours, take it. If it has been nobody's for a month, don't throw it away: someone in this house is waiting for cards."
city.t1h2.notice.8: "Thanks to everyone who wrote to Viktor Sergeyevich these weeks. He says the box is no longer empty and the chess is moving again. He asked me to pass it on. — The concierge."
city.t1h2.notice.fest: "Holiday: the yard is swept and the lamps under the pilotis burn later than usual. Come in, there's room for everyone."
city.t1h2.notice.rain: "It's dry under the pilotis when it rains. Wipe the benches after you."
city.t1h2.post.1: The boxes rustle: bills, a newspaper, somebody's letter with a foreign stamp. Box "0-01 V. Holm" is polished clean and empty. On the floor under the boxes lies a postcard with a lighthouse, unsigned. I put it in my pocket: maybe it has somewhere to go.
city.t1h2.post.2: The morning post isn't sorted yet: newspapers in a pile on the floor. A lighthouse postcard sticks out of them by one corner. No signature. I took it.
city.t1h2.post.3: In the afternoon the boxes are as empty as a canteen after lunch. A lighthouse postcard lies by the wall, where the postman missed it. I picked it up.
city.t1h2.post.n: At night the boxes glint under the pilotis. A lighthouse postcard shows pale under the bottom row. I tucked it inside my jacket so it wouldn't crease.
city.t1h2.pot1.1: Tag: "Fern. Water on Wednesdays. Don't be stingy." The soil is damp: Wednesday wasn't long ago.
city.t1h2.pot1.2: Under a frond, a packet of seeds and a note: "Take them. If they grow, bring one back."
city.t1h2.pot1.rain: The rain doesn't reach in, but the fern leans to the edge all the same: it can tell it's wet outside.
city.t1h2.pot2.1: Tag: "Ficus. Native of the lobby, moved because of the draught. Offended, but holding on."
city.t1h2.pot2.2: One leaf has turned yellow, and on it in pencil: "Don't touch, it's still thinking."
city.t1h2.pot2.cold: The ficus is cold and its leaves have curled. Somebody has covered the pot with an old navigator's jacket.
city.t1h2.pot3.1: Tag: "Fern No. 2. The younger one. Doesn't know yet that it's a fern."
city.t1h2.pot3.2: Beside the pot, chalk marks on the concrete record its height, each with a date. Since autumn it has grown a hand's width.
city.t1h2.radio.1: A wooden receiver on the shelf, the green eye unlit. I turned the knob: silence and a faint crackle, as if it were remembering something.
city.t1h2.radio.2: After the hall I turned the knob here too: silence. But there are fresh pencil marks on the dial: Holm is marking where it used to pick things up.
city.t1h2.radio.3: The log is written up, the receiver silent. It seems to have nothing left to report: somebody else writes the forecast now.
city.t1h2.sextant.d: At noon the sun is straight overhead, which for a sextant is one degree too many. On the case, in pencil: "Latitude 55°. Check at noon, even ashore."
city.t1h2.sextant.e: Towards evening the little mirror catches a yellow like egg yolk. I aimed the spot at the wall and made a small dawn.
city.t1h2.sextant.m: The sextant lies in its case, the brass cold. Catch the morning sun in the little mirror and a spot of light appears on the ceiling. It trembles like a needle looking for north.
city.t1h2.sextant.n: At night the sextant sleeps in its case. Scratched on the lid: "The Pole Star doesn't shine for you, but it doesn't lie."
city.t1h2.shadow.d: At noon the diamonds gather by the legs of the little table and tremble at every passer-by. I put my foot in a bright one and it turned lattice-like.
city.t1h2.shadow.e: Towards evening the diamonds stretch out and drift over the rug like a shoal of fish. One swam into the cup and stayed.
city.t1h2.shadow.m: In the morning the low sun strikes the screen out on the street and long diamonds run across the floor. The cobogo pattern is stamped on the boards like a seal on a letter.
city.t1h2.shadow.n: At night the screen glows outside with the streetlamp and the diamonds lie on the ceiling quite still, like stars in a planetarium.
city.t1h2.stool.1: A three-legged stool with a slight wobble. If you sit properly it stops.
city.t1h2.stool.2: From here you see the whole table and the path beyond it: who goes to the stair, who to the boxes.
city.t1h2.stool.n: At night the tiles show white on the table like teeth. I don't feel like playing, only like sitting and listening to the lamp.
city.t1h2.tap.1: I filled a cup from the brass tap. Cold enough to ache in the teeth. Viktor Sergeyevich calls it "Baltic", though the pipe comes up from the cellar.
city.t1h2.tap.2: The bucket under the tap is shared; somebody's maple leaf floats in it. I tipped it out, filled it fresh and put the leaf back: it may be somebody's bookmark.
city.t1h2.tap.cold: There's frost on the tap and the water runs like glass. I drank in small careful sips.
city.t1h2.tap.n: At night the tap drips evenly, like a ship's clock. I tightened it, and then I could hear somebody walking barefoot upstairs.
city.t1h2.tap.rain: Rain taps on the concrete overhead and the tap answers with a drop. It's dry under the pilotis, and a little like a ship's hold.
city.t1h2.tree.1: Tag on the sapling: "Rowan. Planted when the stair was finished. Won't grow above the pilotis: we agreed."
city.t1h2.tree.2: The branches reach for the gap where the yard opens to the north. The tree knows where the light comes from.
city.t1h2.tree.n: At night the sapling is barely there: a dark patch in a dark patch. But the tag shows white, like a small flag.
city.t1h2.tx.rough.1: The rough copy of the watch log "Ashore". First in pencil, then in ink into the fair book. What isn't worth ink stays here.
city.t1h2.tx.rough.2: Wind W, 3 m/s. Pressure 1009, falling. Overcast. Sunrise 6:12: seen. Kettle boiled on time. Not one postcard since Tuesday.
city.t1h2.tx.rough.3: Wind W, 4 m/s. The receiver's silent. Went down to the hall set: the announcer promises clear, the concierge rain. Both right, as usual.
city.t1h2.tx.rough.4: A young fellow came by and leafed through my pilot books. He asked why write it down if you can see it anyway. I said: "You can see it. Written down, everyone can."
city.t1h2.tx.rough.5: Pressure rising. Wind NW, 5 m/s. Decided: if no move arrives by Friday I'll play the queen blind. No. Nothing to play with. Let the card come.
city.t1h2.tx.rough.6: Under the lamp on the table lay a postcard with a lighthouse: that very cape where K. and I lay at anchor in seventy-six. No signature, but his hand. I wrote down: "Q takes e6, check: received." The box isn't empty any more.
city.t1h2.tx.rough.7: Pressure 1021. Clear. Sunrise 6:31: seen, standing on the steps, and not alone: a young person beside me, in a jacket too thin for the weather. I note it down: "Crew: plus one."
city.t1h2.tx.rough.title: The rough log
city.t1h2.v1.1: From the first-floor gallery you see the whole yard: three benches, five trees and a path worn by people who cut corners.
city.t1h2.v1.2: From above the stair looks like a shell: the steps go round and round and never end. I counted to twenty and lost count.
city.t1h2.v1.fog: There's no yard in the fog: only the rail, my hands and a dog barking far off.
city.t1h2.v1.n: The yard at night is a dark rectangle. The light of the kitchen windows lies on the grass in yellow strips, as if somebody had laid out runners.
city.t1h2.v1.rain: Rain runs off the gallery through the pipes and the whole house rings softly.
city.t1h2.v3.1: From the top gallery, past the trees, you see the neighbouring roofs and an iron-grey strip that may well be the sea.
city.t1h2.v3.2: From here the red cap of the stair tower is a mushroom's. The spiral round it is the stalk, only hollow and with windows.
city.t1h2.v3.fog: The fog lies below the gallery. The house stands above it like a ship over a shoal.
city.t1h2.v3.n: At night from up here you watch the town switch its windows on one by one, as if somebody were checking a watch log.
city.t1h2.v3.rain: From up here you can see the rain: grey threads reaching down to the roofs and drawing them closer.
city.t1h4.chime.1: Five tubes of different lengths sway in the wind. Each rings in its own way; together they make something like an unfinished tune.
city.t1h4.chime.2: Scratched on the little wooden tongue: "G. O. — so I can hear the wind from the studio." So the chime can be heard in the capsule too.
city.t1h4.chime.clear: Clear and windy: the tubes ring without a break, and the radio amateur is surely smiling behind his wall.
city.t1h4.chime.fog: In fog the ringing comes as if from afar, from the other end of the bridge, though the chime is right here.
city.t1h4.chime.n: At night the chime rings seldom and softly, like a star that has just remembered something.
city.t1h4.chime.rain: In rain the tubes are silent; only drops run down them onto the tongue. The ringing will come back with the wind.
city.t1h4.kettle.1: An enamel kettle stands on the stove, warm on one side. Gunnar's note: "Pour, the mug is on the left, sugar in the jar with the postage stamp."
city.t1h4.kettle.2: The tea is strong, with lemon peel. I drink it by the window, and somewhere on the radio a shipping forecast is read softly.
city.t1h4.kettle.m: In the morning the kettle has not cooled from the night: the radio amateur must have been drinking it on air until dawn.
city.t1h4.log.1: "Date, time, call sign, signal, weather, remarks." The first page is ruled neatly. "20:10, S.S. Ladoga, 579. Calm. The navigator sends greetings."
city.t1h4.log.2: "23:00, the capsule opposite. We talked about the weather for forty minutes. A good talk." Beside it: "Tiksi, 4 am, snow. Six words out of twelve. Six is a lot, too."
city.t1h4.log.3: "Bridge, 7 pm. Listened to the air with my neighbour. She brought jam, I brought tea. We caught nothing and regretted nothing."
city.t1h4.log.4: "Marked in red: the tune from 14 May is found. The Saucer café, the jukebox, third button. The boy who came with the reel saved me half a year. Put in the log: he gets tea without a queue."
city.t1h4.log.5: The last entry, in fresh pencil: "Tomorrow I put the antenna on the second bridge. If the key taps evenly, everything is fine. Same call sign: Lyudmilovsk-11. 73."
city.t1h4.log.line: A thick log in an oilcloth cover lies open by the key. The pencil is tied on with thread so it won't get lost.
city.t1h4.log.title: Gunnar's station log
city.t1h4.mail.1: Rows of post boxes with names on slips of paper. One has a sticker reading "QSL", another "No flyers, we have enough air already."
city.t1h4.mail.d: In the afternoon the boxes are empty and hollow. Flyers lie scattered on the floor beneath: nobody likes them but everybody reads them.
city.t1h4.mail.e: By evening the boxes are full again: one door is ajar, and I can see a postcard with a steamer on it.
city.t1h4.mail.m: The postman has already been this morning: corners of postcards and papers stick out. From one box peeks a letter with a foreign stamp.
city.t1h4.mail.n: At night the boxes stand in the dark like a row of little windows. Behind each, somebody's post waits for morning.
city.t1h4.mail.sun: No post on Sunday. A slip on the radio amateur's box says: "Cards arrive on Sundays too. By air."
city.t1h4.morse.after.1: The key is still warm from somebody's palm. The lever springs and the contact rings thinly, like a grasshopper.
city.t1h4.morse.after.2: A slip beside it with a decoding: "·–· ·– –·· ·· ––– RADIO." A good first lesson.
city.t1h4.morse.after.n: At night the key taps especially cleanly: on a night channel there is no interference, only your hand and a stranger's ear.
city.t1h4.morse.draw.1: Half the words got through. Not bad for a first time: six of twelve signs were right.
city.t1h4.morse.keys: E: tap when the marker is in the bright middle
city.t1h4.morse.lose.1: My hand shook and the dots stuck to the dashes. The air answered with a rustle: "Please repeat, did not copy."
city.t1h4.morse.lose.2: Too much haste. The key hates haste: it clinked and fell silent as if offended.
city.t1h4.morse.title: Morse: the key
city.t1h4.morse.win.1: Even as a metronome. In the headphones somebody answered briefly: "73." That means "best regards."
city.t1h4.morse.win.2: The dashes came out long and the dots short. A far station confirmed reception: my fist was recognised, so it seems.
city.t1h4.news.1: "Please don't bang on the bridge rail: in the capsules it sounds like a bell. If you really must tap, there is a key for that on the second floor."
city.t1h4.news.2: "The radio amateur from the studio asks nobody to run loud receivers on the bridge: he is catching weak signals. In return he promises tea and lets people tap the key."
city.t1h4.news.3: "Found: a brown striped scarf, left on the bridge bench. Ask the radio amateur: he has a twin hanging over his bed."
city.t1h4.news.4: "On Saturday at 7 pm we listen to the air together on the bridge. Bring your own mugs. The radio amateur will tune the receiver; whoever can taps along."
city.t1h4.news.base: The house board. "The bridge is for people, the benches for everyone, the lantern is lit at its post." The rest is on other slips.
city.t1h4.news.sat: It is Saturday: we listen to the air on the bridge. They are already moving a bench closer to the lantern.
city.t1h4.p.kettle: Pour some tea from the kettle
city.t1h4.p.qsl: Look at the cards on the wall
city.t1h4.phones.1: Big headphones with leather cups. A thread on the band: so you remember which side goes where.
city.t1h4.phones.d: I put them on for a second: a rustle, then a far-off woman's voice reading numbers in English. I took them off so as not to eavesdrop.
city.t1h4.phones.e: In the evening headphones there is music, quiet and warm. It seems to be that same trumpet from the embankment, only very far away.
city.t1h4.phones.n: At night the headphones hold a steady hum and rare beeps, like a distant lighthouse. I want to put them on and not take them off.
city.t1h4.plant.1: A box of geraniums on the bridge. Somebody pushed a stick with a tag into the soil: "Don't pick, it's for everybody."
city.t1h4.plant.2: The soil is damp: somebody waters it from a kettle while passing with tea in hand. One leaf is bent back like a little palm.
city.t1h4.plant.3: A sparrow sits on the edge of the box and eyes me sideways as if I were suspicious. It flew off without waiting for crumbs.
city.t1h4.plant.rain: The rain has washed the leaves to a shine. The flowers bow but hold on: geraniums are stubborn.
city.t1h4.plant.snow: Under the snow the box holds only brown stalks. Somebody stuck a fir twig in the top so it would not look so bare.
city.t1h4.plant.warm: In the sun the geranium smells sharp and a little bitter. A bumblebee goes round the flowers like an inspector.
city.t1h4.qsl.1: A card from Tiksi: a reindeer on ice, "Tiksi to Lyudmilovsk, 7055 kHz, signal 449." A note below: "Cold, but cheerful."
city.t1h4.qsl.2: A card from Valparaiso with a palm and a steamer. The text is in Spanish, but the word "amigo" needs no translation.
city.t1h4.qsl.3: A card from aboard the Ladoga: the shipping line's stamp, a tea stain and the navigator's signature. "Greetings to the boy with the reel" is added in another hand.
city.t1h4.qsl.4: A card from Reykjavik: the northern lights drawn in green pencil. "We heard you yesterday, you dropped out mid-sentence, please repeat."
city.t1h4.qsl.5: A card from Kyoto with a maple twig. On the back six words in Russian in careful capitals: "Thank you for the music. We listened together."
city.t1h4.qsl.all: All five cards are on the wall now, with a thread of pins strung between them. Above, in hand: "People I have heard."
city.t1h4.tuner.1: A grey box with two knobs and a needle. A coax lead runs into the wall and then out to the antenna on the bridge.
city.t1h4.tuner.clear: Clear: the needle sits right in the green sector and the speaker is clean. Today you could call Tiksi.
city.t1h4.tuner.fog: In fog the needle drifts and the knobs stick with damp. The radio amateur left a note: "Fog is the warmest air."
city.t1h4.tuner.n: At night the tuner's needle sits at the very edge of the scale: after midnight the shortwaves carry far.
city.t1h4.tuner.rain: In rain the needle jumps: the antenna is wet and a rustle comes with the signal. A slip says: "In rain, only the near ones."
city.t1h4.tuner.snow: Snow muffles the air: the needle barely moves. "In winter you hear far, but quietly," is chalked on the case.
city.t1h4.vane.1: The red arrow on the mast has turned toward the sea. Below it is a crosspiece with four brass balls, like on a real ship's vane.
city.t1h4.vane.2: A paper strip is stuck on the mast, pencilled: "North-westerly means rain. Southerly means tea on the bridge."
city.t1h4.vane.clear: Clear, and the arrow points south. The paper below promises tea on the bridge: I will have to believe it.
city.t1h4.vane.fog: In the fog the vane is barely visible, but you can hear it creak: turning this way and that, unable to choose.
city.t1h4.vane.rain: The arrow points north-west, just as the paper promised. The radio amateur was right.
city.t1h4.vane.snow: The arrow is in a crust of ice and barely trembles. The wind has not decided where to go today.
city.t1h4.view1.d1: Below lie the roofs and the street. From the lower bridge, passers-by seem closer than on the pavement: somebody is arguing about change, and you can hear every word.
city.t1h4.view1.d2: A bicycle rolls under the bridge, its bell clinking right against the steel of the rail. The hum comes up through the soles of my shoes.
city.t1h4.view1.fest: A holiday down below: garlands between the poles, and somebody has even hung paper flags on the bridge.
city.t1h4.view1.fog: The street has vanished in fog, only sounds are left: footsteps, a cough, a door. The bridge hangs in milk.
city.t1h4.view1.n: The street lamps below make a chain of yellow dots. The round windows of the capsules opposite glow like the portholes of a night steamer.
city.t1h4.view1.rain: Rain drums on the deck of the bridge, and every step below answers with a wet slap. Umbrellas drift past like coloured jellyfish.
city.t1h4.view1.snow: Snow settles on the rail and melts at once by the lantern. The street below is quiet, as if wrapped in cotton wool.
city.t1h4.view3.d1: From the upper bridge you can see the roofs of the whole block and a strip of sea in the gap. The capsules stick out of the towers like open drawers.
city.t1h4.view3.d2: The wind is stronger here than in the street. It wanders between the towers, tugs at flags and brings a smell of seaweed.
city.t1h4.view3.fest: Holiday lights below are scattered like confetti. From the upper bridge this is the best balcony in the block.
city.t1h4.view3.fog: The upper bridge in fog is like a boat with no shores. You hear people walking below, but not one is there to see.
city.t1h4.view3.n: At night you can see the lighthouse from here, flaring at the edge of the sky every few seconds. In the capsules the lights go out one by one.
city.t1h4.view3.rain: Rain slants across, sea and sky merged into grey. You stand over the void and are dry: the rail does hold.
city.t1h4.view3.snow: Snow falls from above and from below at once, like in a glass globe. Far, far away a snowplough hums.
city.t2.bed.1: The bunk is made with a checked blanket. A note on the pillow: "Lying down allowed, sleeping only for Mette." Added: "A joke. But not quite."
city.t2.deckboard.0: A handwritten notice: "The third cube (house 0-03) gives tours of its greenhouse. Entry: one sweet. Guide: Mette, aged 7."
city.t2.deckboard.1: A slip: "Selling fishing gear in good condition. Not things, stories. Thibault, third cube."
city.t2.deckboard.2: Notice: "Seeking company to watch the Perseids from the deck. Thermos mine, blanket yours. Ananya."
city.t2.deckboard.3: A note: "The snail is back in the greenhouse. Please do not worry. Mette."
city.t2.deckboard.4: A sheet with a drawing: a fish with a rod catching a man. Caption: "Fair." The author is unknown, but suspicion falls on the third cube.
city.t2.fridge.0: On the fridge a felt-tip map: the hall is "entrance", the lift is "the cave", the tip is "top of the world". An X is marked near the tip.
city.t2.fridge.1: Ananya's list: "milk, coffee (lots), red thread, lightbulb." Thibault added: "bait." Mette added: "sweets."
city.t2.fridge.2: A timetable: "Monday, Thibault cooks. Tuesday, Ananya cooks. Wednesday, we order in." The other days are crossed out and replaced with "we order in".
city.t2.fridge.3: A school note: "Mette brought a snail home from school. Parents, please be understanding." Under it: "We were." And: "The snail is in the greenhouse."
city.t2.fridge.4: A drawing by Mette: three little people in a cube, one at the very top with a fishing rod. Caption: "Dad is fishing for clouds."
city.t2.fridge.5: A sheet from Ananya: "Do not call the lift at night without need. It creaks, and Mette then spends half an hour retelling dreams." At the side: "The dreams were good."
city.t2.fridge.f: A fish magnet holds a repair slip for the lift's lightbulb. The bulb, apparently, still burns out of spite.
city.t2.hooks.day: A low hook with a yellow raincoat and a high one with Ananya's coat. The fishing vest is missing: it went to work with its owner.
city.t2.hooks.eve: Every hook is taken. A silver fish-shaped lure dangles from Thibault's vest; Mette said not to touch.
city.t2.ledger.1: The lake by the third pylon. Five in the morning, fog. Caught two perch and a great silence. Let the silence go.
city.t2.ledger.2: Mette came with me. She sat for three minutes, then asked what the fish think about. I said: the same as you. She went quiet.
city.t2.ledger.3: A pike! As long as Ananya's arm. Took a photo, let it go. At home I said it was a metre. Ananya said: "Show me with your hands." I did. She laughed.
city.t2.ledger.4: Brought half a bucket of duckweed home for the greenhouse in the tip. Ananya did not object; Mette did: "The snail lives there." We agreed to share.
city.t2.ledger.title: The fisherman's ledger
city.t2.mette.1: MY GREENHOUSE. Rules: 1. No stamping. 2. Do not touch the snail. 3. If guests come, show them everything. 4. Guests get a sweet.
city.t2.mette.2: Planted peas. They came up overnight, honest. Dad said that does not happen. I said it does if you want it hard enough.
city.t2.mette.3: The snail's name is Lift, because it climbs. Lift likes cucumbers, dislikes salt and loves quiet. Me too.
city.t2.mette.4: If you are reading this you have seen my greenhouse. So you are one of us. Look in the chest nearby: sweets. Not all of them! M.
city.t2.mette.title: Mette's notebook
city.t2.night.1: Night 1. Clear. Jupiter and four dots beside it: moons. Showed Mette; she said "oh, neighbours".
city.t2.night.2: Night 6. The glass over the bed turned out to be the best window in the house: a cube on its edge looks almost at the zenith. Why did we not lie here before?
city.t2.night.3: Night 9. Cloudy. Sat and listened to rain on the glass. Also an observation: rain has constellations too.
city.t2.night.4: Night 14. Mette fell asleep on the cushion under the glass before Orion rose. Covered her with a blanket. Orion is not going anywhere.
city.t2.night.title: The observation notebook
city.t2.p.bed: E — look at the bunk under the glass
city.t2.p.deckboard: E — read the notices on the stand
city.t2.p.hooks: E — look at the coat stand
city.t2.p.ledger: E — leaf through the notebooks on the shelf
city.t2.p.photos: E — look at the photos on the shelf
city.t2.p.sky: E — look up through the glass over the cushion
city.t2.p.slate: E — read the slate by the lift
city.t2.p.tipshelf: E — look over the little shelf
city.t2.p.toys: E — rummage in the toy bin
city.t2.p.trays: E — look at the seed trays
city.t2.photos.1: Photos: Thibault with an enormous pike and a sheepish face; Ananya at night in an observatory; Mette with a gap-toothed smile holding a snail.
city.t2.photos.2: A snapshot of the cubes from the deck in the snow. In Ananya's hand: "Our home stands on a corner. So do we, sometimes."
city.t2.shoes.1: Three pairs: Thibault's knee-high fishing boots, Ananya's heeled shoes and tiny yellow wellies. A piece of chalk lies in a welly.
city.t2.shoes.wet: Thibault's boots stand in a puddle: he did go to the lake after all. The wellies are neatly turned toes to the wall.
city.t2.sky.1: On the cushion under the glass lie an atlas with a bookmark and a child's drawing: the Moon with a very pleased face.
city.t2.slate.eve: The slate: "We are home! Mette asks guests not to step on the stars in the corridor. They are chalk, but very real."
city.t2.slate.map: Below, in a child's hand: "If you find the chest in the tip, it is mine. The map is on the fridge. M."
city.t2.slate.night: The slate: "Quiet. Mette is asleep. Ananya is not, but also quiet. Thibault left at dawn to fish; that is not a joke."
city.t2.slate.week: The slate: "Weekend. Thibault at the lake, Ananya asleep till noon, Mette gives tours of the greenhouse. Ticket: one sweet."
city.t2.slate.work: The slate: "Thibault and Ananya at work, Mette at school. Key with the neighbours. Do not feed the fish: it is drawn."
city.t2.tipshelf.1: The little shelf: a fish guide, a star guide and a guide to "everything else", a squared notebook of drawings.
city.t2.tipshelf.2: Between the books: a tin lure and a postcard with a telescope. Whose collection it is has long been unclear.
city.t2.toys.1: In the bin: a wooden whale, three dinosaurs in varying states of repair and a lift made of matchboxes, which carries a single plastic toy.
city.t2.toys.2: At the bottom a box marked "Secret. Do not open till my birthday." The box has been opened, but very carefully.
city.t2.trays.0: The trays hold peas, cucumbers and one suspicious sprout labelled "don't know what". Mette believes it is a tree.
city.t2.trays.1: The peas already wind up their sticks, the cucumbers spread their leaves. "Don't know what" is tallest of all and looks rather like a weed, but Mette will not give up.
city.t2.treasure.1: A biscuit tin chest. Inside: a shell, five sweets, a tooth (a milk tooth, not a shark's) and a note "Two for guests".
city.t2.treasure.2: The chest still holds the shell, the tooth and a list "what to give guests for their birthdays". You are not on the list yet, but in pencil: "think about".
city.t2.water.1: A watering can with a sticker "Mette". You water the peas, the cucumbers and the corner where Lift the snail lives: just a spray for him.
city.t3.apple.1: In the tub stands a small apple tree, grafted from Ruben's father's orchard. One apple has fallen and lies in the grass, dark on its sides. You pick it up.
city.t3.apple.2: The apple is sour and hard, an Antonovka, as old people call it. A tag on the branch: "Take one each. The rest is for fruit leather."
city.t3.apple.w: The branch is almost bare. Agata has brought an apple from the cellar basket and laid it under the tree on a napkin: "For tea."
city.t3.armchair.d: The armchair faces the window. The arm is rubbed shiny, a plaid over the back. Through the window: the opposite wall and, in it, other people's windows.
city.t3.armchair.n: At night the window reflects the room: the lamp, a cup, you. Beyond the reflection a window opposite is lit, and someone sits there too.
city.t3.barrel.1: A blue barrel under the downpipe, with a tap at the bottom and a metal lid. The water is warm, soft, and smells of the roof.
city.t3.barrel.2: On the lid stands a can with a spout an elbow long. The barrel is half full. There hasn't been much rain these last days, but it is enough.
city.t3.barrel.cold: There is a crust of ice in the barrel. You break it with your palm and the shards ring against the sides like fine china.
city.t3.barrel.rain: In the rain the barrel hums softly as it takes the water. You scoop a handful: cold and sweet.
city.t3.bed.1: A narrow bed made up with a waffle blanket so neatly it seems nobody has ever slept on it. On the bedside table glasses, an alarm clock and a pot of hand cream.
city.t3.bed.2: Under the bed the house slippers stand neatly. The owner will be back, and visitors may not lie on this one. For guests there is the sofa.
city.t3.bench.1: The wall under the window of 3-03 is warm. Through the glass a radio mutters, now and then something about the weather on the coast. It's good the window is so low.
city.t3.bench.2: From here you see across the canyon: windows opposite, washing, rails, a patch of sky. And nobody waiting for you to move on.
city.t3.bench.n: At night the bench is cool, but you can hear Agata inside turning a page of her notebook. The window glows yellow.
city.t3.bike.1: A green bicycle stands leaning on the wall like a person with a tired back. The chain is oiled, the bell stiff, and on the frame a sticker says "Liepaja".
city.t3.bike.2: An oilcloth is clipped to the rack with a note: "Not mine, but I love it." The owner is evidently a good-natured person.
city.t3.bike.n: At night the bicycle is fastened to the rail with a thin chain. There is no lock; the chain is more polite than secure.
city.t3.books.1: The botany shelf: an atlas of weeds, "Seed Raising in the Temperate Zone", a flower directory and a seedling log. The spines are worn by warm hands.
city.t3.books.2: A bookmark in the book on seeds: a pressed poppy and a note, "Germination 94 per cent, that's good, but you could do better." In Agata's hand.
city.t3.books.3: On the bottom shelf a pile of seed catalogues covering thirty years. You can follow how names and prices changed, but not the taste of tomatoes.
city.t3.cat.d: The cat is asleep on the warm concrete, white paws tucked in. She answers any touch with one ear.
city.t3.cat.e: In the evening the cat sits like a sentry: she watches the yard lights below. She purrs softly when you are near and doesn't turn.
city.t3.cat.m: The grey cat waits by her bowl as if the bowl might come to her by itself. You stroke her back: she looks past you at the stairs.
city.t3.cat.n: The bowl is empty and licked shiny. The cat is gone about her night business. Dew glitters on the rim of the bowl.
city.t3.cat.rain: In the rain the cat has squeezed under the bench and watches from there: two of her own eyes and a green one reflected in the bowl.
city.t3.chair.1: A chair at the round table. On the table a small vase of primulas taken from the roof and a cup with a broken handle that Agata doesn't drink from but won't throw away.
city.t3.chair.2: From this spot you see everything at once: the door, the stove, the armchair and the bed. Agata is like a captain on a bridge, only the bridge is made of rug.
city.t3.desk.1: At the desk: a lamp with a green shade, a pile of notebooks and envelopes with stamps of different countries. The paper smells faintly of other people's cities.
city.t3.desk.n: At night the lamp throws a warm circle on the notebook. This is where letters are written: words are printed in mirror image on the blotter.
city.t3.door.d: The door of 3-03 stands wide open, propped with a stool. On the brass plate: "A. Brandt. Ring loudly, I'm in the garden." Inside smells of tea and earth.
city.t3.door.e: The door is ajar and the smell of evening tea comes through the gap. Agata doesn't lock before ten. "Whoever needs me will knock," she says.
city.t3.door.n: The door is pulled to but not locked. Through the gap you see yellow light and the edge of an armchair. Beside it slippers, toes pointing to the stairs.
city.t3.feeder.1: A feeder shaped like a little house with a red roof. Two tits sit on the perch waiting for you to step away. You step away.
city.t3.feeder.2: In the feeder, sunflower seeds and a piece of fat on a string. "Sunflowers are ours, the fat is somebody else's," jokes the tag.
city.t3.feeder.rain: The little house of the feeder is wet and shiny, but dry inside. The birds sit on the rail and wait for the rain to pass.
city.t3.frame.1: A wooden box with a glass lid: a cold frame for seedlings. Inside warm air smelling of earth and tiny green sprouts with two leaves each.
city.t3.frame.2: Condensation on the glass. A stick props the lid open. On a wooden strip in ink: "Cucumbers? No. Basil. Yes."
city.t3.frame.cold: In the cold the frame is covered with a blanket and two bricks. Agata does not hand her seedlings to the frost without a fight.
city.t3.herbs.1: Thyme, savory, mint, sage and something Agata calls "Nino", because the seeds came in an envelope from Tbilisi with only that word on it.
city.t3.herbs.2: The bed smells when you run a hand over it. Slate markers on sticks give the names. "Don't pick without asking, but don't be shy either."
city.t3.herbs.3: You water thinly so as not to wash the soil from the roots. The mint shines at once, the savory pretends not to care.
city.t3.herbs.rain: Herbs in the rain smell so strongly you want to bury your nose in them. No can needed.
city.t3.hop.1: A hopscotch drawn in chalk on the concrete: one square, another, two side by side, and a slice of moon at the end. The numbers are worn off.
city.t3.hop.2: You hop: left, right, both. On the third square you catch your balance, and the rail no longer seems quite so high.
city.t3.hop.3: Someone has added in the last square: "Home!". Nobody manages to land in it on the first go.
city.t3.hop.n: In the dark the chalk is hardly visible. You hop by feel, from memory, and once you set your foot exactly in the middle.
city.t3.jar.1: A glass jar with a paper label: "Seeds that didn't leave. Take them, plant them, write what grew." You tip a handful into your palm.
city.t3.jar.2: The seeds are small and many-coloured: sunflower, poppy, dill and something round. You pour them into your pocket like pebbles.
city.t3.kettle.d: The kettle boils quickly on the stove. Agata has left a tin on the table: "Black tea, blackcurrant leaf, mint from the roof." You take a cup.
city.t3.kettle.n: At night you put the kettle on quietly so as not to wake the house. The roof mint in the cup smells so good you want to go up again.
city.t3.laundry.1: A line sags across the canyon with washing on it: a sheet like a sail, shirts, two towels, a sock without its pair. All of it sways gently in the draught.
city.t3.laundry.2: The pegs have little marks painted on them: a fish, a star, the number "11". Every flat has its own, which is easier than quarrelling.
city.t3.laundry.mon: On Mondays the lines are full from end to end: in this house everybody washes on Monday and then talks about the weather for half the day.
city.t3.laundry.n: At night the washing on the line is dark and heavy; the draught plays with the edge of the sheet. You feel like tiptoeing past.
city.t3.laundry.rain: In the rain the washing was brought in early. The line hangs empty, only one forgotten peg swings on it like a bell's clapper.
city.t3.news.1: Neighbours! A. Brandt (3-03, the door on level three is always ajar) has broken her wrist. Nobody can carry water to the beds on the roof. The tap is on level two, the can is in the barrel on the roof. Thank you. Agata.
city.t3.news.2: The washing lines over the canyon are shared. Don't take down other people's things, mark your pegs with paint. The house committee.
city.t3.news.3: The box on level two lets the wind take the letters. Latch the flap. Collections at ten, sixteen and twenty.
city.t3.news.4: The grey cat with white paws has been found: she sits on level three by her bowl. No sausage, please. Anyone who likes may leave her fish heads, small ones for preference.
city.t3.news.5: The "Pink Heart" tomatoes on the roof of 3-03 are starting to blush. The first fruit goes to the first waterers. Agata asks: don't water the sunflowers in the rain, they will take offence. And thank you, generally.
city.t3.news.6: The lamp on the landing of level four has burned out. I'll change it on Saturday. Whoever can be bothered, bring a forty-watt bulb.
city.t3.news.7: On Sunday there is tea on the roof of 3-03 at four. No pie, but there is tea. Wipe your feet. Agata.
city.t3.news.8: Agata thanks everyone who watered: the apple tree has given nine apples. Take one each, the rest is for fruit leather.
city.t3.news.9: On Saturday we paint the handrails blue. Bring your own brushes, the paint is shared, don't spill it on the floor. The house committee.
city.t3.news.f: Happy holiday, house! Open the curtains, light the string of bulbs on the roof. Whoever passes the door of 3-03, drop in for a minute: Agata has the kettle on.
city.t3.news.r: The stairs are slippery in the rain. Hold the rail and don't hurry, this is not a race. The house committee.
city.t3.note.1: The tap is on level two, the can is in the barrel on the roof. Morning and evening, not in the heat or the rain. Tomatoes at the root, not on the leaf. Sunflowers a lot, herbs a little.
city.t3.note.2: If I happen to be asleep, tiptoe through; the kettle is on the stove. Don't stroke the cat on the roof: she is mine. You may stroke the cat on the stairs: she is everyone's.
city.t3.note.3: The switch for the lamp on the pole is to the right of the garden entrance. The jar on the shelf by the radio is for anyone who wants to plant something at home. Thank you. A.B.
city.t3.note.title: A note for whoever is watering

city.t3.p.barrel: E — scoop water from the barrel
city.t3.p.books: E — take a book from the shelf
city.t3.p.chair: E — sit down at the table
city.t3.p.door: E — knock at the open door
city.t3.p.frame: E — lift the cold frame's glass
city.t3.p.jar: E — open the jar of seeds
city.t3.p.laundry: E — look up at the washing
city.t3.p.packets: E — look over the seed packets
city.t3.p.pots: E — feel the soil in the pots
city.t3.p.sill_w: E — look over the pots on the sill
city.t3.p.sofa: E — lie down on the sofa
city.t3.p.swap: E — take a magazine from the swap shelf
city.t3.p.tap: E — fill a bottle at the tap
city.t3.p.window: E — look out of the window
city.t3.packets.1: A fan of seed packets on the desk: pink heart, thyme, sunflower, poppy, dill, and something with no name. Each has a date and somebody's handwriting.
city.t3.packets.2: A packet of poppies from Mari of Tartu with a note: "Sow in April, no earlier, she will know." Agata doesn't know who "she" is, but obeys.
city.t3.packets.3: A packet with no name: black seeds in the shape of commas inside. On the back in a child's hand: "These are flowers too. Don't laugh."
city.t3.packets.4: One packet is sealed with tape and marked in red pencil: "Do not open until spring. Ruben." Agata has kept it for fifteen years.
city.t3.photo.a: A framed photograph: people in white coats at long tables with bags of seeds. A plate: "Harbour Botanic Station, 1989." Agata is second from the right.
city.t3.photo.a2: A pencil note on the back: "Forty thousand packets in one winter. Our hands smelled of dill until June." Quite a job.
city.t3.photo.b: A photograph: a man in a pilot's uniform on the mole with a cat on his shoulder. A caption: "Ruben, 1997." The cat looks away, like him.
city.t3.photo.b2: By the frame a dried ear of grain. Agata speaks of Ruben in the present tense, and it occurs to nobody to correct her.
city.t3.pigeons.1: Three pigeons stroll the landing like caretakers: one blue-grey, one with a white bib, one simply fat. They look at you without interest.
city.t3.pigeons.2: The pigeons aren't afraid of the stairs: they fly up onto the rail, then walk down again. One likes to walk on the "3" painted on the boxes.
city.t3.pigeons.n: At night the pigeons sleep on the rail, pressed together. One opens an eye and shuts it again.
city.t3.pigeons.rain: In the rain the pigeons sit in a row under the overhang, fluffed up, watching the water. You understand them.
city.t3.post.d: The morning collection has gone: nothing rustles in the slot. The next is at sixteen hundred. A sticker on the tin flap: "The post is a pedestrian's friend."
city.t3.post.e: By the evening collection there is a stack inside: somebody wrote half a dozen postcards at once. The top one is addressed to Niigata.
city.t3.post.m: A small yellow-plated box with a post-horn. The plate: "Collections: 10, 16, 20. None on Sundays." The slot is a little wider than it should be: someone has been posting postcards.
city.t3.post.n: At night the box is cold and dark. The postman has the key, and on the door someone has scratched a "thank you" with a nail.
city.t3.post.sun: It is Sunday: there will be no collection. The box takes letters anyway; they will just wait until Monday.
city.t3.pots.1: In the pots the soil is dry on top and damp below: Agata waters from a long-spouted kettle, a little at a time, every morning.
city.t3.pots.2: The fern by the window has been put out on the landing "to breathe". A tag on the pot: "Don't repot, he knows where he is happy."
city.t3.pots.cold: The pots have been taken in for the night: only empty saucers with a thin crust of ice are left on the landing.
city.t3.pots.rain: The pots have been moved under the overhang so the rain won't drown them. Only the cactus stands out in the rain and doesn't mind.
city.t3.radio.d: By day the announcer reads listeners' letters: somebody in Jelgava has bred a radish that isn't bitter. Agata writes the name in her notebook.
city.t3.radio.e: In the evening, a programme about the stars and the sowing calendar: "Waxing moon, sow what grows upward." It sounds like a spell.
city.t3.radio.m: The morning edition of "For Those in the Field": frost forecast, potato prices, then a song about a fisherman's wife. Agata sings along from the kitchen.
city.t3.radio.n: At night the radio hisses softly and picks up a distant tango station. The volume is set so that the neighbours can't hear.
city.t3.radio.sat: Saturday: the "Garden and Home" programme. The announcer asks who has already sown onion sets. Agata answers the radio aloud; it doesn't take offence.
city.t3.rchair.1: The chair is padded with an old plaid. From here you see the sunflowers from the side and a strip of sky between two walls. The tea cools, but there is no hurry.
city.t3.rchair.2: People sometimes look into the garden from the neighbouring windows to make sure everything is in place. Saying hello isn't done; a nod is enough.
city.t3.rchair.n: At night the garden is dark, only the lamp on its pole sways overhead and the string of bulbs flickers when the wind goes through it.
city.t3.rtable.1: A round table under a canopy of bulbs. On it a cup, a teapot and a box of dominoes with worn corners. Two stools, both warm.
city.t3.rtable.2: The tiles knock on the wood: a sound you can hear across the yard and two floors up. For the neighbours it has long been like a clock.
city.t3.rview.d: Beyond the rail, two neighbouring yards and the roof of a far house. On it a black dot: a crow, with the air of a landlady.
city.t3.rview.d2: The wind carries a smell of sea and wet earth from somebody's bed. From the windows below come radios and the clatter of dishes.
city.t3.rview.n: At night the yard below is black, only one window glows, and someone stands in it with a mug, looking up too.
city.t3.sign.1: A two-sided board at the garden entrance: "SEEDS THAT DIDN'T LEAVE. Wipe your feet. Put the can back. One apple each. Don't call the cat, she'll come."
city.t3.sign.2: On the back, as a list: "The lamp switch is on the pole. Tea on Sundays at 4. Thanks to all who carried water. Agata Brandt, 3-03."
city.t3.sill.e1: On the east sill, three trays of seedlings: peppers, asters and one labelled simply "we'll see". Shoots with two leaves each.
city.t3.sill.e2: The seedlings are turned a quarter-turn toward the light every morning. A slip by the glass: "Don't touch the leaves. Don't breathe. Joking, you can breathe."
city.t3.sill.w1: On the west sill, cacti and two ferns in pots painted by somebody's children: stars, houses, a crooked cow.
city.t3.sill.w2: The cactus by the glass bloomed in September. "Once a year," says the tag, "and always when there are guests. Polite."
city.t3.sofa.bed: You woke to the quiet sound of water: Agata is filling the kettle in the kitchen. A dry towel is folded on the chair by the sofa. The house is already on its feet.
city.t3.sofa.d: The guest sofa with an embroidered cushion. "A friend comes from Riga and sleeps here. You may too, if you are very tired," says a note.
city.t3.sofa.n: The sofa is soft and smells of dry lavender. Agata has thrown a wool plaid over it and left a note on the cushion: "The lamp is on your right."
city.t3.stove.prompt: E — throw water on the stones
city.t3.sun.1: The sunflowers stand in a rank, heads toward the canyon, to the east. "They turn toward the stairs, not the sea. Arguing is useless," says the tag.
city.t3.sun.2: Seeds from Yoshiko of Niigata, 2003. The stems are as thick as a wrist. The lower leaves are big as palms and warm to the touch.
city.t3.sun.3: You water right at the base, carefully stepping around somebody else's shadow on the soil. A sunflower nods, as if it had understood something.
city.t3.sun.rain: In the rain the sunflowers have bowed their heads and wait. Agata asked not to water them in the rain: "They'll take offence." You just stood nearby.
city.t3.swap.1: A narrow cupboard on the landing with a sign: "Take one, leave one." On the shelves, travel magazines, one about gardens, one about bicycles.
city.t3.swap.2: You take a magazine and, by the rules, leave something instead: an old postcard you found in your pocket. The door clicks shut by itself.
city.t3.swap.n: At night the cupboard is shut with a rusty hook; the spines show through the glass. Someone has left it a tidy note: "Till morning."
city.t3.t3_ballcart.1: The ball cart: eight balls. One is flat, they call it "the Sloth," and nobody takes it. I took it. The Sloth turned out heavier than it looked.
city.t3.t3_ballcart.2: The balls smell of rubber and leather and each has its own character. The ginger one bounces highest but on principle won't go in the hoop.
city.t3.t3_ballcart.3: On the cart in chalk: "Return the balls. Yourself too." I returned both.
city.t3.t3_bars.1: The girls lined up at the wall bars: "legs higher, point your toes." I hung to one side, didn't point my toes, but tried.
city.t3.t3_bars.2: The rungs are warm from somebody's hands. I pulled my legs up to my stomach and held until they shook. The coach calls it an "L-sit," my stomach has another word.
