city.t3.t3_bars.3: I hung at the very top and counted the windows. There are so many in the hall that I lost count twice. I liked losing count.
city.t3.t3_bike.1: In the morning the sea outside is a grey blanket. I pedalled and chased it to the very horizon. The horizon didn't give in.
city.t3.t3_bike.2: By day gulls pass the window, and a little ship behind them. The ship and I keep the same pace. I won't overtake it: it seems to be going to Sweden.
city.t3.t3_bike.3: In the evening the lighthouse comes on in the window. Every turn of the pedals, one flash. I counted to forty and lost it.
city.t3.t3_bike.4: At night the window shows only my own outline: a boy on a bicycle that goes nowhere. The boy is very determined.
city.t3.t3_changing.1: Behind the screen it's cramped but cosy: a hook, a mirror with a chipped corner and somebody's socks with kittens. The socks aren't mine, but I like them.
city.t3.t3_changing.2: Changed in three moves and spent three more on the laces. The laces held me to a draw.
city.t3.t3_changing.3: The screen is a fabric with a pattern like grandma's sofa. You change and feel like a guest.
city.t3.t3_changing.4: In winter it's chilly behind the screen, and you change twice as fast. The socks with kittens are still hanging on the hook.
city.t3.t3_changing.5: Saturday, match day: there's a queue for the screen and everyone hurries each other in whispers. I changed without taking my hat off and only noticed afterwards.
city.t3.t3_changing.6: The kitten socks are gone from the hook. In their place a note: "Found. Thanks for not touching them."
city.t3.t3_club_board.1: "Sections: basketball, gymnastics, weights, painting, pottery studio. Sign up with the coach, entry free, socks your own."
city.t3.t3_club_board.2: "Young Marine Painters" circle: Saturday, 11:00. Please bring your own eyes and old shirts: shirts will do for aprons.
city.t3.t3_club_board.3: COURTYARD TOURNAMENT "GOLDEN BALL" on Saturday! The "Surf Juniors" need a fifth player. Skill at shooting is optional.
city.t3.t3_club_board.4: "Surf Juniors" line-up: Lyosha, Taya, Ramil, Vanya and... The fifth line is in pencil: "somebody." "Somebody" is underlined twice.
city.t3.t3_club_board.5: Practice before the tournament: every day at five except Sunday. Late: an extra lap. On time: tea in the buffet (tea is not free).
city.t3.t3_club_board.6: Kit for the "Surf Juniors" is handed out at the till. Jersey No. 5 is free. Size: "still growing."
city.t3.t3_club_board.7: The tournament is on the hall's court, Saturday at 15:00. Fans: seats on the benches. Don't catch the balls. Catch the mood.
city.t3.t3_club_board.8: "SURF JUNIORS: SECOND PLACE!" The team thanks the coach, the buffet lady for the tea, and "number five" for turning up. The certificate is waiting at the till.
city.t3.t3_coach.1: "New here? The hall opens at seven, the sections are on the timetable by the door. Found a free ball? Shoot. Just not at the windows: they cost me more than the balls."
city.t3.t3_coach.10: "Second place is when you're glad and cross at once, and both halves are right. Taya is telling the whole courtyard about your shot. One more time?"
city.t3.t3_coach.2: "You've been around a few days now. I noticed: you come in like it's a job. Good. Sport loves the ones who show up on a boring Tuesday."
city.t3.t3_coach.3: "I hear you were shooting from the far line. Missed, but with a face like you'd scored. In basketball that's half the job. The other half is scoring."
city.t3.t3_coach.4: "Not now, the boys are warming up. Come over when I blow the last whistle."
city.t3.t3_coach.5: "Quiet, the girls are counting their jumps. If anyone loses count they start over, and I'm the one who has to listen."
city.t3.t3_coach.6: "Listen, 'Surf Juniors' have a courtyard tournament and there are only four of us. Vova moved away with his parents, his ball stayed behind. Want to be the fifth? Running is optional. Standing there and not getting in the way is a must."
city.t3.t3_coach.7: "Come to practice at five. The hoop on the back wall is for people who mean to play, not pose for photos."
city.t3.t3_coach.8: "Good that you keep coming. The number-five jersey is at the till, locker five is free. Just don't wipe your face on it: there's one jersey and a lot of faces."
city.t3.t3_coach.9: "Game day. Stick close to Taya: she reads the court better than I read the paper. The rest will sort itself out."
city.t3.t3_court.1: The tournament! Lyosha passed me the ball and the hall suddenly went quiet, as if everyone were waiting for me to do something. I did: I shot. The ball knocked twice on the rim and dropped in. Taya shrieked so that the glasses in the buffet shook.
city.t3.t3_court.2: The Seagulls pressed from all sides. Ramil cut right, Taya took the rebound, and I stood under the hoop and waited. And got what I waited for: the ball came into my hands by itself. We lost the final by one point, but they clapped for us too.
city.t3.t3_court.3: The court after the tournament: sweet wrappers, chalk, somebody's hairpin. The fans' ribbon is still hanging on the hoop.
city.t3.t3_court.4: Two on two: me and Taya against Ramil and Lyosha. We lost 6 to 10. Taya said it was a warm-up and I believed her, with relief.
city.t3.t3_court.5: A scrimmage to ten. I scored two, Lyosha scored eight and apologised a lot. All of this is for the tournament.
city.t3.t3_court.6: On Sunday the five don't meet: everyone has families, grannies, lunches. I dribbled alone on the empty court. The ball obeyed well.
city.t3.t3_easel_lighthouse.1: The lighthouse in the morning is pale as a candle in a sunny room. I painted almost without colour, only white, and it began to glow from inside.
city.t3.t3_easel_lighthouse.2: By day the lighthouse is just a red-and-white tower. I painted a tower and got a chimney. I wrote "Lighthouse" under it. The caption helped.
city.t3.t3_easel_lighthouse.3: At sunset the lighthouse turns pink and its shadow lies all the way to the pier. I spent longer on the shadow than on the tower.
city.t3.t3_easel_lighthouse.4: At night the lighthouse is all about the beam. I painted it in yellow on dark, and the canvas seemed to warm up a little.
city.t3.t3_easel_sea.1: The morning sea is grey as pearl: grey, pink and a little green. I painted with a wet brush and the sea came out wet.
city.t3.t3_easel_sea.2: By day the sea is blue and there's never enough blue. I painted until it looked like a postcard and was upset. The studio leader said: "Somebody paints the postcards too."
city.t3.t3_easel_sea.3: In the evening the sea is gold, then copper, then dark. I couldn't mix paints fast enough: the sea changed faster than the brush.
city.t3.t3_easel_sea.4: At night I painted the sea from memory, by lamplight: black, with a moon path. The leader said: "The night sea isn't painted with the eyes." What with, he didn't say.
city.t3.t3_easel_teacher.1: The teacher's easel: a big canvas with a charcoal sketch: a pier, gulls, a boy in a hood. The boy has no face yet.
city.t3.t3_easel_teacher.2: The teacher has put paint on the pier: a peach sky, a steel sea. The boy still has no face but stands more firmly.
city.t3.t3_easel_teacher.3: The boy has got a face. I look at him and try not to think that it's a little familiar.
city.t3.t3_easel_teacher.4: The canvas is signed and stands by the door with a note: "Hang in the foyer." The boy looks at the sea. Now at the sea, not at me.
city.t3.t3_glaze.1: On the bench, jars of glaze: "green," "blue," "do not touch." "Do not touch" is the prettiest. Nothing to touch until Thursday: the bowls haven't been fired yet.
city.t3.t3_glaze.2: I glazed bowl No. 7: green, with a little blue on the bottom. The potter warned me: in the jar the glaze is one colour, out of the kiln it will be another. Like people.
city.t3.t3_glaze.3: The bench is tidied, the jars are shut. On the newspaper, the print of a bowl's foot: someone checked whether it stands level.
city.t3.t3_glaze.4: The bench is empty, only the "do not touch" jar stands at the edge. I didn't touch it. Apparently I'm growing up.
city.t3.t3_hoop_free.1: The west hoop is warmed up by morning: the sun comes through the window right onto the backboard. I aimed at the patch of sunlight. I hit it more often than the hoop.
city.t3.t3_hoop_free.2: It's quiet at the west wall: people come here who aren't ready for spectators yet. I became one of them. Two in a row, and at once I wished someone were watching.
city.t3.t3_hoop_free.3: By evening the floor creaks louder and the ball bounces more cheerfully. I shot until the shadow of the hoop crept to the middle of the hall.
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.1: A practice is under way at the back wall: five boys, three balls, one whistle. They put me on rebounds. I rebounded honestly and even returned a ball to whoever threw it.
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.2: At the back wall the girls practise shots from under the hoop and count aloud. I stood beside them and shot in time: scored on "seventeen."
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.3: In the morning the hoop is mine. The cleaner was wiping the lines, and the ball left dusty marks on them: exactly as many as my misses.
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.4: In the evening the light over the hoop is warm, like in a film about champions. Ten shots, no spectators, I clapped for myself.
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.5: On Saturdays it's courtyard against courtyard here. They took me "for five minutes." It turned out to be twenty.
city.t3.t3_hoop_main.6: On Sunday there's a grandfather and grandson at the hoop. Grandpa teaches shooting "from the chest," the boy says "from the heart." The boy, by the way, scored.
city.t3.t3_kiln.1: The kiln is cold. On the shelf beside it, raw bowls, grey as mice. You can't pick them up: they'd crumble from a glance.
city.t3.t3_kiln.2: The kiln hums and smells evenly of warm brick. Through the peephole, orange light. A note: "Firing. Do not open. Do not knock. Peek no more than three times."
city.t3.t3_kiln.3: The kiln has cooled. The door is ajar, inside white cups with a pink tinge. One has cracked. The potter says: "That's not a flaw, that's character."
city.t3.t3_kiln.4: The second firing, with glaze. A red peephole, a quiet hum. On the kiln, in chalk, a number: 1060.
city.t3.t3_kiln.5: The kiln is open and the finished ware is inside! It shines like wet stones. Bowl No. 7 is green as the sea on a grey day, with two blue specks.
city.t3.t3_kiln.6: The kiln is resting, like everyone. Warm to the touch. On the floor, crumbs of glaze, green and light blue.
city.t3.t3_lockers.1: Lockers by number. On No. 7 someone scratched: "Do not open until victory." The door opens, so there must have been one.
city.t3.t3_lockers.2: On door No. 3 there's a fish sticker and a note: "Slippers live here. Do not feed."
city.t3.t3_lockers.3: A new paper on locker No. 5: "Free. For the fifth." In the coach's handwriting, pressed hard.
city.t3.t3_lockers.4: Locker No. 5 stands open. Inside, a jersey with a five and a note on the hook: "Size: still growing. Don't lose it."
city.t3.t3_lockers.5: On locker No. 5 my name has been added in chalk. Chalk, so it's easy to wipe off. It doesn't come off: I tried with my sleeve.
city.t3.t3_mats.1: On the mats the girls do the "bridge" and the "birch." Mine came out more of a "stump." Lidiya Pavlovna said: "A stump is a tree too."
city.t3.t3_mats.2: The mats are warm after the gymnasts. I lay down and looked at the ceiling: a cobweb shaped like a constellation. I named it the Vaulting Horse.
city.t3.t3_pool.1: "POOL (tower, upper bridge, turn left) CLOSED. Tiles being replaced. The tiles have arrived, the tiler has arrived. The glue has not."
city.t3.t3_pool.2: "The glue has arrived. The tiler has gone to fetch tiles of another colour. The pool will be 'sea' rather than 'white'. Thank you for your patience."
city.t3.t3_pool.3: "Tiling in progress. Six 25-metre lanes will be painted on the bottom. Lanes are promised straight, though straightness remains at the tiler's discretion."
city.t3.t3_pool.4: "Filling has begun. The pool fills like a cup in the kefir queue: slowly and with dignity." The lifeguards have hung the ring in its proper place. The ring now looks at the water.
city.t3.t3_pool.5: "The pool opens on Monday. A trial swim for those who bring a doctor's note and a cap." A cap can be found in the "Lost caps" box at the till.
city.t3.t3_reception.1: "The pool needs a doctor's note, the gym a season ticket, table tennis a good mood. Which of those have you got?"
city.t3.t3_reception.2: Cups above the desk, and under them a box marked "Lost swimming caps." There are more caps than cups.
city.t3.t3_reception.3: The cashier hands out a locker key on an elastic band: "Number seven, a lucky one. Don't mix it up with eight, that's the coach's."
city.t3.t3_reception.4: Timetable of sections: gymnastics, swimming, "Health after sixty" and "Health before sixteen." The second one is for me.
city.t3.t3_reception.5: "I'm keeping the number-five jersey, but I hand it only to those who promise not to wipe their face on it. The coach said: 'A jersey has a number, not a towel.'"
city.t3.t3_reception.6: "The coach has gone to paint the balls yellow. So that from the stands you can tell which is the ball and which is us. We're visible anyway."
city.t3.t3_results.1: Courtyard league table. 1. Seagulls: 12 points. 2. Lighthouse: 10. 3. Surf Juniors: 8. In pencil: "there will be more."
city.t3.t3_results.2: Hall records. Vault: Lyosha, "with room to spare." Pull-ups: Taya, 14, "not counting sighs." Next to it, an empty line: "a record not yet beaten."
city.t3.t3_results.3: Swimming, 25 m record: 19.4 seconds. The plaque is under repair together with the pool. The record-holder is waiting for water.
city.t3.t3_results.4: Courtyard tournament, results. 1. Seagulls: 3 wins. 2. Surf Juniors: 2. 3. Lighthouse. Best newcomer: No. 5 with 4 points, 3 rebounds, 1 ball into his own hoop. The own-hoop ball has been crossed out "for educational reasons."
city.t3.t3_results.5: Under the table, in chalk: "Thanks, number five." In the match record, a name is written against number five. The one I know already.
city.t3.t3_sauna_sit.1: In the morning the sauna is empty and smells of birch. I sat and listened to the stones cooling: tick, tick, tick.
city.t3.t3_sauna_sit.2: After practice the basketball players pile in, red as crayfish. The whole conversation: "Oof." And the answer: "Yep."
city.t3.t3_sauna_sit.3: Saturday steam! On the top bench a man in a felt hat reads a wet newspaper. The news is as fresh as it gets: straight out of the steam.
city.t3.t3_sauna_sit.4: On Sunday there are two people in the sauna, both asleep sitting up. I sat quieter than water so as not to disturb the Sunday.
city.t3.t3_sauna_water.1: I splashed a ladle onto the stones. They hissed and the steam settled on my shoulders like a warm blanket.
city.t3.t3_sauna_water.2: A ladle, a bucket, the stones: very simple. Only the steam doesn't listen and goes where it likes, usually into my face.
city.t3.t3_sauna_water.3: A sign on the stove: "Pour water in moderation." I poured in moderation. Moderation, it turns out, smells of a birch whisk.
city.t3.t3_sauna_water.4: Frost outside, and in here the stones hiss and the steam smells of summer. Someone on the top bench says, "Now winter can come."
city.t3.t3_sauna_water.5: After the Saturday game the whole team is in the steam room. The ladle goes round, and everyone splashes a little so there's enough for all.
city.t3.t3_sauna_water.6: The attendant showed me how to pour properly: not in the middle but round the edge, in a thin stream. The steam rose evenly, as if by the score.
city.t3.t3_scoreboard.1: The scoreboard is alive: "SURF JUNIORS 41 : 42 SEAGULLS." Taya's sister flips the number cards, and the hall greets every flip with a sigh.
city.t3.t3_scoreboard.2: The scoreboard is frozen at 41:42. Nobody flipped it back: let it remember how it was.
city.t3.t3_scoreboard.3: The scoreboard says 00:00. The number cards have faded a little, as if they too wanted to win all those matches.
city.t3.t3_scoreboard.4: The scoreboard says 00:00. On Sunday it has the day off and the numbers sleep face down.
city.t3.t3_sections.2: Today: basketball, "Surf Juniors", 15:00–19:00. Please don't step on the court in street shoes. We ask politely. The coach asks impolitely.
city.t3.t3_sections.3: Today: gymnastics, Lidiya Pavlovna's group. The vaulting horse is warming up, the wall bars are taken until six. Spectators: the bench.
city.t3.t3_sections.4: From 7 to 15 the hall is free; at 11:00 there's a PE lesson for class 6B. Please don't mistake the balls for heads.
city.t3.t3_sections.5: Saturday: weights until lunch, games after. Spectators free, players: bring water, leave the nerves.
city.t3.t3_sections.6: Sunday: short day, no coach. The ball is the responsibility of whoever picked it up.
city.t3.t3_sections.7: The hall closes at 21:00. The night watchman asks to be reminded of this very politely and very early.
city.t3.t3_shower.1: The hot water came in fits, like thoughts after practice. Then it steadied, and I stood there until I remembered the queue.
city.t3.t3_shower.2: The soap fell, I went after it, it went away from me. Caught it on the third try. Sport, basically.
city.t3.t3_shower.3: The water washed off the dust, the tiredness and half of my misses. The rest will dry by themselves.
city.t3.t3_shower.4: Steam, the noise of water, an echo. I sing without an ear but loudly. The shower is the one place where I'm surely the champion.
city.t3.t3_shower.5: In the morning there's still plenty of hot water and nobody in the showers. Steam hangs under the ceiling like fog over the bay.
city.t3.t3_shower.6: In the evening after training the hot water runs out at the third person. I was fourth. A cold shower, the coach says, toughens the character.
city.t3.t3_shower.7: In winter you come out of the showers as red as a lobster and stand by the radiator until your hair stops steaming.
city.t3.t3_tactics.1: A chalk diagram on the board: circles are ours, crosses are not. One arrow leads to the basket. Another leads to the buffet, and it looks thicker.
city.t3.t3_tactics.2: A play called "Five": four circles stand firm, the fifth is empty with a question mark. Underneath: "newcomer: don't get in the way, but do teach."
city.t3.t3_tactics.3: The fifth circle has moved to the left wing and is ringed twice. Beside it: "don't let him fall, pass on time, make noise only when it counts."
city.t3.t3_tactics.4: The plan for Saturday: the Seagulls play rough, so play fast. Over it, big: "Run!" and small: "and think."
city.t3.t3_tactics.5: The board has been wiped clean. In the corner, a circled five and one word: "Thanks."
city.t3.t3_vault.1: Lidiya Pavlovna's group: two vaults each over the horse. I got one counted: the second was more of a fall.
city.t3.t3_vault.2: Ran up, pushed off the springboard, cleared it, this time with room to spare. The horse nodded, or I imagined it.
city.t3.t3_ware.1: The shelf is empty apart from somebody's old cups and a bag of plaster.
city.t3.t3_ware.2: On the shelf, raw bowls by number, still grey and damp. No. 7 stands between two others and looks confident.
city.t3.t3_ware.3: The bowls have dried and paled like bread. They stand in line for the kiln. No touching: a finger can leave you in them forever.
city.t3.t3_ware.4: After the first firing the bowls are pink and ring when flicked. No. 7 is whole. Beside it, a cracked No. 3: the potter kept it "for beauty."
city.t3.t3_ware.5: The glazed bowls look wet but matt: the colour will come out in the kiln. Hard to believe, but it will.
city.t3.t3_ware.6: Finished! Green, blue, speckled. Beside them a note: "Take them yourselves. If you can't take them, give them away." No. 7 is mine.
city.t3.t3_ware.7: The shelf is resting. On it, one bowl, somebody's, with a note: "This one's mine. Not for giving." Beside it an empty spot for mine.
city.t3.t3_weights.1: The weightlifting section clatters in the corner: two huge men lift plates and whisper curses at them. I joined the queue for the bar: it moved slowly but respectfully.
city.t3.t3_weights.2: The basketball boys are working their legs. "Squat until you're lower than the hoop," the coach orders. "Then stand up and you'll be taller." I squatted five times. Stood up taller.
city.t3.t3_weights.3: Quiet and iron. I loaded the plates the way the coach taught me: the strength is in the legs, not the face. The face went red anyway.
city.t3.t3_weights.4: Held the bar without lifting. The bar didn't care: it's iron. I did. I think I've made friends with iron.
city.t3.t3_wheel.1: The potter said: "Centre it. Clay is like character: press and it runs away, don't press and it won't stand." On the third try the walls held. Bowl No. 7 came out with one side higher than the other. It was put aside to dry.
city.t3.t3_wheel.2: The wheel is quiet today: the kiln is firing and the potter looks into it every ten minutes, like into an oven with a pie. I just centred clay, for the feel of it.
city.t3.t3_wheel.3: Nobody sits at the wheel today: everyone is waiting. The bowls came out of the kiln after the first firing, No. 7 turned pink and rings like a bell. Next comes glaze, and that's not the wheel, that's the bench.
city.t3.t3_wheel.4: At the weekend the wheel goes to the little ones: they make "wrong" hares. They left me a lump too. I made a hare with one ear. The potter said: "That's not a hare, that's a running hare."
city.t3.tap.1: A cast-iron standpipe with a red handle. The water is icy and smells of stone; at the bottom of the bucket yesterday's last drop rings.
city.t3.tap.2: A note is pinned over the tap: "Take roof water here. Don't spill on the stairs, it freezes. A. B."
city.t3.tap.3: The grating under the tap is rinsed clean: somebody sweeps here in the mornings. The bucket is new and blue, with a "3" stamped on it.
city.t3.tap.cold: The tap is wrapped in rags and tied with string. The water comes in a thin thread: one more night and it will freeze solid.
city.t3.tap.n: At night the tap drips into the bucket, once every three seconds. All the way up the stairs you can hear the drops being counted.
city.t3.tap.rain: In the rain the tap water is hard to tell from the rain itself. The bucket fills by itself while you stand there.
city.t3.tomato.1: Twelve bushes on stakes, tied with strips of an old sheet. The soil is dark and damp below. The water goes into it without a trace and without regret.
city.t3.tomato.2: A tag on a stake: "Pink Heart, Kaunas, 1994". The bushes are heavy with green fruit; two are already blushing on one side.
city.t3.tomato.3: You water at the root as the note says: not on the leaves, not at midday, not from the bucket but from the can with the rose. It smells of tomato leaf.
city.t3.tomato.cold: There is frost on the leaves this morning. The bush by the wall is covered with a cloth: Agata remembers the frosts even with her arm in plaster.
city.t3.tomato.rain: The rain is watering the tomatoes for you. You stand beside an empty can and add nothing, which is also a form of care.
city.t3.tx.let.1: A letter on thin paper in a round hand: "Dear Agata, I'm sending 'Pink Heart'. Sow in March, plant out in May, and when they blush, call me. Vilma."
city.t3.tx.let.2: A postcard of mountains: "Agata, for forty years we've written to each other and you still haven't come. Seeds enclosed, tea too. Nino." At the bottom of the envelope, light dry mint.
city.t3.tx.let.3: A letter with Japanese stamps, a pen drawing of a sunflower at the bottom. "Dear Agata-san, my daughters have grown up. The variety stayed. They don't know where it comes from, but they love it. Yoshiko."
city.t3.tx.let.4: A short note no longer about seeds: "Agata, I'm coming in April. I'll bring seedlings from Riga and Rupert in a basket. He has grown up and fears nothing. Your Ilze."
city.t3.tx.let.title: Letters with seeds
city.t3.tx.nb.1: An oilcloth cover with a check pattern. On the first page in block letters: "SEEDS THAT DIDN'T LEAVE." Below in small writing: "Every packet anyone sent me. Every one sown. Every one written down."
city.t3.tx.nb.2: "Tomatoes 'Pink Heart'. Vilma, Kaunas, 1994. She writes: water only in the evening and don't spare it. I spared it once and she knew from my letter. How, I don't understand."
city.t3.tx.nb.3: "Herbs. Nino, Tbilisi, 2001. The envelope held only the word 'Nino' and seven unnamed packets. I named everything by smell. Thyme I knew at once, the rest can wait."
city.t3.tx.nb.4: "Sunflowers. Yoshiko, Niigata, 2003. She writes: they look east. For me east is the canyon, so the sunflowers look at the stairs. The neighbours are pleased; I think the sunflowers like it too."
city.t3.tx.nb.5: "October. Fell on the stairs with the can and broke my wrist. The worst of it: I can't carry water up from level four. I wrote a note for the board. If nobody comes the tomatoes will manage, and I won't."
city.t3.tx.nb.6: "Someone has watered the beds while I slept. No trace but wet soil and the track of the can in the dust. I didn't find out who and I won't. I left the jar of seeds on the shelf; whoever needs it may take it."
city.t3.tx.nb.7: "In spring I'll sow everything again. From this year I'll leave ten seeds of each kind on the sill and let them go wherever they like. Only let them remember to write. Agata."
city.t3.tx.nb.title: Agata Brandt's seed notebook
city.t3.view.1: Down the canyon as down a pipe: steps, rails, white washing. At the very end a narrow strip of yard and the street.
city.t3.view.2: Beyond the roofs of the lower rows a piece of sea shows: a grey ribbon with a white dot. The dot is a tug, and it has been standing for two hours.
city.t3.view.3: To the right of the sea a thin needle of the lighthouse stands. By day it is white and does nothing, and yet it seems to look back at you.
city.t3.view.fog: The fog has eaten the sea and the lighthouse. What remains is the canyon, the stairs and a pair of binoculars faithfully showing grey wool.
city.t3.view.n: In the dark you can see the lighthouse beam turn: one, two, three, pause. Below, the yard is scattered with yellow windows.
city.t3.view.n2: At night the canyon is empty, only the landing lamps burn in a chain downward like beads on a thread.
city.t3.view.rain: In the rain the eyepieces mist up, but the main thing shows: water runs down the stairs in thin streams, as if the house were washing its face.
city.t3.window.d: In the daytime the canyon is quiet. Opposite, somebody is watering a geranium, and you stand at the window guessing who by the colour of the can.
city.t3.window.m: In the morning from the window you see the opposite wall and a stripe of light on it that moves half a floor lower every hour.
city.t3.window.n: At night the window is black, the stairs below burn with separate lamps like a string of beads, and above them, right over the roof, hangs the lighthouse.
city.t5.cassette.1: A cassette without its case lies on the bench. On the label in pencil: Sea. Side B. Do not erase. The handwriting is familiar: the same as on the notes in the capsule.
city.t5.cassette.2: A cup ring on the bench beside it: someone waited, or just sat. The cassette must go back before Nora starts looking for it all over the house.
city.t5.hooks.1: On the hooks: a scarf with mountain goats and a rucksack with lecture notes sticking out. The scarf smells of smoke and snow.
city.t5.hooks.rain: The rucksack is wet, the notes inside wrapped in a bag: Nora knows about water.
city.t5.news.1: Nora from the capsule by the entrance is preparing for her oceanology exam. Please keep the lobby quiet after 8 pm. Her mountain songs play softly; those are allowed.
city.t5.news.2: A cassette was found on the bench of the seventh-floor bridge. On the label in pencil: Sea. Side B. Looking for the owner. Hardly anybody's lecture.
city.t5.news.3: Whoever carries the cassette from the seventh-floor bridge to the student in the capsule by the entrance has the thanks of the whole house. The box "For whoever helps Nora with physics" stands by the front desk.
city.t5.news.4: Thank you all. The cassette turned up; the sea on it was recorded from the cape. Nora promises: she'll pass the exam and treat the whole lobby to biscuits.
city.t5.news.base: House 2. The lift runs until 11 pm; the bridge is for people, not bicycles; the front desk is downstairs and the bell works. The rest is on other slips.
city.t5.news.sun: On Sunday evenings the telephone rings in the capsule by the entrance: that's Mum from the mountains. Please don't hold the lift then, or Nora runs for the stairs.
city.t5.phone.1: A green dial telephone. A list beside it: Sunday, 7 pm: Mum calls. Do not block the line!
city.t5.phone.n: At night the telephone is silent, its cable tucked under the skirting. Nora will sleep, and then Mum can get through.
city.t5.phone.sun: Sunday evening: the receiver is warm. Any moment now the hum of distant mountains will arrive here.
city.t5.sill.1: A second jar stands beside the first: Samples. Week 2. The water in it is a little cloudier.
city.t5.sill.n: At night the jars catch the streetlamp and turn into little lighthouses. Nora probably looks at them before sleep.
city.t5.sill.rain: Rain on the glass, and the water in the jars sways in waves: as if the sea has come to visit.
city.t5.table.1: The fold-down table is lowered: a teapot, "exam" biscuits in a paper bag and a chewed pencil. Here you study standing up once you're tired of sitting.
city.t5.table.2: The biscuits are hard as formulae. Nora puts two in the bag for each exam question.
city.t5.tapes.1: A cassette recorder with a handle: worn keys, a sticker "Lectures" on the lid. Three cassettes without cases beside it.
city.t5.tapesp.1: Cassette Lectures, 2nd year. The professor talks about tides, then a pause, then Nora in a whisper: "I don't understand. But I'll write it down."
city.t5.tapesp.2: Side B: the sea from the cape. You can hear her breathing and somebody's steps on the shingle. She wrote on it: The teacher who doesn't know he's teaching.
city.t5.tapesp.3: Cassette Mum. A voice from the mountains, laughter, somebody's cough and a song Nora hums along to quietly: "I'll come as soon as the sea lets me go."
city.t5.tapesp.4: Cassette For the exam. Nora reads the questions aloud. Question 14: Tides. She reads it eight times, each more correct. On the ninth she laughs: "I'll pass."
city.t5.tapesp.title: Nora's cassettes
city.take.any.1: Nothing left here. Someone got here first.
city.take.any.2: Empty. Only a dusty rectangle where something used to lie.
city.take.daily_paper.1: I took a paper. On the front page, a fisherman with a flounder the size of a saucepan lid.
city.take.daily_paper.2: Today's issue. Forecast: clear, wind off the sea, music in the park possible in the evening.
city.take.daily_paper.3: The paper's still warm, as if it had just been printed behind the wall.
city.take.postcard.1: I took a postcard of the promenade. The sky on it is bluer than it ever really is.
city.take.postcard.2: A "Greetings from Lyudmilovsk!" card. Nobody to send it to, but I'll keep it.
city.take.postcard.3: On the back someone had pencilled "Dear…" and never finished.
city.talk.butcher.1: The butcher hones his knife and nods to me like an old friend. There's nothing for me to buy from him.
city.talk.butcher.2: "Out of mince, come early tomorrow. Scraps for the cats are free."
city.talk.butcher.3: Above the counter, a chart of beef cuts. The cow on it looks very calm.
city.talk.butcher.4: "What a sun today, eh? Even the meat looks rosier," said the butcher, surprised at himself.
city.talk.caretaker.1: The caretaker is mending a stool and says without looking up: "Stairs were mopped on Wednesday. Shuffle quieter."
city.talk.caretaker.2: Keys hang on nails, each with a tag: "Cellar", "Roof", "Fuse room", "Can't remember". The last one is the shiniest.
city.talk.caretaker.3: "I put a bulb in on the fourth, and it's gone again. Must like the dark," the caretaker sighs.
city.talk.caretaker.4: The radio in the cubbyhole mutters the weather report. The caretaker nods at each figure as if greeting old friends.
city.talk.cashier.1: "First the department, they write you a slip, then me, then back to the department. Clear?" "Clear."
city.talk.cashier.2: The cashier clacks the till so fast she seems to be playing a polka on it.
city.talk.cashier.3: "No small change? What if you look?" I looked. Found a button.
city.talk.cashier.4: By the till there's a saucer for change with one sweet in it. Change too, apparently.
city.talk.cloakroom.1: "Don't lose your token," said the attendant, though I had nothing to hand in.
city.talk.cloakroom.2: The hangers sway and chime softly, like wind chimes.
city.talk.cloakroom.3: "In summer we get only umbrellas, and one hat. The hat's been here since the spring before last."
city.talk.cloakroom.4: The attendant is knitting something long and striped. A scarf, she says. Three years now, she says.
city.talk.closed.1: Nobody. A note on the glass: "Gone to the depot. Back at 15:00." No date.
city.talk.closed.2: The counter's bare: an abacus and a glass of pencils. I tapped on the glass. Silence.
city.talk.closed.3: "Stocktaking." The sign hangs crooked, as if it went up in a hurry long ago.
city.talk.closed.4: Looks like they only sell to the neighbours, and the neighbours are all at home.
city.talk.club_lending.1: "The club's books are for circle members only. Join the chess circle and we'll lend you The Caro-Kann Defence. Gripping."
city.talk.club_lending.2: Names in a column on the record card, each marked "returned". Except one. Next to it, a sad little face.
city.talk.club_lending.3: "Take Radio magazine instead," the attendant suggests. "Lots of diagrams, few words. Rests the eyes."
city.talk.club_lending.4: The "Cog Club Library" stamp goes on everything: books, tickets and once, they say, the cat.
city.talk.concierge.1: The concierge looks up from her knitting. "Who for? Oh, just looking… Well, sit a while, there's a good draught here, off the sea."
city.talk.concierge.2: "The lift's thinking again on the seventh. If you get stuck, sing, I'll hear. Everyone who gets stuck sings. We've got a choir here."
city.talk.concierge.3: On the desk, a book for "Letters and parcels received" and a jar of toffees "for those who say hello politely". I said hello very politely.
city.talk.concierge.4: "Forty-two moved out, forty-three moved in, and the cat from forty-one visits both." The concierge knows the house by heart.
city.talk.counter.1: "Can I help you, young man?" "Just looking." "Look all you like."
city.talk.counter.2: Behind the counter someone is writing in a fat ledger and raises a finger: "One moment."
city.talk.counter.3: "Our break's from one to two, but for you, all right."
city.talk.counter.4: They smiled at me as if I came in every day. Maybe I really do.
city.talk.fishmonger.1: "The flounder's this morning's, the herring's yesterday's, and the gobies — don't ask."
city.talk.fishmonger.2: The fishwife weighs fish in her hand more exactly than the scales. The scales don't argue.
city.talk.fishmonger.3: "Catch something yourself, bring it here, I'll buy it," she said with a wink.
city.talk.fishmonger.4: One fish with a golden flank lies on the ice. "Not for sale," they say. "It's for luck."
city.talk.heard.title: Talks at the counters
city.talk.keys: 1–9, A, D choose · E ask · Esc, W, S leave
city.talk.keys_answer: E next · Esc, W, S leave
city.talk.keys_back: E ask more · Esc, W, S leave
city.talk.market_office.1: The market manager checks a weight on the control scales. "A hundred grams must be a hundred grams. Even by the sea."
city.talk.market_office.2: On the door: "Complaints book available on request." The book is brand new. Either there are no complaints or nobody requests it.
city.talk.market_office.3: "Tomorrow's pitches are all taken. Want to sell? Come at five in the morning with a crate and a smile."
city.talk.market_office.4: The little office smells of paper, smoked fish and tangerines. So does the whole market, only here it's official.
city.talk.office.1: "Pass? No pass, no entry. Sit on the sofa and think about it."
city.talk.office.2: The porter doesn't look up from his crossword. "Heavenly body, three letters?" "Sun." "Fits."
city.talk.office.3: "Visitors from nine. And whom are you here to see?" "I… nobody yet."
city.talk.office.4: A bell on the desk and a sign: "Ring once." I rang once. That was enough.
city.talk.reception.1: "Are you a guest? No? Then at least have some water, ours is medicinal."
city.talk.reception.2: A bell on the desk and a booking book for treatments. Next to every name, a little drawn sun.
city.talk.reception.3: "Breakfast from eight, dinner till seven, the sea round the clock," the receptionist rattled off.
city.talk.reception.4: "No rooms. But if you really need one, in 204 only one floorboard creaks."
city.talk.records.1: The record man drops the needle and lifts a finger. "Listen. Here, at two minutes, the singer sighed. That's not in the score."
city.talk.records.2: "No new ones, only good ones." He flicks through the sleeves like cards and pulls one out: "For you, this. You'll thank me later."
city.talk.records.3: On the wall, a record broken in half and glued. "My first waltz," says the man. "I danced on it. Literally."
city.talk.records.4: "Records are tinned time," the man said, and blew on the disc as if it were hot.
city.talk.registry.1: "Surname? Year of birth? I can't find your card. That means you're healthy," the registrar decided.
city.talk.registry.2: The appointment slip comes out of a little wooden box. Number 13. "Don't worry, thirteen's the quickest one here."
city.talk.registry.3: Behind the window, thousands of cards in drawers, alphabetical. The whole town, by its aches. Mine isn't among them.
city.talk.registry.4: "First the scales, then the eye chart, then the doctor. In that order, or the doctor gets offended."
city.talk.rentals.1: "Boats till sunset, deckchairs till six, umbrellas till the first rain."
city.talk.rentals.2: "Deposit's a passport. No passport? Then your word of honour. Got one of those?"
city.talk.rentals.3: Oars stand along the wall, numbered in paint. Number seven is missing: it went to sea last July.
city.talk.rentals.4: "The bikes are being repaired," sighed the man. "All of them. At once. A mystery."
city.talk.repair.1: The repairman doesn't look up from the watch. "Leave it, a week." "I've nothing to leave." "Even better."
city.talk.repair.2: On the shelf an iron, a transistor radio and a toy railway wait for their owners. The tag says "Urgent. 1987".
city.talk.repair.3: "You can fix anything but the weather and a mood," the repairman said, and fixed my shoelace.
city.talk.repair.4: It smells of rosin and machine oil. Somewhere in a corner twenty clocks tick at once, all out of step.
city.talk.salon.1: "Half-box, Canadian, or Like Dad's? No dad here? Then Like the Sea: in waves."
city.talk.salon.2: It smells of Chypre cologne and hot tongs. On the table, magazines of hairstyles that exist only in pictures.
city.talk.salon.3: The barber snips the air like a grasshopper. "Booking for tomorrow. Today I'm only cutting clouds."
city.talk.salon.4: An old lady waits on the sofa with a newspaper. "I'm not here for a haircut," she whispers. "I come for the news. Better than the radio."
city.talk.savings.1: "Got a passbook? No? We'll open one when there's something to put in it," the cashier says, so kindly it hardly stings.
city.talk.savings.2: A poster: "Keep your money in the savings bank." On it a piggy bank smiles as if it has saved up everything already.
city.talk.savings.3: They showed me someone's old passbook as an example: a deposit of 3 roubles 40 kopecks, opened in 1961. "He'll be back," they say.
city.talk.savings.4: The stamp thumped the paper so hard the inkwell jumped. "That's not for you, that's for order," the cashier explained.
city.talk.shoes.1: "What size? Forty-one? We've got forty-three, to grow into. Wool socks and they'll fit like a glove."
city.talk.shoes.2: The saleswoman taps a sole. "Our shoes last for ages. You can't wear them out, only outgrow them."
city.talk.shoes.3: On the shelf, lonely galoshes lined in red. "Nobody buys them," they say, "because everyone's waiting for rain, and it doesn't come."
city.talk.shoes.4: They set out a stool and a shoehorn for me. I didn't buy anything, but I sat there like a real customer.
city.talk.speaker: Behind the counter
city.talk.sport_reception.1: "The pool needs a doctor's note, the gym a season ticket, table tennis a good mood. Which of those have you got?"
city.talk.sport_reception.2: Trophies above the desk, and under them a box: "Lost swimming caps". There are more caps than trophies.
city.talk.sport_reception.3: The cashier hands over a locker key on an elastic band. "Number seven, a lucky one. Don't mix it up with eight, that's the coach's."
city.talk.sport_reception.4: The club timetable: gymnastics, swimming, "Health after sixty" and "Health before sixteen". The second one's mine.
city.talk.tickets.1: "Tickets are thirty roubles, pay in the hall. Sit anywhere, it's not busy."
city.talk.tickets.2: "Today it's The Man Who Waited for the Lighthouse. They say everyone cries at the end, even the projectionist."
city.talk.tickets.3: The cashier checks the poster against the wall clock, though the clock has stopped.
city.talk.tickets.4: "Under sixteens aren't allowed at the late show. How old are you? Never mind, don't answer."
city.text.birds_starlings.1: The common starling reaches Lyudmilovsk in early March, while snow still lies on the promenade in the shade of the lamp posts. The first to notice are not the ornithologists but the street sweepers: a starling lands on a broom and studies it, as if weighing it up for a nest.
city.text.birds_starlings.2: Voice. The starling is a mimic. Birds here have learned the creak of the cable car, the bell of a tram the town hasn't had for twenty years, and the market watchman's whistle. If you think someone is calling your name from the bushes by the sanatorium, don't turn round at once. It is most likely him.
city.text.birds_starlings.3: The flock. On autumn evenings, half an hour before sunset, the starlings gather over the lighthouse into a single cloud. The cloud folds, unfolds, becomes a fish, a funnel, something with no name at all. Scientists call it a murmuration. Old-timers put it more simply: "The starlings are writing."
city.text.birds_starlings.4: For the watcher. Stand still and watch the edge of the flock, not its middle: the decisions are made at the edges. Do not try to read what they write. In the margin someone has objected in pencil: "I read it once. It said 'home'."
city.text.birds_starlings.title: Birds of the Coast. Chapter Seven: Starlings
city.text.cog_minutes.1: Minutes No. 41. Present: 23 club members and the doorman's cat (non-voting). Agenda: 1. The missing chess clock. 2. Any other business. Chair: Giuseppe González. Secretary: Kenji Kask.
city.text.cog_minutes.2: Heard: G. González. The clock vanished on Monday night, and with it the habit of playing fast. Games timed with the hourglass from the first-aid room now last until closing. L. Nowak added that yesterday, for the first time in thirty years, he had time to think a move over, and didn't like the move.
city.text.cog_minutes.3: Debate. J. Zhaksybekov proposed replacing the clock with the metronome from the music room. Rejected: with a metronome everyone starts moving in time. K. Kask proposed timing a move by the cable car, while a cabin travels from Lighthouse to Zenith. Rejected: on Sundays the cabins run slower.
city.text.cog_minutes.4: Resolved: 1. To announce a search for the clock with the cracked left dial. 2. To award the finder a game with the chair and the choice of colour. 3. Until it is found, to regard a draw as an honourable result. Votes: for, 22; against, none; abstained, 1 (the cat left).
city.text.cog_minutes.5: Added a week later, in another hand: "The clock turned up among the props for the play Time, Forward! The left dial runs two minutes fast. We won't repair it: let White hurry." Below it, a cat's paw print. The cat, it seems, has voted after the fact.
city.text.cog_minutes.title: Minutes of the General Meeting of the Cog Club
city.text.cookbook_soup.1: Serves four. Two fish, whatever bit (better two kinds: one for the broth, one for the conversation). Three potatoes, one whole onion, a carrot, a bay leaf, peppercorns. Salt to the sea: when the wind blows off the land, salt more boldly.
city.text.cookbook_soup.2: Potatoes and onion into cold water, the fish when it boils, and from that moment on, don't leave the stove. Skim the foam with a spoon, not with words. Simmer until somebody looks into the kitchen and asks, "What's that smell?" That's the sign: five minutes more and it's ready.
city.text.cookbook_soup.3: Three hands in the margins. In blue ink: "Before serving, a glass of vodka into the pot. For the fish." In pencil: "It's still fish soup without the vodka." Neatly, in green pen: "Tested at the Yantar restaurant: the chef added dill and said that was the idea all along."
city.text.cookbook_soup.title: Lyudmilovsk Fish Soup (a page from a cookbook)
city.text.kids_hedgehog.1: Once upon a time a hedgehog lived on the terraces above the town. Every morning he heard the sea murmuring below, but he had never seen it: from down in the grass, a hedgehog sees only grass. "I'll go and have a look," he said one day, and took an apple with him, just in case.
city.text.kids_hedgehog.2: On the way he met a starling. "The sea is like the sky, only wet," said the starling. Then he met the cat from the market. "The sea is where the fish are," said the cat. Then he met the old tortoise from the sanatorium. "The sea is a long time," said the tortoise, and fell asleep.
city.text.kids_hedgehog.3: The hedgehog reached the cable car and got into a cabin with a grandmother and her basket. The cabin rose over the roofs, over the lighthouse, and suddenly there was so much blue ahead that the hedgehog shut his eyes tight. "Don't be afraid," said the grandmother. "It's just the sea looking at you."
city.text.kids_hedgehog.4: The hedgehog opened his eyes and looked all the way to the last stop. He got home after dark and never ate the apple. He left it by his burrow, for whoever else might want to see the sea. The End. At the foot of the page, in a child's hand: "I've seen it. It's big."
city.text.kids_hedgehog.title: The Hedgehog Who Wanted to See the Sea
city.text.library_rules.1: 1. One reader per capsule. Two only if they are reading one book aloud. 2. Whoever switched on the capsule's light switches it off. 3. Feet on the cushion: yes. On the book: no.
city.text.library_rules.2: 4. Books about the sea are not to be taken onto the balcony: they get homesick. 5. After 10 p.m. books about the stars are lent to take home only: a capsule has a round window, and readers stay till morning. 6. Tea is drunk in the librarian's office, not over the pages.
city.text.library_rules.3: 7. A book returned late is accepted without a fine if the reader can retell one page of it. 8. Anything more than ten years late counts not as a debt but as a story. Come in and tell it.
city.text.library_rules.4: Rules adopted by the readers' council on 14 May 1968. Signed by the librarian, the council's chairman and one more, in pencil, illegible. Underneath, in the same pencil: "Rule 8 was my idea. As if I knew."
city.text.library_rules.title: Reading Room Rules (for the Capsules)
city.text.paper_today.1: Front page. "The promenade awaits its guests": deckchair hire opens by the breakwater this weekend. A half-page photo of a fisherman with a flounder the size of a saucepan lid. Caption: "He let it go. Said it should grow a bit more."
city.text.paper_today.3: Back page. Weather: wind off the sea, calmer by evening. The cable car runs to its usual timetable. Small ads: "Will swap an aquarium for a bicycle." "Seeking a dominoes partner, patient." "The Druzhba sanatorium invites you to the spring: the water is warm, the conversation free."
city.text.paper_today.p2_1: Page two. Town news: Kesha the parrot at the Saucer café is announcing stops again. Hearing "Next stop, the Saucer", visitors get up from their tables. The management asks everyone to stay calm: nobody needs to go anywhere.
city.text.paper_today.p2_2: Page two. Culture: the projectionist at the Rassvet culture house asks for the return of the reel with part three of the film. "We have two parts, we know the ending, and we remember the middle only vaguely."
city.text.paper_today.p2_3: Page two. Market: the jam contest has been put off for a week, as the judges cannot agree whether pine-cone jam counts as jam. Last year's winner has brought a jar "with no name" and refuses to explain.
city.text.paper_today.p2_4: Page two. A reader's letter: "For a month now a yellow umbrella has been standing in the department store's lost-and-found. It's mine. But let it stay: everyone who walks past it smiles."
city.text.paper_today.title: Evening Lyudmilovsk, today's issue
city.un.album.1: You find the twelfth page, the one that was empty. The postcard slips into the corners as if it had grown there: the sea, grey and real. The album seems to sigh.
city.un.album.2: The album has twelve pages, each captioned in Priya's hand. On the last: "To Shira from everyone who wrote here. The sea was found by a young man."
city.un.album.3: The pages with the lighthouse and the pier are worn at the corners: they've been turned more than the others. Priya says the sea is turned less often, it isn't for hands.
city.un.apples.1: In the morning the apples smell of an orchard. The seller sorts the crate like cards and puts the dented ones aside for his own tea.
city.un.apples.2: By evening the apples are just apples. The rosiest one has been held in somebody's hand and put back.
city.un.apples.3: The apple crates are covered with sacking for the night. It is quiet under it, like a cellar.
city.un.badminton.1: A shuttlecock with mixed feathers, some long since missing. It flies crooked, but the players pretend it's meant to.
city.un.badminton.2: The net is stretched between two drainpipes and the lines are chalked: on the roof the wind won't let you play seriously, but lets you laugh.
city.un.bike.1: A red bicycle, the chain freshly oiled. Somebody rides it to the sea every morning and comes back with wet shoelaces.
city.un.bike.2: The bicycle stands there, tyres pumped. On the handlebar a bell with two letters scratched by a fingernail: "N. T."
city.un.bike.3: At night the bicycle is chained to the pipe. The saddle is covered with a bag: a careful owner.
city.un.bread.1: The bread is still hot, the crust crackling. Rye, a long loaf, a plait. The assistant counts out loud so as not to lose track.
city.un.bread.2: A tag "yesterday's, cheaper" has stood on one loaf for the third day. It's holding up well.
city.un.bread.3: Three loaves and a sad long one are left. The assistant moves them closer to the light: they look fresher so.
city.un.bread.4: The shelves are empty and covered with a cloth. From under it comes the smell of yesterday, a pleasant one.
city.un.buttons.1: You pull out a drawer: buttons like sweets, sorted by colour. They say Priya used to hem skirts here until she retired, and the buttons still wink at her.
city.un.buttons.2: The bottom drawer holds only mother-of-pearl ones. On a card in pencil: "Not for sale, looking allowed."
city.un.buttons.3: In the middle drawer, one button from a sailor's jacket and one from a child's coat. They lie side by side and don't quarrel.
city.un.closed.flat: The door is shut: Priya keeps her own hours, she expects no guests before nine or after ten at night.
city.un.closed.pool: The water has been drained, the pool is covered with tarpaulin: the paddling pool does not open again till tomorrow.
city.un.closed.sand: The sandbox is covered with a net against cats and gulls. The children are at home in the evening, let the castle sleep.
city.un.deck.1: The deck chair creaks and folds just enough to lie in comfortably. Gulls overhead, and above them only the sky, today like a clean sheet of paper.
city.un.deck.2: The clouds go low and fast. One looks like a boot, another like a loaf, a third like Rafael Benítez with a fish.
city.un.deck.3: Evening sky: pink below, green in the middle, blue above. In the west the first star lights, the most impatient one.
city.un.deck.4: The night sky over the house: stars like sugar on a blue tablecloth. The Plough hangs over the ventilation stack, and the lighthouse beam draws across the clouds.
city.un.deck.5: At night the sky is shut, and only the lighthouse beam passes over the clouds once in ten seconds, like a clock's hand.
city.un.deck.6: At dawn the sky over the sea turns peach, then lemon, then just white. The deck chair still keeps some warmth.
city.un.desk1.1: The concierge looks up from a crossword: "Good morning. Fifteen floors, and everyone wants something at once."
city.un.desk1.2: "Good afternoon. Post, keys, or just a sit? The bench by the wall doesn't bite."
city.un.desk1.3: "It's late. I lock the door at eleven, ring after that. And don't stamp on the stairs: the walls are thin."
city.un.desk1.4: "The shopping street? Halfway up the house, on the seventh. Bread, haberdashery, toys, the barber. And the games room: noisy, but kindly."
city.un.desk1.5: "Priya Tulegenova? Fifth floor, number twelve. Her door is on the shopping street, the blue one. You go down the stair to her: with us it's the other way round."
city.un.desk1.6: "The roof is open round the clock. A paddling pool, a track, a sandbox, badminton. Just don't run along the edge."
city.un.desk2.1: The lobby warden looks up from her knitting: "Good morning. Tea's on the hotplate if anyone is cold."
city.un.desk2.2: "Good afternoon. If you've come for the fish, they've just eaten, don't ask them for affection."
city.un.desk2.3: "We dim the hall lights for the night. If you can't sleep, the aquarium glows till morning, you can sit with it."
city.un.desk2.4: "The games room on the shopping street? Rafael Benítez from the thirteenth is there every evening, looking for someone to beat."
city.un.desk2.5: "The roof? Håkon Jansen runs there with the children on Wednesdays and Saturdays. If you want to, he'll make you run too."
city.un.desk2.6: "The post? Something goes astray once a week anyway. Postcards come more often than letters: people find five words easier."
city.un.fabsew.1: The machine rattles evenly. In the clamp, somebody's trousers: on a slip "Håkon Jansen, 13-09, by Friday." A good thing the hem is short.
city.un.fabsew.2: Green thread, a new needle. You try a seam: it comes out crooked, but honest.
city.un.feeder.1: A little feeder house on a post. Sparrows jostle, a tit is quick and neat: grabs one and is off.
city.un.feeder.2: In the daytime the feeder is empty, the birds have gone to the sea. Only crows are left on the roof, they are philosophers.
city.un.feeder.3: Towards evening a gull settles on the feeder and looks as if it were waiting for an apology. You don't feed it and it flies off offended.
city.un.feeder.4: In winter twice as much feed is put out. In the snow around the feeder there's a pattern of bird feet.
city.un.feeder.night: The feeder is empty and still. The birds sleep somewhere under the eaves, and the terraces' windows glow below.
city.un.g_checkers.1: Checkers on a board of linoleum squares: the black ones worn at the edges, the white ones chewed. Somebody was nervous.
city.un.g_checkers.2: One king is marked with a red dot: the lucky one. People take it by turns, and nobody admits they think it's lucky.
city.un.g_chess.1: An adjourned game on the board: White wrote the move on a slip and put it under a knight. They've been at it for three weeks.
city.un.g_chess.2: The black bishop has lost its base and stands on a bit of plasticine. The players prefer it to new ones.
city.un.g_dominoes.1: The tiles are yellow from fingers. The double-six was lost long ago, a cardboard one is cut in its place. They play with it too.
city.un.g_dominoes.2: Beside it on a saucer, three cooled tea bags: today's score. The winner chooses whose to brew.
city.un.g_football.1: The little players on the rods are painted in the colours of two schools. The left forward is bald: the paint was rubbed off by somebody's little finger.
city.un.g_football.2: The ball sometimes sticks by the post. Then everybody thumps the table until it jumps out: the room's rule.
city.un.g_pingpong.1: The paddles lie crosswise: the right one with a rubber face, the left plain wood. The cracked ball bounces sideways and everyone has got used to it.
city.un.g_pingpong.2: The net sags in the middle. By the rules of the room, serves that hit it count as "a good try".
city.un.gbench.1: From the bench you can see three tables at once. Supporters sit here, and each plays for somebody silently.
city.un.gbench.2: The knock of the ball, the rustle of tiles, and no music. After the stairwell radios it is almost silence.
city.un.hats.1: The coat stand by the door. A red scarf has hung here since autumn and everybody knows it: the owner never turns up.
city.un.hats.2: Wet umbrellas on the stand, under them a puddle the shape of a continent. The holey umbrella belongs to everybody: first come, first served.
city.un.hats.3: Hats and mittens hang in pairs, the children's on elastic so they won't get lost. One pair got lost anyway.
city.un.hours.1: Bakery, haberdashery, news, groceries, toys, barber: nine in the morning to eight in the evening, Monday to Saturday. A handwritten slip: "Lunch as the mood takes us."
city.un.hours.2: Games room: open as long as the light is on. Bring your own tea, we look after the chessmen. Table football: don't spin the rods until they ring.
city.un.hours.3: Barber: a haircut is forty roubles, ladies' and gentlemen's alike. The queue is lively but well brought up.
city.un.hours.4: On Sundays everything on the street is shut except the games room and the benches. Tulegenova's door is shut too: Sunday is for herself.
city.un.l1c.1: The games room on the shopping street has chess, checkers, dominoes, table tennis and table football. Everyone may play, the stakes are tea.
city.un.l1c.2: House dominoes championship: Saturday at six, in the games room. Last year's champion Rafael Benítez (13-19) accepts challenges.
city.un.l1c.3: Championship result: Rafael Benítez and Gennady Sorokin (15-11) drew. They agreed to play on until the first mug of tea.
city.un.l1n.1: Priya Tulegenova of no. 5-12 is putting together an album of postcards of the town. One is missing: the sea. The blue door on the shopping street, next to the haberdashery. Tea is on me.
city.un.l1n.2: A glove has turned up: left, grey, knitted. It hangs on the hook by the letter boxes. If it is yours, it is waiting for you.
city.un.l1n.3: A bicycle-lock key has been found. Ask the concierge, but say the colour of your bicycle first.
city.un.l2c.1: A blue child's sock was found on the roof. It hangs on the sandbox fence. If it's yours, it misses you.
city.un.l2c.2: Looking for a fourth for dominoes on Tuesdays in the games room. Rafael Benítez, 13-19. Gennady Sorokin of 15-11 will do too, but he cheats quietly.
city.un.l2n.1: Håkon Jansen (13-09) runs with the children on the roof on Wednesdays and Saturdays at five. Come and run or cheer, he brings his own stopwatch.
city.un.l2n.2: The paddling pool on the roof is filled. Grown-ups on duty in the deck chairs, from eight in the morning to nine in the evening. No diving, it's shallow.
city.un.l2n.3: Please do not carry sand from the roof sandbox into the entrance in your pockets. The caretaker asks, and he has a broom.
city.un.laps.1: A sheet on the stand: "Wednesday and Saturday, 17:00, running for all. A lap is 400 m. House record: Despina Jansen, aged 7, 2 min 40 sec. Håkon Jansen asks you not to mind: he held the stopwatch."
city.un.laps.2: The sheet is updated: "House record: Despina Jansen, 2:31. Sigurd and Kalev Tehrani ask for a recount: they ran together, which is quicker for two."
city.un.laps.3: A new pencilled entry at the bottom: "Good today, a tailwind on the second bend. H. J." Next to it a child's hand outlined in chalk.
city.un.mail.1: The boxes are still empty: the postman comes at eleven. On one box, in pen: "No junk mail, we have a cat."
city.un.mail.2: Eighteen boxes on this wall, and a hundred and ninety-six flats in the house: the postman carries the rest further up.
city.un.mail.3: The boxes are locked for the night. The corner of a postcard with a lighthouse sticks out of a slot: somebody will be glad in the morning.
city.un.mail.4: Bills come on Mondays: the Kasks' box has already swollen like a loaf.
city.un.mail.5: Water drips from the ceiling by the boxes, a bucket stands under it. The letters inside are dry: the slots face down.
city.un.p.album: E — paste the postcard into the album
city.un.p.door: E — step up to the door
city.un.p.hats: E — look over the coat stand
city.un.p.mail: E — look in the letter boxes
city.un.plants.1: A watering can with a broken handle stands by the planter. A note is pinned to a leaf: "Water once a week, not once a day. D. K."
city.un.plants.2: The soil is damp: somebody has watered it already, against the note. The rubber-plant leaf shines and behaves itself.
city.un.plants.3: The can is empty, the planter sleeps. Through the glass of the door the light of a street lamp falls on a leaf.
city.un.playhouse.1: A house for the little ones: inside a bench, a plastic tea set and a note on the wall "Grown-ups, duck."
city.un.playhouse.2: On the windowsill a painted sun, on the door a painted lock. Everything one needs for living.
city.un.pool.1: The water is ankle-deep and warm from the sun on the concrete. The children walk round in a circle and call it swimming. You dip a hand: yes, it's the sea, only tamed.
city.un.pool.2: The water is cold: the concrete has cooled. A yellow rubber duck floats by the rim and looks like a hero.
city.un.pool.3: The pool looks empty: everyone has gone to lunch. On the bottom, two pebbles and one hairpin. At noon it's quiet here, you can hear the ventilation hum.
city.un.pram.1: A blue pram with a hood, the brake on. Inside, a toy rabbit and two pairs of mittens: the owners are upstairs, judging by the sounds.
city.un.pram.2: The pram is empty, the hood down. A bag with a long loaf hangs from the handle: the walk ended with bread.
city.un.roofchess.1: Chess under the pergola, the board taut in the wind like a sail: the pieces are stuck to the squares with plasticine. That's why they play here even in a storm.
city.un.roofchess.2: Sorokin sometimes comes here alone in the morning and plays himself, always better as Black than as White.
city.un.rules.1: Rules of the games room. 1. The loser puts the kettle on. 2. The winner gloats for no more than a minute. 3. We look after the chessmen.
city.un.rules.2: 4. After nine in the evening the table-tennis ball doesn't knock, it whispers. 5. Do not open the windows: it blows on the chess players.
city.un.rules.3: Note: "The key to the cupboard with the pieces is with Rafael Benítez. If he isn't here, neither are the pieces."
city.un.sand.1: In the sandbox, a castle with three towers and a moat. The moat was filled from the pool one bucket at a time: they say half an hour and thirty buckets.
city.un.sand.2: The spade is stuck in the sand like a flag. Scratched on the handle: "Sigurd + Kalev." Somebody has added "and Despina."
city.un.sb.1: The shopping street is open from nine to eight in the evening, except Sundays. Please do not leave prams by the bakery, the door is narrow.
city.un.sb.2: Bakery: apple pies today. The cherry ones are gone, don't ask. And whoever left the green umbrella at the haberdashery, please collect it: it has been there since Tuesday.
city.un.sb.3: Priya Tulegenova (5-12, the blue door by the haberdashery) is asking for a postcard of the sea for her album. The album is a present for Shira Nakamura's eighty-fifth birthday. A postcard buys you tea and a chat.
city.un.sb.4: Priya's album is almost ready: eleven places out of twelve are filled, the twelfth, with the sea, is empty. She will wait until Saturday. Where to buy: the news stand, the haberdashery, any kiosk.
city.un.scores.1: The games room table. Dominoes: Benítez 11, Sorokin 9. Checkers: Sorokin 14, Benítez 12. Table tennis: Novotný 8, the rest "no score".
city.un.scores.2: The table has been updated. Dominoes: Benítez 13, Sorokin 13. A pencilled note: "Tea is on Sorokin." Under it, in another hand: "No, on Benítez."
city.un.scores.3: The table is framed with blue tape. Above it: "House championship. Final: replay. Spectators, quietly."
city.un.sit.1: It smells of bread from the bakery. People pass with string bags, greeting every other person, but gladly.
city.un.sit.2: A grey light from the sea moves in the glass. Dominoes clack from the games room, a radio murmurs from the barber's.
city.un.sit.3: In the evening the lamps burn every other one, steps echo from the ceiling. The bench is still warm from somebody's back.
city.un.sit.4: At night the street is empty and very long. Somewhere a tap drips, and you hear it from the other end of the house.
city.un.tcards.1: On a cork board are pinned postcards: a lighthouse in fog, a pier with fishermen, dunes, a pine wood. Twelve corners, eleven postcards.
city.un.tcards.2: The empty corner in the bottom row is labelled in pencil: "Sea. A real one, not painted. Priya."
city.un.tcards.3: On the back of one postcard: "For Shira Nakamura, so that she remembers us." Priya wrote this on every one.
city.un.tdoor.1: A blue door with a card "5-12 T." Tea drifts from under it. Here the flats lie under the shopping street: you enter from above and go down.
city.un.tdoor.2: A strip of light under the door, so Priya is awake. But it's late to knock: she'd come, brew tea, and the talk would last till dawn.
city.un.toybins.1: In the bin, blocks with letters. They spell the Russian word for "sea" with one letter too many. The seller says that is intended.
city.un.toybins.2: Under the blocks, a tin boat with a key. You wind it up: it sails along the counter until it falls off.
city.un.toybins.3: At the bottom, a wooden horse with one leg missing. It isn't sold, but isn't thrown out either.
city.un.toyhouse.1: The little house holds two plush bears and one cross rabbit. A sign on the door: "Ring three times."
city.un.toyhouse.2: Through the tiny window you see a bed made of matchboxes. The quilt is sewn from somebody's mitten.
city.un.tphotos.1: A photo: Priya, Shira Nakamura and Zeynep Bērziņa on the pier, each with a cup of something hot. All laughing, none remembers at what.
city.un.tphotos.2: A photo: Rafael Benítez at a railing with an enormous fish, which, judging by his face, he did not catch himself.
city.un.tphotos.3: A yellowed photograph behind glass: a young woman at a sewing machine. The handwriting on the back is small and even.
city.un.track.1: You run a lap, the red rubber answers every step softly. At the bend the wind pushes you in the back: it knows where to hurry.
city.un.track.2: Håkon Jansen sits on the kerb with a stopwatch and notes the children's times. To you he says "not bad" and holds out the stopwatch.
city.un.track.3: In the dusk the track is empty and warm. Running along the city lights as along an embankment, but at fifteen floors' height.
city.un.track.4: At night the track is empty, the red rubber looks black. You may run, but best not for long: the parapet is low.
city.un.tradio.1: The set picks up the lighthouse bulletin: wind, visibility, swell. Priya writes the numbers on a tear-off calendar, out of habit.
city.un.tradio.2: A daytime request concert: a waltz for somebody on the sixth floor. The set crackles, but the waltz gets through.
city.un.tradio.3: An evening radio play. Somebody in it keeps leaving, and nobody can say where to.
city.un.tradio.4: Quiet night air: only an even voice and sometimes a crackle. Good to listen to with your eyes closed.
city.un.trophies.1: A tin cup "For Fortitude at Dominoes". The date plate is worn off, but the dent from a fall has survived: more authentic that way.
city.un.trophies.2: Next to it a pennant "House 3 v House 2, 7:6", table football, an old story. Who won is not specified.
city.un.trophies.3: A framed photo: two elderly men with the cup, both with the faces of men who won and are terribly pleased about it.
city.un.tsew.1: On the table, hemmed trousers, a slip "Håkon Jansen, 13-09, by Friday". Priya hems for the whole house and takes no money, only the word "thanks".
city.un.tsew.2: The machine is old, treadle-driven. Priya says it's half a century old and has never let her down: unlike people.
city.un.tsink.1: Two cups on the drying rack, and one cracked: the best loved. Priya says a cracked cup holds the tea better.
city.un.tsink.2: The tap drips in time with the radio. Priya says she would mend it, but then it would be too quiet.
city.un.tstove.1: A pot of noodle soup, a whistling kettle beside it. It smells of cardamom: Priya puts it into the soup and into the tea.
city.un.tstove.2: On the second ring, a pan of pancakes under a plate. Six pancakes: five for guests, one for the kitchen.
city.un.ttea.1: The samovar sings thin. Priya doesn't like it sweet, but there's always a lump of sugar on the saucer "for the guest". You take a glass in its holder.
city.un.ttea.2: The tea is strong, the colour of old wood. While you drink, a corner of grey light shows in the window, and everything settles.
city.un.ttea.3: Evening tea with lemon. There's one lemon a week, and today is its turn.
city.un.ttv.1: Morning exercises: the presenter is brisk, the viewers are invited to bend forward. The set won't notice if you just sit.
city.un.ttv.2: A programme about fish: a flounder is shown, looking as if it knew everything already. Priya calls it "Zeynep".
city.un.ttv.3: Evening news, then the forecast: a cyclone is coming from the sea. On the map it looks like a question mark.
city.un.ttv.4: A test card and an even hiss. The most honest programme of the day.
city.un.twardrobe.1: The wardrobe smells of lavender and mothballs. Four dresses, two coats, a rain mac. On a hanger a man's jacket: Priya keeps it "for order's sake".
city.un.twardrobe.2: In a box at the bottom, spools of every colour, a thimble and a tailor's chalk. The chalk is worn to a stub.
city.un.twin.1: The hour before dawn: Priya meets it in the chair by the window. Far below, the sea is darker than the sky, and the line between them thin as a thread.
city.un.twin.2: By day you see only a grey strip and the bakery's roof with a gull stuck to it. Priya says the sea should be looked at in the morning, the rest of the time it should be remembered.
city.un.twin.3: In the evening the harbour lights come on in the window. They blink in time with what the radio plays in the kitchen.
city.un.twin.4: At night the window is black and the lamp is reflected in it. It makes it seem there is another room in the room.

city.wave.basket.1: Bublik sleeps on his side, filling the whole basket. A green chimney with a red rim sticks out from under the blanket. I carefully drew out the little engine "Sever". The cat opened one eye, yawned and turned away. Under the blanket there is also a red comb, a thimble and five nails.
city.wave.basket.2: Bublik lies with his paws tucked in. Under his warm side: a green toy engine, a comb, a thimble and nails. He purred as if to say "It's not my fault, it was shiny." I put the engine in my pocket.
city.wave.basket.3: Bublik is curled up in a ball, warm as a stove. Under the blanket lies everything shiny: a green toy engine, a comb, a thimble, nails. I took the engine and left the rest: the owners can come for it themselves.
city.wave.bmenu.fri: Friday: fish pie for everyone, the sweet one for those who came before lunch. The queue's tail reaches the arcade.
city.wave.bmenu.mon: Monday: sourdough rye, cabbage pies. In chalk: "Cinnamon buns, when the cinnamon arrives."
city.wave.bmenu.sat: Saturday: puff pastries, bagels and a big sweet pie "for Sunday". All gone by noon.
city.wave.bmenu.sun: Sunday: the bakery is closed. A note: "Bread on Monday. Bublik is asleep, do not wake."
city.wave.bmenu.thu: Thursday: curd turnovers and apple pies. Fish pie only until two.
city.wave.bmenu.tue: Tuesday: long white loaves and sweet buns. Added: "With raisins, by popular request."
city.wave.bmenu.wed: Wednesday: a plaited loaf for tea and curd tarts. The price is in chalk, slightly smudged by a sleeve.
city.wave.bond.fri: BOND LOAN. THE DRAW IS TODAY. At four the table goes up, and whoever checks their number first will shout across the hall. Or keep quiet.
city.wave.bond.mon: BOND LOAN. Four days to the draw. The board shows a table of series; some are ringed in pencil: somebody's hopes.
city.wave.bond.sat: BOND LOAN. The draw table is up: series 7, number 318 wins. Written under it: "It matches! Joy at the counter until lunch." People smile and check again.
city.wave.bond.sun: BOND LOAN. The counter is closed. A note on the board: "Payouts on Monday, bring your documents."
city.wave.bond.thu: BOND LOAN. The draw is tomorrow. The queue for bonds reaches the door, and the counter keeps its little window shut so the papers don't blow away.
city.wave.bond.tue: BOND LOAN. Three days to the draw. A hand has scribbled: "Series 7, number 318 is mine, don't claim it!"
city.wave.bond.wed: BOND LOAN. Two days to the draw. A fresh sheet with last draw's numbers. Small print, the part about tax even smaller.
city.wave.booth.fri: Friday: foxtrots for the dance evening. My feet tap by themselves under the table. No need to be shy: nobody can see through the glass anyway.
city.wave.booth.mon: Monday: the card says "Baltic Waltzes", the naval college orchestra. Headphones on: violins, as if a swell were rocking the deck.
city.wave.booth.prompt: E — listen to a record on headphones
city.wave.booth.sat: Saturday: "The Seasons", winter. A blizzard in the headphones, and the windows seem to mist over. When it ended there was sunshine outside all the same, a pleasant surprise.
city.wave.booth.sun: Sunday: the card says "Intermission: listen to the silence." Headphones on. A soft hiss, like the sea when you hold a shell to your ear.
city.wave.booth.thu: Thursday: the radio play "Lighthouse in the Fog". The headphones smell of dust and other people's secrets. Somebody in the fog is calling a dog, and it feels uneasy for some reason.
city.wave.booth.tue: Tuesday: a jazz quartet from Riga. Brushes on a snare drum in the headphones, like rain on a roof. The queue for this record is one person long: whoever put it on.
city.wave.booth.wed: Wednesday: a children's choir, "The Little Ship Song". By the last verse I was mouthing along, then glanced round to see whether anyone noticed.
city.wave.cart.1: In the trolley, jumbled: "Dunes and Wind", a well-worn Jules Verne and a houseplant care manual without a cover.
city.wave.cart.2: One book carries a stamp: "Returned by reader no. 14 with thanks." The thanks is an ink blot on page forty.
city.wave.cart.3: Found a bookmark, an old cinema ticket: the 18:30 show, row five, seat eight. I wonder how the film ended.
city.wave.cart.4: The trolley creaked a step away. The sign says "Reduced". In fact they were simply loved: soft spines, rounded corners.
city.wave.cart.5: At the bottom a bundle of postcards of Lyudmilovsk: the same pier, but the gulls on the cards are somehow bigger.
city.wave.depot.1: I set "Sever" on the rails by the depot and nudged it. The wheels turned twice, and the green engine rolled into the gate by itself. The depot lamp blinked, as if in thanks.
city.wave.depot.2: The engine is back: green, chimney with a red rim. A ginger cat hair is stuck to the rails. I picked it off and blew the dust from the tracks.
city.wave.depot.3: Beside the depot someone has left a note: "Thank you to whoever brought it." I don't know who wrote it, but I'd sign under every word.
city.wave.depot.prompt: E — return the "Sever" engine to its depot
city.wave.dryer.1: I sat under the hood. It hums evenly, like a distant plane. The warm air smells of shampoo and slightly scorched camomile. For twenty minutes nobody expects anything clever of me.
city.wave.dryer.2: It is hot under the hood and all the sounds drift far off: voices, scissors, the radio. I closed my eyes and it felt like a bathhouse, only a quiet one.
city.wave.dryer.3: In the evening it is nice under the hood: outside the arcade lamps come on while warm air hums in my ears. I climbed out feeling rested.
city.wave.dryer.prompt: E — sit under the hood drier
city.wave.feed.a1: In autumn feeders go up at the end of October, when the birds start to look in. A sign: "Empty at first, let them get used to it. Food a week later."
city.wave.feed.a2: On the table, packs of feed: millet, sunflower seed, peanuts in the shell, lard. A note: "Take a little at a time, or the whole flock will be after you."
city.wave.feed.s1: In spring feeders must be scrubbed with a brush and boiling water. A basin and a brush on a chain: "Wash after every flock." From April the lard goes away: birds need grubs, not fat.
city.wave.feed.s2: A card: "From April less food, more water. Let them learn to find their own. Nest boxes go up before mid-March."
city.wave.feed.u1: In summer the feeders stand almost empty: there is food everywhere. But on the table lies a stack of drinkers: a saucer of water with pebbles so bees don't drown.
city.wave.feed.u2: A card: "Summer means water. Saucer in the shade, fresh water each morning. Grain only for fledglings the parents can't feed."
city.wave.feed.w1: In winter the feeder hangs at human height, away from cats. A card on the table: "Unsalted lard, sunflower seed, millet. No bread: it makes birds ill."
city.wave.feed.w2: A card by the feeders: "If you began with the first snow, keep feeding until the thaw and don't stop midwinter. The birds get used to it."
city.wave.feeders.1: A little house on a post, for tits and sparrows. The roof is red so it can be seen from the sky. The price tag says: "Place away from windows, birds fly into them."
city.wave.feeders.2: A hanging tube with perches, for siskins and goldfinches. The holes are narrow: seeds come one by one, and there is no hurry for the birds.
city.wave.feeders.3: A net for lard, for tits and nuthatches: they hang from it head down, very pleased. The tag: "Throw the net away after winter."
city.wave.feeders.4: A homemade feeder from a milk carton: a sample, not for sale. A drawing is pinned beside it: "Make your own. It will be like everyone's, but yours."
city.wave.hits.1: Hit parade of the week. First place: "Baltic Waltzes". Second: "Four Drops of Rain" (jazz). Third: "The Little Ship Song". In pencil: "First place has a crack again. Don't take it without checking."
city.wave.hits.2: Hit parade. The radio play "Lighthouse in the Fog" has climbed to first place. Someone drew a fat tick and wrote: "Scary. Take it."
city.wave.hits.3: Hit parade. The foxtrots have reached second place. Beside them: "Please do not play a 33 record at 45!"
city.wave.hits.4: A list headed "Expected from Riga": five lines, three crossed out. Below, in pen: "The rest are on their way."
city.wave.mags.1: "Rabotnitsa": tips on turning a coat into a jacket. Beside it, moustaches in ballpoint pen on a film star's photograph, drawn with enthusiasm.
city.wave.mags.2: "Ogonyok": a milkmaid with a record on the cover, inside a crossword already filled in another hand, with a mistake in the word "barometer".
