city.wave.mags.3: "Health": an article saying you should have your hair cut less often than hairdressers think. Surprisingly, it lies right on their own table.
city.wave.mags.4: A fashion magazine from Tallinn: belted dresses, black-and-white photos, and on the cover "the colour of spring: lilac". I'd like to see lilac in black and white.
city.wave.mags.5: A bound volume of "Krokodil": funny, but it's awkward to laugh in a hairdresser's with scissors at your ear.
city.wave.nails.1: I poured a handful of nails onto the pan: a hundred and twenty grams. The hundred-gram weight lost, so the seller would have to take five out. I took them out myself, honestly.
city.wave.nails.2: Screws, half a kilo by the needle. Just right for one shelf on a wall. Too many for a nest box.
city.wave.nails.3: The scales have no little brass wheel and the needle catches slightly at a hundred grams. A note: "Being mended, don't thump."
city.wave.nails.4: I weighed an empty palm: the needle trembled and went down. The scales seemed to think I was cheating them.
city.wave.new.fri: Friday: magazines, "Science and Life" and "Around the World". The pile melts before your eyes, so leaf through while you can.
city.wave.new.mon: Monday's new arrivals: the "Atlas of Baltic Birds", two volumes of fairy tales and a collection of sea stories. The gull on the atlas cover was clearly drawn from life: noisy.
city.wave.new.sat: Saturday: postcards of a new print run (lighthouse, dunes, pines) and a guide to the coast, the thinnest of all, as if the coast were small.
city.wave.new.sun: Sunday: the crates of new books stand unopened. A note on the string: "Until Monday."
city.wave.new.thu: Thursday: children's books. "Adventures of a Submarine", colouring books and an alphabet with a toothy letter Щ.
city.wave.new.tue: On Tuesday they brought "Physics for Fun" and "The Angler's School". The seller counted the bundles and quietly scolded the porters.
city.wave.new.wed: Wednesday: poetry. A thin book in a blue cover and a thick one in red. The thin one is already being snapped up.
city.wave.pattern.1: The pattern album. On the first page, checked wool, labelled "for a coat, warm". On the second a grey herringbone, strict as a teacher.
city.wave.pattern.2: A page of cotton print: tiny flowers on blue. The label: "for a dress, allow extra for the hem." A pattern is pinned beside it, covered in arrows.
city.wave.pattern.3: Linen: coarse, warm to the touch, the colour of sand. In neat handwriting: "for tablecloths and summer trousers."
city.wave.pattern.4: Silk in broad stripes: red, yellow, blue. The label: "for beach umbrellas and very brave people."
city.wave.pattern.5: The last page: samples of lace and braid. A note pinned to the lace: "Out of scarlet thread, waiting for more." And small: "A reel has vanished."
city.wave.pattern.prompt: E — leaf through the pattern album
city.wave.rail.1: The red engine pulls three little wagons round the oval, vanishes into the tunnel and comes out the other side. The cotton-wool stationmaster doesn't stir.
city.wave.rail.2: A switch clicked and the train went off onto the siding. There is an empty dead end and a sign "Depot Sever". The gates are open. No engine, but they left the depot light on anyway.
city.wave.rail.3: If you flatten your nose against the glass, you can see the stationmaster has painted-on whiskers. The train runs steadily as a clock. Three wagons, counted three times.
city.wave.rail.4: The little lamps in the window are lit: the station glows yellow, the wagons have tiny windows. The train sets off on its evening run. I don't want to go home any more.
city.wave.rail.5: On the evening tracks the train goes slower, as if tired. Tunnel, station, tunnel. I watched until my legs went numb.
city.wave.ticket.1: I pulled the little lever: ticket no. 12. The display shows 9. Three people ahead, one with a huge bag of small change. A long wait.
city.wave.ticket.2: Ticket no. 31. The display shows 29. Two grannies ahead are arguing about deposit interest. I'll have to sit.
city.wave.ticket.3: Ticket no. 48. The display shows 47. My turn is almost here: the clerk behind the glass is finishing a line, stamping and glancing at the clock.
city.wave.weigh.1: The needle shivered and settled: forty-nine kilos. A ticket dropped out of the slot: "A small piece of luck awaits you today. Don't miss it."
city.wave.weigh.2: Fifty-two and a half. The ticket says: "The early riser lives closer to the bakery."
city.wave.weigh.3: The machine sighed and showed a number I decided to count as wrong. The ticket: "Not every number deserves belief."
city.wave.weigh.4: Forty-eight. But I stood on my toes, and the ticket said so: "One should stand on one's heels."
city.wave.weigh.5: Fifty-one. The ticket: "Expect a letter." What letter? Well, we'll wait.
city.wave.weigh.6: The needle swung for a long time, as if thinking. The ticket: "Fewer doubts, more bread."
city.wave2.bin.1: Ticket stubs, wrappers and one shoelace. Just as it should be.
city.wave2.bin.2: On top an empty ice-cream cup and a token somebody rejected.
city.wave2.bin.3: Not a single note about records. Serious players do not throw them away.
city.wave2.bin.rain: The bottom is wet: umbrellas get shaken out here.
city.wave2.broken.1: The screen is dark; you see your own reflection. The coin slot is taped over.
city.wave2.broken.2: A cooling tube ticks softly inside the cabinet.
city.wave2.broken.3: The screen blinks and says INSERT COIN. The tape holds.
city.wave2.broken.4: The cabinet sings again, little figures run behind the glass. The coin slot is free.
city.wave2.change.1: The rouble goes in; the steel tray clinks: five tokens, one with a nick.
city.wave2.change.2: The machine chews the corner of the note, then gives up the tokens.
city.wave2.change.3: The tokens are warm, as if just cast.
city.wave2.change.prompt: E — change a rouble for tokens
city.wave2.change.sat: On Saturdays the tray is empty by noon; the caretaker tops it up from a pail.
city.wave2.closed.any.1: The alley is dim, only the lamp over the entrance. The games are quiet till morning.
city.wave2.closed.board.1: The board is in shadow, the chalk unreadable. Come back by day.
city.wave2.closed.cab.1: The cabinet sleeps: dark screen, cord tucked under until morning.
city.wave2.closed.cab.2: The coin slot is locked. The alley runs nine to ten at night.
city.wave2.closed.counter.1: The counter is under a cloth and the shelf is bare. Prizes by day.
city.wave2.coll.title: The arcade alley
city.wave2.hisc.1: HIGH SCORES. Sea Battle: 1. HIROSHI 940. 2. DINA 910. 3. VALERA 880. Challenge accepted.
city.wave2.hisc.2: Racing: best lap VALERA 1:07. Below in pencil: "His wheel was moved!"
city.wave2.hisc.3: Pinball: DINA 5,400. HIROSHI 5,380. A difference of one jackpot lamp.
city.wave2.hisc.fri: FRIDAY. New Sea Battle record: 960! Signed with a single "H".
city.wave2.hisc.mon: MONDAY. Chalked underneath: "The board never lies; only Valera does."
city.wave2.hisc.rec: A fresh sheet: the fourth line is free. Sign it yourself; the chalk is on the frame.
city.wave2.hisc.sat: SATURDAY. Hiro does not know yet that his record fell. Somebody will tell him.
city.wave2.hisc.sun: SUNDAY. Somebody left a token by the board: "For whoever beats Dina at pinball."
city.wave2.lift.up: The lift hums behind the door. The indicator says "Roof".
city.wave2.note.1: "OUT OF ORDER. Ate three tokens. Do not hit or shake. Management."
city.wave2.note.2: A second slip on top: "Repairman came. Needs an LE-6 tube, ordered from the depot."
city.wave2.note.3: New line: "The tube came, the wrong one. Waiting for the right one. Please do not call."
city.wave2.note.4: "Tube in! The screen flickers, but it shows numbers now. We test it on a token tomorrow. Kolya."
city.wave2.note.5: "WORKS. The first record is on the board. Thanks to all who didn't hit it. Kolya." Somebody has drawn a small heart beside it.
city.wave2.pin.after.1: Out of balls. TILT blinks like a warning: no shaking.
city.wave2.pin.after.2: A palm print on the glass. People play with feeling here.
city.wave2.pin.draw.1: Three bumpers and no jackpot. Fair for a first ball.
city.wave2.pin.lose.1: The ball slid between the flippers before you pressed.
city.wave2.pin.title: Pinball
city.wave2.pin.win.1: The ball ricochets between bumpers into a full jackpot. The bell rattles.
city.wave2.prize.1: On the shelf behind the counter: badges, candy, postcards. Not for tokens, only roubles.
city.wave2.prize.2: A note over the shelf: "Prizes for honest play."
city.wave2.prize.3: Three stamps on your card now: the seller dusts the brightest box and moves it closer.
city.wave2.prize.6: Six stamps, the whole card! The seller shakes your hand and quietly props up a plate: "Regular".
city.wave2.race.after.1: The wheel is still warm. The board shows somebody else's lap, faster than yours.
city.wave2.race.after.2: The stool wobbles. Somebody has clearly sat here for hours.
city.wave2.race.draw.1: A side-by-side finish; the cabinet judge calls it a draw.
city.wave2.race.lose.1: {0} comes out of the bend first. Your car is stuck in the sand.
city.wave2.race.title: Racing
city.wave2.race.win.1: You cross the line first, and {0} is still clinging to the wheel.
city.wave2.reg.dina.hello: Don't rush the start, that's where everyone slips.
city.wave2.reg.dina.lose: Don't mind: half an hour's practice and we're level.
city.wave2.reg.dina.win: Nicely driven. Will you show me how you took that bend?
city.wave2.reg.valera.hello: Sit down, I'm warmed up. Just don't touch my wheel.
city.wave2.reg.valera.lose: The first bend is mine and so are the rest. Get used to it.
city.wave2.reg.valera.win: Well, well. The wheel let me down, you'll see.
city.wave2.roofsea.clear: Clear to the horizon; you almost see the curve of the earth.
city.wave2.roofsea.cold: Cold: your eyes water in the wind, but the air is sharp as lemon.
city.wave2.roofsea.d1: From here the sea is one even line, as if ruled. The gulls below are specks.
city.wave2.roofsea.d2: Brass rings engraved with directions and distances: lighthouse 9 km, the spit 14.
city.wave2.roofsea.d3: The wind nudges your shoulder. The rail is cold, but you can see the waves come in rows.
city.wave2.roofsea.d4: A ferry crawls over the sea, its long wake slow to close.
city.wave2.roofsea.fog: There is almost no sea, only a white wall and a horn from far below.
city.wave2.roofsea.lantern: In the evening sky lanterns are lit on the beach. From up here they are sparks, then they rise past you.
city.wave2.roofsea.n1: At night the sea is black; the horizon shows only where the stars stop.
city.wave2.roofsea.n2: The lighthouse beam passes every ten seconds, brightening the wall for a moment.
city.wave2.roofsea.n3: Fishing-boat lights stand on the water like dots in a notebook.
city.wave2.roofsea.nfog: Fog has eaten everything but the lamp under the canopy and the siren's voice.
city.wave2.roofsea.rain: The rain comes in bands: you can watch the grey curtain approach from the sea.
city.wave2.roofsea.snow: Snow settles on the brass and melts by the figures where hands warmed it.
city.wave2.roofsea.warm: Even up here it is warm. The concrete is a stove under your palm.
city.wave2.rooftown.d: By day the town is a model: every street neat, every car tiny.
city.wave2.rooftown.e: In the evening windows light up one by one. Find yours by the warmest lamp.
city.wave2.rooftown.m: Morning smoke over the roofs and the smell of bread: the bakery below is already at work.
city.wave2.rooftown.n1: At night the town glows with yellow windows. The dark patches are the park, the bay and your yard.
city.wave2.rooftown.n2: The last bus rounds the square, its windows glowing like a lantern.
city.wave2.rooftown.we: On weekends it is busy below: stalls open on the square like coloured umbrellas.
city.wave2.shoot.after.1: Out of plays for today. The attract screen loops: the sub nods its periscope.
city.wave2.shoot.after.2: Somebody waits their turn behind you, breathing.
city.wave2.shoot.after.sun: On Sundays Sea Battle has a queue all the way to the record shop.
city.wave2.shoot.draw.1: Exactly half the ships. The cabinet nods: once more.
city.wave2.shoot.lose.1: The torpedoes missed. One blinking little ship is left.
city.wave2.shoot.lose.2: GAME OVER, and your score, which is a bit shy to show.
city.wave2.shoot.title: Sea Battle
city.wave2.shoot.win.1: The sub goes down, numbers dance on the screen. The day's record is close.
city.wave2.shoot.win.2: The cabinet flashes WIN three times and goes quiet, pleased with itself.
city.weather.cloakroom.1: "Wet raincoat on the end hook, over the radiator. It'll be dry by the end of the show."
city.weather.cloakroom.2: "Shake the snow off your collar onto the mat, not onto me. Felt boots can stay under the rack."
city.weather.counter.1: "Put your umbrella in the corner, please, I've got a whole sea on the floor already."
city.xcl.aq.0: A fish, orange as a boiled sweet, drifts unhurriedly from one end of the glass to the other. A little plate under the tank says "Head Doctor".
city.xcl.aq.1: In the morning the fish hangs right against the glass, by the reception side, as if queuing too.
city.xcl.aq.2: After lunch the hall is quiet. The fish stands by the weed, flicking a fin. Thinking.
city.xcl.aq.3: Towards evening the hall is nearly empty and the fish grows bold: out to the middle of the tank, looking at the front door.
city.xcl.aq.4: At night one ceiling lamp is on. The filter bubbles in the tank and the fish sleeps upright. Fish can do that.
city.xcl.aq.5: The children call the fish the Head Doctor: it swims by the reception with the look of someone who already knows everything. Nobody hung the plate, it just appeared, in a child's handwriting.
city.xcl.aq.6: The tank feels roomy. There used to be a second fish with the Head Doctor; now only a clay house is left on the bottom, and it is empty.
city.xcl.aq.7: The water is a little cloudy. A watering can stands beside it with a note: "Top up with settled water. Not straight from the tap, the fish has nerves."
city.xcl.aq.8: There are now two orange flecks in the tank. The Head Doctor keeps stoutly to the middle and pretends to be displeased.
city.xcl.aqw.1: You pour water from your bottle into the can, let it settle and carefully top up the tank. The fish backs away, then returns to check whether you are ashamed.
city.xcl.aqw.2: The water rises two fingers' width. The fish does a lap of honour along the glass and you could swear it nodded.
city.xcl.aqx.1: Somebody hung a paper garland on the aquarium. The Head Doctor swims beneath it with a solemn look.
city.xcl.aqx.2: Rain outside and quiet in the tank: the fish hangs by the glass watching the drops. Her favourite film.
city.xcl.baby_scales.1: Baby scales: a shallow tray and a brass beam with a weight. The doctor slides the weight and the beam hangs level in the middle. "Three-five," says the doctor. Not to me, of course.
city.xcl.baby_scales.2: A warm flowery nappy is spread in the tray. The doctor says the scale is more accurate with it: babies dislike cold, and their readings are more honest.
city.xcl.ball.1: A heavy red ball lies on the mat. Throw it at the wall, it comes back, catch it, throw again. It's stuffed with sand and patience.
city.xcl.ball.title: Medicine ball
city.xcl.bl.1: A notice: "Autumn: change your socks, don't lose your scarf, don't chill your throat. Consultation with the district doctor on weekdays."
city.xcl.bl.2: "Next week is Vaccination Week. Sign up at the reception. Bring your card and a good mood." The word "good" is underlined.
city.xcl.bl.3: "VACCINATION WEEK. Room 3, from 9 to 12. The procedure takes a moment, the sweet afterwards is compulsory." A sweet is drawn under the text, impossible to miss.
city.xcl.bl.4: "Thank you to everyone who had their jab! The sheet bears 112 signatures and one nose print."
city.xcl.bl.5: "Winter: walks before lunch, hot tea afterwards. Mind your ears: a hat is not an ornament."
city.xcl.bl.6: "Spring and summer: sun in moderation, water not icy, bicycles with helmets (helmets issued at reception)."
city.xcl.blx.1: Under the old notices hangs a new one: "Please don't knock on the registry window or ask who's last more than three times. The last one is whoever asks."
city.xcl.bp.1: The cuff swells, the needle jumps. The nurse listens through the stethoscope, her lips moving, and nods: "Like an astronaut's. Only an astronaut's is a little lower."
city.xcl.bp.2: "A hundred and twenty over eighty." You don't know if that's a lot or a little, but the nurse smiles. So it's good.
city.xcl.bp.3: The cuff lets go of your arm with a long sigh, and you sigh too. The nurse writes the figures in your card and underlines them twice.
city.xcl.card_book.1: "Medical card" on the cover. Inside, five empty squares for stamps: therapist, eye doctor, children's doctor, the vaccination table, the wall bars.
city.xcl.card_book.2: The therapist's stamp: round, violet, "Examined. Healthy."
city.xcl.card_book.3: The eye doctor's stamp: two letters, "Sh" and "B", and a signature that looks like spectacles.
city.xcl.card_book.4: The children's doctor's stamp: a giraffe's face. Beside it, in pen: "growing!"
city.xcl.card_book.5: The vaccination table's stamp: a blue drop. "All on schedule."
city.xcl.card_book.6: The physio stamp: a little man hanging off the wall bars.
city.xcl.card_book.7: All five squares are filled. The card is thicker and more serious now. The registrar will like it.
city.xcl.cf.1: The card file: little drawers with letters. The cards stand tight as books on a shelf. Each has a surname, a birth year, vaccinations and Galina Petrovna's handwriting, round and quite legible.
city.xcl.cf.2: From the drawer marked K sticks a card with a note: "Fell off his bicycle. For the last time? No, not the last." In another hand beside it: "Helmet issued."
city.xcl.cf.3: The schoolchildren's cards are bound with a red elastic band: height and weight for every year, and in the margins notes like "reads at meals" and "climbs fences".
city.xcl.cf.4: The thickest card belongs to a man who, going by the entries, comes to the clinic to have someone to talk to. The nurse's note: "Listen. Pour tea."
city.xcl.clock.1: The clock over the registry says {time}. Appointments eight to eight, except Sundays.
city.xcl.clock.2: {time}. Mornings are busiest: every door has a queue, and every queue its own theory of who gets called first.
city.xcl.clock.3: {time}. By evening the doctors go home and only the nurse stays. If you need something, hurry.
city.xcl.clock.4: {time}. Appointments are over. At night the clock ticks louder than by day: no queue to drown it.
city.xcl.closed_any.1: Dark and quiet. Behind the glass door the porter rustles a newspaper. At night the clinic is just a quiet house that smells of iodine and a little of valerian.
city.xcl.closed_any.2: Sunday: the clinic is resting. A note on the door: "Ambulance: 03. Doctors are people too, and will be back on Monday."
city.xcl.closed_any.3: Appointments are over for now: the doctors have gone home, leaving the smell of iodine and a plate with the hours.
city.xcl.closed_counter.1: It is dark behind the little window. The night porter opens one eye: "Appointments from eight. Come in the morning."
city.xcl.closed_counter.2: The window is shut. A notice on the door: "Open Monday to Saturday, eight to eight."
city.xcl.closed_counter.3: The doctor left at five. A note on the desk: "The nurse is here until eight, ask her."
city.xcl.closed_counter.4: Nobody is here at the moment. A little sign on the desk: "Back soon."
city.xcl.closed_seat.1: The chairs stand with their backs to the wall. At night the queue exists only in the porter's log: it says who is first tomorrow.
city.xcl.closed_seat.2: Nobody to sit with and no reason to: there is no appointment today. The chairs rest along with the doctors.
city.xcl.closed_seat.3: Nobody sits here now: appointments are over, everything strictly by the timetable.
city.xcl.dn.0: A white door without a pane. The plate: "Room 4. Dentist. By appointment." Nobody sits on the chair by the door, but the chair is squared up as if waiting.
city.xcl.dn.1: A drill hums softly behind the door. Everyone in the hall has suddenly become interested in the poster above the bench.
city.xcl.dn.2: The door opens: a boy with red ears comes out, palm pressed to his cheek. "It didn't hurt!" he tells his mum, and sits so that nobody can see his face.
city.xcl.dn.3: Instruments clink in a steel dish behind the door. It sounds like somebody counting out small change for your future.
city.xcl.dn.4: The door is locked. In the dark the "Room 4" plate looks sterner than by day.
city.xcl.dn.5: The room is shut at weekends. A note on the door: "Toothache? Emergencies at the duty nurse's reception desk. Be brave."
city.xcl.doc0_talk.1: "Come in, sit down. What hurts? Nothing? Then you're a rare visitor."
city.xcl.doc0_talk.2: "The main medicine is routine: bed on time, up on time, lunch on time. The rest is seasoning."
city.xcl.doc0_talk.3: "Three rules against autumn: thermometer under the arm, throat 'aah', scarf on the neck. The scarf matters most."
city.xcl.doc0_talk.4: "I got this stethoscope back at medical school. It knows more about me than I do."
city.xcl.doc0_talk.5: "Rain: a cough will go round town like a rumour. Did you bring a scarf?"
city.xcl.doc1_talk.1: "Sit on the chair by the red line. Cover your left eye. No, not with your palm, with this paddle."
city.xcl.doc1_talk.2: "Nearly everyone sees up close. It's the distance that needs testing: five metres, from the tape on the floor to the chart."
city.xcl.doc1_talk.3: "Glasses aren't a weakness, they're a hint. The world really is sharp, it's just that nobody told some of us."
city.xcl.doc1_talk.4: "Reading in the dark won't ruin your eyes. It ruins your mood. The lamp goes on by the window, there's the switch."
city.xcl.doc1_talk.5: "In the rain everyone squints the same, the sharp-eyed and the bespectacled alike. A fair kind of weather."
city.xcl.doc2_talk.1: "Hi there! We measure height at the giraffe, weight later, once we've sorted the toys."
city.xcl.doc2_talk.2: "There's a sweet in my desk. Not for bravery, but for turning up on time. That's a feat too."
city.xcl.doc2_talk.3: "This ruler here. Catch it and your reflexes are fine. Miss it and you were thinking of something nice."
city.xcl.doc2_talk.4: "The mobile above the couch. Babies watch it and forget to cry. Grown-ups do too, by the way."
city.xcl.doc2_talk.5: "In the rain the children come in wellies. Wellies in the corner, toys on the rug, puddles outside for now."
city.xcl.ep.1: Rabkin's plates: speckled circles with numbers hidden in them. Some see the number at once, others after a long look. Yesterday one patient saw a cat.
city.xcl.ep.2: A case of trial lenses: thin discs of glass in metal rims. The doctor swaps them one after another: "And this? And this? And now?"
city.xcl.eye_game.1: The pointer leans on the wall, the chart glows. The top row, then lower, then a really tiny one. The tape on the floor is red so nobody creeps closer.
city.xcl.eye_game.2: Sh B M N K. Close one eye and half the world hides. Close both and the chart is still there: that's how well it's memorised.
city.xcl.eye_game.draw.1: Five rows read, then guesswork. "Good," says the eye doctor. "Nearly an eagle. Come back after the holidays."
city.xcl.eye_game.lose.1: Past the third row everything blurs to grey specks. "Spectacles soon," the eye doctor consoles. "Nice ones, we'll choose together."
city.xcl.eye_game.title: Eye test
city.xcl.eye_game.win.1: Read down to the smallest row: "Sh B M N K". The eye doctor nods: "Eagle-eyed." The stamp goes on the card at once.
city.xcl.frames.1: Frames on the shelf: round like a professor's, square like an accountant's, one with no lenses at all, for trying on.
city.xcl.frames.2: Beside them an open box of trial lenses: each in its slot like sweets in a box. Every one changes the world a little.
city.xcl.growth.1: Back to the wall, heels together, chin up. The doctor slides the ruler over my head: "A metre sixty exactly and a little bit more." A pencil line and the giraffe stamp.
city.xcl.growth.2: The giraffe is covered in children's marks: lines with dates and names. The lowest says "Me at three". Above it a whole little ladder.
city.xcl.growth.3: The doctor squints: "A finger taller since last time. Either you've got your shoes on, or it's true." The second line lands above the first.
city.xcl.hm.1: The rubber hammer taps below your kneecap and your leg kicks out by itself. The nurse is pleased: "Reflexes fine. Manners, a C."
city.xcl.hm.2: You follow the hammer's shiny tip with your eyes and forget you have another leg. Tap. The leg jumps. You laugh.
city.xcl.ht.1: You stand with your back to the wall, chin up. The slider comes down on your head with a clink. Beside it, pencil marks in the plaster; the lowest ones carry the names of toddlers.
city.xcl.ht.2: A hundred and sixty-something. The "150" mark is worn to a shine: every schoolchild in the district has been measured here, and every one rose a little on tiptoe.
city.xcl.ht.3: A paper by the ruler: "No tiptoes. No heels. No sulking: you will still grow."
city.xcl.in.1: The nurse switches the machine on: alkaline water bubbles in the glass jar. You breathe warm steam. It smells of baking soda and winter.
city.xcl.in.2: Fifteen minutes. Your nose clears, and your thoughts with it. Beside you an old lady sits over the other glass with the face of someone at the baths, not a clinic.
city.xcl.in.3: The nurse times it with an hourglass. The hourglass is small, the steam is large. "One more minute. No, I didn't decide, the sand did."
city.xcl.jar.1: The coin clunks to the bottom of the jar. The paper on the glass says "For the Head Doctor's friend", and someone has drawn a second fish under the words.
city.xcl.jar.2: The nurse nods from her window: "Thank you. The Head Doctor doesn't know yet, but when he does he'll be glad. He'll pretend not to be."
city.xcl.jar.3: The jar is full now. The nurse laughs: "That covers guppies, food and a pretty pebble besides. The rest I put back in the till, don't worry."
city.xcl.listen.1: The doctor warms the stethoscope between her palms. "Breathe. Hold it. Breathe." All I can hear is my own heart, which seems to be in a hurry.
city.xcl.listen.2: "Clear," says the therapist. "Lungs like a songbird's. Just wear a scarf." The stamp lands on the card with a soft thump.
city.xcl.listen.3: After lunch the room smells of tea with lemon. The stethoscope is warm, the fingers are warm. Just as it should be.
city.xcl.listen.4: A smell of wet raincoat from outside. "Caught in the rain too? Then we'll listen extra carefully."
city.xcl.listen.5: A holiday card stands on the doctor's desk. "People fall ill on holidays too. More often they just want someone to listen."
city.xcl.mg.1: Last year's "Health" and a cover-less "Ogonyok". The crossword in "Health" is half done: "Part of the ear, five letters" and somebody has written "lobe" in, underlined with pleasure.
city.xcl.mg.2: A magazine piece "How to learn to wait" has been cut out with scissors. What is left is the edge of the page and "To be continued in the next issue".
city.xcl.mg.3: An old newspaper folded in four: telephone numbers jotted on it and a recipe for pickles. The stains suggest the recipe has been tested.
city.xcl.mg.v: A magazine lies open at "A jab isn't scary". Over the picture someone has pencilled a smiling face on the sleeve.
city.xcl.mobile.1: Above the couch, a mobile turns: red square, blue, yellow, green. It turns by warm air from the radiator, not by hand.
city.xcl.mobile.2: The threads are thin, the crossbar light wood. Lie on the couch and you see the squares sway to someone's breathing.
city.xcl.nurse_talk.1: "Here for me? The vaccination table's here by the cooler. Don't worry, only a check today. The rest is on schedule."
city.xcl.nurse_talk.2: "The fridge holds the vaccines and my sandwich. Vaccines on top, sandwich below. Mixed them up once. Never again."
city.xcl.nurse_talk.3: "A queue isn't lost time. It's the one place grown-ups read the posters to the end."
city.xcl.nurse_talk.4: "The wall bars by the window aren't for show. After a cold: ten squats and your shoulders stop aching."
city.xcl.nurse_talk.5: "Rain outside, but it's dry in here and the tea is hot. Sit, dry off, then we'll see what's wrong."
city.xcl.nurse_talk.6: "A holiday and I'm on shift. Never mind, there's cake in the fridge: on the top shelf, with the vaccines."
city.xcl.p.baby: E — look at the baby scales
city.xcl.p.bars: E — do exercises at the wall bars
city.xcl.p.bp: E — have my blood pressure taken
city.xcl.p.cards: E — peek into the card file
city.xcl.p.eyetest: E — read the chart by the pointer
city.xcl.p.jar: E — drop a coin in the jar
city.xcl.p.listen: E — have my chest listened to
city.xcl.p.mags: E — pick a magazine off the table
city.xcl.p.porter: E — step up to the porter's table
city.xcl.p.scale: E — weigh something on the apothecary scale
city.xcl.p.slit: E — look into the slit lamp
city.xcl.pad.1: A prescription pad. Today's entry: "Rest, warm drinks, woollen socks. A prescription for all."
city.xcl.pad.2: On the pad: "A twenty-minute walk, never without a hat." Underlined twice.
city.xcl.pad.3: The pad is blank except for the violet stamp on top. The Sunday entry: "Rest."
city.xcl.ph.j1: Jars with Latin labels. Only "Aqua" and "Mel" look familiar. The rest sounds like a spell.
city.xcl.ph.j2: A paper over the jars: "Prescription goods not sold without a prescription. Medicine without a prescription is called a sweet. Sweets are over here."
city.xcl.ph.j3: On the shelf a white mortar with its pestle. They say nobody grinds powders any more, they arrive ready-made. But the mortar is wiped every morning.
city.xcl.ph.r1: "Prescriptions are accepted 8 to 12. Dispensed 2 to 5. An unreadable prescription goes back to the doctor who wrote it. He sometimes cannot read it himself."
city.xcl.ph.r2: "Please do not ask us for honey, raspberries or cherry jam. That is for your grandmother. Thermometers are for measuring, not for biting."
city.xcl.ph.s1: Apothecary scales: two little pans and a brass beam. The nurse puts a five-gram weight on one and a pinch of sugar on the other. They balance. "Just checking," she says. "The scales are honest."
city.xcl.ph.s2: On the scales, foil from a chocolate bar: exactly one gram. "We used to check nobody was being short-changed. Now I check the pharmacy isn't short-changing itself."
city.xcl.pharm_talk.1: "A prescription, or just browsing? Either's fine, but without one it's only tea, water and sweets."
city.xcl.pharm_talk.2: "The scale is old but true. Twenty years it hasn't drifted: I don't touch it, it respects me."
city.xcl.pharm_talk.3: "The jars on the shelf are labelled in Latin. No need to read them, just to know what's in which."
city.xcl.pharm_talk.4: "Honey for a cough, viburnum for a cold, quiet for the nerves. Quiet is free, help yourself."
city.xcl.pharm_talk.5: "Rain is our busiest day: the tea goes, the umbrellas dry by the door. Mind the puddle."
city.xcl.pharm_talk.6: "Frost: tea, sweets, hot drinks. That's all of pharmacology."
city.xcl.physio_ball.draw.1: Two throws in a row, then a miss. The ball lies on the floor as if smiling. "A good start," the nurse decides.
city.xcl.physio_ball.lose.1: The ball slips and rolls under the bench. "Never mind," says the nurse. "Once more. I'm the one who sits, you're the one who moves."
city.xcl.physio_ball.win.1: Four throws in a row without a miss. The ball comes back like an obedient dog. The nurse ticks a box without turning around.
city.xcl.physio_bars.1: The nurse shows: arms up, pull, hang. Deft and dull, like everything good for you. After ten seconds the shoulders hum.
city.xcl.physio_bars.2: "Straight back, breathe," the nurse commands. "Doctors dislike sitting. You've got to move in any weather."
city.xcl.physio_bars.3: Heel dents are left on the mat. The nurse notes in the card: "physio, done." The wall bars creak like an old ship.
city.xcl.pl.0: The plate on the door: "Hours 8 to 17, break 13 to 14." In pencil underneath: "A break is when the doctor eats, not when he can't hear you."
city.xcl.pl.1: "Today the duty nurse sees patients. Doctors from Monday." The paper has yellowed at the edges: it has hung there a long time, weekends do repeat.
city.xcl.porter.1: At the table sits the night porter: tea in a faceted glass, a chess problem in the paper. "Closed," he says without looking up. "Come in the morning."
city.xcl.porter.2: "Don't touch the lamp," the porter warns. "It's mine for the whole night. There are switches, but I have a conscience."
city.xcl.porter.3: The porter says: "At night you can hear everything here: the clock, the aquarium, a fish turning over. You get used to it, then you miss it."
city.xcl.porter_day.1: The porter's table is empty. A clean faceted glass in the holder, a scarf on the back of the chair. The porter comes in the evening.
city.xcl.porter_day.2: A newspaper on the table with yesterday's chess problem. In pencil: "Knight to e5?" No answer yet.
city.xcl.qb.1: The board reads "17". Under it a lamp blinks "Room 2". As long as it blinks, somebody inside is telling the long story of their knee.
city.xcl.qb.2: The board shows "CLOSED" and the red digits are dark. A paper under it says: "Surgery over. Tomorrow from 8:00."
city.xcl.qb.3: At weekends the board is silent: one duty nurse sees everybody, and she needs no queue. "Come on up, don't be shy."
city.xcl.qbx.1: The board says 41. In this cold the queue stretches to the door and back: it's warmer standing near the radiator.
city.xcl.rd.1: The loudspeaker softly draws out the morning exercises: "Deep breath in... and deeper still..." Half the queue straightens its back without meaning to.
city.xcl.rd.2: The wall radio quietly gives news of steel output and the weather on the coast. The weather is more interesting.
city.xcl.rd.3: An orchestra is playing. An old woman by the wall taps her toe in time and pretends not to be listening.
city.xcl.rd.4: The evening request show. The announcer reads a letter: "For Mum, who is late at the clinic today. We are waiting at home."
city.xcl.rd.5: The wall radio is silent. In the quiet you can hear the aquarium filter bubbling.
city.xcl.remedies.1: In the glass cabinet: thermometers in a tumbler, a stack of mustard plasters, iodine, brilliant green. Every label hand-written, all in one hand.
city.xcl.remedies.2: On the bottom shelf, woollen socks in neat bags. The bags say: "Issued from a temperature of 37.5."
city.xcl.remedies.3: Beside the thermometers, a jar of lime blossom. The date is pencilled and already rubbed away, so it must be fresh.
city.xcl.rg.1: "Have you taken a ticket? See the board? Look at that, and at me afterwards."
city.xcl.rg.2: "Surname? Year of birth? No, not mine, yours."
city.xcl.rg.3: "The doctor sees patients until five. Not until five to five, until five. You'll make it if you don't read the whole poster."
city.xcl.rg.4: "After five it is just me and the thermometer. But it's a good thermometer, German, pre-war."
city.xcl.rg.5: "On Saturdays there are no doctors, I'm all of them. What hurts? Tell me, I'll write it down and say who to see on Monday."
city.xcl.rg.6: "Want to help? There's the jar. The money isn't for me, it's for the Head Doctor. The fish, I mean. Don't get ideas."
city.xcl.rg.7: "Thank you for coming in. Take tickets in order, not out of greed. Then there'll be enough for everyone."
city.xcl.rgx.1: "New here? Card first. We'll start one, so there's something to stamp. The rooms do the stamping, not me: I only count."
city.xcl.rgx.2: "Don't lose the ticket. Without a number you're just a nice person here; with one, you're a patient."
city.xcl.rgx.3: "The board over the passage: the number is who's being called. Don't take offence if it isn't a name. That's how we do it here."
city.xcl.rgx.4: "Any room you need. The therapist listens, the eye doctor looks, the children's doctor has a giraffe. All good, each in their own way."
city.xcl.rgx.5: "Two stamps already? It's coming along. Five, and the card goes in a frame."
city.xcl.rgx.6: "All five! Your card is lovelier than my own now. Take care of it."
city.xcl.rgx.7: "It's freezing and the place is packed like a bathhouse. Everyone comes to warm up and, while they're at it, check their throat." The queue is indeed longer than usual.
city.xcl.rgx.8: "A holiday, so we stamp twice as cheerfully. But the queue is the same: ailments take no days off."
city.xcl.ruler.1: The ruler hangs above a cup of pencils. The doctor says: "Ready." Fingers open, and suddenly it falls.
city.xcl.ruler.2: The lower the number where you catch it, the faster the reaction. Catching it at the very end means "once more."
city.xcl.ruler.draw.1: Half caught, half dropped. "Excellent for the first half of the day," the doctor says without looking at the clock.
city.xcl.ruler.lose.1: The ruler slips between my fingers and clatters to the floor. "Never mind," says the doctor. "It means you were thinking of something nice."
city.xcl.ruler.title: Ruler drop: reflexes
city.xcl.ruler.win.1: The ruler is caught on the very lowest number. "Quicker than my patients," the doctor sighs and takes a sweet from the desk.
city.xcl.slit_lamp.1: Through the eyepiece: an upside-down window and my own eyelash the size of a fir tree. "Please don't blink." Easy to say.
city.xcl.slit_lamp.2: Chin on the rest, forehead on the bar. A narrow strip of light creeps across the iris like a sunbeam on water.
city.xcl.slit_lamp.3: The eye doctor turns a little lever: "Now look at my nose." The nose, incidentally, is huge and kind in the lens.
city.xcl.tk.1: The machine gives you ticket no. 6. The board shows "3", so a couple of people ahead. Everyone in the hall pretends not to be counting.
city.xcl.tk.2: Ticket no. 41, the board says "17". The old woman beside you sighs and straightens her scarf: "They used to call you by name. At least you knew it was a person being called."
city.xcl.tk.3: Ticket no. 58. After lunch the queue melts away: the board shows "55" and you will be called soon.
city.xcl.tk.4: The roll of tickets has run out and a note is taped to the machine: "No more tickets today. Emergency help is at the reception."
city.xcl.tkx.1: Ticket: 31. In this cold the queue is longer: everyone came in to warm up and check their throat while at it.
city.xcl.tkx.2: The ticket went soft in the rain: the numbers ran, but "23" can still be made out. The queue by the door is an umbrella queue.
city.xcl.tkx.3: A festive ticket: number 7, with a little fir tree drawn on the back. On holidays the queue is shorter, most people self-medicate with jam.
city.xcl.toys.1: In the box: blocks, a ball, a plush bear with one ear. The other ear came off long ago, but everyone acts as if it should be that way.
city.xcl.toys.2: The blocks are stacked in a tower. The top one has the letter "I". It seems to be the first word anyone learns here.
city.xcl.toys.3: The ball rolled under the box and came back. It seems even the balls here don't want to leave without a check-up.
city.xcl.toys.4: Wet wellies in the corner, and the bear in the box wears somebody's scarf, neatly tied. Rain gives everyone away.
city.xcl.umbrellas.1: The umbrellas stand in the rack, folded and dry like a row of soldiers. One blue, one black, one checked, without an owner.
city.xcl.umbrellas.2: Three wet umbrellas drip into the tray: plink, plink, out of step. The puddle by the door grows. There's no cloakroom here, the umbrellas stand on trust.
city.xcl.umbrellas.3: The tray under the umbrellas is full of clear water: the snow they carried in has melted. Somebody's ski pole stands there too.
city.xcl.umbrellas.4: Umbrellas aren't needed at night but they stand: the clinic never tidies anything away. The checked one has probably waited a year for its owner.
city.xcl.vaccine.1: The nurse turns the pasted-in sheet: measles, diphtheria, tetanus. "All on schedule," and stamps a blue drop. A sugar cube on a saucer is the reward.
city.xcl.vaccine.2: "I won't jab anything just in case," the nurse smiles. "I checked, you're fine." The stamp lies straight, as if glued.
city.xcl.vaccine.3: A table in a quiet corner: a tray, cotton balls, a bottle of iodine. A stool alongside, always a little warm from the last patient.
city.xcl.vaccine_fridge.1: A note on the door: "Not to be opened without the nurse." Through the gap, cold blue light and a row of little boxes labelled in Latin.
city.xcl.vaccine_fridge.2: The fridge hums evenly and caringly. A "Greetings from Palanga" magnet on top, who knows whose, and a list of temperatures for every day.
city.xcl.vaccine_schedule.1: Vaccination schedule: flu until the end of November, measles by appointment, diphtheria once in ten years. Written below by hand: "Don't be afraid, it's quick."
city.xcl.vaccine_schedule.2: "Flu season: come ahead of time, not once you're already sneezing." The notice is underlined in red and pinned with three tacks against draughts.
city.xf.alb.1: An album in an oilcloth cover with a sticker: "Traveller". On the first page: "I photograph those who came on business and those who came for no reason. The second kind come out better."
city.xf.alb.2: A print on the second page: the lighthouse at sunset, upside down. Caption: "This way you can see how firmly it stands."
city.xf.alb.3: A new print is pasted in: a sandal on a bench, yellow, with a broken buckle. "Looking for its pair. Please look under the benches, not over them."
city.xf.alb.4: Next print: the Lost and Found basket by the scales, with a pair of yellow sandals in it. Below: "End of story. Filmed without actors."
city.xf.alb.5: A print by the strongman: two people shaking hands before the strike. "Beresnev and Melnikova. The bell is out of the frame, but you can hear it."
city.xf.alb.6: On the last page an empty frame. Caption: "Third place is free. Discount for schoolchildren." Beside it a little pocket for the print of whoever comes next.
city.xf.alb.prompt: E — leaf through the photographer's album
city.xf.albl.1: The album lies on the little table under a stone from the embankment. The stone is smooth and very proud.
city.xf.albl.2: The photographer's table is without the photographer for now: he has gone to develop prints or to talk to a gull.
city.xf.car.1: Daisy the horse set off round the circle and the clouds set off after her. A round, another round: the horse and I have the same speed and the same delight.
city.xf.car.fest: On a holiday the keeper rings twice instead of once: "One for you, one for everybody."
city.xf.car.pm: In the evening the rim of the roof glows, the horse glides in the beams, the festoons on the canopy sway in time. A waltz plays.
city.xf.car.rain: Rain on the canopy and dry under the roundabout's roof. We ride in privacy, like in a little theatre.
city.xf.car.we: At the weekend a little one rides the next horse, holding the mane with both hands and me with his eyes. We ride together.
city.xf.closed.any.1: The fair is closed. The canopy stands over an empty walk like an umbrella over a forgotten bench.
city.xf.closed.any.2: Quiet. The festoons sway a little: nobody forbade the wind.
city.xf.closed.any.3: A sign on the post: "The fair is open Friday, Saturday and Sunday, 11 a.m. to 10 p.m."
city.xf.closed.board.1: The board in the dark: the letters can't be made out, you can only guess it says something about tomorrow.
city.xf.closed.board.2: The notices can't be read now: the wind turns them over and the pegs are asleep. I'll be back in the morning.
city.xf.closed.counter.1: The counter is shuttered, with chalk on the shutter: "Back on Friday. Don't be bored."
city.xf.closed.counter.2: Behind the shut counter it is empty and clean. Only yesterday's coin on the shelf: left there for luck.
city.xf.closed.machine.1: The machine is switched off. The glass is dark and shows only me and the canopy.
city.xf.closed.machine.2: Switched off. On the back someone has chalked an arrow: "Switch at the entrance, but not now."
city.xf.closed.play.1: The game is closed and covered with oilcloth. Under the oilcloth something seems to be sleeping, or maybe it's just a ball.
city.xf.closed.play.2: The table is covered, the pieces put away in a box. The box is marked: "Don't shake, they don't like it."
city.xf.closed.shelf.1: The stand is covered with oilcloth. A corner of a postcard peeks out, but it can't be pulled.
city.xf.closed.sport.1: The strongman is shut: the mallet has gone home, the puck sits at the bottom waiting for Friday.
city.xf.closed.sport.2: The kettlebells are tucked under the bench with a note: "Hands off, they are still asleep."
city.xf.closed.take.1: They leave no free papers out at night: the wind reads them faster than people.
city.xf.coll.prizes.title: The fair's prize stand
city.xf.dom.1: Dominoes on the fair's little table: the tiles are smooth as sea pebbles and also like lying in rows.
city.xf.dom.pm: In the evening the tiles gleam under the lights. A quick game, supper is waiting.
city.xf.dom.rain: Rain taps the canopy in time with the tiles. Whoever doesn't lose count wins.
city.xf.galp.1: Gallery: five shots, five roubles. Hit the little bell and get a postcard. Hit Claudia the duck: we don't know, nobody ever has.
city.xf.galp.sat: Saturday: five shots, five roubles, three for schoolchildren. The rifle pulls left: that is how it is done.
city.xf.galp.sun: Sunday: whoever knocks down three ducks in a row gets a sip of water and the keeper's applause.
city.xf.height.1: I leaned the back of my head on the post and lowered the slider onto my crown. Exactly at the mark the schoolchildren call "grown-up".
city.xf.height.2: The slider rested on my hair. Someone shouts from afar: "No jumping, this is not a ride!"
city.xf.height.3: By evening, they say, we are all a centimetre shorter. The post has nothing to do with it, that is tiredness.
city.xf.height.prompt: E — stand by the height post
city.xf.keep.car.h1: The ticket from the keeper, the keeper at the lever. Climb on, the horses don't bite.
city.xf.keep.car.h2: In the evening the roof's rim glows. They are the only bulbs allowed to go round.
city.xf.keep.car.t1.1: Six horses: Daisy, Grozny, Tulip, Wisp, Hussar and Quiet. Quiet is the quietest but the fastest.
city.xf.keep.car.t1.2: Hussar has been repainted three times: the children ask for blue, then dappled. Now he is dappled but misses blue.
city.xf.keep.car.t2.1: A round takes five minutes. A bell to begin, a bell to end, music between.
city.xf.keep.car.t2.2: If the second round is boring, you have grown up. It isn't terrible, just come back at weekends.
city.xf.keep.car.t3.1: The festoon switch is on a post at each end of the canopy. I switch it on at dusk if nobody has.
city.xf.keep.car.t3.2: Thanks to whoever switched them on. Double thanks to whoever switched them off in time.
city.xf.keep.gal.h1: Five shots, five roubles. My ducks are old, my eye is sharp.
city.xf.keep.gal.h2: By evening the ducks are lazier: they go slowly, as if tired too.
city.xf.keep.gal.t1.1: Seven ducks, all named. The left one is Claudia: she doesn't fall, she has character.
city.xf.keep.gal.t1.2: Knock down Claudia and you get a postcard and I get a lesson. Nobody has yet, but she's getting nervous.
city.xf.keep.gal.t2.1: It catches one station, but steadily: gymnastics in the morning, news by day, a waltz in the evening.
city.xf.keep.gal.t2.2: I turn it off at night so the ducks sleep. Without music they fall asleep faster than I do.
city.xf.keep.gal.t3.1: Cork. The children collect them after closing and I pretend not to see. That is part of the gallery too.
city.xf.keep.gal.t3.2: No lead ones, don't worry. Not even the tin hedgehog has ever been hurt.
city.xf.keep.lot.h1: A ticket for ten roubles, always a win: a postcard or a postcard. Turn it.
city.xf.keep.lot.h2: By evening the drum creaks tenderly, like a violin in the pit.
city.xf.keep.lot.t1.1: The board on the post changes every day: the colour of the square I've chalked in is the day's lucky colour.
city.xf.keep.lot.t1.2: If you draw the day's colour you get the postcard with the lighthouse. If not, an ordinary postcard. Everyone is happy.
city.xf.keep.lot.t2.1: From the embankment, the lighthouse, the market. The travelling photographer sends new ones, the old ones have spread all over town.
city.xf.keep.lot.t2.2: You've drawn from me already. Keep the lighthouse postcard in view: it is lucky until it fades.
city.xf.keep.lot.t3.1: Those are won and forgotten. The owner comes, takes down his own, and the rest hang and wait.
city.xf.keep.lot.t3.2: One has hung since Friday. I know it by heart by now, and still no owner.
city.xf.keep.ring.h1: A ring on a bottle neck, a bottle neck for luck. Three throws, three roubles.
city.xf.keep.ring.h2: In the evening the rings roll better: polished by palms.
city.xf.keep.ring.t1: About the prizes on the stand
city.xf.keep.ring.t1.1: A clockwork duck, a tin lighthouse, a plaster hedgehog. Everything on the shelf can be won. What isn't on the shelf can't.
city.xf.keep.ring.t1.2: The bear went to a boy in a blue cap, the eye will follow by post. He promised to write.
city.xf.keep.ring.t2.1: The rings are wooden, I painted them myself. The red flies farther, the yellow is more exact, the green is just pretty.
city.xf.keep.ring.t2.2: One ring flew onto a kiosk roof and was fetched with a mop. Now I hang a hat nearby so the luck isn't lost.
city.xf.keep.ring.t3: About the boy in the blue cap
city.xf.keep.ring.t3.1: He came two days running and on the third he won. He says the bear winked at him. I kept quiet: the bear has one eye.
city.xf.keep.ring.t3.2: His postcard has already come: a drawn bear with two eyes. One in green, the other in pencil.
city.xf.keep.str.h1: The mallet is heavy, the hand is light: that's the whole science. Will you strike?
city.xf.keep.str.h2: By evening the mallet has warmed from the palms and strikes easier. Step up.
city.xf.keep.str.t1: About the record on the plaque
city.xf.keep.str.t1.1: Beresnev is a ship's mechanic, goes off on voyages and always comes back to the fair. He guards the record like a dinner voucher.
city.xf.keep.str.t1.2: Melnikova strikes without a run-up, with one shoulder. Beresnev took offence and went to train on an anchor chain.
city.xf.keep.str.t2: Why the mallet is so heavy
city.xf.keep.str.t2.1: Oak, with a lead plug inside. It used to be light, but then everybody struck it and the bell broke.
city.xf.keep.str.t2.2: I balanced it myself, the handle has been lighter since. You can see I tried.
city.xf.keep.str.t3.1: The bell is from a fishing schooner. It can be heard at the lighthouse if the wind is off the shore.
city.xf.keep.str.t3.2: I heard you strike. An honest sound: no "almost" and no "oops".
city.xf.led.1:
THE STRONGMAN'S LEDGER.
Write down: the surname, the points and how the bell rang.
Fair record: 71. Beresnev N., ship's mechanic.
The bell is silent for now, but ready.
city.xf.led.2: Empty lines next to Beresnev's name: "at sea". The others have signed, though: 38, a schoolboy, a quiet ring; 46, a postman, rang by the book; 52, no surname, with a note: "I need to catch my breath."
city.xf.led.3: 74, Beresnev N. Came back early, struck straight off the road with a suitcase in his left hand. Beside it a ring in a child's chalk that nobody has rubbed out.
city.xf.led.4: 77, Melnikova L. Three strikes: 63, 69, 77. Beresnev has added underneath: "Congratulations. Rematch on Sunday, and let the mallet be honest."
city.xf.led.5: The Sunday rematch. Beresnev: 76, 79, 80. Melnikova: 75, 78. Hands shaken before the strike, not after. The bell was heard at the lighthouse, the keeper confirmed in writing.
city.xf.led.6: The last line: "Third place is free." Below it in pencil: "Discount for schoolchildren", and lower still in red, unsigned: "And you?"
city.xf.ledl.1: The ledger lies on a clipboard under a clothes-peg. The wind tries to read it, the peg won't let it.
city.xf.ledl.2: While I leafed through the ledger somebody struck at the bell and all the pages jumped at once.
city.xf.lotn.1: On the post, a board of twelve coloured squares. The winning one is whichever the seller marks with chalk. She hasn't yet.
city.xf.lotn.fest: A holiday: all twelve squares are painted gold. Written below: "Today everybody wins, but in turn."
city.xf.lotn.fri: Friday: a red square with a dot. "Red on a Friday means a postcard," said the seller.
city.xf.lotn.prompt: E — look at the winning numbers
city.xf.lotn.sat: Saturday: a blue square. A note beside it: "If you draw blue, wink at the drum."
city.xf.lotn.sun: Sunday: yellow. On Sunday the colour closest to the sun wins.
city.xf.player.rashid.hello: Three cups, one pea, no guarantees. Your move.
city.xf.player.rashid.lose: That's my trick. Come back tomorrow, the trick will be here too.
city.xf.player.rashid.win: What an eye! Consider the pea yours.
city.xf.pp.after.1: The table stands under the canopy, the ball is fragile, the bats are ginger from a thousand palms.
city.xf.pp.after.2: The ball bounced off under a bench. I fetch it the way you fetch sandals: kneeling, with dignity.
city.xf.pp.after.rain: Rain on the canopy, the ball on the table. The sounds are alike, so it is not at once clear who has won.
city.xf.pp.title: Tennis under the canopy
city.xf.prog.1:
THE FAIR UNDER THE WAVE CANOPY.
Open Friday, Saturday and Sunday, 11 a.m. to 10 p.m. On weekdays the canopy keeps itself company: dry, clean and quiet underneath.
Roundabout tickets from the keeper, everything else from whoever stands behind a counter.
city.xf.prog.fri:
FRIDAY.
11:00 opening, the gallery for schoolchildren.
16:30 the stallholders change shift, the first strings of lights go on.
20:00 the lottery "for locals".
Prize of the day: the clockwork duck.
city.xf.prog.late: In red pencil: "Sunday evening, the week's results: the strongman's ledger, the Lost and Found basket and the prize stand by the ring toss. Come and see who won what."
city.xf.prog.pr.fri:
FRIDAY'S PRIZES.
Ring toss: a lollipop, and for five out of five we'll have to invent something.
Gallery: a postcard.
Lottery: a postcard, sometimes one with the lighthouse.
Photographer: not here yet.
city.xf.prog.pr.sat:
SATURDAY'S PRIZES.
Strongman: a badge, and for 60 points a badge with a ribbon.
Ring toss: a lollipop and the right to touch the lighthouse.
The cups by the lottery: a lollipop and the tin gull.
Gallery: a postcard.
city.xf.prog.pr.sun:
SUNDAY'S PRIZES.
Table tennis: a harmonica for whoever beats Kask.
The cups: the gull with a key.
Ring toss: the hedgehog.
For everyone who lasts until the evening: a lollipop.
city.xf.prog.rules:
RULES.
1. Hit the strongman once at a time; shoot the ducks lengthways, not sideways.
2. Do not touch the bulbs, even the good ones.
3. Lost things go to the scales, into the Lost and Found basket.
4. The festoon switch is on the posts at both ends of the canopy: you switch it on, you switch it off.
city.xf.prog.sat:
SATURDAY.
12:00 the roundabout for little ones.
18:00 the open contest at the strongman: Beresnev against all comers.
20:30 the photographer works until dusk.
Prize of the day: the tin lighthouse.
city.xf.prog.sun:
SUNDAY.
12:00 dominoes under the canopy.
15:00 table tennis, whoever turns up plays.
19:00 the rematch at the strongman.
21:30 the lights go out one by one.
Prize of the day: the plaster hedgehog.
city.xf.progl.1: The fair's programme hangs in a frame under the canopy. In pencil at the bottom: "Changes every day."
city.xf.progl.rain: Rain drums on the canopy overhead, the programme hangs below. Rain is not in it, but nothing is cancelled.
city.xf.radio.am: The radio, briskly: "Feet shoulder-width apart! And one, and two, and..." Behind the counter the gallery keeper does a squat without taking his hands out of his pockets.
city.xf.radio.day: The news: "All quiet on the embankment, noisy at the fair, the weather makes no demands." The gallery keeper pretends he isn't listening on purpose.
city.xf.radio.eve: A waltz. The ducks on their chain seem to move in time, and the little bell in the corner rings on the strong beat.
city.xf.radio.night: A quiet hiss and distant music. Before leaving, the keeper turns the radio off so the ducks can sleep.
city.xf.radio.rain: Rain on the canopy and a waltz from the radio. You could not invent a better pair.
city.xf.shell.after.1: Three cups stand in a row, no pea under any of them. They play without me and I watch.
city.xf.shell.after.2: Rashid spins a cup on his finger: "That's enough for today. Tomorrow the pea will be fresh and well rested."
city.xf.shell.draw.1: A draw: nobody found the pea, it sits in Rashid's sleeve and grins.
city.xf.shell.lose.1: Missed. The pea was under the one I never even looked at. Rashid shakes his head in sympathy.
city.xf.shell.lose.2: I thought I had it, but I hadn't. Rashid rearranges the cups for the next player: "Don't be upset, everyone here loses smiling."
city.xf.shell.prompt: E — guess where the pea is
city.xf.shell.tell.1: {0} glances a little to the left as if something interesting were there.
city.xf.shell.tell.2: {0} straightens the middle cup with a finger and at once takes the hand away.
city.xf.shell.tell.3: {0} looks at the right cup far too calmly.
city.xf.shell.title: Three cups
city.xf.shell.win.1: The pea is under my cup. Rashid admits: "Clean. Just don't tell anyone I have a system."
city.xf.shell.win.2: Guessed on the third try. Rashid takes a lollipop from his pocket: "This isn't a prize, it's consolation for us both."
city.xf.stand.1: A tiered prize stand: the duck and hedgehog below, the lighthouse and harmonica in the middle, a tin gull on top. Labelled: "Do not touch, win."
city.xf.stand.all: The stand is full: every place carries a tag "Won". The seller nods: "You've got the lot. The stand bows to you, politely, with one top corner."
city.xf.stand.duck: The clockwork duck on the bottom tier looks as if it knows I am the one who won it. I know too.
city.xf.stand.gull: The tin gull with a key: won from Rashid at the cups. She takes three steps and ponders.
city.xf.stand.harmonica: A harmonica in a frame: I beat Kask at table tennis. One note doesn't work, but it's a note I can't play anyway.
city.xf.stand.hedgehog: The plaster hedgehog with matchstick spines. I won it at the gallery, and it now has surprised eyebrows, like every prize.
city.xf.stand.lighthouse: The tin lighthouse on the middle tier, with a bulb from a signal lamp. I won it at the strongman, and it remembers.
city.xf.stand.postcard: A postcard with the lighthouse from the lottery is pinned to the stand. The seller says it is lucky until it fades.
city.xf.stand.prompt: E — look at the prize stand
city.xf.talk.car.prompt: E — talk to the roundabout's keeper
city.xf.text.alb.title: The traveller's album
city.xf.text.led.title: The strongman's ledger
city.xf.text.prog.title: The fair's programme
city.xf.weights.1: Three kettlebells: 16, 24 and 32 kilos. The sixteen rose like a feather, the twenty-four like a promise. The thirty-two stayed where it was and nodded politely with its handle.
city.xf.weights.am: In the morning the kettlebells are cold as fish from the ice-house. Lifting one at the first go is a feat, at the second a habit.
city.xf.weights.pm: By evening the kettlebells have warmed from all the palms. The middle one feels lighter than it is, and that is part of the trick too.
city.xf.weights.rain: It is dry under the canopy, the kettlebell does not slip. I lifted the twenty-four twice. Nearly a record, but there is nowhere to write it down.
city.xf.weights.we: At the weekend two people wait beside me for the kettlebells, pretending to study the bunting. I lifted the twenty-four, and it looked good.
city.xf.win.gallery: The third duck in a row is down. The keeper puts the hedgehog on the shelf: "This one has matchstick spines, don't touch it wet."
city.xf.win.ring: The ring settled on the bottle. The seller takes a lollipop from the lower shelf and shows the clockwork duck from a distance: "Look for now, don't take."
city.xf.win.strong: Clang! Beresnev would be proud and Melnikova would probably nod. The seller writes me in the ledger in red.
city.xh.aud.after.1: Isla puts the tuning fork in her pocket: "Enough auditions for today. A voice tires too. Come tomorrow if you like."
city.xh.aud.draw.1: A draw. Isla says: "Odd, but I have not understood how it ended." And she laughs herself, for the first time this evening.
city.xh.aud.lose.1: On the second line my voice swerved like a boat on a wave. Isla puts the tuning fork on the table: "No matter. A clean note is not born, it is grown. Come on Wednesday."
city.xh.aud.lose.2: I tried so hard to show feeling that I forgot the words. Isla says kindly: "You have the feeling, you do not have the words. Words can be learned, feeling must be kept."
city.xh.aud.prompt: E — step onto the mark: a voice trial
city.xh.aud.tell.1: {0} closes her eyes and listens to a single note, as you listen to a tap that drips.
city.xh.aud.tell.2: {0} turns the tuning fork on her palm and frowns: she hears loud ones from the corridor.
city.xh.aud.tell.3: {0} suddenly smiles at something of her own and forgets to conduct.
city.xh.aud.title: A voice trial
city.xh.aud.win.1: I sang to the end and Isla is silent. Then she says, "Now it is clear you were listening." And hands me a cup of coffee: "That is not a prize, that is prevention. Look after your throat."
city.xh.aud.win.2: The last note went up into the vaults and came back a second later, a little lower. Isla nods: "The echo has accepted you. The choir does not take everybody, but coming to terms with the echo matters more."
city.xh.booklet.1:
THE VAULTS COMMUNITY HALL.
The week's programme. Above us four white vaults: the tallest over the hall, the widest over the dancing, the most modest over the kitchen, and the first meets you at the door and holds your coat.
city.xh.booklet.2: What when: Tuesday the lecture, Wednesday the «Surf» choir, Thursday a rehearsal of the «Wave» theatre, Friday dancing, Saturday the premiere and dancing after, Sunday tea dances. Mondays we rest. Admission is free, seats by love.
city.xh.booklet.3: House rules: do not applaud in the final pause, the echo applauds for you. Do not step on the stage in dancing shoes. Drink tea at the bar, not in the stalls. If you forget something, it waits on the shelf in the cloakroom, and nobody judges it.
city.xh.booklet.4: Who is who. The caretaker: keys, cloakroom, bar. The choir leader Isla Bērziņa: «Surf», Wednesday to Sunday, five to nine. The steward, who is also the Watchmaker: until nine in the evening, by agreement. The kitchen: bread in the morning, soup by day, pies towards evening, tea until closing.
city.xh.bread.1: The bread comes out of the oven: the crust crackles like a campfire. The cook cuts off the heel: "Here, while it is hot. Just do not tell anyone."
city.xh.bread.2: The morning bread smells so good that two from the choir, who are really due at five, look in through the kitchen door. The cook pretends not to see.
city.xh.bread.closed: The oven has gone cool: bread is baked here from morning until one. On the tray only flour dust and a note: "Tomorrow from nine."
city.xh.bread.prompt: E — take the bread out of the oven
city.xh.case.fri: "Friday. Dance shoes of thirty years." One pair is worn through at the left toe. Caption: "The left foot led."
city.xh.case.mon: A plaque on the case: "Monday. Fishing floats of Lyudmilovsk." Glass ones, blue and green. On the biggest, scratched: "Not mine."
city.xh.case.prompt: E — look into the display case
city.xh.case.sat: "Saturday. What is left after a premiere." A prop key, a dried rose, a programme signed by the whole company. An empty space beside them: "For tomorrow's things."
city.xh.case.sun: The case is being cleaned; the plaque says "Sunday. Resting." The glass shines, and inside it a nose is reflected. Yours, it seems.
city.xh.case.thu: "Thursday. Theatre programmes of different years." The oldest is printed on the back of a cable car ticket. Print run: "as many as friends."
city.xh.case.tue: "Tuesday. School exercise books with views of the town." In one, the lighthouse is drawn three times, from a new side each time. At the bottom, a mark: "Good for a first attempt."
city.xh.case.wed: "Wednesday. Musical instruments: a harmonica, a tuning fork, a cracked guitar top." The fork lies by the harmonica as if it had argued with it and lost.
city.xh.chalk.cold: Along the edge of the board in big chalk: "HOT TEA". Under it a wisp of steam and three exclamation marks. One is crossed out: too many.
city.xh.chalk.dance: In chalk, big: "DANCE! Duchesse 18, pie 18, tea 15, coffee 30. Napkin free for dancers." The napkin is drawn too.
city.xh.chalk.day: In chalk: "By day: soup from the kitchen, if the kitchen has not changed its mind. Tea 15, coffee 30, pie 18." At the bottom: "Duchesse 18, cold and very sweet."
city.xh.chalk.eve: In chalk: "In the evening, the same, only quieter. Tea 15, coffee 30, pie 18, Duchesse 18." Beside it, a drawn teapot that seems to wink.
city.xh.chalk.morning: In chalk on the board: "Tea 15. Coffee 30. Pie 18. Duchesse 18." Below: "Yesterday's pie: discounted, with an honest confession." The last line is underlined.
city.xh.chalk.warm: In chalk: "Hot. Duchesse from the fridge, three roubles extra for the chill." The three roubles are crossed out, because the caretaker is out of breath himself.
city.xh.choir.fest: A festive repertoire: the choir sings an old song about the sea, and half the hall suddenly knows the words. The leader smiles and stops conducting: from here they manage on their own.
city.xh.choir.rain: Rain outside, and the choir sings about rain. It came out by chance, but the leader kept it in the programme: "The weather rehearses us."
city.xh.choir.wed: On Wednesdays the rehearsal is open: you may sit in the hall and keep quiet. Singing along is allowed only in a whisper, that is the leader's condition.
city.xh.choirtalk.hello.1: Isla raises a hand and the choir falls silent. "One minute," she tells the hall. "Someone has come to see me." Twenty-two people pretend not to listen.
city.xh.choirtalk.hello.2: "Altos a tone higher, basses a step lower, me a glass of water," says Isla without turning. And only then turns: "Yes? I am listening."
city.xh.choirtalk.prompt: E — talk to the choir leader
city.xh.choirtalk.t1.1: "«Surf» is twenty-two people and not one perfect ear," Isla smiles. "We grow the ear. The first year we sing in unison, the second in thirds, and in the third somebody always starts a solo and everyone acts as if that was the plan."
city.xh.choirtalk.t1.2: "Wednesday rehearsals are open. Sit anywhere, only not where the music lies: those are the basses' seats, and they are touchy."
city.xh.choirtalk.t2.1: "Want to try? Stand on the chalk cross at the front of the stage," says Isla. "You can sing it clean, loud or with feeling. I will tell you what suited. The choir does not care, but your pride does."
city.xh.choirtalk.t2.2: "A draw is not really possible," she adds. "But sometimes I do not understand myself how it ended. Then we say the echo won."
city.xh.choirtalk.t3.1: "In the play the choir is the clocks backstage," Isla explains. "We tick. First 'tick', then 'tock'. The hardest thing is not to hurry: a clock that hurries is an alarm."
city.xh.choirtalk.t3.2: "The prompter's copy lies by the left wing, you can read it. Only there is one line about the choir in it. The rest we invent ourselves."
city.xh.cloak.hello.1: "Good morning," says the caretaker, laying out the tags on the hooks. "Empty for now, you can pick any hook. In the evening they fight over them."
city.xh.cloak.hello.2: "Come in," nods the caretaker from behind the rail. "Want to leave something, leave it. Want to find something, ask the lost-property shelf."
city.xh.cloak.hello.3: "Take a tag," says the caretaker without leaving the rail. "In the evening it is coat on coat here, and all alike."
city.xh.cloak.hello.rain: "Wet things on the end hook, over the radiator," says the caretaker. "Umbrellas in the bucket by the door. The bucket, by the way, is in the programme too."
city.xh.cloak.t1.1: "Forty tags," the caretaker explains. "Thirty-nine round and one square. The square one is for the director. The director lost it and now goes without a coat."
city.xh.cloak.t1.2: "If you lose your tag, describe the coat," he adds. "The rail and I remember each other better than we remember people."
city.xh.cloak.t2.1: "Here is the shelf," the caretaker shows under the counter. "A left glove, a checked scarf, violin rosin, spectacles missing a lens. People come for them less often than you would think."
city.xh.cloak.t2.2: "The oddest is a little key on a string. For half a year nobody has asked. It lies and waits. Perhaps it is not for a door at all."
city.xh.cloak.t3.1: "Wednesday the choir, all with music," the caretaker lists. "Friday the dancers, all with spare shoes. Saturday everyone with flowers and nowhere to put them."
city.xh.cloak.t3.2: "Have you been to the choir? Then you know Isla. She arrives five minutes early and every time apologises for being late."
city.xh.cloaktalk.prompt: E — talk to the cloakroom attendant
city.xh.clock.dance.1: {time}. A slip is stuck to the clock face over the dance floor: "There is still time before the last waltz." The slip is old, and the waltz is still the last.
city.xh.clock.dance.fri: {time}. The clock above the dance floor runs a little slower than usual, as if ordered. On Fridays nobody corrects it.
city.xh.clock.foyer.day: {time}. The foyer clock runs three minutes fast: the steward's order, so the actors are not late. The actors have long known and are late by exactly three minutes.
city.xh.clock.foyer.eve: {time}. The foyer smells of wet wool and pies, the evening's poster is up, and the clock ticks as if counting those who come in.
city.xh.clock.foyer.morning: The clock above the pictures says {time}. The first evening is far off: the caretaker goes round the hall with a duster, talking to the frames.
city.xh.clock.foyer.rain: {time}. The clock ticks in time with the rain on the vaults. Together it makes something like a slow waltz.
city.xh.clock.foyer.sat: {time}. Tonight is the premiere and the foyer clock ticks louder than usual. Or it is a heart, you cannot tell yet.
city.xh.clock.hall.1: {time}. The hall clock hangs right by the door so latecomers can see by how much. Under it in chalk: "Slow and steady, but on time."
city.xh.clock.hall.sat: {time}. The clock above the door, under it the caretaker's back. He watches the hands as if the play starting depends on them. Perhaps it does.
city.xh.clock.kitchen.1: {time}. The cook sets the time by the clock and the clock by the pies. If a pie has risen, it is later than the hands say.
city.xh.clock.kitchen.eve: {time}. The kitchen clock is splashed with flour, but the hands can be seen. The bread is long out, the pies are coming, the tea is already bubbling.
city.xh.closed.any.1: The hall is closed. A lantern moves in the foyer window: the night watchman is making his round and does not like being watched. The sound of his steps in the vaults lasts longer than the watchman.
city.xh.closed.any.2: Beyond the glass a dark hall, and on the stage the ghost light glows. It is left so the stage does not feel abandoned. The watchman says the lamp is the one in charge and he is only its helper.
city.xh.closed.any.3: On the door a sign: "Open from ten until eleven at night. The watchman is on duty but sells nothing and talks to nobody after nine."
city.xh.closed.counter.1: The counter is shut behind a grille with a note: "Gone to heat the kettle. Back with tea or not back." Under it a drawing of a cup and a very sad little man.
city.xh.closed.counter.2: In the closed counter's glass flickers the reflection of the ghost light from the stage. It burns, so the key is with the watchman, and the watchman is somewhere in the hall.
city.xh.closed.play.1: The lid is closed with a note: "Do not touch the music, the tuner comes on Monday." On Mondays he comes and says the strings are tired too.
city.xh.closed.screen.1: The curtain is closed. A strip of the ghost light shows under it, and it seems that someone very quiet is rehearsing behind. That is, of course, a draught.
city.xh.closed.seat.1: The chairs are pushed to the wall and covered with old curtains against the dust. The watchman would say the chairs are resting, but the watchman is nowhere to be seen.
city.xh.closed.seat.2: You cannot sit now: on the seats a note "Do not warm." The watchman says a chair that has been sat on at night then spends all day thinking it is a sofa.
city.xh.closed.sport.1: The floor is polished like a mirror and roped off: the watchman says that at night he rehearses a waltz himself. He sets the rope straight on the right side.
city.xh.coll.hall_evenings.title: Ticket stubs of the evenings in the Vaults
city.xh.cook.t1.1: "Bread until one, soup from twelve to four, samovar tea from three until closing, pies from four to nine," the cook lists. "Everything by the clock, like trains. Only the pies are late."
city.xh.cook.t1.2: "One loaf a day per person. This is not a bakery, it is a community hall: you cannot bake for everyone, but for a good person something turns up."
city.xh.cook.t2.1: "Hear how the choir comes through the vent?" the cook raises a finger. "This is my third year cooking to «Surf». My borscht has come out steadier for it."
city.xh.cook.t2.2: "The props people sometimes borrow my rolling pin to play a mace. It comes back with pathos and in flour. I do not complain, I take note."
city.xh.cook.t3.1: "Sandwiches for the actors, so they do not eat backstage. Pies for the dancers, so they do not collapse after the waltz. Warm drinks for the choir, to mind the throat. The caretaker gets everything at once."
city.xh.cook.t3.2: "Audiences are not on the list, but whoever stands at the kitchen door pretending to pass by always finds something."
city.xh.cooktalk.hello.1: Somebody in an apron stands at the stove, something already bubbling on it. "What did you want?" comes without a turn. "Bread is in the oven, no hands."
city.xh.cooktalk.hello.2: "Soup will be at one," the cook announces, stirring. "Meanwhile you can just sit and sniff. It is free and counts as supper too."
city.xh.cooktalk.hello.3: The cook wipes his hands on his apron. "I am taking the pies out. The quick get a pie. The slow get tea, which is not bad either."
city.xh.costumes.fri: Dress rehearsal: every costume in place, ironed, smelling of a hot iron. "Echo" and "Second Echo" are identical grey cloaks; the second is tagged "This is the second one."
city.xh.costumes.mon: The rail backstage. Tags on the hangers: "Clockmaker", "Mayor", "Postwoman", "Echo", "Second Echo". The Clockmaker tag is pinned to the handyman's waistcoat. He objected, but it fits like a glove.
city.xh.costumes.prompt: E — sort through the costume rail
city.xh.costumes.sat: The rail is almost empty: the costumes are on the actors. One hanger is left, tagged "Spare". The spare is nervous too.
city.xh.costumes.sun: The costumes are back on the rail, smelling of the stage and a little of pies. On the Clockmaker's hanger, a card from someone in the audience: "You were better than all the clocks."
city.xh.costumes.thu: The Postwoman's dress is hemmed in a hurry, threads sticking out. Pencilled on the hem: "Hem after the dress rehearsal. If I'm late, nobody will notice. If they do, I'll say it's deliberate."
city.xh.costumes.tue: A pocket-watch chain has joined the waistcoat. There is no watch on it. A note: "The prop master will bring the watch. Prop master, where are you?"
city.xh.costumes.wed: The Mayor's jacket is two sizes too big for the Mayor. Pins beside it and the dresser's note: "Mayor, no pies until Saturday. Or eat them, but quietly."
city.xh.dance.band.1: Live music: a pianist from the next building and a drummer on a stool. You waltz with someone who keeps looking at their feet. Then they look at you, and that is better.
city.xh.dance.band.2: A fast dance. Everyone spins, the mirror ball scatters spots of light over faces and walls. For a second the hall is an aquarium of glowing fish.
city.xh.dance.band.3: Ladies' choice: the girls do the asking. Someone bows to you and you bow back. Your partner says: "Don't look at your feet, they know." They do.
city.xh.dance.fest: A holiday, and the caretaker puts the records on himself: "Everyone dances with everyone, no questions." A couple glides past: he in a coat, she with a kettle. It bothers nobody.
city.xh.dance.fri_idle.1: The empty floor waits for evening. The mirror ball is silent, the pennants stir in the draught, and in the corner the piano remembers a waltz. You take one step, just in case.
city.xh.dance.sun_idle.1: Sunday outside the tea hours: the floor gleams as if just washed. It was.
city.xh.dance.sun_tea.1: Tea dances: elderly couples dance slowly and very beautifully. Your partner whispers: "One-two-three, don't hurry." You don't hurry, and the waltz works.
city.xh.dance.wk_class.1: The dance club: the teacher claps the count and says loudly, "And one, and two!" You try. It comes out nearly like everyone else's.
city.xh.dance.wk_idle.1: The polished floor reflects the vault well. You can move without witnesses: no one sees you trip over your own shadow.
city.xh.dancemirror.prompt: E — stand at the barre mirror
city.xh.dancenight.prompt: E — step onto the dance floor
city.xh.evenings.0: A board covered in green baize with five brass nails. Under each a label: "Choir", "Dancing", "Lecture", "Rehearsal", "Premiere". Whoever has been to an evening hangs a stub. The free nails wait.
city.xh.evenings.choir: On the "Choir" nail a red stub: "Surf, row 3, seat by love." On the back in pencil: "Sang along in a whisper. They noticed me."
city.xh.evenings.dance: On the "Dancing" nail a yellow stub with a tea stain. Under it in small writing: "Waltz. Did not tread on anyone. Almost."
city.xh.evenings.lecture: On the "Lecture" nail a blue stub with a parabola drawn on it. Drawn well, with little rays.
city.xh.evenings.premiere: On the "Premiere" nail a pink stub bigger than the others. A note: "The echo clapped longer than I did."
city.xh.evenings.prompt: E — look at the stub board
city.xh.evenings.t1: One stub on the board, and it already looks livelier. The caretaker says the whole hall began like that, with one evening.
city.xh.evenings.t3: Three stubs out of five. The caretaker nods: "You are no longer a guest, you are nearly one of us."
city.xh.evenings.t5: All five nails are taken. Beside them the caretaker has pinned a slip: "One of us. We are not giving out a key yet, but he gets his tea without queueing."
city.xh.evenings.theatre: On the "Rehearsal" nail a green stub with a fingerprint: the Watchmaker held it while he looked for the words he had forgotten.
city.xh.exh.east.1: «The Sea We Know». On the wall this week: amateurs' work, fishing boats, a lighthouse in fog, a sand spit. A sheet is pinned to the label: "We vote in pencil: which sea is best." The one with the gull is ahead.
city.xh.exh.east.2: «Neighbours». A new hang: portraits of the residents of the serpentine house, painted in oils but in the manner of a postcard. Under each, a name and a floor. One neighbour came out so true that he now hides from his own portrait.
city.xh.exh.east.3: «Evenings in the Vaults». Photographs of the choir and the dances, printed at the club. In one the choir sings with open mouths and no sound, and that makes the whole hall louder.
